jobs.title: Senior Android Engineer - Engine by Starling
jobs.description:
At Engine by Starling, we are on a mission to find and work with leading banks all around the world who have the ambition to build rapid growth businesses, on our technology. 

Engine is Starling's software-as-a-service (SaaS) business, the technology that was built to power Starling, and a year ago we split out as a separate business. 

Starling has seen exceptional growth and success, and a large part of that is down to the fact that we have built our own modern technology from the ground up. This SaaS technology platform is now available to banks and financial institutions all around the world, enabling them to benefit from the innovative digital features, and efficient back-office processes that has helped achieve Starling's success.

Our technologists are at the very heart of Engine and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment that is all about building things, creating new stuff, and disruptive technology that keeps us on the cutting edge of fintech. We operate a flat structure to empower you to make decisions regardless of what your primary responsibilities may be, innovation and collaboration will be at the core of everything you do. Help is never far away in our open culture, you will find support in your team and from across the business, we are in this together!

The way to thrive and shine within Engine is to be a self-driven individual and be able to take full ownership of everything around you: From building things, designing, and discovering to sharing knowledge with your colleagues and making sure all processes are efficient and productive to deliver the best possible results for our customers. Our purpose is underpinned by five values: Listen, Keep It Simple, Do The Right Thing, Own It, and Aim For Greatness.

Hybrid Working

We have a Hybrid approach to working here at Engine - our preference is that you're located within a commutable distance of our offices so that we're able to interact and collaborate in person.

About Engineering at Engine by Starling - https://enginebystarling.com/engineering-careers/ 

Engine by Starling engineers are excited about helping us deliver new features, regardless of what their primary tech stack may be. Hear more from the team in some case studies below, and our work with Women In Tech.
• Day in the Life of a Mobile Engineer
• Working as a Mobile QA
• Leading the Android Team
• Engineering careers page

We are looking for engineers at all levels to join the team. We value people being engaged and caring about customers, caring about the code they write and the contribution they make to banking worldwide. People with a broad ability to apply themselves to a multitude of problems and challenges, who can work across teams do great things here at Engine, to continue changing banking for good.

As an Engineer you will:
• Contribute to our award winning Android app and internal tooling
• Build new features and products from scratch in a configurable way
• Share your knowledge with those around you, contributing to our learning culture
• Own your projects, working in small teams across the bank to collaboratively deliver
• Aim for greatness in everything you do, staying curious and inquisitive
• Be part of a scaling team and organisation as we change banking for good

You are empowered to make the decisions necessary for the project and to provide insight to the team leads. You’ll also be working closely with other Android engineers with a variety of experience levels and interests, helping us improve and develop our Android app, CI automations and tooling. You’ll be committing, reviewing and shipping new code right from the first week! 

As an Android engineer, you’ll report to and catch-up regularly with a mobile lead engineer who will support you on your journey in Engine. We have a strong collaborative and open culture here so you’ll find support outside your team too. 

As a fully digital bank, we are looking for engineers that are able to understand and prioritise security when implementing new features, fixing bugs or making technical improvements, across all the layers. Our team is designing, building and releasing new screens every day, for this reason we are interested in people with a particular focus on Accessibility along with writing clean and maintainable code. 

The way to thrive and shine within Engine is to be a self-driven individual and be able to take full ownership of everything around you: From building the code, shipping and maintaining it, to sharing knowledge with your colleagues and making sure all processes are efficient and productive to deliver the best possible results for our customers. 

Our aim is to deliver stable, resilient and high quality code, that is why testing is another key quality we look for when expanding our team. We use Espresso to write our UI/E2E Test and JUnit to write our Unit Tests across all layers of the application, as well as manually test all features before they go into production. We also work closely with QA engineers to ensure we have an additional level of testing when working on complex feature delivery. 

The Android world 

At Engine, we are proud to be working with some of the latest technologies in the industry. When adopting new technologies we always consider as a team whether it’s the best choice for our product and our users. 

We are currently in the process of building a number of SDKs for our clients utilising the modules we’ve already created in the Starling UK App. We’ll be using these to support the development of an app in Romania with Salt Bank and build an entirely new banking app for one of our partners in Australia called AMP Bank, a really exciting opportunity! In the Engine SDKs we generally aim to use the latest technology as our clients would expect, but, we also rely heavily on the existing Starling codebase which uses some older libraries too, so you’ll need a good understanding of a wide range of libraries and technologies. We use Dagger, Realm, Retrofit, Coil, Compose, Coroutines and Compose, but there’s still a lot of work to do migrating from XML layouts and RxJava2.

Building SDKs that we plan to launch internationally can present some new challenges, so if you’ve ever had experience maintaining a library, contributing to OSS, or have dealt with Internationalisation we’d love to hear about it. If that’s all new to you, don’t worry, we’re learning too!

We want our app to look great for the Android platform and have worked closely with our designers to set up a component library and have themed our app accordingly. Feature parity is important to us so Android and iOS apps are often built alongside each other. 

As a team we meet together every week to talk through pain points and potential improvements we’ll like to make to the project. We regularly meet in real life to attend conferences and meet-ups together too! 

Interview process

Interviewing is a two way process and we want you to have the time and opportunity to get to know us, as much as we are getting to know you! Our interviews are conversational and we want to get the best from you, so come with questions and be curious. In general you can expect the below, following a chat with one of our Talent Team:
• First interview: ~45 minutes
• Take home technical test (no time limit)
• Technical face to face: ~1.5 hours
• Final Interview: ~45 minutes
• 33 days holiday (including public holidays, which you can take when it works best for you)
• An extra day’s holiday for your birthday
• Annual leave is increased with length of service, and you can choose to buy or sell up to five extra days off
• 16 hours paid volunteering time a year
• Salary sacrifice, company enhanced pension scheme
• Life insurance at 4x your salary & group income protection
• Private Medical Insurance with VitalityHealth including mental health support and cancer care. Partner benefits include discounts with Waitrose, Mr&Mrs Smith and Peloton
• Generous family-friendly policies
• Incentives refer a friend scheme
• Perkbox membership giving access to retail discounts, a wellness platform for physical and mental health, and weekly free and boosted perks
• Access to initiatives like Cycle to Work, Salary Sacrificed Gym partnerships and Electric Vehicle (EV) leasing

About us:

You may be put off applying for a role because you don't tick every box. Forget that! While we can’t accommodate every flexible working request, we're always open to discussion. So, if you're excited about working with us, but aren’t sure if you're 100% there yet, get in touch anyway. We’re on a mission to radically reshape banking – and that starts with our brilliant team. Whatever came before, we’re proud to bring together people of all backgrounds and experiences who love working together to solve problems.

Engine by Starling is an equal opportunity employer, and we’re proud of our ongoing efforts to foster diversity & inclusion in the workplace. Individuals seeking employment at Engine by Starling are considered without regard to race, religion, national origin, age, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, medical condition, ancestry, physical or mental disability, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. 

When you provide us with this information, you are doing so at your own consent, with full knowledge that we will process this personal data in accordance with our Privacy Notice. By submitting your application, you agree that Engine by Starling and Starling will collect your personal data for recruiting and related purposes. Our Privacy Notice explains what personal information we will process, where we will process your personal information, its purposes for processing your personal information, and the rights you can exercise over our use of your personal information.

We are on a mission to find and work with leading banks all around the world who have the ambition to build rapid growth businesses, on our technology. We are looking for future leaders to come and join our team, to build client relationships, and work with them to understand their needs and how we can solve them with Engine’s technology.

Who are Engine by Starling

Engine by Starling is transforming the banking landscape with our cutting-edge core banking software. Originally developed to power Starling, our cloud-native SaaS platform is now enabling banks and financial institutions globally to modernize operations and deliver exceptional digital banking experiences. 

We are headquartered in London with offices in Dublin, Sydney and Dubai. We've recently launched in North America where we are establishing an East Coast HQ, as well as our presence in Canada. 

This role will be based in the Charlotte, NC, our preference is that you're located within a commutable distance. The role will involve regular national and across north America with some international travel, .

About the role

As a Solution Architect (SA) you will use your understanding of the Engine technology and architecture to explain the Engine product, uncover client requirements and support the design of client solutions.

You will be involved in both the sales and delivery phases of a project as well as ongoing client success, collaborating with teams across Engine in Technology, Delivery, Product, Client Success and Business Development.
Supporting these activities on client sites means the role will require travel around North America, and occasional further travel.

What you'll get to do:

This role blends deep technical expertise with strong communication and collaboration skills. You'll become an Engine expert, understanding its architecture, technology, and functionality, allowing you to effectively communicate its capabilities and value to both technical and non-technical audiences.

You’ll lead on technical designs during the Engine implementation phase, building relationships with a variety of stakeholders within clients and SI partners such as their Engineering leads and Service Owners. 

You will work closely with our clients and SI partners on the technical detail of implementing Engine, providing solutions to identified requirements and working with our Product and engineering teams to fulfil them. Your contributions will also extend to shaping Engine's product roadmap and supporting existing clients with additional capabilities to meet their strategic aims. You’ll help them maximise Engine’s current and future capabilities to solve their requirements and meticulously document scope and roadmap decisions to guide subsequent delivery waves, bringing in expertise from our Product Owners and engineering teams where required.

You will also be a technical champion for our existing clients, ensuring their ongoing success. This includes taking ownership of the technical aspects of client deliveries, collaborating closely with our SI partners to overcome challenges and achieve seamless integrations. You'll provide expert guidance to client engineering teams, using documentation, API specifications, and sequence diagrams to foster a deep understanding of Engine's architecture and functionalities. Additionally, you will collaborate closely with our Client Success team to troubleshoot technical issues, translate client needs into new technical requirements, and architect innovative solutions that enhance the Engine platform.

Must Have
• Experience of end-to-end software engineering / solution architecture across the software delivery lifecycle
• Experience with software service design and integration, such as RESTful APIs, OpenAPI specification and sequence diagrams
• Experience of cloud infrastructure and large-scale cloud applications
• Experience working in a client-facing role and building relationships with stakeholders
• Strong interpersonal communication and collaboration skills. Experience delivering complex messaging to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Nice to Have
• Experience relating to retail or business banking, core banking, card processing or payments.
• Experience of delivery and implementation of core banking or large-scale digital transformation programmes, application migration and solution integration
• Commercial acumen with experience of building business cases
• Experience in a SaaS organisation in a Client Solutions or Client Engineering role
• Knowledge of financial regulations around the world

About you
• You have a focus on delivery and getting things done for a client

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer II - Data Onboarding & Reporting
jobs.description:
About

the Role:

Wise is on a mission to create money without borders—making it instant, transparent, and eventually free. To support this rapid global growth, our Finance Squad ensures that our financial processes run in an efficient, scalable, and controlled manner.

We are looking for a talented Senior Software Engineer II to join our Data Onboarding Team in London. In this role, you will be the driving force behind building, scaling, and optimizing the critical data pipelines on top of our Lakehouse (Trino + Iceberg) infrastructure following a strict Medallion Architecture (Bronze, Silver, Gold layers). You will build robust data pipelines that serve as the foundational bedrock for reporting and assurance across the entire Finance squad.

The Finance Squad is responsible for steward-shipping the financial truth of Wise. The Data Onboarding team operates alongside Core Accounting, Finance Implementation, and Data & Assurance. Our team's mandate is to abstract product complexity and build reusable, domain-agnostic stream-enrichment pipelines. We handle high-throughput financial event data (processing hundreds of millions of events daily) to bridge the gap between immutable product events and audit-ready data structures.

What will you be working on?

Technical Leadership & Pipeline Engineering
• Lakehouse Architecture: Design, build, and optimize robust end-to-end data pipelines on top of our Trino + Iceberg Lakehouse stack.
• Medallion Implementation: Own the extraction, cleaning, and modeling layers to progressively refine raw event logs (Bronze) into verified subledgers (Silver) and structured Gold metrics.
• Stream Processing: Work closely with high-throughput messaging queues (Kafka) and real-time computation models to maintain our data freshness SLAs.
• Data Quality & Assurance: Embed rigorous, automated reconciliation checks within the data pipelines (e.g., balance and double-entry validations) to catch data discrepancies before they reach financial reporting layers.

Strategic Impact & Collaboration
• Product & Stakeholder Alignment: Partner directly with finance controllers, analysts, product and engineering to turn complex corporate finance needs into production-ready data schemas.
• Platform Alignment: Address data scaling constraints, structural technical debt, and compute optimizations to directly align infrastructure costs with Wise's financial targets.

Mentorship & Engineering Excellence
• Upskilling: Assist and coach mid-level/junior engineers within the team, performing thorough code and technical design reviews.

Must Haves (Hard Skills)
• Data Lakehouse Mastery: Proven experience building data infrastructure using Trino / Presto and open table formats like Apache Iceberg or Delta Lake.
• Advanced Data Modeling: Deep expertise in Medallion Architecture patterns, Star Schemas, and processing semi-structured financial data logs (JSON/Avro).
• Robust ETL/ELT Orchestration: Expert proficiency in data transformation engines (such as dbt) and scheduling tools (such as Airflow).
• Stream/Message Queues: Solid understanding of event-driven architectures and streaming processing via Apache Kafka.
• Strong Programming Foundations: Proficiency in Python, SQL, or an Object-Oriented language (Java/Scala).

Nice to Haves
• Experience operating data assets within a regulated SOX/PCAOB compliance environment.
• Familiarity with cloud data warehouses (e.g., Snowflake) and cloud compute orchestration.
• Prior domain exposure to financial flows, double-entry ledger systems, or accounting integrations.

Soft Skills
• A strong sense of long-term technical ownership.
• Excellent communication skills with the ability to bridge technical engineering realities with financial analyst requirements.

What We Offer / Selling Points
• The rare opportunity to help engineer the core "Engine of Trust" for a fast-growing global fintech moving billions in cross-border volume.
• A chance to work beyond isolated data pipelines, building reusable libraries and system-wide framework layers rather than bespoke, one-off fixes.
• Direct interaction and collaboration with top-tier product minds, data platform engineers, and global financial stakeholders.

 

Interested? Find out more:
• How we work – a practical guide
• DEI @ Wise
• Wise Tech Stack (2025 update)

What do we offer:
• Starting salary: £111k - £145k + RSUs
• Wise Benefits
• #LI-AB3 #LI-Hybrid
• Paved Paths: Create structured framework documentation and automated tooling to reduce onboarding friction for new data sources.

jobs.title: Group Regulatory Affairs Lead
jobs.description:
As a Regulatory Affairs Lead, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and executing a new global capability within the Group Core Compliance function. Today, Wise holds over 80 regulatory licences across the UK, Europe, North America, APAC, MEA and LATAM. To sustain our global growth and further elevate our regulatory relationship management, we are establishing a dedicated, centralized Regulatory Affairs function.

Reporting to the Director of Group Core Compliance, you will serve as the single source of truth for the status and strategic trajectory of our regulatory relationships globally. You will work closely with regional Compliance Officers, Risk, Legal, Government Relations and Banking & Expansion teams to establish a centralized view of our global regulatory priorities, providing clear visibility into how these are managed across markets and proactively identifying and resolving any resulting intra-group conflicts or competing interests.

We are looking for a strong stakeholder manager and problem solver who thrives on turning ambiguity into scalable structure. You will bridge the gap between regional Compliance Officers, Group executive leadership, and functional partners (Legal, Risk, Banking & Expansion, Government Relations, Product), ensuring Wise engages with supervisors around the world with one aligned and proactive voice.

 

Your Mission:
• Global Relationship Oversight: Establish enterprise-wide visibility over Wise’s supervisory footprint. Maintain a real-time overview of regional regulatory owners, active supervisory touchpoints, open inquiries, inspections, and regulatory commitments (including remediations) across all operating entities.
• Regulatory Relationship Strategy: In collaboration with regional Compliance Officers and functional partners, anticipate supervisory shifts, thematic review trends, and administrative changes in key markets. Help leadership formulate proactive engagement strategies before risks materialize.
• Regulatory Information Governance: Own the framework for tracking all material regulatory correspondence, bilateral engagements, information requests (RFIs), and regulatory notifications. Eliminate regional blind spots to ensure Wise speaks to supervisors globally with a unified narrative. Translate complex initiatives into clear, consistent external regulatory communications.
• Executive Strategic Reporting: Design data-driven systems that will produce Management Information (MI) for the Director of Group Compliance, executive leadership, Boards and Risk Committees. Strategic reporting will clearly articulate relationship health, emerging issues, and supervisory trends. Translate complex regulatory interactions into actionable reports and advice that can be used to make decisions quickly.
• Supervisory Read-Across & Lessons Learned: Partner with regional Compliance Officers and Product Compliance to evaluate material supervisory inquiries, examination findings, and enforcement precedents across jurisdictions. Ensure critical lessons learned are systematically cascaded to protect parallel licenses.
• Cross-Functional Information Sharing: Drive the agenda and operational cadence for cross-functional information sharing to align on high-impact supervisory developments, market intelligence, and collective remediation without duplicating formal committee governance - exercising strict discretion around confidential topics.
• Incident Response: Act as an advisor for Core Compliance during complex, regulatory incidents, ensuring aligned briefing for regional Compliance Officers, prompt factual verification, and coordinated global regulatory messaging across impacted jurisdictions.

This role will give you the opportunity to:
• Build a function: Take a developing concept and design the global operating model, engagement standards, and data from scratch.
• Influence executive strategy: Shape how leadership and regional Compliance Officers navigate key regulatory engagements and evolving multi-supervisor coalitions.
• Gain unmatched global breadth: Work across a diverse regulatory landscape - collaborating daily with teams across the UK, Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific, LATAM and MEA.
• Champion a data-driven approach: Move regulatory relations beyond traditional narrative memos by embedding quantitative metrics and structured trend analytics into our supervisory governance.

A bit

about you:
• Proven Track Record: Significant experience (10+ years) in Regulatory Affairs and Relations or Compliance within a financial institution or regulatory authority.
• Supervisory Expertise: In-depth understanding of how regulators operate, examine, and communicate. Proven track record managing complex regulatory interactions, audits, thematic inquiries, and executive briefing processes.
• Strategic Thinker: You can connect the dots and build systems. You have experience implementing structured tracking mechanisms, reporting cycles, and relationship management frameworks across multi-entity, cross-border corporate structures.
• Executive Presence & Influence: High emotional intelligence with outstanding written and verbal communication skills. You can distill voluminous, ambiguous regulatory dialogue into succinct executive summaries and comfortably challenge senior stakeholders on regulatory risk.
• Autonomous: You’re comfortable with ambiguity and have a clear bias for action. You can take high-level objectives, work with the Director of Group Core Compliance to define your own milestones, and build collaborative alliances across separate teams.

jobs.title: Principal Content Designer, Fincrime - AUP
jobs.description:
How do you help more people and businesses move money while keeping financial crime out? How do you make complex restrictions understandable, and help customers take the right next step? How do you challenge policies that create unnecessary barriers?

These are some of the challenges you’ll work on as a Principal (IC) Content Designer in Wise’s AUP team, supporting our mission to build an open and fair financial system.

Your mission:

You’ll lead content design for AUP, helping Wise support more legitimate customers and lawful activities while managing risk effectively.

Our team is moving from a policy-first approach to a risk-driven one. That means questioning blanket restrictions, understanding the risks behind different activities, and designing proportionate responses. You’ll turn that strategy into clear policy and useful experiences, so customers understand what they can do with Wise, which conditions apply, and what to do when something goes wrong.

You’ll set the content direction and stay hands-on, working with Product Design, Product, Engineering, Operations, Compliance and other FinCrime teams. Your work will connect the public policy with what customers experience when they join Wise, move money or encounter a restriction.

About

the role:

The Acceptable Use Policy sets out how people and businesses can use Wise. The AUP team sits within the Servicing Tribe and FinCrime Chapter. Today, it focuses on monitoring transactions, with an ambition to address AUP risks across the customer lifecycle.

Our priorities include enabling transfers to regulated crypto platforms, removing unnecessary restrictions on lawful, lower-risk activities, and exploring ways to serve businesses we currently restrict. We’re also improving how we detect risky activity and helping our Operations teams make effective decisions.

Content design is central to making these changes work. A shorter policy needs to remain accurate. A warning needs to explain what action a customer should take. A limit needs to be understandable at the moment it affects someone. And a customer using a personal account for business may need a practical route to the right account.

We’re looking for someone who can make complex rules understandable, question the experience behind the words, and bring teams together around a clear direction.

What you’ll work on:
• Make new permissions and limits understandable. Design experiences that explain supported activities, eligibility and restrictions. For regulated crypto transfers, this could include guidance, scam warnings and clear explanations of transfer limits and next steps.
• Help customers avoid repeated violations. Improve contextual in-app warnings and supporting communications so customers notice them, understand the issue and know how to respond.
• Explore alternatives to unnecessary account closure. Help customers understand the difference between personal and business use, and test journeys that guide eligible customers towards a business account. Support discovery into onboarding and exception journeys for currently restricted business use cases.
• Support consistent operational decisions. Partner with Operations on clear guidance, terminology and customer communications as controls and review processes evolve, including those supported by machine learning and AI.
• Measure and improve the experience. Use research, customer feedback and behavioural data to test understanding and action. Evaluate whether content helps reduce repeated violations and avoidable friction, supports legitimate customer growth, and maintains appropriate safeguards.
• Rethink the public AUP. Lead the content design of a shorter, clearer policy that focuses on illegal and high-risk use cases and explicitly distinguishes personal and business restrictions. Work with Compliance and other policy owners to make it accurate, accessible and useful.
• Build lasting content governance. Establish clear ownership, review and approval processes, and a way to keep policy and product communications aligned as rules change across activities and markets.

Who you’ll be designing for:

People and businesses carrying out legitimate activities. They need to understand whether Wise supports their use case, which conditions apply and how to keep moving money without unnecessary disruption.

Customers who misunderstand a rule or use the wrong account type. They need timely, specific guidance and a practical next step. You’ll help distinguish a correctable mistake from behaviour that requires a firmer response.

People who may be vulnerable or exposed to harm. You’ll bring empathy and care to sensitive journeys, including scam warnings and restrictions that could affect someone’s access to financial services.

Customers whose activity presents significant risk or breaches our terms. You’ll design firm, clear and proportionate communications, working with Compliance and Operations to explain what we can disclose and what happens next.

Across these experiences, you’ll help Wise communicate fairly without assuming that a restricted activity or an automated alert makes someone a bad actor.

What you’ll bring:
• Hands-on content design experience across complex product journeys, with evidence that your work improved customer understanding and outcomes.
• The ability to set strategy at Staff level, influence decisions across teams and deliver detailed content yourself.
• Strong information architecture and plain-language skills, including experience turning complex policies or requirements into usable content.
• Sound judgement in sensitive situations: knowing when to reassure, when to be direct and how to explain consequences fairly.
• Experience using research and data to challenge assumptions, prioritise work and evaluate results.
• The ability to build sustainable content practices and help colleagues make better content decisions.

Experience in financial services, compliance or another regulated environment would be useful. What matters most is your ability to learn a complex domain, ask thoughtful questions and design clear experiences within its constraints.

Heads up, this probably isn’t for you if:

Your experience is mostly in marketing content, advertising, copywriting, journalism or social media, and you have no hands-on experience of content design or working in UX.

This role needs someone who can shape policy, journeys and product decisions as well as write the words.

jobs.title: Payment Operations Global Processing Function Lead
jobs.description:
We’re looking for a Function Lead to oversee Global Processing Operations!

As a Function Lead, you'll be a strong people leader with a sharp focus on delivering world-class service at scale across a 24/7 global operating footprint. You'll drive operational excellence through a deep understanding of service delivery, multi-site team development, and continuous process improvement. You'll support and empower Team Leads across our global locations, foster collaboration across stakeholders, and act as a bridge between Global Processing and other payment operation verticals. 

Your Mission

Our mission in Global Processing Operations is clear: We guarantee the seamless flow of customer funds by consistently providing excellent customer experience without any delays. 

In this role, you'll be a key force in executing that mission—leading 24/7 operations, maintaining strict SLA standards across 50+ currencies, minimizing processing losses, and building a sustainable, future-proof operating model.

You will:

This role will give you the opportunity to:

jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer II - Send Experience
jobs.description:
Send is at the core of our product, with over 10 million customers using it to transfer money around the world. We work at scale: building world-class experiences that cater for every currency route and payment method.

As a Senior Backend Engineer, you'll own problem spaces end-to-end, from understanding the problem to shipping the solution and measuring its impact. Think of a new customer's first transfer, a step that slows people down, or a point where customers drop off. You'll help set the technical direction in your areas, find problems before they're assigned, and work across teams when a solution needs it.

How we work:
• We're a cross-functional team of Backend, Web, iOS and Android engineers working closely with Product Managers, Designers and Analysts, based in London, Budapest and Tallinn.
• We are not a ticket factory. Engineers work with product and design from day one, question what "best" looks like, and ship their answer. Our strongest features started with an engineer saying "what if we did it this way instead?".
• We own our services end to end, from architecture to production and the next iteration.
• We make decisions based on data and experiments.
• We use AI-assisted development throughout our workflow.

 

What will you be working on?:
• First

experience:

making a new customer's first transfer feel simple and trustworthy, because it decides whether they stay and tell their friends.
• Convenience: simplifying the Send and Add money flows by removing steps, smart defaults, and making every part of the journey effortless for returning customers too.
• Conversion: finding where customers drop off across routes, currencies and payment methods, then fixing the causes and measuring the impact through experiments.
• Ownership: owning the team's technical and product roadmap together with your Engineering Lead and Product Manager. Drive large projects end-to-end, from spotting the problem to rollout, measuring impact and deciding what comes next.
• Reliability at scale: keeping the core flows fast and reliable, building the metrics, alerting and dashboards that show how our systems behave, and turning recurring incidents into prevented ones.
• Raising the bar: shaping your domain's technical direction, mentoring engineers, and advocating for best practice.

What do you need?:

If you have most of these and are hungry to learn the rest, you should apply.
• A track record of owning large, customer-facing projects end to end, with impact you can show.
• Deep backend experience with Java or Kotlin, Spring and microservices. You know the difference between code that works and architecture that scales.
• A strong understanding of how systems work end to end: distributed and concurrent systems, relational databases, integration patterns, and the client–backend boundary.
• An ability to balance risk, operational scalability and growth when making technical decisions.
• A product mindset: you understand the "why" behind the "what", connect technical work to customer value and business goals, and suggest what should exist instead of just building what's asked.
• Data-driven decisions, backed by metrics, monitoring and experiments.
• Experience driving work across teams without formal authority, getting buy-in and making sure it lands.
• Clear communication: you explain complex technical decisions to non-technical partners, challenge constructively, and hold strong opinions loosely.
• You make the people around you better through mentoring, code reviews and sharing what you know.

Nice to have:
• Experience building AI-powered products.
• Experience in payments, fintech or another global, regulated product.
• Experience building high-throughput APIs.
• Hands-on use of AI-native development tools at every stage of development, from design and coding to testing, review and debugging.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager – Payment integrations
jobs.description:

• Partnering with engineering to remove processing bottlenecks and build infrastructure that scales with Wise.

Marketing at Brex

Marketing tells the story of Brex to the world. From acquisition to activation, we translate product value into business results. Our team spans Revenue, Product, and Brand Marketing, and works closely with nearly every function at Brex. We move fast, experiment often, and think deeply about customer behavior. If you want your creativity to drive growth and shape perception, this is the place.

What You'll Do

As a Field Marketing Coordinator, Upmarket, you'll play an important role in helping Brex scale regional marketing programs that drive pipeline generation, accelerate opportunities, and strengthen relationships with senior finance, accounting, and procurement leaders across Enterprise and Mid-Market organizations.

Reporting directly to the Field Marketing Lead, Upmarket, you'll support a diverse portfolio of revenue-driving initiatives, including executive experiences, regional events, account-based marketing (ABM), and digital campaigns.

You'll take ownership of day-to-day program execution and operational coordination, working closely with Sales, Marketing, and cross-functional partners to bring programs to life. Your work will help expand our regional presence, improve program efficiency, and ensure consistent Sales activation before, during, and after each program.

The ideal candidate is a proactive, highly organized marketer who thrives in a fast-paced environment, builds strong relationships with Sales, and understands how thoughtful execution drives business growth. • Support integrated digital marketing campaigns across email and paid media, coordinating audience lists, creative assets, landing pages, campaign launches, and performance tracking.
• Coordinate ABM and direct-mail campaigns, including prospect targeting, vendor management, gifting, fulfillment, and delivery tracking.
• Maintain the Field Marketing events calendar, campaign documentation, and performance reporting across Salesforce, registration platforms, and marketing automation tools, tracking meetings generated, qualified pipeline, and pipeline influence.

• 2+ years of experience in field marketing, event marketing, demand generation, project management or a related role.

• Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work cross-functionally.
• Proactive, resourceful, and comfortable taking ownership of day-to-day execution with minimal supervision.
• Ability to adapt to changing priorities, solve problems quickly, and maintain high-quality execution under tight deadlines.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Expenses
jobs.description:
Why join us

Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.

Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

Product at Brex

The Product team is at the forefront of Brex's mission to empower employees anywhere to make better financial decisions. With a deep understanding of the business, we identify and scope the most impactful opportunities for Brex to tackle. We align cross-functional teams—including Engineering, Legal, Compliance, and Design—on key decisions, set strategy, and drive products from inception to launch.

What you’ll do

Processing a single expense is becoming commoditized. Managing expenses across an enterprise is not. Companies must distribute cards broadly while controlling risk, documenting transactions, enforcing policy, routing approvals, preparing for audit, and producing ERP-ready records.

As Senior Product Manager for Expenses, you will turn that complexity into one intelligent system for employees, managers, finance teams, and accountants. You will lead the strategy across documentation, policy, compliance, approvals, substantiation, audit, and accounting readiness.

You will align specialized product teams across Engineering, Design, Risk, Compliance, Accounting, and GTM. Using AI and automation, you will eliminate routine work, surface meaningful exceptions, help finance teams close faster, and build capabilities that win major enterprise relationships.

Where you’ll work

This role will be based in either our San Francisco, Seattle, or New York office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

Responsibilities
• Own the end-to-end strategy for enterprise expense management.
• Unify documentation, policy, compliance, approvals, substantiation, audit, and ERP readiness.
• Define the systems, data models, configurations, and controls complex enterprises require.
• Align specialized product teams around the complete expense lifecycle.
• Use AI to automate routine work and route only judgment-heavy exceptions to people.
• Partner with Design to make sophisticated enterprise workflows intuitive.
• Align Engineering, Design, Risk, Compliance, Accounting, Sales, and Customer Success around enterprise outcomes.
• Own adoption, workflow completion, manual-work reduction, close speed, retention, and software revenue.

Requirements
• A track record of leading complex enterprise workflow or systems products.
• Strong technical fluency in backend systems, data models, integrations, and configurable product architecture.
• Experience supporting extensive customer permutations without sacrificing usability.
• Ability to unite multiple domains under one strategy and operating model.
• Strong customer and Design judgment across employee, manager, finance, and accounting experiences.
• Concrete judgment about where AI should remove work and where human review matters.
• Strong cross-functional influence and an understanding of how product capabilities affect enterprise sales and adoption.
• Expense management experience is preferred; accounting, ERP, procurement, compliance, or adjacent enterprise-software experience can substitute.

Compensation

The expected salary range for this role is $184,000 - $230,000. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package.

Please be aware, job-seekers may be at risk of targeting by malicious actors looking for personal data. Brex recruiters will only reach out via LinkedIn or email with a brex.com domain. Any outreach claiming to be from Brex via other sources should be ignored.

Accounting at Brex

The Accounting team at Brex ensures we produce accurate and timely financial results to stakeholders to guide the business forward. We go beyond closing the books — we automate, iterate, and improve processes in close collaboration with partners across the business. The team also serves as power users and thought leaders for Brex's own products. We bring precision and curiosity to everything we build, combining deep ownership with a product mindset to help shape the future of finance.

What you’ll do

We are seeking a detail-oriented and analytical Travel Expense (T E) Manager to lead, optimize, and scale our global corporate travel and expense program. In this role, you will be the absolute owner of our T E policies, corporate card management, and automated expense systems within the Brex product. Your primary goal will be to balance strict financial compliance and cost control with a seamless, user-friendly experience for our employees .The T E Manager is expected to serve as the primary subject matter expert for all internal inquiries regarding travel policies and expense guidelines. You will also partner closely with many cross functional teams, including our Engineering, Product, and Design teams on Brex product features.

Where you’ll work

This role will be based in our NYC office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

Responsibilities
• Oversee employee access to the Brex platform (onboarding, offboarding, and limit provisioning)
• Maintain the company expense policy, related FAQ documents, and employee education regarding the T E program
• Review, audit, and approve employee expenses to ensure compliance with the company expense policy
• Oversee employee travel bookings in the Brex Travel product
• Partner with the People team on Brex employee events where travel is required
• Partner with the Procurement team regarding allowable non-T E spend on Brex
• Work with the FP A team and budget owners bi-annually to update the budget structure within Brex and educate owners on best practices
• Partner closely with the AP (Accounts Payable) Sr. Accountant on accounting rules for Brex transactions
• Work with internal Engineering, Product, and Design teams to test and provide feedback on Brex product features

Requirements
• 5+ years of experience in corporate finance, accounting operations, or procurement
• 2+ years managing T E programs
• Exceptional communication skills with the ability to firmly enforce policy while maintaining a supportive, customer-service-driven attitude.
• Solid understanding of IRS corporate travel regulations, global VAT/GST reclaim processes, and SOX compliance controls
• Ability to work independently and manage deadlines effectively
• Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and address difficult situations in a professional manner
• Strong interpersonal and written communication skills

Bonus Points
• Prior experience with Brex
• Knowledge and experience using AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude and/or Google Gemini
• Knowledge and experience using NetSuite or Workday ERPs

Compensation

The expected salary range for this role is $150,968 - $188,710. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package.

jobs.title: Brand Partnership Associate - esports, Gaming & Internet Culture
jobs.description:
Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? Coinbase is building the future of finance for people, institutions and their agents, with one place to trade crypto, equities, derivatives and prediction markets, use stablecoins, and connect AI agents with clear controls. The bar is high and the pace is intense, and we like it that way. This isn’t a place for complacency. It’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits and do the best work of your career. If you’re ready to build the future of finance with a championship team who refuse to settle for “good enough,” you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for in-person working sessions

52 million Americans own crypto, and they skew younger, more diverse, and more digitally engaged. Coinbase is building the platform for the onchain economy, from crypto trading to tokenized stocks, prediction markets, and beyond. The Brand Partnerships team meets this audience where they already are, partnering with premium sports, gaming, and lifestyle properties to build cultural relevance and shift brand perception through activations that feel unconventional yet native. As a Brand Partnership Associate - esports, Gaming Internet Culture, you'll own the coordination and operational execution across Coinbase’s gaming and crypto portfolio, including partnerships with Riot Games, Polytopia, and gaming and crypto-native creators, managing timelines, partner deliverables, and activation logistics.

 

What you’ll do:
• Develop and maintain relationships with key gaming partners and support the Sr. Manager and cross-functional teams on brand initiatives leveraging the gaming and creator portfolio.
• Own asset inventories, activation trackers, and timeline management for Riot Games, Polytopia, and gaming and crypto-native creator partnerships, and maintain a tracker for emerging pilot opportunities.
• Lead day-to-day project management for gaming activations, including weekly status updates, meeting notes, creative approvals, partner follow-ups, and coordination with external partners.
• Support GTM strategy and briefing/ideation for marquee moments like Worlds and Champs, and build mid-season and end-of-season recaps.
• Surface and track emerging gaming, esports, and internet culture experiments and unofficial partnership opportunities for senior leadership.
• Drive budget tracker upkeep, purchase order processing, and invoice reconciliation across the sports portfolio.

Required Skills and

Experience:
• 2+ years of experience in esports, gaming marketing, and/or creator/influencer marketing partnerships.
• Demonstrated ability to manage multiple concurrent project timelines, deliverables, and external partner relationships simultaneously.
• Hands-on experience coordinating with agencies and creators, including managing briefs, content approvals, deliverables, and posting schedules.
• Proven success working cross-functionally with creative, social, communications, and analytics teams to deliver activations on time.
• Familiarity with the gaming, esports, or internet culture ecosystem, including publishers, tournament organizers, streaming platforms, and creator networks.
• A pulse on emerging gaming, internet and crypto culture trends, with a track record of identifying moments early and connecting them to brand opportunities. Agency-side experience in gaming partnerships is a plus.
• Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.

jobs.title: Marketing Operations Director
jobs.description:
Greenlight is a family technology company on a mission to help families raise financially smart kids and navigate life together. Its suite of products — including the Greenlight app, debit card, Safe Family GPS trackers, and Family Hub — brings together financial tools, safety features, and everyday family management in one connected experience. Designed for busy families who want convenience without compromise, Greenlight continues to innovate alongside the evolving needs of modern life. Today, more than 6.5 million family members trust Greenlight to stay in sync.
At Greenlight, we're here to make the day-to-day easier and futures brighter, so families can spend less time managing life, and more time living it. That's why we get out of bed every morning.
 

We are looking for an organized, process-driven Marketing Operations Director to keep our creative engine running smoothly. This role sits at the center of our marketing team, partnering closely with our ad creative and brand design teams to turn great ideas into finished work, on time and with clear ownership at every step. You’ll run the rhythms that move work forward (brainstorms, reporting shareouts, task assignment), define the processes that make us faster, and coordinate the cross-functional campaigns that bring big moments like product launches and promotions to life.
Our ideal candidate is a seasoned project manager who loves creative teams and knows how to make them more effective without slowing them down. You’ll need a true ownership mindset, exceptional organizational and communication skills, and the ability to build structure that people actually want to follow.
This role reports to the Chief Marketing Officer.

Our stance on salaries:
Greenlight provides a competitive compensation package with a market-based approach to pay and will vary depending on your location, experience and skill set. The total compensation package for this position will also include a discretionary performance bonus, equity rewards, medical benefits, 401K match, and more. Greenlight conducts continuous compensation evaluations across departments and geographies to ensure we are keeping our pay current and competitive.
 
The estimated base pay range for this position in (NY, CA, WA): $155,000- 185,000
The estimated base pay range for this position in (CO): $155,000- 165,000

Who we are:
It takes a talented team to aim for a mission like ours. We're looking for people who ask "is it bold enough?" jobs.title: Product Marketing Manager - Banking & Payments
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
In 1933, Harry Beck introduced a radically different map of the London Underground. Rather than faithfully depicting the geography of London, he simplified the sprawling transit network into clean lines, clear connections, and a system that anyone could navigate. Distances were distorted, angles were standardized, and unnecessary details disappeared. The result was something far more useful than a geographically accurate map: a way for millions of people to understand a complex system and confidently find their way through it.

Beck understood something fundamental. The best way to explain something complicated isn't to show people everything. It's to understand what matters to them and make that unmistakably clear.

At Mercury, we believe great product marketing works the same way. Banking* and payments can be complex, but the value they create for customers shouldn't be. Our job is to understand what people need, find the essence of what we're building, and help customers see how it can make their lives better.

We're a financial technology company building products that help ambitious businesses do more with their money. From everyday banking and payments to international money movement and emerging capabilities like agentic payments, we're making complex financial workflows feel remarkably simple.

We're looking for a Product Marketing Manager to help bring these products to market, communicate their value, and make sure customers discover and use what we're building.

This role sits at the intersection of Product, Marketing, and Revenue. You'll develop positioning, lead go-to-market strategies, drive successful product launches, and identify opportunities to increase adoption and revenue.

We care deeply about craft, but successful product marketing is about more than a beautiful campaign or a well-executed announcement. It's about understanding customers, building an effective plan, and driving meaningful results.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

• Lead impactful product launches. Own end-to-end go-to-market strategy and execution for new banking and payments capabilities, including emerging agentic features. Develop launch plans, align cross-functional teams, prepare customer-facing partners, and measure impact on product adoption and business goals.
• Get close to our customers. Build a deep understanding of how founders and finance teams manage money, what challenges they face, and why they choose one financial product over another. Turn these insights into compelling positioning, messaging, and GTM strategies.
• Execute AI-first. Use AI to work smarter, move faster, and produce better outcomes. You’ll build and use existing workflows, automations, and repeatable processes that improve how you approach research, launch execution, competitive intelligence, and other core responsibilities.
• Help more customers discover and use Mercury. Partner with Product, Lifecycle, Activation, and Revenue to drive adoption of banking and payments capabilities. Identify growth opportunities, test hypotheses, and improve product usage over time.
• Become an expert on our market. Develop a sharp understanding of the banking and payments competitive landscape, including emerging fintech products and traditional financial institutions. Translate market insights into differentiated positioning and actionable recommendations.
• Equip our Revenue teams to win. Build trusted relationships with customer-facing teams and develop the competitive intelligence, battlecards, messaging, and training they need to communicate Mercury's value confidently and accurately.
• Work with exceptional cross-functional partners. Collaborate with Product, Brand, Creative, Lifecycle, and Revenue to bring go-to-market strategies to life. Help shape strong campaign briefs and channel strategies, drawing on specialized creative expertise when needed.
• Connect marketing to business impact. Define clear objectives for launches and growth initiatives, track meaningful performance indicators, and communicate what worked, what didn't, and what we should do next.
• Own the full picture. Manage multiple projects and product areas simultaneously, make thoughtful tradeoffs, and prioritize the work that will have the greatest impact on Mercury and its customers.

You might be a great fit if you:
• Have 2-3 years of B2B product marketing experience and have taken meaningful ownership of product launches and go-to-market initiatives.
• Have successfully brought new products or features to market and can explain the business impact of your work.
• Know how to build a complete GTM strategy, from customer insight and positioning through launch execution, field readiness, and post-launch measurement.

• Are comfortable using customer feedback, data, and experimentation to evaluate and improve marketing performance.
• Enjoy working closely with Product, Marketing, and Revenue teams and know how to build trusted relationships across functions.

jobs.description:
About the Role

Mercury's Detection and Response team writes detections, triages alerts, responds to incidents, hunts for threats, and protects the Mercury brand. As a Senior Detection and Response Engineer you'll own that work from start to finish on a small, fast-moving team. You'll lead incidents, run detection projects from scoping to rollout, and set the quality bar for the engineers working with you. At this level you take an open-ended problem, break it into workstreams, write the tickets, and see it through. You're the person the team trusts to run an incident and write the summary leadership reads. You'll ship security outcomes, not checkbox compliance. You'll lead the response when a supply chain compromise or account takeover hits, decide what the team builds in your detection domain, and help the engineers around you grow. The platform you protect is one businesses depend on to run their finances every day.

What You'll Do
• Incident Response: Lead incidents as incident lead: scope the impact, coordinate containment with Engineering, IT, and Legal, run the war room, and write the executive summary and post-incident review. Handle supply chain compromises, account takeovers, insider threats, and phishing.
• Detection Engineering and SIEM Operations: Own detection work for a domain such as identity, cloud, endpoint, or SaaS. Decide what to build, write detections as code in Python, set severity, routing, and suppression, and track false-positive rates. Onboard new log sources and fix data quality problems.
• Threat Hunting and Intelligence: Write hunting hypotheses from threat reports and active campaigns, run them against endpoint telemetry and the security data lake, and turn the results into detection coverage.
• Brand Protection and Fraud Detection: Run takedown workflows for impersonation and phishing domains, and work with Fraud and Risk teams to put external fraud feeds to use.
• Endpoint Security and DLP: Tune EDR and data loss prevention policies, and work with IT on endpoint compliance.
• Automation and Tooling: Build enrichment pipelines and integrations between security platforms that remove manual triage work.
• Team: Break projects into tickets that other engineers execute, review detection pull requests, mentor teammates, and interview candidates.

Must Have
• 5+ years in detection and response, SOC, incident response, security operations, or adjacent security experience
• Has led incidents from detection through post-incident review, including containment decisions and communication to leadership
• Hands-on detection writing in a SIEM (ideally Python) with detections-as-code workflows (Git, pull requests, CI/CD)
• Deep fundamentals in networking, operating systems (macOS, Linux, Windows), and identity (SSO, MFA, OAuth, session tokens), and the ability to explain attacker behavior at each layer
• Cloud security experience in AWS and/or GCP: audit logs, IAM, and common attack paths
• EDR platform experience and SQL proficiency for log analysis and threat hunting
• Has owned a project from scoping to delivery: broke it into workstreams, sequenced the risky parts first, and kept stakeholders informed
• Clear written communication for incident summaries, runbooks, and cross-functional updates

Nice to Have
• Financial services or fintech background (fraud detection, account takeover, financial crime)
• Threat intelligence platforms and standards (STIX/TAXII, MITRE ATT CK)
• Identity-based attack detection (credential stuffing, impossible travel, privilege escalation)
• Brand protection, anti-phishing takedowns, or DLP and insider threat experience
• Python or Bash automation across security tools
• Experience mentoring engineers or reviewing their detection work
• Participation in industry information-sharing communities
• Has built LLM-assisted security operations automations, tools, and capabilities with deterministic, reviewable outputs, and understands prompting, context windows, tool use, and failure modes such as hallucination and prompt injection

Our Credit Oversight team⭐

Our Borrowing (lending) business is growing rapidly across both existing products and with the planned launch of new initiatives. As our lending portfolio grows, our second line of defence Credit Risk Oversight team is growing with it - and we’re looking for a Credit Risk Oversight Manager to join us!

Our Credit Risk Oversight team is crucial in providing support and challenge to our Borrowing teams in the first line of defence to help Monzo grow safely. We’re looking for someone (maybe you?!) with proven experience in consumer credit risk who likes getting into the details and analysing data to deliver independent assurance - and challenge - of credit risk management across the lifecycle. 

Ideally you’ll have experience and in-depth knowledge of retail unsecured or small business credit risk strategy within financial services. You’ll have seen first-hand how a credit portfolio performs at different stages of the credit cycle, and have hands-on experience in shaping or overseeing lending strategies. You’ll have a collaborative approach, and be comfortable working across a broad range of stakeholders. You’ll also be someone who likes getting into the details, analysing data and providing constructive challenges.

🔑You’ll play a key role by...

Providing ongoing oversight of credit risk - this includes analysing and understanding the performance of our existing lending products, developing and enhancing monitoring metrics and providing input to relevant committees and forums
• Partnering with our first line of defence teams to support credit strategy changes - including new product launches and pilots - ensuring that we deliver magical lending products for our customers while meeting our Risk Appetite
• Delivering deep insight, feedback and challenge on our credit strategies - including data-driven analysis and actionable counter-proposals - to support management decision making and shaping better outcomes for our customers
• Leading second line assurance work on thematic reviews
• Collaborating with our model validation and model development teams to ensure understanding of the models that underpin our credit strategies
• Providing credit expertise and input into relevant strategic projects and critical Monzo-wide processes, such as stress-testing and forecasting
• Supporting us in maintaining our Credit Risk Framework and making sure it is well embedded within the business
• Taking a balanced and proportionate approach to risk management, making sure that managing risks becomes part of everyone at Monzo’s day-to-day role

🤩 We’d love to hear from you if you …
• Have a strong background in credit risk management within consumer or small business lending - experience in unsecured product, such as credit cards, loans or overdrafts would be particularly beneficial
• Have proven analytical skills, and can use these to interrogate data, build monitoring and look for early indicators of trends
• Have hands-on experience and/or understanding of how to use credit risk scorecards and NPV models to develop strategies for making credit decisions
• Have a solid technical toolkit; SQL or similar is a must-have, and experience using a data visualisation tool (such as Looker, PowerBI or Tableau) is a plus
• Are excited to explore how we can use AI tools to improve our credit and risk management processes
• Can convey problems and solutions using clear and simple language, both written and verbal (see Monzo’s tone of voice guide). This is particularly important for communicating complex issues and priorities to non-experts
• Have a track record of building and maintaining trusting relationships with stakeholders, while providing effective and respectful challenge
• Are passionate about technology, and what we’re doing here at Monzo excites you!

Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! Studies show that women and people of colour might hesitate to apply unless they meet every single requirement. At Monzo, we’re dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming team. If you’re passionate about this role and keen to learn and grow with us, we encourage you to apply - even if you don’t have everything that's listed just yet. Drop us your application, we’d love to hear from you!

🙌 What’s in it for you

💰 £79,900-95,000 ➕Incentive Awards tied to your performance.

📍This role can be based in our London office, but we're open to distributed working within the UK (with ad hoc meetings in London) 

⏰ We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, and at times that suit you and your team. 

📚 £1,000 learning budget each year to use on books, training courses and conferences.

🏡 We will set you up to work from home; all employees are given Macbooks and for fully remote workers we will provide extra support for your work-from-home setup. 

➕ Plus lots more! Read our full list of benefits.

🌈 The application journey has 4 key steps
• An initial call with our recruiter
• A call with one of our Credit Risk Oversight Managers, the hiring manager(s) for the role
• A take-home task
• Two competency, based interviews - one role specific technical interview and one behaviours and values interview

This process should take around 4-8 weeks - your schedule is really important to us, so we promise to be as flexible as possible! 

We have some guidelines on using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to ace an application and interview at Monzo. You can read them here.

You will apply robust analytical approaches, including experimentation and causal inference methods where appropriate, to understand the impact of product and business decisions on customer and business outcomes. You are here to establish a data mindset and thereby foster a culture of continuous learning and improvement. • Support your team in discovery of new product ideas, identifying user friction points and business opportunities.

What you need to be successful:

Background:

jobs.title: Manager für Beschwerdeaudits
jobs.description:
Unter der Aufsicht der BaFin steuert N26 die Interaktionen mit 7 Millionen Kundinnen und Kunden in 24 Märkten. Im Rahmen unseres ambitionierten Vorhabens, den Bereich Compliance in diesen Interaktionen weiter zu stärken, schaffen wir eine Position zur federführenden Operationalisierung der regulatorischen Dimension im Austausch mit Kundinnen und Kunden sowie Behörden.

Sie verantworten das Kontrollwesen: Sie konzipieren Kontrollmechanismen, dokumentieren diese und erbringen die Nachweise, die von der Internen Revision, unseren externen Prüfern sowie der Aufsichtsbehörde geprüft werden. Dabei steigen Sie zu einem Zeitpunkt ein, zu dem wesentliche Gestaltungs- und Richtungsentscheidungen noch aktiv getroffen werden – nicht erst im Nachhinein.

 

Was Sie verantworten
• Die Umsetzungs-Roadmap: jede Maßnahme zu jedem Feststellungspunkt termingerecht konzipiert, dokumentiert, eingeführt und nachgewiesen (Test of Design, Test of Effectiveness).
• Präventive Ursachenanalyse: ein risikobasiertes Verfahren, das Beschwerden nach Auswirkung (finanzieller Schaden, aufsichtsrechtlich, Reputation) auswählt, nicht nur nach Volumen, und sie in Produkt- und Prozessänderungen überführt.
• Die schriftlich fixierte Ordnung des Beschwerdemanagements über alle Märkte: aktuell, konsistent, prüfbar.
• Die laufende Schnittstelle zu Compliance, Risikomanagement, Interner Revision und externen Prüfern für Kontrollen im Beschwerdemanagement.
• Eine Associate-Stelle (Compliance Prevention) sowie die bereichsübergreifenden Arbeitsstränge mit Produkt, Technik, Legal und Customer Service.

Was Sie mitbringen: drei Dinge
• Deutsch verhandlungssicher (mindestens C1); Englisch fließend.
• Mindestens 5 Jahre Berufserfahrung, davon Prüfungs-, Assurance-, IKS- oder Compliance-Tätigkeit in einem regulierten Umfeld: Bank, Zahlungs- oder E-Geld-Institut, Versicherer oder die Prüfungs- und Beratungsgesellschaften, die diese betreuen. Auf welcher Seite des Tisches Sie saßen, ist zweitrangig.
• Sie können eine aufsichtsrechtliche Anforderung in eine dokumentierte Kontrolle übersetzen, einführen und deren Wirksamkeit nachweisen, und Sie haben das unter Prüfungsdruck schon getan.

Hilfreich, nicht Bedingung
• Erfahrung in Beschwerdebearbeitung, Streitbeilegung oder Ombudsverfahren.
• Kenntnis der BaFin-Rundschreiben zum Beschwerdemanagement (MaBeschwer, MaComp BT 12) oder ihrer Entsprechung für Versicherer (Rundschreiben 3/2013 (VA), EIOPA-Leitlinien); PSD2-Fristen.
• Fallbearbeitungs- und BI-Tools (Salesforce, Metabase oder vergleichbar).
• Leitung eines Arbeitsstrangs, Prüfungsteams oder kleinen Teams.

Wer Sie heute sein könnten

Senior Consultant oder Manager in einer Regulatory-Praxis für Finanzdienstleister, der oder die das Ergebnis verantworten will, nicht den Bericht. Interne Revisorin oder Compliance-Beauftragter bei Bank oder Versicherer, die lieber aufbauen als prüfen. Jemand mit Erfahrung in einer Aufsichtsbehörde, der die andere Seite kennenlernen will.

Was wir bieten
• Ein klares Mandat, eine klare Frist und das Budget, es umzusetzen.
• Direkter Kontakt zu Interner Revision, Wirtschaftsprüfern und Aufsicht: die Arbeit, die eine Compliance-Laufbahn ausmacht.
• Berlin, hybrid; Umzugspaket und Visa-Unterstützung bei Bedarf.
• Weiterbildungsbudget, Homeoffice-Budget, Zuschüsse für Fitness, Sprach-Apps und ÖPNV, N26 Premium für Sie und Abos für Familie und Freunde, ein zusätzlicher Urlaubstag pro Beschäftigungsjahr.

The complaints market managers report to you; you steer the quality-assurance and workforce-management specialists who support complaints; you work hand in hand with our Compliance Prevention function, which designs the controls you operate; and you act as designated deputy to the Head of department for complaints operations. As OKX continues to expand its products, markets and investment activities, we are looking for a Global Tax Business Partner at Senior Manager level to join our lean, high-impact tax team. The role will partner closely with Product, Finance, Legal, Compliance and Operations teams, to provide commercially practical tax advice, support informed decision-making and ensure that material tax considerations are addressed early and implemented effectively.

 

What You’ll Be Doing
• Act as the primary tax business partner for the Group’s business globally including its CeFi, Web3, investment arm businesses, building strong relationships with Business, Product, Finance, Legal, Compliance and Operations teams
• Develop a strong understanding of each business’s products, operating model, fund flows and growth priorities to identify tax considerations early in the decision-making process
• Partner with the finance BP to determine tax implications of new products, listings, licensing initiatives, new fiat rails and various other initiatives
• Coordinate the assessment of direct tax, indirect tax, withholding tax, transfer pricing, permanent establishment, nexus and tax-reporting implications, working with Group Tax specialists and external advisers as required. This role owns the business interface: identifying tax issues early, framing commercial options, escalating to the right internal or external SME, and driving approved positions into implementation.
• Translate complex tax issues into clear commercial implications, practical options and recommendations that enable stakeholders to make informed decisions
• Work with finance transformation team to establish appropriate tax review gates for material products, transactions and operating-model changes etc and ensure that all material products, listings and market entries receive documented tax sign-off before launch
• Support the design and implementation of commercially practical and technically supportable entity, contractual, transaction and fund-flow arrangements
• Work with Finance, Legal, Product, Operations and tax specialists to ensure approved tax positions are implemented consistently in legal agreements, systems, processes, data and accounting treatment
• Monitor relevant tax legislative, administrative and enforcement developments and proactively assess their impact on the Group’s businesses and planned initiatives
• Maintain a business tax risk register and documentation of material tax positions, decisions and assumptions, ensuring that identified risks are escalated and remediated on a timely basis
• Contribute to process improvement initiatives, including enhancement of tax intake processes, documentation standards, knowledge sharing and the use of technology, data analytics or AI in tax workflows
• Undertake any other tasks and projects assigned.

 

What We Look For In You
• 10+ years of relevant international tax experience, ideally with a mix of Big 4 or advisoryand in-house roles
• Broad technical grounding across international tax, permanent establishment and nexus, withholding tax, transfer pricing and indirect tax, with the judgement to identify when specialist advice is required
• Proven business partnering experience, including advising on new products, transactions, investments, operating-model changes or market-entry initiatives;
• Strong understanding of commercial and operational considerations, with the ability to translate complex tax issues into practical options and balanced recommendations
• Experience in digital assets, fintech, financial services, asset management, venture capital or another highly regulated or transaction-driven business is highly preferred
• Familiarity with crypto is a strong advantage
• Strong stakeholder-management and communication skills, including the ability to influence senior stakeholders and coordinate cross-functional teams without direct authority
• Strong analytical and project-management skills, with keen attention to both detail and the bigger picture and the ability to manage multiple priorities across jurisdictions and time zones
• Self-starter, comfortable operating with ambiguity in a fast-paced, start-up-like environment; resourceful, adaptable and collaborative
• Demonstrated ability to manage external advisers and drive recommendations through to implementation
• Familiarity with tax technology, data analytics or AI applications in tax processes is a plus.
