Legal at Brex

The Legal team helps the company grow responsibly, advocating for Brex and for the thousands of growing businesses we serve. We provide strategic advice and guidance to all Brex teams, protect Brex, advise on risk, and represent the company externally, negotiating with partners and interacting with regulators. Reimagining the financial system in a highly regulated environment requires creativity and resourcefulness, and we welcome the challenge.

Where you’ll work

This role will be based in our New York City office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

What you'll do

As Risk Counsel, you will own the legal response to the moments that matter most: disputes, incidents, collections, and regulatory inquiries. You will be the connective tissue between Legal, Compliance, Risk, Operations, and our product teams when things go wrong, and you will drive them to resolution. Specifically, you will:
• Manage pre-litigation matters end to end, including demand letters, disputes with customers, vendors, and counterparties, and early case assessment, working with outside counsel where escalation is warranted
• Lead the legal resolution of account and funds ownership disputes, including competing claims to accounts, deceased or dissolved account holders, business partner separations, and interpleader-adjacent scenarios
• Oversee the legal side of collections on delinquent commercial card and lending balances, including strategy for escalated accounts, engagement and management of collections agencies and outside counsel, and ensuring collections practices comply with applicable law and our bank partner requirements
• Manage bankruptcy matters involving Brex customers and counterparties, including proof of claim filings, automatic stay compliance, preference and clawback exposure, and coordinating recovery strategy in Chapter 7 and Chapter 11 proceedings
• Serve as legal lead on incidents across the company, from intake through root cause, coordinating cross-functional response and ensuring privilege is appropriately established and maintained
• Drive remediation programs arising from incidents, including scoping affected customer populations, structuring remediation approaches, and documenting completion
• Own legal review and strategy for customer outreach connected to incidents and remediations, including notification content, timing, and channel decisions
• Prepare and manage responses to regulatory inquiries, examinations, and information requests related to incidents, disputes, and remediation matters, in partnership with Compliance and our bank and broker-dealer partners
• Supervise responses to subpoenas, civil investigative demands, and other third-party legal process served on Brex, including intake, objections, negotiation of scope, coordination of document collection and production, and customer notice where required
• Build and improve playbooks, escalation frameworks, and reporting so the company handles recurring dispute, collections, and incident types consistently and quickly
• Advise product, operations, and support teams on reducing dispute and incident risk upstream

Requirements
• Juris Doctor (JD) and active bar membership in good standing of at least one U.S. jurisdiction
• 4+ years of experience as an attorney, including at least 3 years focused on one or more of the following: litigation or commercial disputes, creditors’ rights or collections, bankruptcy, regulatory investigations or enforcement, or incident response
• Experience owning pre-litigation disputes end to end, including demand letters, early case assessment, and deciding when to bring in outside counsel
• Working knowledge of the regulatory landscape applicable to fintech, such as state money transmission, UDAAP, Reg E and Reg Z, BSA/AML, and bank partnership models
• Demonstrated ability to run a high-volume, high-stakes docket independently, with excellent judgment on what to resolve, what to escalate, and what to fight
• Strong drafting instincts for customer-facing and regulator-facing communications, where precision and tone both matter
• A calm, structured approach under pressure and a bias toward action and clear ownership
• Low ego, high accountability, and comfort operating cross-functionally with Compliance, Risk, Operations, and Engineering, Product Design

Nice to have
• 2+ years of experience as an in-house attorney at a fintech, bank, broker-dealer, or payments company
• Experience responding to bank regulatory examinations or inquiries, including from the OCC or the Federal Reserve
• Broker-dealer regulatory experience, such as responding to FINRA or SEC examinations and information requests, handling FINRA customer arbitrations and complaints, Rule 4530 reporting, or advising on SEC enforcement inquiries and subpoenas
• Experience managing collections agencies or recovery counsel, including recovery strategy in Chapter 7 and Chapter 11 proceedings
• Experience with account ownership and beneficiary dispute frameworks
• Experience managing subpoena and third-party legal process response, including under RFPA, GLBA, and similar financial privacy frameworks

Compensation

The expected salary range for this role is $220,000 - $270,000 USD. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors, including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package.

Our teams operate with high autonomy and deep collaboration, own outcomes end to end, and push for excellence from architecture to deployment. It’s an environment where engineering is a craft and builders grow by solving meaningful technical problems.

What you’ll do

As a Senior GRC Engineer at Brex, you’ll lead the IT security compliance workstreams that connect our technical control owners to the people who examine our controls: external auditors, Internal Audit, state regulators, and Finance. You’ll coordinate and test the technical controls behind our financial reporting (SOX/ITGC), our annual SOC 1 Type 2 report, our state money transmitter examinations, and our FINRA IT requirements. You’ll also run the annual business continuity and disaster recovery (BC/DR) testing calendar.

As part of the GRC team you may also contribute to the following operational tasks:
• Third party risk management
• Risk register maintenance and reporting
• Customer Trust / GTM due diligence support
• Tooling access requests
• Assist with requests related to other certifications like SOC 2 Type 2, PCI DSS, or ISO 27001

Where you’ll work

This role will be based in our New York City office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

Responsibilities
• Lead IT SOX/ITGC test procedures, walkthroughs, evidence, workpapers, and remediation across logical access, change management, computer operations, and IT governance.
• Manage our annual SOC 1 Type 2 engagement, including external auditor coordination, control descriptions, evidence, deficiency tracking, and review of draft report sections.
• Support state money transmitter (MTL) examinations by working with Legal, Compliance, and Finance on IT documentation, examiner requests, and tracking of IT findings.

jobs.location: Chicago, IL, USA; New York, NY, USA; San Francisco, CA, USA
jobs.description:
About the role

We are looking for a Product Security Manager to lead a team focused on cloud, application, and AI security within our Product Security organization.

This role is responsible for securing our cloud infrastructure, protecting applications, and enabling safe adoption of AI across our products and internal systems. You will work closely with engineering, product, and platform teams to ensure that Chime applications and systems are designed and operated securely.

While cloud and application security are core pillars of this role, AI security is an increasingly critical area of focus. You will help define how we safely leverage AI technologies while managing risks such as data exposure, misuse, and insecure integrations.

This role operates within a flexible POD model, requiring you and your team to move fluidly across security domains based on business priorities.

In this role, you can expect to
• Own the security posture of cloud infrastructure, application systems, and AI-enabled applications across product surfaces
• Influence platform teams' roadmaps and drive alignment on security priorities without direct authority
• Partner with engineering and product teams to embed security into system design and development workflows
• Lead and grow a team of security engineers, setting a high bar for technical execution, ownership, and impact
• Define and execute strategy for securing cloud-native architectures and applications at scale
• Establish guardrails and secure design patterns for AI adoption, including safe integration of third-party and internal AI systems
• Identify and mitigate risks related to AI systems, including prompt injection, data leakage, and misuse of models or APIs
• Build scalable controls and automation around identity, access, encryption, and application security, including secure SDLC and vulnerability management processes
• Lead and support response efforts for security incidents related to cloud, application, and AI risks

To begin in this role, you have
• 5+ years of experience in security engineering, with significant experience in cloud and application security
• 2+ years of experience managing or leading security engineers
• Strong understanding of cloud platforms (AWS, GCP), Infrastructure as Code (IaC), and modern infrastructure patterns
• Experience with industry tooling for SAST, DAST, SCA, WAF, and CNAPP
• Experience designing or securing applications that handle sensitive or regulated data
• Experience securing or evaluating AI/ML systems, or demonstrated ability to operate effectively in ambiguous and emerging security domains
• Strong technical judgment and the ability to go deep in architecture and security discussions when needed
• Experience operating in fast-paced, product-driven environments with shifting priorities
• Strong communication skills with the ability to translate security risks into business impact

jobs.location: New York, NY, USA; San Francisco, CA, USA
jobs.description:
About the role

Opening a new financial account is a moment of trust. People want to know what they’re signing up for, why it’s worth their time, and what happens next. As a Product Designer on Chime’s Growth team, you’ll shape those first impressions and help people go from exploring Chime to confidently taking their first steps as members.

Visual craft matters at every step. A clear hierarchy can make a complicated choice feel manageable. Thoughtful typography and layout can make important information easier to understand at a glance. A well-designed interaction can reassure someone that they’ve completed a step and show them where to go next. You’ll bring that level of care to the screens, flows, and small details that make the Chime app feel approachable and cohesive.

You’ll own design projects from the first sketch through launch and iteration. You’ll work with Product, Engineering, Research, and Analytics to find where people hesitate or drop off, explore different ways to solve the problem, and test what helps. jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist, Membership
jobs.description:
About the role

In this role you will define how Chime measures membership value and the drivers of direct-deposit retention — and lead the strategic analyses that shape decisions made by senior leaders across the company. Chime's Membership XFN owns end-to-end DD retention by making membership more valuable, more flexible, and more resilient across the member lifecycle, spanning tiering and eligibility, benefits and value realization, tier transitions, retention/resurrection, and resilience experiences that support members through transitions like job loss. You'll set the agenda for understanding how members experience and realize value from their membership, what's working and what isn't, and what those signals mean for Chime's product and business — framing the questions others aren't yet asking. By driving deep dive analysis on the trends you uncover in Chime's data, you'll not only explain why retention and value-realization metrics move but shape the strategy your partners pursue in response. This is a role where you'll think holistically about the member lifecycle, operate as a strategic partner to leaders across the company, and still be in the data to discover the story behind the metrics.

In this role, you can expect to
• Define and own the measurement framework for Chime's membership metrics — the definitions, methodology, and read-outs that other analytics teams and stakeholders across Product, Engineering, Design, Marketing/LCM, Risk, and Research rely on as the source of truth, with DD Retention as the north star and membership value realization, retention, and tier-related outcomes as supporting metrics.
• Set the strategy for how Chime understands membership tiering and eligibility, benefit value realization, tier transitions, and resilience experiences. Unlike anyone else, you will anticipate changes in how members move through the lifecycle, build the understanding for why, and shape what leaders do in response.
• Be the arbiter of truth with data. You'll raise the methodological bar for the highest-stakes analyses and define what "good" looks like for how the organization understands DD retention and membership value across the Benefits, Expansion/Eligibility, and Resilience/In Between Jobs squads.
• Partner widely and at altitude. You'll be a strategic thought partner to leaders across Product, Engineering, Design, Marketing/LCM, Risk, and Research — pressure-testing what's worth doing, not just answering the questions handed to you. The stronger these partnerships, the more successful you and Chime will be.
• Ask why a lot, and raise the bar for those around you. Your proactive inquisitiveness, supported by your data dexterity, means you lead first-of-its-kind analyses and mentor the data scientists around you to do the same.

To thrive in this role, you have
• 5-7 years in data-focused roles, leading analyses or building data tools that shape the decisions of an executive audience and frame the trade-offs leaders weigh.
• Deep proficiency in retention and lifecycle metrics — engagement, value realization, tier transitions, and the leading indicators of member resilience — enough to set the narrative, not just report it. Familiarity with measuring membership or subscription-style value across a lifecycle is a strong plus.
• Extensive stakeholder management experience at the Director/VP+ altitude, and a clear Northstar for how Analytics partners with and influences product, engineering, and risk teams.
• Expertise in SQL — you innately translate business questions to queries, understand the edge cases of joins, and with dexterity explore a warehouse to find data most appropriate to the problem.
• Analytics engineering depth — you have built data models in dbt that you and others rely on, and you set standards for how the team creates durable data products.
• Sound statistical inference skills, with the ability to communicate uncertainty appropriately to senior business partners and raise the methodological bar for others. Experience designing and interpreting experiments (A/B tests) is valued.
• A focus on impact — you don't stop with just recommendations but ensure to see work through to changing the product, and you multiply that impact by mentoring the data scientists around you.

About the role

Chime's Product Security team is looking for a Senior Infrastructure Security Engineer II to help secure the cloud infrastructure and data platforms that power Chime. This is a hands-on engineering role: you'll work side by side with infrastructure, platform and data engineering teams to find real risks, build guardrails and automation that scale, and make the secure path the easy path. Your work will span AWS, Kubernetes, network edge and data security, and it directly protects the millions of members who trust Chime with their money.

In this role, you can expect to
• Design, build and improve security controls, guardrails and automation across our AWS infrastructure, Kubernetes platforms and data systems.
• Partner with infrastructure, platform and data engineering teams to find and fix security risks, with practical guidance that keeps teams moving.
• Strengthen our cloud security posture across infrastructure configuration, network and edge security (including WAF and bot management), identity and access, and sensitive data protection.
• Review architecture and technical designs, assess new technologies, and turn what you find into clear, prioritized recommendations.
• Drive security vulnerabilities from discovery to fix, prioritizing by real exposure and exploitability.
• Use AI and automation to speed up security reviews, triage and remediation, and cut down repetitive operational work.
• Join an on-call rotation for vulnerability management, responding to issues outside regular hours when needed.

To thrive in this role, you have
• Deep, hands-on experience securing AWS production environments
• Recent production experience with Terraform, including rolling out security changes safely across many accounts or resources.
• Hands-on Kubernetes security experience, ideally on EKS, and a solid understanding of container and CI/CD security.
• Strong networking fundamentals (DNS, TLS, load balancers, firewalls) and hands-on experience with WAF or bot management.
• Practical scripting skills for security automation, and the judgment to review and validate code and infrastructure-as-code, including code written with AI.
• A track record of owning security initiatives end to end and explaining risks and tradeoffs in a way that earns buy-in from engineering teams.
• Bonus: experience with Snowflake or data security concepts such as access control, masking or tokenization, encryption and exfiltration risk.

About the role

Chime is looking for an engineering leader to help manage and guide one of the Cards engineering teams within the Spending, Saving Investing (SSI) organization. SSI is on a mission to make Chime the top choice for everyday spending by building innovative, reliable, and member-first financial tools. We focus on driving active spend and usage, increasing reliability and availability, and delivering seamless, trusted experiences across cards, credit, money movement, saving and investing, deals, and transaction intelligence. Our work empowers members to manage their money with confidence, spend smarter, and improve their long-term financial health.

We're hiring Tech Lead Managers (TLM) for multiple squads in Cards. TLMs at Chime manage a team of 3 to 5 engineers: Setting the hiring bar, coaching and developing talent, and driving all formal people management activities. They own execution and delivery for the squad. They stay in the code, authoring and shipping features alongside their team. 

In this role, you can expect to
• Manage and develop a squad of 4-5 engineers: Hiring, 1:1s, career coaching, managing for performance
• Own delivery for your squad end to end, from sprint planning and delivery commitments through service SLAs and operational health
• Write and ship code alongside your team, authoring pull requests that land in production
• Be accountable for the squad's technical direction, architecture, and quality bar, either via a tech lead on the squad, or by taking on the tech lead role yourself.
• Use AI coding agents and tooling to raise both your own leverage and your squad's, and establish the practices that make that durable for the team

• Identify technical debt and advocate for sustainable engineering, staying an active contributor to the codebase
• Ensure quality, performance, and operational health, including a healthy on-call and incident-response culture
• Build growth paths for the engineers on your squad towards the higher IC levels or a future TLM role
• Contribute to broader SSI and Chime engineering initiatives as a member of the engineering leadership team

To thrive in this role, you have
• 2+ years in people management responsibilities.
• Current, hands-on coding ability and the desire to keep it. You are writing code today and want a role where that continues.
• A track record of using AI-assisted development tools such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor to accelerate real delivery, and of getting a team to adopt them with measurable impact on output

• Enjoyment in learning and diving into the deepest levels of how things work.

• Experience with similar tech: Ruby, React Native, Distributed Systems, AWS services (data, compute) and Service Oriented Architectures.

What you’ll do:
• Lead month-end and quarter-end close activities across global entities, including journal entries, reconciliations, account analysis, foreign-currency revaluation and remeasurement, and consolidated reporting.

• Lead the automation of the accruals process, increasing automated accrual coverage and reducing manual journal entries in partnership with FP A and Engineering.
• Coach and develop staff, fostering accountability, sound judgment, and continuous improvement.

Experience:
• CPA and a bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
• 9+ years of progressive accounting experience, including 2+ years leading or managing people or accounting work.

jobs.title: VP, Global Compliance Strategy and Policies
jobs.description:
Key Responsibilities
Global Compliance Strategy
• Define and own the multi-year global compliance strategy, aligned to the firm's market expansion, product roadmap, and regulatory licensing plans.
• Serve as a senior advisor to the CCO and executive leadership on regulatory risk appetite, new-market entry, and product launches (e.g., derivatives, payments, prediction markets, stablecoins, tokenized assets).
• Conduct horizon scanning across major regulatory regimes (MiCA, EU AMLR/AMLA, UK FCA, US federal and state frameworks, MAS, HKMA/SFC, VARA) and translate emerging requirements into proactive strategy.
• Lead regulatory change management: assess impact, prioritize workstreams, and drive cross-functional implementation.

Policy Governance and Framework
• Own the global compliance policy suite: AML/CFT, sanctions, market abuse, KYC/CDD, transaction monitoring, travel rule, advertising, data and recordkeeping, and code of conduct policies.
• Establish policy architecture and governance standards — drafting conventions, tiering (global policy vs. local procedure), approval workflows, review cadence, and version control.
• Ensure consistent global standards with legitimate local tailoring; arbitrate conflicts between group policy and jurisdictional requirements.
• Design and track policy effectiveness metrics; report periodically to executive management and boards/committees as required.

Leadership and Stakeholder Management
• Build, lead, and develop a high-performing central team of policy and strategy professionals.
• Partner with regional compliance heads, Legal, Product, Risk, Operations, and Government Affairs to embed policy requirements into systems, processes, and product design.
• Represent the firm with regulators, industry bodies, and working groups; support license applications, examinations, and audits with policy evidence.
• Own policy-related training strategy and compliance culture initiatives in partnership with HR/Learning.

Requirements
• 12+ years in compliance, financial crime, or regulatory affairs, with at least 5 years in a senior leadership role managing teams.
• Demonstrated experience owning a global or multi-jurisdiction policy framework at a regulated financial institution (bank, payments, broker-dealer, e-money, or crypto exchange).
• Deep working knowledge of AML/CFT and sanctions regimes; strong grasp of market conduct regulation.
• Track record engaging directly with regulators and supporting licensing, examinations, or enforcement matters.
• Experience operating in matrixed, global organizations across at least two of the US / EU-UK / APAC regions.
• Excellent written communication — able to draft board-grade and regulator-grade documents.

Nice to have
• Crypto/digital assets experience, including travel rule implementation, VASP licensing (MiCA, VARA, NYDFS, MAS), or blockchain analytics tooling.
• Experience standing up or restructuring a central policy function during hypergrowth or market expansion.
• Legal qualification (JD/LLB) or compliance certifications (CAMS, ICA, CRCM).
• Familiarity with GRC platforms and policy management tooling.

jobs.title: Head of Credit, Kenya
jobs.description:
About us

Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times, Moniepoint is Africa's fastest growing fintech, trusted by over 10 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of naira in transactions monthly. Our mission is to enable financial happiness for every African, everywhere.

About this role

The Head of Credit, Kenya owns Moniepoint's credit business in Kenya: who we lend to, on what terms and at what price, and running the credit unit economics profitably within the risk appetite. They own the value proposition and unit economics of every credit product in Kenya, starting with SME lending to our merchant base and also consumer base. They work with the Head of Business in Kenya and functionally with the Group Head of Product, Credit. They write the briefs (RFC) for product architects and engineering to build the product and lending experience.

Responsibilities
• Set the credit strategy for Kenya: which segments to serve, which credit products to offer, and how to price for risk, starting with SME lending to Moniepoint merchants and then consumers.
• Own the credit unit economics in Kenya, covering interest and fee, cost of funds, credit losses, and operating costs, with the budget, forecast, and reporting that give the Head of Business and Group Head of Credit clear visibility.
• Design credit value propositions with sound unit economics, grounded in evidence of what Kenyan businesses (and eventually for consumers) need and in what is already proven in Nigeria.
• Apply the Group credit policy framework in Kenya, and agree local risk limits and pricing changes with the Group Head of Credit and Risk Compliance.
• Make sure every Kenya credit proposition is validated with in depth customer contacts before the RFC goes to product architects, and that every credit RFC meets the RFC standard.
• Work with Data Science to define what a good underwriting decision looks like in a thin-file market, and keep tightening it using portfolio performance.
• Work with Growth on distribution, deciding how credit reaches customers through direct sales, the merchant base, and partner channels.
• Make sure the credit business complies with Kenyan regulation from the start, including Central Bank of Kenya lending rules, credit reference bureau reporting, and data protection.

Experience Background
• Over 7 years of experience in fintech and ideally in lending specifically in Kenya.
• Direct ownership of a lending unit economics, with the ability to explain the full economics of a portfolio you ran and how you balanced growth against portfolio quality.
• Track record of building or scaling an SME (or comparable) lending book, ideally in a market with thin credit history data.
• Experience launching credit products in a new market or business, from first disbursement to scale.
• Experience leading lending teams across portfolio management, credit operations, and collections.
• Experience working with product, data science, and risk teams to turn credit needs into clear requirements and better underwriting.

Skills Competencies
• Deep understanding of how a lending business makes or loses money, and of SME credit needs.
• Strong grasp of credit risk and lending economics: pricing for risk, cost of funds, loss rates, vintage and roll-rate analysis, and collections.
• Able to interrogate a credit model's output rather than simply consume it.
• Disciplined at framing credit bets as hypotheses and validating them before scaling.
• Ability to shape the work of functions you do not own through influence and a clear commercial point of view.
• Strong analytical skills, comfortable using data and AI-assisted tools.

What success looks like in this role
• A clear credit strategy for Kenya agreed with the Head of Business and Group Head of Credit.
• The credit book growing to plan in disbursement and revenue, with credit losses within the agreed risk appetite.
• Credit products meeting contribution margin targets.
• Every Kenya credit RFC meeting the RFC standard and moving to build with little rework.
• Clean regulatory standing with the Central Bank of Kenya, and accurate credit reference bureau reporting.

Why join us
• Build a credit business from the ground up in one of Africa's most dynamic markets.
• Serve SMEs that remain underserved by credit despite Kenya's advanced financial infrastructure.
• Apply a model already proven at scale in Nigeria, with the backing of the Group credit team.
• Work in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment with significant responsibility.

jobs.title: Head of Operations & Compliance Audit
jobs.description:
About us

Ranked in 2024 by the Financial Times, Moniepoint is Africa's fastest growing fintech, trusted by over 24 million business and individual accounts, processing billions of naira in transactions monthly. Our mission is to enable financial happiness for every African, everywhere.

About this role

The Head, Operations Compliance Audit is responsible for leading, managing, and executing comprehensive, risk-based internal audit engagements across operational, financial, compliance, and corporate support functions of Moniepoint Microfinance Bank. Grounded in professional standards (IIA, CBN Guidelines), you will provide independent, objective assurance and consulting services to Executive Management and the Board Finance, Audit Risk Committee (FARCO). The primary mandate is to evaluate and enhance the effectiveness of governance, risk management, internal controls, financial reporting integrity, regulatory compliance, and operational efficiency across all assigned domains.

Responsibilities
• Develop, execute, and continuously update the annual risk-based internal audit plan for all assigned business units and supporting functions, aligning with the Bank's risk assessment framework.
• Provide strategic insights to senior management and the Board Audit Committee on material risks, control weaknesses, and emerging exposures.
• Drive continuous auditing, data analytics, and automation to improve audit coverage, detect revenue leakage, and identify duplicate or unauthorized ledger postings.
• Lead and develop a high-performing team of auditors overseeing finance, fraud management, regulatory compliance, and branch operations.
• Evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of Internal Control over Financial Reporting (ICFR) across core banking and ERP modules, as well as bank-wide cost optimization frameworks.
• Oversee fraud risk screens, assess anti-fraud controls and whistle-blowing mechanisms, and ensure immediate escalation of established fraud cases.
• Evaluate compliance with Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) regulations, the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 (NDPA), and Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing (AML/CFT) frameworks.
• Manage routine and unannounced audits across the branch network, vendor lifecycle, corporate governance processes, and enterprise marketing spend.
• Ensure all working papers, audit programs, compliance tests, and draft reports adhere strictly to IIA Standards.

Experience background
• Minimum of 12-15 years progressive internal audit, control, or risk management experience within Financial Services (Fintech, Microfinance Banking, Deposit Money Banks).
• Minimum of 5 years in a senior supervisory or managerial role leading internal audit teams.
• Proven track record in revenue assurance, financial controls, branch operations audit, and regulatory compliance.
• Minimum of a Bachelor's Degree (B.Sc. / HND) in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or related fields (Master's Degree is an added advantage).

Skills competencies
• Mandatory professional qualification such as ACA, ACCA, CPA, or equivalent; specialized certifications (CIA, CISA, CFE, or CRISC) are highly preferred.
• Deep understanding of CBN regulations, MFB Prudential Guidelines, Consumer Protection Framework, AML/CFT Regulations, NDPA, and IIA International Standards.
• Advanced expertise in exploratory, predictive, and prescriptive data analytics and automated audit working paper tools.
• Sound knowledge of core banking systems, general ledger integrity, financial statements, and payment workflows.
• Uncompromising integrity, unwavering commitment to independence, and exceptional executive communication skills for board-level (FARCO) reporting.

What success looks like in the role
• A comprehensively executed annual risk-based internal audit plan that aligns perfectly with the Bank's risk framework.
• Quality assurance, working papers, and draft reports that adhere strictly to IIA Standards.
• Proactive assessment of risks and accurate immediate escalation of material exposures and fraud cases to the CAO and Management.
• High-performing and continuously developing internal audit teams delivering cross-functional process audits that successfully identify control gaps and bottlenecks.

jobs.title: Implementation Officer (Lagos)
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Moniepoint is Africa’s all-in-one financial ecosystem, empowering businesses and their customers with seamless payment, banking, credit, and management tools. In 2023, we processed $182 billion and are Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer. We are on a mission to create financial happiness for everyone, everywhere.

What We Do

At Moniepoint, we are a customer-focused community dedicated to crafting solutions that redefine our industry. We leverage artificial intelligence and data-driven best practices to support our businesses, from providing credit and overdrafts to ensuring every transaction is secure.

Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out our stories on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth.

Job Title: Implementation Officer

Reports To: Lead, Onboarding

Location: Lagos State - Ajah, Epe, Sangotedo, and Ikoyi

Work Mode: Hybrid

Employment Type: Outsourcing

 

Job Purpose

The Implementation Officer ensures new retail customers successfully adopt Moniebook POS into their daily store operations through structured, high-touch onboarding experiences. This role bridges the gap between sales and long-term customer success by transforming newly signed customers into confident, active users who derive maximum value from the platform within their first 30-60 days.

Operating as the customer's primary guide during the critical early adoption phase, you will understand each retailer's unique operational needs, configure Moniebook to fit their workflow, deliver effective training, and drive product adoption that sets the foundation for retention and expansion. Success is measured by activation rates, time-to-value, feature adoption depth, and seamless handoffs to Account Managers.

Key Responsibilities
• Onboarding Program Design Execution: Create and execute tailored onboarding plans that guide customers from signup to full operational usage. Define clear milestones, timelines, and success metrics for each customer's onboarding journey.
• Product Setup Configuration: Guide customers through initial Moniebook POS setup.
• Training Delivery Enablement: Conduct engaging live training sessions (both one-on-one and group) that educate retail staff on core Moniebook features, best practices, and operational workflows. Create an environment where users feel confident and empowered to use the POS system independently.
• Adoption Monitoring Progress Tracking: Monitor customer usage data, transaction volume, feature adoption, and engagement signals. Proactively identify at-risk customers showing low adoption and intervene with targeted support to get them back on track.
• Relationship Building Trust Establishment: Build strong, trust-based relationships with key stakeholders during the onboarding period. Be responsive, empathetic, and solutions-oriented in addressing concerns and questions.
• Issue Resolution Escalation Management: Provide troubleshooting support for technical issues, user errors, or configuration challenges during onboarding. Escalate complex technical issues to Product/Engineering teams while maintaining customer communication and managing expectations.
• Documentation Knowledge Sharing: Maintain accurate records of customer interactions, onboarding progress, configuration details, and issues in CRM/CS platform. Document common customer questions and best practices to improve onboarding resources and internal knowledge base.
• Account Manager Handoff: Execute smooth, well-documented handoffs to the account manager upon onboarding completion. Provide context on customer goals, usage patterns, relationship notes, and any ongoing concerns to ensure continuity of support.
• Feedback Loop Product Insights: Capture and share customer feedback, feature requests, usability issues, and competitive insights with Product and Account management teams. Act as the voice of the customer to inform product development and onboarding process improvements.

Qualifications
• 2-4 years of experience in customer onboarding, customer success, implementation, or account management roles (preferably in SaaS, retail technology, or POS systems)
• Proven track record of successfully onboarding customers to software platforms and driving product adoption
• Excellent communication and presentation skills with ability to train diverse audiences
• Strong problem-solving and analytical skills, able to diagnose customer challenges and recommend effective solutions
• Customer-first mindset with genuine passion for helping people succeed and delivering exceptional experiences
• Highly organised and detail-oriented, capable of managing multiple onboarding projects simultaneously while maintaining quality
• Self-motivated, proactive, and adaptable, comfortable working independently and taking ownership of customer outcomes
• Technical aptitude and comfort with software tools
• Bachelor's degree in Business, Technology, Communication, or related field (or equivalent work experience) 

Preferred Qualifications
• Experience creating training materials, documentation, or knowledge base content
• Exposure to SaaS onboarding methodologies, customer health scoring, or CS best practices
• The candidate should be based in either Ajah, Epe, Sangotedo, and Ikoyi (Include your residential address on your CV)

About You
• You're deeply customer-obsessed, you measure your success by your customers' success and genuinely care about their outcomes
• You're an exceptional teacher and communicator who can explain complex concepts simply and make technology accessible to non-technical users
• You're naturally empathetic and patient, you understand that change is hard and meet customers where they are with understanding and support
• You're process-driven but flexible, you follow structured onboarding frameworks while adapting to each customer's unique needs and pace
• You thrive on problem-solving and troubleshooting, you're resourceful, persistent, and don't give up until the customer succeeds
• You're a team player who collaborates seamlessly across Sales, Product, Support, and Account managers to deliver great customer experiences
• You're energised by fast-paced, dynamic environments where no two days are the same and continuous learning is the norm
• You take initiative and ownership. When you see a problem or an opportunity to improve the customer experience, you act on it

What Success Looks Like
• 90%+ of onboarded customers reach 'active user' status (defined by processing transactions and using key features) within their first 30 - 60 days
• Customers go live with Moniebook POS in their retail operations within the target onboarding timeline (typically 1-2 weeks from signup)
• Customers actively use 3+ core Moniebook features by the end of onboarding, demonstrating comprehensive platform adoption beyond basic transactions
• Achieve a 4.5+ average rating score on post-onboarding surveys.

What we can offer you

What to expect in the hiring process

jobs.title: Senior Third Party Risk Manager
jobs.description:
🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.

We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.

After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as personal and business bank accounts, we offer joint accounts, accounts for 16-17 year olds, a free kids account and credit cards in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. Our UK customers can also save, invest and combine their pensions with us. 

With our hot coral cards and get-paid-early feature, combined with financial education on social media and our award winning customer service, we have a long history of creating magical moments for our customers!

We’re not only about selling products - we want to solve problems and change lives through Monzo.

 

📍London/Cardiff/UK Remote | 💰£85,000 - £115,000 + Incentive Awards tied to your performance + Benefits ✨

⭐️ Our Third Party Outsourcing Risk Management Team

We are a high-performing Global team focused on delivering pragmatic Third Party Risk Management (‘TPRM’) that protects Monzo and our customers globally. As Monzo expands across new markets and scales its product range, the operational footprint is growing fast, and the operating environment is becoming more complex.

We’re looking for a Senior Third Party Risk Manager to help shape and deliver our approach. As well as ensuring Monzo’s TPRM has well defined controls, processes and governance models in place to meet the continually growing and evolving demands of global Third Party Risk Management regulations - you’ll also set priorities and turn them into measurable improvements.

Reporting to the Director of Third Party Risk, this is a hands-on role, with strategic scope. You’ll work across the global team, and with a variety of stakeholders throughout Monzo, to strengthen our framework, manage complex risks and improve how we deliver TPRM both tactically and strategically. 

🔑 You’ll play a key role by...
• Delivering Core TPRM Operations Globally: Operating end-to-end operational activities, including supplier tiering, materiality assessments, due diligence reviews, exit planning support, and regulatory reporting.
• Driving Operational Excellence: Taking ownership of process quality, making sure TPRM activities are completed accurately, consistently and on time. You’ll look for ways to improve how we manage third party risk in practice.
• Helping shape our priorities: Identifying emerging risks, gaps and opportunities across third party risk management, and making recommendations to inform the team’s strategy and roadmap. You’ll develop practical solutions and help deliver improvements through to completion.
• Enabling Strategic Delivery: Supporting and feeding into higher-level strategic initiatives and complex risk landscapes. Leading agreed initiatives from problem definition through implementation autonomously, working across teams and global markets to deliver measurable improvements and ensuring clear visibility throughout.
• Collaborating Across Teams: Working directly with internal stakeholders across the 3LOD, and external suppliers to clear blockers, follow up on actions, and resolve issues effectively.
• Sharing your expertise: Support colleagues and stakeholders with practical guidance, helping them understand how to deliver their third party risk responsibilities.

🤩 We’d love to hear from you if…
• You know Outsourcing, Third Party Risk Regulation: You have substantial practical TPRM experience (ideally in banking or financial services) operating in both the UK and EU financial markets.
• You’ve contributed to a risk strategy, framework or operating model: You can demonstrate how you translated an identified gap into a practical improvement.
• You’re comfortable leading complex assessments: You make balanced, well-reasoned recommendations when information is incomplete or stakeholders have different priorities.
• You have experience working with various technologies: TPR tooling and AI to build innovative solutions and streamline operational workflows.
• You hold a high quality bar: You pay close attention to detail and care about accuracy. You use data and reporting to spot patterns, make evidence-based decisions and improve processes.
• You take ownership: You work independently, take initiative and prioritise your workload in a fast-moving environment. You use sound risk judgement and know when to seek guidance or involve others.
• You focus on outcomes, not just activity: You measure success by what has materially improved whether that's faster turnaround times, clearer risk ownership, or cleaner supplier data.
• You are a clear, pragmatic communicator: You build strong relationships with internal teams, third parties and regulators. You’re comfortable holding colleagues accountable and offering constructive challenges when needed. You bring together input from specialists across Information Security, Data Protection, Legal and Operational Resilience to form a clear view of risk.
• You are comfortable escalating: You use sound judgement to know when to involve your team or manager in emerging issues or concerns, and communicate your priorities and workload clearly and regularly, defaulting to transparency and taking accountability.

jobs.title: Deputy Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), US
jobs.location: New York, United States; San Jose, California, United States
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom. OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.

About the opportunity

We're looking for a security leader for the Americas who's equally comfortable in front of a regulator, inside a risk assessment, or reviewing a piece of technical architecture as part of a lean team. You'll start as Deputy CISO, Americas, with a path to taking on the full Regional CISO role as you build track record in the seat. How quickly that happens is up to you.

 

This isn't a role for someone who wants to operate purely at policy level, nor for a deep specialist engineer who wants to be configuring tools. It's for someone who can move between both worlds: fluent enough in the technical detail to challenge the Engineers or spot a gap in an architecture review, but credible enough in governance to own a regulatory conversation or a board pack. This is a lean team, so we're not looking for someone to sit back and build a big team under them, this is a direct delivery role. More than anything, we want someone hungry to learn, genuinely curious, and comfortable solving problems they haven't solved before — that matters more to us than ticking every experience box.

 

What you'll be doing
• Leading on audit defence, risk assessments, and technical architecture reviews across the Americas estate — this is a working role, not an oversight one.
• Own the Americas security risk and compliance programme: policy, controls, risk register, regulatory engagement, and reporting.
• Manage the US GRC lead directly, and work closely with the US SecOps team lead on operational risk and incident response.
• Build relationships with Legal, Compliance, Risk and Internal Audit, and represent security in Americas leadership forums.
• Prepare for and take an increasing share of regulator and licensing engagement, building toward owning it outright.
• Spot what's missing before it becomes a problem, raise an issue, build an action plan and drive it through to delivery.

 

What we look for
• A security professional with solid GRC and risk grounding, ideally from a regulated industry — TradFi (bank, broker-dealer, payments) or regulated crypto is a strong plus, though direct crypto experience isn't required.
• Enough technical depth to hold your own in an architecture or risk conversation with highly technical engineers — you don't need to be the most technical person in the room, but you can't be lost in it either.
• A track record of genuine curiosity and self-directed learning over pure years-of-experience — we'd rather hire the sharp problem-solver who's two years light on paper than the person coasting on a long CV.
• Confident, clear communication with executives, auditors and regulators alike.
• Comfortable with ambiguity.
• Happy to work as part of a lean team and within an outsourcing model to central Group affiliates.

 

Nice to have
• Direct exposure to NYDFS, SEC, FinCEN or similar regulators.
• Prior experience in a role explicitly building toward a CISO or equivalent leadership seat.
• Digital assets or crypto industry familiarity.

 

Perks Benefits
• Competitive total compensation package
• L D programs and Education subsidy for employees' growth and development
• Various team building programs and company events
• Wellness and meal allowances
• Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependents
• More that we love to tell you along the process!

 

OKX Statement:

OKX is committed to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, genetic information, creed, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, lawful alien status, national origin, age, marital status, and non-job related physical or mental disability, or protected veteran status. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

The salary offered depends on a variety of factors, including job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and market location. In addition to the salary, a performance bonus and long-term incentives may be provided as part of the compensation package, as well as a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the position offered. jobs.title: Solution Architect - Engine by Starling
jobs.description:
Starling Bank is the UK’s first and leading digital bank on a mission to fix banking with more than 3,000 people in our UK offices and 4 MILLION customers in the UK! We built a new kind of bank because we knew technology had the power to help people save, spend and manage their money in a new and transformative way. Now we present… Engine by Starling.

Engine by Starling is Starling’s software-as-a-service (SaaS) business, the technology that was built to power Starling Bank, and over a year ago we split out as a separate business. We are on a mission to find and work with leading banks all around the world who have the ambition to build rapid growth businesses, on our technology.

This SaaS technology platform is now available to banks and financial institutions all around the world, enabling them to benefit from the innovative digital features, and efficient back-office processes that has helped achieve Starling's success.

At Engine by Starling, our technologists are at our very heart and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment that is all about building things, creating new stuff, and disruptive technology that keeps us on the cutting edge of fintech. We operate a flat structure to empower you to make decisions regardless of what your primary responsibilities may be, innovation and collaboration will be at the core of everything you do. Help is never far away in our open culture, you will find support in your team and from across the business, we are in this together!

The way to thrive and shine within Engine is to be a self-driven individual and be able to take full ownership of everything around you: From building things, designing, and discovering to sharing knowledge with your colleagues and making sure all processes are efficient and productive to deliver the best possible results for our customers. Our purpose is underpinned by five values: Listen, Keep It Simple, Do The Right Thing, Own It, and Aim For Greatness.

Hybrid Working

We have a Hybrid approach to working here at Engine - our preference is that you're located within a commutable distance of our Sydney office in the CBD, so that we're able to interact and collaborate in person. 

About the role

As a Solution Architect (SA) you will use your understanding of the Engine technology and architecture to explain the Engine product, uncover client requirements and support the design of client solutions.

You will be involved in both the sales and delivery phases of a project as well as ongoing client success, collaborating with teams across Engine in Technology, Delivery, Product, Client Success and Business Development..

Supporting these activities on client sites means the role will require travel around Australia and New Zealand, and occasional further travel.

What you'll get to do:

This role blends deep technical expertise with strong communication and collaboration skills. You'll become an Engine expert, understanding its architecture, technology, and functionality, allowing you to effectively communicate its capabilities and value to both technical and non-technical audiences.

You’ll lead on technical designs during the Engine implementation phase, building relationships with a variety of stakeholders within clients and SI partners such as their Engineering leads and Service Owners. 

You will work closely with our clients and SI partners on the technical detail of implementing Engine, providing solutions to identified requirements and working with our Product and engineering teams to fulfil them. Your contributions will also extend to shaping Engine's product roadmap and supporting existing clients with additional capabilities to meet their strategic aims. You’ll help them maximise Engine’s current and future capabilities to solve their requirements and meticulously document scope and roadmap decisions to guide subsequent delivery waves, bringing in expertise from our Product Owners and engineering teams where required.

You will also be a technical champion for our existing clients, ensuring their ongoing success. This includes taking ownership of the technical aspects of client deliveries, collaborating closely with our SI partners to overcome challenges and achieve seamless integrations. You'll provide expert guidance to client engineering teams, using documentation, API specifications, and sequence diagrams to foster a deep understanding of Engine's architecture and functionalities. Additionally, you will collaborate closely with our Client Success team to troubleshoot technical issues, translate client needs into new technical requirements, and architect innovative solutions that enhance the Engine platform.

Must Have:
• Experience of end-to-end software engineering / solution architecture across the software delivery lifecycle
• Experience with software service design and integration, such as RESTful APIs, OpenAPI specification and sequence diagrams
• Experience of cloud infrastructure and large-scale cloud applications
• Experience working in a client-facing role and building relationships with stakeholders
• Strong interpersonal communication and collaboration skills. Experience delivering complex messaging to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Nice to Have:
• Experience relating to retail or business banking, core banking, card processing or payments.
• Experience of delivery and implementation of core banking or large-scale digital transformation programmes, application migration and solution integration
• Commercial acumen with experience of building business cases
• Experience in a SaaS organisation in a Client Solutions or Client Engineering role
• Knowledge of financial regulations around the world

About you:
• You have a focus on delivery and getting things done for a client
• You have the ability to work well with people from a variety of levels, roles and technical backgrounds
• You’re able to communicate clearly about technical subjects
• You’re comfortable working in a varied role, collaboratively in a team, with a flat structure
• You’re comfortable travelling nationally to our London office (initial upskilling will require a period of time working with our Engineers & Product team in London)
• You’re comfortable travelling internationally

Interview Process: 

Interviewing is a two way process and we want you to have the time and opportunity to get to know us, as much as we are getting to know you! Our interviews are conversational and we want to get the best from you, so come with questions and be curious. In general you can expect the below, following a chat with one of our Talent Team:

You may be put off applying for a role because you don't tick every box. Forget that! While we can’t accommodate every flexible working request, we're always open to discussion. jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer: Safer Changes - Java
jobs.description:
At our scale, "testing" isn't about manual checks or writing scripts; it’s a massive distributed systems problem. The Safer Changes team within Developer Enablement is responsible for building the internal platforms that allow 1,000+ engineers and autonomous agents to ship code with maximum confidence and zero friction.

Note: This is a Backend Engineering role, not a QA or SDET position. You won't be writing test cases for features. You will be architecting the Java-based infrastructure, intelligence layers, agentic layers and orchestration engines that power the entire Wise engineering organisation.

You will be solving problems at scale, with large engineering-wide organisational impact. When you create platforms, services and opinionated standards/best practices, you help accelerate Wise Engineers to solving problems for our customers even faster. Specific challenges include:
• Distributed Test Orchestration: Architecting a high-throughput framework that automates the execution, analysis, and collation of results across thousands of concurrent jobs. You'll build the systems so that product engineers never have to think about how their code is validated—it just happens.
• Predictive Impact Intelligence: Building the logic and services that understand our microservice graph. Your code will determine exactly which business flows are impacted by a specific change, automatically designing test scenarios and provisioning purpose-built ephemeral environments on the fly.
• Production-Grade Isolation: Developing the tooling and infrastructure that allows unmerged, "dirty" code to be tested in pre-production environments safely, ensuring engineers can experiment without impacting the stability of the testing platform or other developers.
• Agent-driven Verification: Build the APIs, tooling and feedback loops that enable coding agents to prepare test data, run relevant checks and diagnose failures without human intervention. Work with our Agentic Coding Environment team to make verification a reliable, auditable part of the development loop.

jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer - Conversational Money Transfers
jobs.description:
We're looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to join Customer Activation team. New Send Money customers struggle for many reasons: a confusing step, a missing detail, not knowing what to do next. Your job will be to remove each of those reasons by letting customers set up a transfer just by talking to our AI assistant.

Every new customer compares Wise with their bank and our competitors, and their experience with the first few transfers decide whether they stay and tell their friends. The team influences and owns the experience, and that makes this team one of the biggest drivers of Wise's growth. You'll build the backend behind those moments, across Send, Add money, Pay-in flows and Money tracker. You'll also help move our assistant from text conversations to actionable UI responses, so customers can complete a transfer, not just ask about one. Conversational transfers are still new in banking, and we want to lead the way.

How we work:
• We're a cross-functional team of Backend, Web, iOS and Android engineers working closely with a Product Manager, Analyst and Designers, based in London and Budapest.
• Engineers take part in product discovery, ideation from day one, not just delivery.
• We make decisions based on data and experiments.
• We own our product features end to end, from architecture plan to production.
• We use AI-assisted development throughout the whole process.
• We value strong feature ownership, knowledge sharing and stable, scalable systems, and we learn and iterate fast.

 

What will you be working on?:
• Finding where new customers get stuck on each currency route and building flows that let them finish on their own.
• Influencing key architectural decisions and building robust, scalable backend systems.
• Powering our AI assistant's move from text replies to actionable UI responses.
• Shaping the new customer roadmap for Send, Add money, Pay-in flows and Money tracker.
• Owning projects end to end, from the first idea to delivery, and coordinating the engineers working on them.
• Working closely with every discipline in the team: PM, Designers, Analyst, and mobile and web engineers.
• Working with other teams, stakeholders and regional teams who know their local customers, and aligning everyone on shared goals.

 

What do you need?:
• Real interest in AI and LLM-based products, and a solid understanding of how agentic systems work (tool calling, planning, guardrails).
• A strong product mindset: you put customers first and make decisions based on data.
• A sense of ownership and the communication skills to drive projects across teams.
• A proven ability to get things done without formal authority by influencing, aligning and moving work forward.
• 4+ years of experience with Java or Kotlin, plus the Spring framework and microservice best practices.
• Experience making architectural decisions and designing distributed, concurrent systems.
• Experience with relational databases, schema design and query optimisation.
• Hands-on knowledge of system integration patterns and CI/CD pipelines.
• A commitment to good coding practice: clean, testable code, TDD, code reviews and open feedback.

Nice to have:
• Experience building or working with AI and LLM-based products.
• Hands-on use of AI coding tools at every stage of development, from design and coding to testing, review and debugging.

jobs.title: Product Manager - Connect (Cloud Platform)
jobs.description:
Connect’s mission is to enable services and customers to communicate securely, reliably, efficiently and conveniently. The team owns Wise’s public ingress, making extensive use of Cloudflare, and our custom service mesh; the foundations that connect customers to Wise and enable our services to communicate with each other. Annotation 2

As the Product Manager, you’ll own the product strategy, roadmap and key success metrics for Connect, shaping how Wise manages traffic into and between its services. You’ll connect a wide range of strategic business needs with an ever-evolving technology landscape to tackle some of Wise’s hardest problems; whether that’s supporting growing customer demand, strengthening security and resilience, or making connectivity simpler for engineering teams.

To succeed, you’ll be skilled at finding the real problem behind the symptoms, defining clear outcomes, and taking stakeholders, your engineering team, and your products on the journey from ambiguity to practical, high-impact solutions.

How we work

Wise teams are empowered to make decisions close to the problem. We care about clear ownership, fast learning, strong partnerships and measurable impact.

As Product Manager for Connect, you’ll operate as part of the leadership group of our Cloud Platform Squad, comprising three other teams. You’ll be tasked with creating clarity where there is ambiguity, balancing business needs with technical realities, and making pragmatic decisions that help Wise scale securely and productively.

You’ll work in partnership with Engineering, Security, and Analytics; aligning teams around the highest-impact problems and building connectivity foundations that are reliable, scalable and easy to use.

Read more about how we work here.

What You’ll Do (Responsibilities)
• Set the product and technical direction for Connect, including the roadmap, priorities and success measures for the domain.
• Build scalable foundations across public ingress and our custom service mesh, enabling customers to reach Wise and services to communicate securely, reliably and efficiently.
• Translate strategy into delivery by turning Wise’s often nebulous connectivity, resilience, and security priorities into clear product outcomes and practical execution plans. Annotation 1
• Lead through influence by aligning the team, senior stakeholders, and stakeholders across Cloud, the wider Platform, and Security.
• Drive measurable impact by defining KPIs and OKRs, learning from delivery and continuously improving how the domain operates.
• Solve the hardest problems by taking accountability for success and failure, and going the extra mile to ensure your team and its products flourish.

jobs.title: Engineering Lead - API Experience

jobs.title: Engineering Lead - Send for Partners
jobs.description:

jobs.title: FP&A Analyst (Finance Business Partnering)

jobs.title: FinCrime Operations Team Lead - PEP
jobs.description:
Role & Job purpose

As a FinCrime Operations Team Lead PEP - Screening you will develop and oversee the daily operations of a team of FinCrime Operations Analysts or Specialists. Your primary purpose is to ensure the effective mitigation of financial crime risks associated with Wise's customers, while maintaining a strong focus on operational efficiency, regulatory compliance and a customer-centric approach. You will foster a high-performing team, drive operational excellence, and act as a subject matter expert in KYC/AML/Fraud/Screening and financial crime prevention. You will be responsible for ensuring your team meets performance targets, maintains or elevates quality standards, and contributes to a culture of continuous improvement within the FinCrime Operations organization.

The FinCrime Operations Team Lead is a dual-focused leader, combining strong people leadership with domain and operational expertise. You will be instrumental in building and refining processes that prioritise customer impact while maintaining focus on the evolving risks within the financial services industry, specific product vulnerabilities, and the requirements set by regulations and partners. This includes supporting the development of compliant and scalable processes and possessing an understanding of financial crime risks associated with our customers, products, and tooling.

Job Responsibilities

Team Leadership
• You will lead by example, driving a customer-focused mindset across your team and the wider fincrime organization. You are instrumental in fostering a high-performance, results-driven culture defined by strong ownership and accountability. This involves building and nurturing high-performing teams that value knowledge sharing, continuous learning, and adaptability in our change-oriented environment. Fincrime Operations Team Lead demonstrates strong capabilities in timely conflict resolution and fosters open communication and guides effective mediation to ensure a positive working environment. You should be visible and actively engaged in team management. Your focus is on unifying the team behind shared goals (and wider FinCrime/servicing strategies) and driving collective actions.

People management
• Coach and develop a strong team of FinCrime Operations Analysts or Specialists with varying levels of experience, providing tailored guidance, and taking swift, decisive action to manage performance issues effectively, ensuring sustained excellence and growth. Provide regular, constructive, and actionable feedback to your direct reports. Coach and mentor team members to support their growth, develop their skills, and help them reach their full potential. Design and manage performance or development plans in identified areas. Conduct career map check-ins and make recommendations for demotions, promotions, salary raises, and other role related decisions.

Operational management
• You will oversee the daily operations of the team, ensuring adherence to relevant regulations and internal policies and processes. Identify and propose opportunities for process and tooling improvements. Collaborate with central functions and other operational teams as needed to increase operational efficiency or to ensure effective cross-team collaboration on joint initiatives. Provide guidance and support on complex, high-risk cases and escalations. Be on top of timely admin related tasks including but not limited to scheduling, training, hiring, interviewing, organising team activities, and others.

Performance management
• Measure team and individual KPIs and ensure performance targets and quality standards are consistently met while maintaining focus on customer experience and adherence to internal guidelines. Drive high-quality results for both the team and individuals, continuously enhancing overall quality outcomes. Conduct timely quality reviews, ensuring high decision accuracy and effectively communicate the importance of quality assurance. Conduct regular and impactful one on one coaching sessions (usually on a weekly or biweekly basis), provide clear and actionable feedback. Ensure tasks are managed timely and aligned with the team’s goals. Run team meetings to ensure that your team is kept up to date with the latest information, share best practices and enhance overall team spirit. Addresses underperformance promptly through coaching and setting SMART goals, and ensures all interventions are well-documented. Understand and be able to articulate how to move key metrics at team and individual level through efficient performance and task management.

Expertise sharing
• Be a subject matter expert in financial crime areas with the ability to obtain and maintain sufficient subject matter expertise required to train, develop and coach your team. Maintain a comprehensive understanding of our regulatory obligations, internal policies, domain-specific processes and best practices. Apply a risk-based approach to deterring and preventing money laundering and financial crime. Perform and support deep dives, understand root causes of problematic cases and propose solutions to senior leadership. Assist senior leadership with reviews and developing our processes, task management and in other operational areas as requested to ensure compliant and effective servicing function

Issue Management and Escalation
• Escalate tooling or processing incidents, high-risk customer issues, control weaknesses, or other material problems to direct leadership in a timely and informative manner, following established protocols.

Planning and execution
• Be accountable for driving your direct team's performance outcomes, ensuring key performance indicators (KPIs) are consistently met and enhanced. Possess strong knowledge of team processes and tooling, leveraging data to support initiative execution. This involves taking full ownership of your team's results, setting targets for improvement, and providing insights to stakeholders. Set and progress towards goals, adeptly identifying and resolving blockers or issues, whether performance or metric-related, to optimize output and results.

Stakeholder management and communication
• Collaborate closely with stakeholders ensuring clear communication and coordination of actions. Your initiatives and reports are well documented and you choose the right platforms to communicate to a wider audience in a timely manner. The documentation has a clear scope and includes potential impact in different areas. You can communicate confidently with difficult stakeholders on varied operational or domain related topics. Proactively work on improving cross-team communication and collaboration, acting as the liaison between different layers of the organization and your own team. Employ impactful and inspiring communication skills, unifying individuals behind shared goals, and leverage strong presentation skills to convey vision and progress.

Other: Perform additional tasks as assigned by your lead, demonstrating adaptability and a proactive approach. This includes actively participating in meetings, trainings, workshops, and internal events to support broader team and company objectives.

jobs.title: Engineering Lead - Send Convenience
jobs.description:
People should be able to pay anything, anywhere, with Wise.

Send Convenience is building the experience that makes that possible. From sending money home to paying rent, utilities, and taxes, we’re making Wise the account people can rely on for everyday life across borders.

As an Engineering Lead, you’ll lead the team improving how 15M+ customers send money, and opening up new ways for them to pay. Every unnecessary step we remove and every confusing choice we fix makes a difference at that scale.

You’ll own the technical vision and the roadmap with Product and Design: deciding which customer problems matter most, what we build, and how we get it into customers’ hands. You’ll give engineers the context, support, and honest feedback to do their best work.

How we work:

You’ll lead a full-stack team of seven engineers: four backend, one iOS, one Android, and one web. The team works across Tallinn and London, bringing engineering, product, design, and research together from the start of an idea.

What will you be working on?:
• Make everyday sending easier. Lead improvements to the send flow and better ways to pay bills, turning different local payment methods into experiences that feel familiar.
• Own the roadmap. Work with Product and Design to understand customer problems, test ideas, choose priorities, and measure what changes after launch.
• Set the technical direction. Guide decisions across backend, mobile, and web,, balancing useful releases with long-term reliability, security, and maintainability.
• Build a strong team. Coach engineers, support their growth, manage performance, and hire well. Create room for engineers to challenge ideas and own decisions.
• Take responsibility for what we ship. Keep delivery focused, work through dependencies, and own the reliability, availability, and security of the team’s systems. Make sure incidents have clear ownership and lead to improvements.

What do you need?:
• You’ve built and operated customer-facing products at scale. You can explain the technical decisions, the customer experience, and the outcomes you were responsible for.
• You’ve managed and developed engineers. You can show how your coaching, feedback, and performance decisions helped people and the team improve.
• You’ve shaped a product roadmap with Product and Design. You use customer feedback and data to decide what matters, make trade-offs, and change direction when the evidence calls for it.
• You bring depth in a product engineering discipline and strong judgement across client and backend systems. You stay close enough to the technology to challenge designs and guide complex decisions.
• You notice when a customer journey feels wrong and take the initiative to improve it. You communicate clearly, work through disagreement, and help people make progress through ambiguity.
• Your background can be in mobile, web, or backend engineering.

Nice to Have:
• Experience with payments or international products.
• Experience leading teams working across locations.
• Fintech experience is not required.
