jobs.title: Operational Resilience Manager
jobs.description:
Starling is the UK’s first and leading digital bank on a mission to fix banking! We built a new kind of bank because we knew technology had the power to help people save, spend and manage their money in a new and transformative way.

We’re a fully licensed UK bank with the culture and spirit of a fast-moving, disruptive tech company. We’re a bank, but better: fairer, easier to use and designed to demystify money for everyone. We employ more than 3,000 people across our London, Southampton, Cardiff and Manchester offices.

Our technologists are at the very heart of Starling and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment that is all about building things, creating new stuff, and disruptive technology that keeps us on the cutting edge of fintech. We operate a flat structure to empower you to make decisions regardless of what your primary responsibilities may be, innovation and collaboration will be at the core of everything you do. Help is never far away in our open culture, you will find support in your team and from across the business, we are in this together!

The way to thrive and shine within Starling is to be a self-driven individual and be able to take full ownership of everything around you: From building things, designing, discovering, to sharing knowledge with your colleagues and making sure all processes are efficient and productive to deliver the best possible results for our customers. Our purpose is underpinned by five Starling values: Listen, Keep It Simple, Do The Right Thing, Own It, and Aim For Greatness.

Hybrid Working

We have a Hybrid approach to working here at Starling - our preference is that you're located within a commutable distance of one of our offices so that we're able to interact and collaborate in person. In Technology, we're asking that you attend the office a minimum of 1 day per week.

About the Role

Starling is looking for an experienced, highly motivated and delivery focussed Operational Resilience Manager to join our established Operational Resilience Team within a fast paced first line regulated environment.

Reporting directly to the Operational Resilience Director, you will play a key role in strengthening the Bank’s ability to prevent, respond to, recover from and learn from operational disruptions, ensuring that we continue to deliver our important business services within agreed impact tolerances.

This is a broad, demanding and highly visible role, working collaboratively across the Bank on operational resilience, technology and cyber resilience, incident management, business continuity, disaster recovery, third-party resilience and IT Risk Management.

We are looking for someone who is generally hands-on. You will need to be equally comfortable developing frameworks and standards, challenging senior stakeholders, coordinating live incidents, conducting resilience exercises and getting into the details to ensure that plans , controls and processes are effective, practical and operationally embedded.

You will be joining an existing team where priorities move quickly, expectations are high and the ability to take ownership, solve problems and deliver at pace is essential.

What you'll get to do
• Support the Operational Resilience Director in the ongoing development and continuous improvement of the Bank’s operational Resilience Framework ensuring alignment with UK regulatory requirements PRA SS1/21, SS2/21 and FCA SYSC 15A.
• Coordinate the development, review and ongoing maintenance of the Bank’s Operational Resilience Self Assessment (ORSA) ensuring it accurately reflects resilience capabilities, vulnerabilities, testing outcomes and remediation activities.
• Take a hands-on role across incident and crisis management, business continuity planning, disaster recovery, third-party and supply chain resilience, and outsourcing exit planning.
• Maintain, enhance and embed practical operational resilience frameworks, policies, methodologies, standards and controls across the Bank, ensuring alignment with regulatory expectations and a consistent implementation
• Lead and support the identification and mapping of Important Business Services (IBS) including the assessment, calibration and ongoing validation of impact tolerances, critical dependencies and associated vulnerabilities
• Support the development and maintenance of Operational Continuity in Resolution (OCiR) arrangements, working with key stakeholders to identify critical services, assess operational dependencies and ensure appropriate continuity arrangements are in place to support the Bank’s resolvability
• Design, coordinate and execute severe but plausible testing, business impact assessments, resilience exercises and disaster recovery testing, identifying vulnerabilities, assessing the Bank’s ability to remain within impact tolerances and driving remediation through to completion
• Work closely with Technology, Cyber Security, IT Risk and Operations teams to strengthen technology and cyber-resilience, support major incident response and recovery, and improve overall operational resilience capabilities
• Assess third-party and supply chain resilience, including the development, maintenance and testing of credible outsourcing exit and contingency plans
• Support incident reviews, root cause analysis and lessons learned activities, ensuring identified risk, issues and control weaknesses are appropriately addressed.
• Contribute to risk assessments, regulatory compliance activities, governance and reporting and the production of meaningful management information for senior stakeholders
• Build effective relationships across the Bank providing constructive challenge, managing competing priorities and driving practical, measurable improvements in a demanding, fast-paced and highly regulated environment

We are looking for someone who can demonstrate:
• Have proven, hands-on experience in operational resilience within a UK regulated financial services environment, ideally banking
• Have experience developing, implementing and continuously improving operational resilience frameworks, policies, processes and controls
• Demonstrate practical experience of system and process mapping, impact tolerance assessment, business impact analysis and severe but plausible scenario testing.
• Have experience across incident and crisis management, business continuity planning, disaster recovery, and third party resilience, with the ability to identify vulnerabilities and drive effective remediation
• Have a sound understanding of technology and cyber resilience, IT risk management and critical business and technology dependencies
• Be highly organised analytical and solutions-focused, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deliver quality outcomes under pressure
• Have excellent communication, stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the confidence to constructively challenge and work collaboratively across all levels of the Bank
• Demonstrate a proactive, pragmatic and hands-on approach, taking ownership of complex activities and bringing them through to completion with minimal supervision
• Be adaptable, resilient and comfortable operating in a demanding fast-paced environment, with a commitment to continuous improvement and delivering positive customer outcomes

The following skills and experience are desirable:
• Previous experience working within a challenger bank, digital bank or similar fast-paced financial services organisation
• Demonstrate a strong understanding of UK operational resilience regulatory requirements , such as PRA SS1/21, SS2/21 and FCA SYSC 15A, and their practical application.
• Knowledge and practical experience of Operational Continuity in Resolution (OCiR) including critical services, operational dependencies and continuity arrangements
• Experience developing or contributing to Operational Resilience Self Assessments, regulatory submissions and senior management reporting
• Experience developing, reviewing and testing third-party resilience arrangements, outsourcing exit strategies and contingency plans
• Understanding of cloud technologies, cyber recovery, technology infrastructure and associated operational resilience risks
• Knowledge of relevant industry standards and frameworks, including ISO 22301, ISO 27001, NIST, COBIT and ITIL
• Experience supporting regulatory engagement, internal or external audits and assurance activities
• Relevant professional qualifications such as CBCI, MBCI, ISO 22301, CISM or CRISC, or equivalent practical experience

Interview Process

Interviewing is a two way process and we want you to have the time and opportunity to get to know us, as much as we are getting to know you! Our interviews are conversational and we want to get the best from you, so come with questions and be curious. In general you can expect the below, following a chat with one of our Talent Team:
• First stage with the one members of the Op Resilience team ~ 45 minutes
• Second stage with two additional members of the Op Resilience team ~ 1 hour
• Final stage, including meeting Operational Resilience Director and Head of IT Risk & Controls ~ 45 minutes
• 33 days holiday (including public holidays, which you can take when it works best for you)
• An extra day’s holiday for your birthday
• Annual leave is increased with length of service, and you can choose to buy or sell
• up to five extra days off
• 16 hours paid volunteering time a year
• Salary sacrifice, company enhanced pension scheme
• Life insurance at 4x your salary & group income protection
• Private Medical Insurance with VitalityHealth including mental health support and cancer care. Partner benefits include discounts with Waitrose, Mr&Mrs Smith and Peloton
• Generous family-friendly policies
• Incentives refer a friend scheme
• Perkbox membership giving access to retail discounts, a wellness platform for physical and mental health, and weekly free and boosted perks
• Access to initiatives like Cycle to Work, Salary Sacrificed Gym partnerships and Electric Vehicle (EV) leasing

About us

You may be put off applying for a role because you don't tick every box. Forget that! So, if you're excited about working with us, but aren’t sure if you're 100% there yet, get in touch anyway. We’re on a mission to radically reshape banking – and that starts with our brilliant team. Whatever came before, we’re proud to bring together people of all backgrounds and experiences who love working together to solve problems.

Starling is an equal opportunity employer, and we’re proud of our ongoing efforts to foster diversity & inclusion in the workplace. Individuals seeking employment at Starling are considered without regard to race, religion, national origin, age, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, medical condition, ancestry, physical or mental disability, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. 

When you provide us with this information, you are doing so at your own consent, with full knowledge that we will process this personal data in accordance with our Privacy Notice. By submitting your application, you agree that Starling will collect your personal data for recruiting and related purposes. Our Privacy Notice explains what personal information we will process, where we will process your personal information, its purposes for processing your personal information, and the rights you can exercise over our use of your personal information.

jobs.title: French Speaking Customer Support Team Lead (Night Shift) 3AM
jobs.description:
In the Customer Support Team Lead role we define the job purpose through 3 pillars that are connected to Wise values:

DELIVER (We get it done): Focus on execution, results, and operational excellence, always with a disruptive, improvement-focused mindset.

Key

Responsibilities:

● Product and Customer Knowledge: Procedural expertise in Customer Support tools, policies and case handling processes. Strong understanding of customer expectations to help coach agents to solve cases appropriately.

● Complex Case Resolution: Drive the team’s ability to handle complex cases independently through targeted training and delegation. Actively monitor complex contact resolution and case handling, ensuring the team resolves cases end-to-end.

● Data driven analysis: Analyse performance patterns and use analytical tools to make informed decisions regarding individual and team targets. Identify patterns in customer behaviours and link to potential product gaps. Conduct deep-dive root cause analysis on low resolution areas to bridge the gap between agent performance and customer perception.

● Process Optimisation: Proactively identify opportunities for performance improvement and optimise team workflows. Partner with cross-functional teams (Workforce Management, Quality Assurance, Knowledge Management) to remove blockers and improve processes.

● Incident Management: Support with the resolution of incidents efficiently. Includes communicating with affected customers, relevant internal teams and Senior Team Leads, and helping with the resolution process to minimise disruption.

● Innovation & Strategic Connection: Involvement in Taskforces (where possible) and other contribution to Global projects to initiate and implement change. Demonstrate understanding of how the team contributes to the wider ecosystem and operational health of the specific site.

● Strategic & Operational Planning: Ensure every team member understands their contribution to broader company objectives.

● Performance & KPI Management: Ensure every team member understands how their individual KPIs and metrics contribute to the broader company objectives. Monitor team performance against all service standards (Resolution Rate, Handling Time, Quality, Adherence), ensuring targets are met without compromising customer experience. Empower the team to hit targets by identifying performance gaps and providing real time coaching.

● Operational execution: Manage daily tasks using critical thinking to solve problems. Ensure team members are following and completing daily tasks, and find opportunities to optimise team workflows. ● AI-Agent Performance Management: Monitor the accuracy of automated triage and provide feedback to Product teams to refine AI-driven intent mapping.

DEVELOP (Customer>Team>Ego): Create an environment focused on ongoing development through knowledge sharing and feedback.

Key

Responsibilities:

● Growth Mindset: Proactively identify growth opportunities by establishing robust Personal Development Plans (PDPs), that empower staff to set and achieve goals that align to their career aspirations and Wise’s mission.

● Mentorship and Training: Facilitate continuous upskilling to ensure the team is equipped to cover all necessary tasks. Ensure agents have completed all mandatory training. Proactively manage the career glide-paths for L3 Specialists into Team Lead or Senior Specialist roles.

● Performance Management: Ability to adhere to performance management guidelines, including supporting agents through the salary increase process, and support agents to develop themselves. Understand when and how to initiate a formal process to manage performance issues.

● Culture of Excellence: Lead by example with correct tone of voice. Lead by example by embodying Wise values in every interaction. Responsible for setting the “Tone of Voice” for the team by maintaining a professional, transparent, and constructive atmosphere.

● Resource Management: Manage the assigned team budget and ensure agents have the necessary tools and resources to perform their daily tasks.

● Talent Acquisition: Lead interviews and hiring decisions, clearly communicating job expectations to ensure a high-quality talent bar.

NURTURE (No drama, good karma): Build a culture where the team has maximum impact by being and challenging themselves.

Key

Responsibilities:

● Inclusive & Values-Driven Leadership: Represent Wise values and code of conduct. Build a diverse, equitable environment by adjusting leadership styles to accommodate individual needs.

● Transparent Communication: Act as the primary advocate for the team, maintaining transparent top-down and bottom-up communication between agents, leadership and stakeholders.

● Wellbeing Advocacy: Regularly check in on the team’s mental and physical safety. Actively prevent burnout by promoting a healthy work-life balance and efficient time management.

● Consistent Feedback: Foster a safe space for two-way feedback. Navigate disagreements effectively and maintain a bond of trust within the team. Provide effective feedback via regular 1:1s and bi-yearly performancereview process.

jobs.title: Senior Audit Manager Professional Practices
jobs.description:
A bit about the role

Wise is looking for an Internal Audit Senior Manager Professional Practices to support the Head of the Audit Innovation and Management (AIM) and wider team to Support the maintenance and enhancement of the Methodology and tools that support the Methodology (tooling, guidance, templates and AI agents).

The role will help us maintain a high-bar and scale our function and will be responsible for operationalising IA’s methodology, as well as leading and coordinating internal audit operational processes globally. This includes working closely with the wider team, particularly on technology enablement and data-driven continuous assessments.

As a key IA team member, you'll coach and mentor auditors, identify training needs, and elevate risk awareness. Stay current on professional practices, earning trust and lead through influence. Drive continuous improvement, simplify processes, and uphold the highest standards.

We are a fast growing team, therefore you have the unique opportunity to collaborate, innovate, and shape the operations, methodology and approaches of the Internal Audit function. 

 

Your mission
• Work in close partnership with peers, business heads and senior leadership members to constantly evaluate where opportunities exist to simplify, strengthen and improve the methodology, learning and training resources, and methodology guidance, as well as support the improvement of assurance processes and requirements.
• Specifically partner with the people and other teams to develop, run and maintain training across the audit lifecycle and wider Internal Audit operations.
• Identify knowledge gaps and implement targeted learning solutions, and provide effective communications related to the Methodology.
• Maintain IA’s methodology, guidance, processes knowledge base, template and partner with AIM Technology Senior Manager to maintain effective system guidance, as well as developing a robust content management process.
• Lead complex projects to deliver and implement methodology related enhancements creating user centric solutions, identifying and structuring the problem, analysing root causes, communicating project results, and obtaining buy-in for change.
• Support the maintenance and enhancement of the tools that support the Methodology, e.g., job aids, guidance, templates and chatbot, including smartly identifying challenges and developing practical solutions.
• Lead on the remediation of methodology related issues which arise and proactively contribute to IA’s robust internal control environment.
• Collaborate with partners in the 1st and 2nd line risk and control functions on governance, risk and compliance related initiatives which can support the firm’s risk management objectives.
• Use communication skills to influence a wide range of internal audiences, and provide function wide training and briefings.
• This is a growing team, so there will be other responsibilities and opportunities arising as we evolve.

A bit about you

Skills:
• CPA, CISA, CIA, ACA, ACCA or similar professional certification is strongly preferred
• Strong verbal and written communication skills, and solid analytical skills
• Ability to manage multiple tasks and work well under pressure
• Strong interpersonal and communication skills
• You take ownership over complex areas and solve problems with no or very limited guidance.
• Highly motivated, self-starter
• You have very strong coordination skills and you are able to hold teams accountable for meeting deadlines and delivering high quality outputs.
• You are not afraid of making decisions, can work autonomously and take initiative.
• Experience developing continuous auditing methodology strongly preferred.
• You have, or have a strong desire, to harness analytics and AI to innovate and solve problems with impact, e.g. SQL.

Experience:
• 6+ years of experience in an audit/assurance/internal controls role within the financial services industry/ technology/ fintech organisation.
• You have proven experience working in risk, control or assurance.
• You have proven experience in solving complex problems through innovation.
• Experience in auditing business controls or auditing technology controls or experience in a professional practice role, with exposure to regulated financial services environment
• Strong project management and / or operational management experience.
• You have managed collaboration projects involving internal and external teams.
• You have worked in a multinational environment across different cultures and countries.

 

Some Of Your

Benefits:
• Stock options
• Generous parental leave
• Travel to other global Wise offices
• Loads of growth and development opportunities
• A fun work environment with social activities and events
• The opportunity to work with super smart, curious people
• To truly make an impact in a young and growing team

 

We’re people without borders — without judgement or prejudice, too. We want to work with the best people, no matter their background. So if you’re passionate about learning new things and keen to join our mission, you’ll fit right in.

 

Also, where and what you studied isn’t important to us. If you’ve got great experience, the right skills for the role and you’re great at articulating your thinking, we’d like to hear from you.

jobs.title: High Volume Support Specialist
jobs.description:
Case Ownership & Resolution:
• Take full cradle-to-grave ownership of customer enquiries and issues by default. You are the customer’s single point of contact until the issue is resolved.; you do not "pass the buck." You consistently aim for first contact resolution, demonstrating your commitment to getting the right outcome and not just completing a task.
• Manage a dynamic workflow across different channels, ensuring high-volume demand is met without sacrificing quality.
• Use creative thinking to diagnose complex issues. Move beyond standard operating procedures when needed to find solutions that work for the customer and the business, from both a regulatory and efficiency perspective
• Work closely with other teams, such as KYC and Financial Crime to seamlessly facilitate customer issues and act as an advocate for the customer.

Retention & Loyalty:
• Treat every interaction as a retention opportunity. Identify "at-risk" behaviors or sentiments and intervene with high-touch service and real time conversations, anticipating potential needs and likely friction to prevent churn.
• Educate customers on how to get the most out of our products, moving the conversation from "fixing a problem" to "adding value."
• De-escalate friction with professional empathy, transparency and confidence, turning negative sentiment into positive advocacy.
• Participate in initiatives and programmes designed to improve customer retention eg. re-contacting self deactivated customers.
• Deliver empowered solutions that solve for tomorrow by proactively addressing future friction points before the customer even identifies them. 

Operational Excellence & Feedback:
• Maintain rigorous adherence to High Volume KPI’s.
• Act as a feedback loop for the High Volume Senior Lead and wider management team. Use high-level root cause analysis to identify recurring trends, broken processes, customer education opportunities and product bugs that are driving high contact volumes.

jobs.title: Senior Analytics Manager - AML Prevent
jobs.description:
Why this role

AML Prevent’s mandate is to create the systems and processes that identify emerging and evolving risk trends, and to build and maintain controls (or proofs of concept for controls) that enable faster prevention, detection and escalation, including introducing user-friction where appropriate. As Wise grows, our risk exposure grows with it; scaling risk prevention in a cost-effective, technology-led way is therefore critical without disproportionately impacting our good customer population.

In this context, the domain mission is to identify AML risk early signals scalably and efficiently by leveraging technology, while maintaining strong control performance and insight into where exposure is changing.

This role operates across the AML Risk and AML Handling Preventative space, focused on understanding known risk signals and emerging risk signals before reporting is required. Success will be measured through the effectiveness and efficiency of controls and insights, using metrics such as recall and precision of prevention, control leakage, SAR rate, and SAR value rate, alongside broader indicators of trend discovery and control health.

This is a growth role as we’ve expanded the size and capabilities of our AML analytics function. It will directly manage a team of three analysts initially, growing to five or six direct reports as the function scales.

You’ll be the dedicated leader for the risk-based prevention analytics team that observes, interprets, and quantifies AML risk trends, and builds, maintains, and improves our prevention system—ensuring the team can operate effectively as it grows.

You’ll work closely with two full-stack teams (each with product and engineering capability), currently supported by two PMs and 6+ engineers, with plans to introduce additional PM and engineering leadership as roadmaps mature. Key stakeholders include Servicing Platform, KYC Onboarding, Fraud, Compliance and Internal Audit Analytics, and Compliance / Risk 2LoD, reflecting the cross-functional nature of risk prevention, control design, and governance.

What you’ll do
• Own the AML Prevent measurement framework: define and iterate control and insight KPIs (e.g., recall/precision, leakage rate, trend discovery metrics, control health/coverage, false positives, latency/SLAs) and ensure a single source of truth for Product, Ops, and Compliance.
• Act as a leader across the domain: partner with Product, Engineering, AML/EDD Operations, and 2LoD to translate evolving risk exposure into scalable prevention strategy, prioritised roadmaps, and measurable outcomes.
• Lead and develop a team of analysts: help them set priorities, coach for impact, and uplevel stakeholder influence, analytical rigor, and narrative quality.
• Generate insights to improve prevention and control performance: identify emerging customer behaviour anomalies, shifting risk concentrations, and blind spots in existing preventative controls; quantify impact, exposure, and expected effectiveness of preventative control changes.
• Own and evolve Wise’s preventative control approaches (analytics side): build, maintain, and improve the related prevention logic, including clear testing, monitoring, documentation, and change control.
• Build and maintain reliable, self-serve BI views: standardize definitions and documentation so stakeholders make consistent decisions across AML Prevent identification and control performance.
• Partner with QA, Training, Vendor Ops, and Continuous Improvement loops (as relevant): align on quality signals, feedback mechanisms, and learning loops to improve detection performance without overloading downstream operations.
• Drive analysis quality, documentation standards, and reproducibility: ensure methodologies are auditable, repeatable, and well-governed given the compliance-critical nature of AML risk prevention.

jobs.title: Senior Software Developer - Fraud Risk
jobs.description:
The team you will join: Fraud Risk Team

Join the Fraud Risk team, where we are dedicated to preventing fraud before it happens and keeping Wise customers safe in real time. Our mission is to stop fraudulent activity at the point of attempt by running instant checks on transfers and customer profiles, making accurate risk decisions with minimal friction. We build scalable, low-latency systems, improve our detection and decisioning tooling, and partner closely with fraud specialists to continuously raise the bar on prevention using data, automation, and AI-driven signals to reduce losses and protect legitimate customers.

Our vision:
• Create an automated, real-time fraud prevention experience that blocks bad activity while keeping genuine customers moving.
• Build fast, reliable risk decisioning capabilities for transfers and profiles, optimised for accuracy, latency, and scale.
• Foster a strong partnership between fraud prevention specialists and the product/engineering team to translate expert knowledge into effective controls.
• Use AI-driven detection and decisioning, and work closely with Data Scientists to productionise models and signals, improving precision, reducing false positives, and lowering operational costs.

What will you be working on?
• Real-World Impact: Shape and build the systems that prevent fraud and scams through real-time transfer and profile decisioning.
• Technical Ownership: Own the technical roadmap and deliverables of key projects in our prevention domain, delivering them predictably and with clear customer impact.
• Domain & Platform Evolution: Build deep expertise across our technical and fraud domains, driving continuous improvements in latency, reliability, and decision quality across our decisioning platform.
• System Health: Address technical debt, keep risk within appetite, and enforce Wise's engineering best practices (observability, security, Kafka/DB usage, testing).
• Engineering Leadership: Multiply team impact by mentoring engineers, sharing knowledge to eliminate single points of failure, leading onboarding, and interviewing future talent.
• Cross-Team Collaboration: Contribute beyond the team through guilds and cross-team engineering efforts to reduce duplicated work across fraud and risk domains.

Overview of the Current Team: The Fraud Risk team is a passionate group of prevention-focused crime fighters based in Budapest and Tallinn. We're a mix of engineers and fraud specialists committed to making Wise a safer platform through fast, accurate decisions on transfers and customer profiles. Our collaborative environment encourages innovation, ownership, and teamwork, making it an exciting place to work on cutting-edge solutions in fraud prevention.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Send High Volume
jobs.description:
The Send High Volume team tackles the challenges unique to customers sending large amounts internationally — think relocators moving their life savings, people managing investments abroad, or businesses running a global enterprise.

For most of them, sending an amount this big is nerve-wracking. A tiny shift in the exchange rate can cost thousands, higher risk and scrutiny mean slow-downs at every step (navigating daily and monthly limits, proving the legitimacy of funds, waiting on risk clearance from banks on either side, etc.), and possibly a far more severe consequence of missing the payment timelines.

They monitor, and worry throughout — Did it arrive? Why is it held? Will the rate hold? When it works, it's magic. When it doesn't, it's one of the most stressful things they'll ever go through.

Our mission is to make sending £5M just as effortless as sending £500, matching our products to the unique needs of these customers:
• Predictability and simplicity of process: seeing upfront what's needed and how to navigate a transfer this big, instead of hitting surprises mid-way.
• Predictability of price and ETAs: a consistent, reliable forecast, so they can plan their expenses, budget and timelines with confidence and peace of mind.
• Accessibility and quality of support: having a fast, direct access to a representative who specialises in the navigating the complexities of their route, and shows the same urgency and care they feel themselves.

What You’ll Do

You'll be one of the engineers shaping how we build for our highest-value customers. You'll own the technical design and delivery of large, high-stakes projects, and stay accountable for what you build long after launch. Day to day, that looks like:
• Leading the technical design of large projects — breaking ambiguous problems down into milestones the team can deliver, writing and reviewing RFCs, making technical decisions around the solutions we build.
• Building the hardest parts yourself — designing reliable, secure, and API-first solutions with clean, well-documented interfaces within our existing micro-services architecture using Java/Spring, Kafka, and relational databases.
• Owning what we run in production — being accountable for the availability, reliability and security of the team's systems. That means setting the bar for observability and testing, being part of the on-call rota, leading incident response and post-mortems, and paying down tech debt before it turns into risk.
• Multiplying the team — mentoring and coaching engineers, onboarding new joiners, spreading knowledge so nobody (including you) is a single point of failure, and interviewing regularly to keep raising our hiring bar.
• Shaping the roadmap — giving strong, product-minded feedback on the roadmap and working closely with product, design, analytics and operations, so we're always working on the most impactful thing and delivering at a predictable pace.

It's backend-focused and AI-first, but the role spans all of Wise: you'll redefine UX, reshape architecture and fix foundations wherever the biggest problems are.

jobs.title: KYC Operations Analyst - Platform
jobs.description:
Role & Job purpose

As a KYC Operations Analyst, you will play a critical role in ensuring that Wise adheres to regulatory and compliance requirements. You will be responsible for conducting thorough customer due diligence, analysing customer activities, and ensuring that our KYC records are kept up to date according to our internal standards. This role is a great opportunity for people who are interested in development in the KYC domain. 

 

Job Responsibilities
• Customer and business onboarding: Conduct initial and ongoing Customer Due Diligence (CDD) and Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) reviews. Take risk-based-approach decisions in your reviews ensuring risk mitigation standards are met. Collect, analyse, and verify customer information according to KYC/AML guidelines and understand potential risks associated with each customer type. Assess customer identity documents, online company registries, complex business structures, ultimate beneficial ownership, customer source of wealth documentation, adverse media screening and other sources to make your decisions.
• Transaction monitoring and periodic reviews: Review customer transaction history and provide insights into customer behaviour patterns that may indicate risks. Conduct periodic reviews and analyse changes in customers history and account usage.
• Documentation and record keeping: Ensure customer records are accurate and updated as required. Maintain organised and detailed records of customers and decisions made during the KYC process. Ensure compliance with data privacy regulations and internal data security protocols.
• Risk assessment and escalation: Perform and document customer risk assessment based on collected information. Escalate to relevant teams when identifying activities exceeding our internal risk tolerance. Identify potential money laundering and fraudulent activities and file Suspicious Activity Reports as needed, ensuring proper documentation and rationale.
• Compliance guidelines: Ensure compliance with local regulations depending on the various jurisdictions Wise operates. Maintain a good understanding of KYC/AML regulations, and internal policies.
• Process improvement: Assist in identifying opportunities to improve KYC processes and contribute to policy updates, training materials, and standard operating procedures. Support the company in partner, audit and regulatory process related queries.
• Team collaboration: Support KYC Operations Associate Analysts, by providing training and mentoring to enhance team capabilities as needed.
• Customer communication: Effective communication with customers by the relevant communication channels that Wise operates with (e.g. phone, email, and chat).
• KPIs: Perform your tasks and responsibilities within the expected key performance indicators set by the leadership team.
• Other: Tasks that are related to the position and are assigned to you by your lead. Participating in meetings, training, internal and external events.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Java
jobs.description:
Who we are 

We simplify wealth creation. Founded in 2014 in Vienna, Austria by Eric Demuth, Paul Klanschek and Christian Trummer, we’re here to help people trust themselves enough to build their financial freedom — for now and the future. Our user-friendly, trade-everything platform empowers both first-time investors and seasoned experts to invest in the cryptocurrencies, crypto indices, stocks*, precious metals and commodities* they want — with any sized budget, 24/7. Our global team works across different cultures and time zones, bringing our products to more than 7 million customers, making us one of Europe’s safest and most secure platforms that powers modern investing.

 

Headquartered in Austria but operating across Europe, our products are built by fast-moving, talented, “roll-up-your-sleeves-and-make-it-happen” kind of people. It’s these diverse perspectives and innovative minds operating as ONE TEAM that keep Bitpanda at the cutting edge of our industry. So if you’re someone who thinks big, moves fast and wants to make an impact right from day one, then get ready to join our industry-changing team. Let’s go!

 

Your mission

As a Senior Engineer at Bitpanda, your mission is to own, design, and scale the highly available, resilient back-end systems powering our core financial ecosystem. Whether building low-latency margin trading infrastructure, real-time risk assessment engines, or seamless payment and compliance pipelines, this work will directly shape how customers interact with digital assets at scale.

Collaborating closely with cross-functional stakeholders, spanning Product, Risk, Compliance, and Finance, will be essential to architect services that safeguard the platform, ensure regulatory compliance, and enable seamless growth as we expand across Europe and beyond.

What you’ll do
• Design and develop scalable, resilient, message-driven services using Java 25 Micronaut.
• Write clean and future proof code with 80% unit test test coverage, end to end and integration testing before deploying into event driven microservices architecture.
• Optimise payment modules/services to ensure reliability, maintainability, performance and scalability.
• Drive innovation by researching and adopting the latest trends and technologies in backend development, ensuring our applications remain cutting-edge.
• Be a technical mentor for junior developers, providing guidance and support to help them grow and excel in their careers.

Who you are
• 6+ years of experience of software development using modern frameworks such as Micronaut/Spring Boot, with Java 17+ as your main programming language.
• Good understanding of relational and non-relational databases (bonus points for experience with Postgres and MongoDB).
• Experience creating and maintaining publicly available REST APIs with a keen understanding of performance optimisation and scalability.
• Practical knowledge in using message-oriented middleware as we’re working with event driven microservices (ideally Apache Kafka, RabbitMQ, SQS or ZeroMQ).
• Good understanding of CI/CD: familiarity with AWS and Kubernetes is ideal but any public cloud experience is fine.

What’s in it for you
• Flexibility to work where you thrive – Enjoy the freedom of our Hybrid working model, combining onsite collaboration and remote work, with an additional 25 days per year to work from a city or country of your choice.
• Reward for your impact – Receive a competitive total compensation package aligned with Bitpanda’s pay-for-impact policy, including participation in our stock option plan.
• Support for your mental wellbeing – Access confidential coaching, counselling, and mental health resources whenever you need them through OpenUP.
• Time to recharge – On top of your standard annual leave, prioritise your wellbeing in 2027 with 3 additional days of paid time off to rest, reset, and recharge, available once you’ve been with us for 6 months.
• Continuous learning and growth – Grow your skills and stay ahead in your career with unlimited access to Udemy’s library of online courses at your own pace.
• Exclusive perks and rewards – Enjoy discounts, rewards, and perks from partners worldwide across lifestyle, wellness, tech, and travel.
• Support during life milestones – Take advantage of up to 8 additional weeks of gender-neutral new parent leave to welcome and bond with your new addition to the family.
• Fuel and focus on-site – Pandas in Vienna, Bucharest, Barcelona, and Berlin can enjoy free onsite dining, with freshly prepared lunches and snacks to keep you fueled and focused all day long.
• Recognition for your contributions – Celebrate milestones and achievements with recognition and rewards for your Tenure at Bitpanda.
• Show your Bitpanda pride – Access exclusive Bitpanda-branded merchandise and gear to represent.

About

the role:

Branch's Risk Recovery organization operates as two arms. Operations owns execution: the queues, service levels, case work and day-to-day vendor delivery that keep users whole. Enablement owns intent: what the operation should aim at, how it is measured, and which controls, tooling and processes get built to get there. As Director of Risk Recovery Enablement, you lead the second arm.

You will own the strategy and roadmap for how Branch detects, prevents and responds to fraud, scams, first-party fraud, identity abuse and financial crime, and the control environment underneath it. That includes the detection rules, the control paths users go through once flagged, and the financial crime tooling and process. You will not run daily case execution. You decide what that execution is aiming at, and you are accountable for whether the strategy measurably reduces loss without adding friction for legitimate users.

This is a player-coach role. You will lead a small team of specialists and do substantive analytical and design work yourself. You partner with the Risk Recovery Operations leader as a peer; neither role reports to the other. This role suits someone who builds things rather than waiting to receive them.

Responsibilities:

Strategy Roadmap:
• Partner with the head of Risk Recovery to set the organization's annual priorities, and own the roadmap, milestones and measures that deliver the Enablement priorities
• Translate loss performance, portfolio exposure and regulatory change into a prioritized investment agenda, and defend that prioritization to executive leadership
• Define the measurement framework the organization is held to: what counts as a loss, including consistent definitions of scam, first-party and third-party fraud losses across Fraud, Disputes and Collections, how detection lift is quantified, and how false-positive cost and good-user friction are accounted for
• Make build-versus-buy recommendations across the risk platform stack, holding vendors to modeled outcomes rather than roadmap promises
• Partner with the Operations arm to turn strategy into operational requirements, and resolve the cases where operational reality contradicts a strategic assumption
• Own Branch's membership in the Global Anti-Scam Alliance (GASA) and similar industry intelligence-sharing bodies. Direct how shared scam signals are used in detection and controls, and track scam regulation, including US reimbursement proposals

Detection Control Environment:
• Own the design and tuning strategy for Branch's automated fraud and risk controls, including real-time decisioning on card authorizations, and real-time alerting
• Set risk tolerance thresholds and approve material rule and threshold changes, balancing loss exposure against user friction and approval rates
• Own the control paths users enter once flagged (step-up, holds, locks, review queues, unlock and recovery), and the standard for when each applies and how a legitimate user exits
• Own the results of Branch's User Risk Score, the user-level view that sets each user's treatment: approve its design, risk bands and material changes. The Program Lead (Fraud Controls) builds and runs it
• Ensure each control change reaches the operation: queue design, procedures and BPO rollout are updated with the Operations arm before a change goes live
• Keep the control environment documented, explainable and defensible to Compliance, partner banks and external audit
• Direct the response to emerging fraud typologies and post-incident findings, deciding what changes in the control layer when a new attack pattern appears

FinCrime Tooling Process:
• Lead the FinCrime Manager in owning Branch's transaction monitoring and case management platform and the investigation process built on it, including mule accounts that receive scam proceeds
• Set the requirements, rollout sequence and success measures for financial crime tooling, in partnership with Data and Engineering
• Partner with Compliance, which owns AML and BSA obligations, policy, risk tolerance and UAR decisions; this arm owns the tooling, process and operational performance inside them

Identity Fraud Guardrails:
• Own the fraud and identity verification guardrails Branch's onboarding experience operates within. Product owns the onboarding experience end to end and the identity verification tools
• Own the fraud and identity metrics that come out of onboarding and bring them to the cross-functional onboarding review
• Recommend verification thresholds with the risk and conversion tradeoff modeled; where Product accepts more risk for a better experience, document the tradeoff and agree it with Product
• Own identity risk after the front door: account takeover detection and response, re-verification triggers, and the identity basis for offboarding

Automation AI

Requirements:
• Set Risk Recovery's requirements and priorities for automation and AI, and secure delivery from Branch's enterprise data, AI and engineering teams through clear requirements, sequencing and credibility
• Judge where automation and AI are not warranted, and protect the organization from tooling that adds complexity without reducing loss

Governance Standards:
• Own Risk Recovery's governance layer: standard operating procedures, rule documentation and change records that are kept current and auditable
• Own the working relationships with Compliance, Product and Engineering on behalf of the Enablement arm
• Represent the organization's capabilities and gaps accurately to partner banks, auditors and executive stakeholders

Leadership Team Development:
• Lead a team of specialist owners covering rules and monitoring, financial crime, fraud controls and project delivery, and develop each into a strategic operator
• Establish the operating cadence, prioritization discipline and written standards for an arm that does not yet have them
• Build the function's credibility so partner teams seek its input before decisions are made rather than after

What We're Looking For:

Required
• 8+ years in financial services or fintech risk, fraud or payments, with meaningful exposure to consumer deposit and/or card products
• 4+ years leading a risk program or team, including ownership of a roadmap and the investment case behind it
• Depth in fraud prevention and detection strategy: rules, models, vendor decisioning platforms, and the tradeoff between loss reduction and user friction
• Experience with transaction monitoring and case management platforms, and with how financial crime tooling supports AML and BSA programs
• Hands-on experience with identity verification, account takeover and onboarding fraud controls
• Data fluency sufficient to interrogate analysis independently: comfortable with SQL and business intelligence tooling, and able to tell a defensible model from a persuasive one
• A record of securing delivery from partner teams and vendors through clear requirements and credibility rather than escalation
• Executive-level written and verbal communication; able to defend a prioritization decision to a chief operating officer and to a partner bank in the same week
• Comfort building in the absence of structure, and the discipline to create it

Nice to Have

About us:

About

the role:

Every risk control at Branch, whether for fraud, financial crime, disputes or collections, answers two questions. The first is detection: should this user, login or transaction be flagged? The second is treatment: once it is flagged, what happens to the user, how quickly, and how does a legitimate user get back to normal? Our rules team owns the first question. This role owns the second.

As Risk Controls Manager, you own the control paths users move through once a control fires: step-up verification, holds, locks, review queues, unlock and recovery, and the handoff to offboarding. You decide who goes down each path, when, and on what exit criteria, across onboarding, login and account takeover, money movement and card activity, for fraud, financial crime, disputes and collections alike, including how Branch treats scams and first-party fraud. You also build and run Branch's User Risk Score, the user-level view that decides which treatment each user gets. Then you make the changes happen.

The role exists to close the gap between a strategy decision and the frontline. You will take ideas from the Enablement Director and carry them through Product, Engineering, Operations and our BPO partner until they are live, measured and understood by the people working the queues.

This is an individual contributor role with program ownership. You will not have direct reports.

Responsibilities:

Own the Control Paths and User Risk Score
• Map and document every control path Branch uses today: the trigger, the treatment, the owner, the service level and the exit criteria for each
• Set the standard for which treatment applies to which risk, so similar risks get similar treatment across products and channels
• Keep the map current as rules, products and vendors change, and make it the reference Operations, Support and Product work from
• Document each control path, with its rationale, approvals and change history, to a standard our partner banks, internal audit and examiners can follow, and support partner bank reviews, audits and exams of the control environment, working with Compliance
• Build and run Branch's User Risk Score: a lifetime view of each user that starts at enrollment and moves with behavior, money movement, payouts and account changes. You own the factors, weights, risk bands and the treatment each band receives; the Enablement Director owns the score's results and approves material changes
• Combine existing signals (device and login intelligence, transaction monitoring, disbursement and payout models, organization risk classification, dispute and collections outcomes) into a single user-level view, working with the Manager of Risk Rules and Monitoring and Data
• Measure and tune the score on capture rate, false positive rate and approval-rate cost, and feed confirmed fraud back into it, so every user removed changes how the next one is scored
• Set the identity verification and step-up standards for phone and chat contacts, including unlocks and ATO recovery, and close the social engineering gaps the Manager of Risk and Recovery Contact Operations surfaces from live contacts

Change Management Operationalization
• Use loss, friction and operational data to find the paths that cost the most in loss, user friction or manual work, and redesign them
• Write the requirements for each change, sequence it with Product and Engineering, and run it from design through testing to live
• Before a change goes live, map its upstream and downstream impacts on disputes, collections, Support and other control paths, so a fix in one place does not create loss, friction or volume in another
• Measure each change after launch and report whether it did what it was meant to do
• For every control change, update the operational side before it goes live: queue design, SOPs, BPO procedures and agent guidance, working with the Managers of Risk and Recovery Program Operations and the BPO partner
• Write procedures that meet audit and partner bank requirements and that an agent can still follow in the middle of a live queue
• Brief Operations on what changed and why, so the frontline understands the controls it works with
• Consult on improvements that start inside Operations; those remain with the Managers of Risk and Recovery Program Operations

Protect Good Users
• Own the friction legitimate users absorb from fraud controls: step-up pass and drop-off rates, time to unlock or resolve, and the volume of escalations controls create
• Design recovery paths for account takeover victims and good users caught by a control, in partnership with Support
• Track loss on users released from controls, so friction reductions are not paid for in fraud

Scams and First-Party Fraud
• Design the treatment paths for scams: warnings and added friction on high-risk outbound payments (P2P, Branch Direct, instant transfer), protective holds when a user appears to be acting under a scammer's direction, and recovery paths for scam victims, in partnership with Support
• Build first-party fraud factors into the User Risk Score, such as repeat or unsupported disputes, bust-out patterns, negative-balance abuse and payback failures. Set the treatment each band receives, from limits to dispute scrutiny to offboarding
• Apply Branch's scam and first-party fraud definitions consistently across control paths. Set the standard, with Disputes Operations and Compliance, for separating authorized scam payments from unauthorized transfers at the handoff to disputes

Onboarding Guardrails
• Bring Risk Recovery's control requirements to the cross-functional onboarding review led by the User Onboarding Product Manager, who owns the onboarding experience end to end
• Model the risk and conversion tradeoff of proposed step-up and verification changes; Product makes the final call, and agreed tradeoffs are documented

What We're Looking For:

Required
• 4 to 6+ years in fraud strategy, fraud operations, account takeover or customer risk at a financial institution, fintech or payments company
• Experience designing or changing fraud control flows: step-up authentication, holds, locks, review and recovery
• Experience designing or owning a customer-level risk score or risk rating model: factor selection, weighting, banding and treatment design
• A record of taking process and product changes from design to adoption across Product, Engineering and Operations
• Able to size exposure and measure friction, false positives and loss from data; SQL and BI fluency
• Working knowledge of Regulation E as it applies to unauthorized transfers, account takeover and scam claims, including the authorized versus unauthorized distinction
• Clear writing; able to turn a control design into requirements an engineer can build and an SOP an agent can follow
• Comfort operating with program accountability and no direct reports

Nice to Have

jobs.description:
Why join us

Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.

Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

Sales at Brex

The Sales team is the driving factor behind revenue for Brex and every member of our team directly affects our bottom line. We focus on generating new opportunities, acquiring new customers, and building even stronger relationships with our current customers. Our winning culture recognizes big team wins and celebrates individual accomplishments. We ensure that top performers are recognized and have built a competitive environment to motivate and unify the team.

What you’ll do

Brex is hiring a Director of Revenue Operations to own the operating model for our New Business (AE and SDR) motions. You will report into the Head of Revenue Operations as a strategic leader. This role sets the coverage model, incentive architecture, and operating cadence for the teams you support, and is accountable for their overall performance. You'll manage a team of RevOps managers and individual contributors, and be the decision maker on tradeoffs between speed, rigor, and scale across your domain. This role requires someone who can move fluidly between executive-level narratives and the underlying mechanics that drive performance and coach their team to do the same.

Where You'll Work 

This role will be based in our Seattle office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

Responsibilities
• Be a trusted business partner to the SVP Sales in owning and improving the strategies, coverage models, operating rhythms, efficiency, and incentive compensation structure to drive revenue growth
• Lead initiatives with enablement, data, finance, systems, marketing, operations, and other revenue operations team members to support your business partners and implement improvements
• Own and improve upon cadences for forecasting, pipeline, capacity planning, rep productivity, territory carving, quota setting, and incentive design
• Lead and develop a team of 6+ supporting New Business Account Executives and Sales Development Representatives Organization
• Present to senior leaders on business strategy, segment performance, and analytical deep dives
• Drive the annual planning process for the GTM teams you support, working closely with business partners, finance, and other teams to set the strategy, align incentives, and ensure operational excellence
• Identify and prioritize efficiency improvements within the Rev Ops org, including processes, reporting, and automation leveraging AI or other tools.

Requirements
• 8+ years of experience in revenue operations, sales strategy, or sales operations with at least 2+ years managing managers; preferably at a Fintech or SaaS company
• Bachelor Degree required
• A passion for coaching and developing a team with varying levels of experience
• Comprehensive understanding of sales funnels, processes, and methodologies in a scaled revenue organization, including with partners
• Demonstrated success operating in a complex cross functional environment to deliver impactful outcomes
• Direct experience owning incentive compensation design and coverage models for AE and SDR organizations at scale

jobs.title: Lead Product Counsel
jobs.description:
About the role

We’re hiring a Lead Product Counsel to join Chime’s Legal team and advise on our lending and credit products. You’ll partner with Product, Compliance, Risk, Credit, Engineering, Design, and Operations to launch and grow products that help members access credit, while managing legal and regulatory risk. You’ll be a go-to advisor for lending and credit work on a close-knit legal team, bringing practical judgment, clear communication and strong relationships. This role is based in our San Francisco, Chicago or New York City office.

In this role, you can expect to
• Advise on Chime’s lending and credit products from early design through launch and beyond, spotting legal risk and giving practical, business-focused guidance.
• Translate federal and state lending and credit requirements into clear product, disclosure and operational requirements.
• Partner with Product, Engineering, Design, Compliance, Risk, Credit and Operations so legal input shapes products early.
• Draft and review member-facing terms and conditions, disclosures and agreements for lending and credit products.
• Support Chime’s bank partnership programs, working through regulatory and partner requirements.
• Track regulatory and industry developments in consumer lending and help the business understand what they mean.
• Use outside counsel strategically and efficiently.

To thrive in this role, you have
• 5+ years of combined law firm, in-house and/or government experience, ideally including time in an in-house role.
• Hands-on experience counseling consumer lending or credit products at a fintech, a consumer tech company with a payments business, or a bank.
• Working knowledge of consumer lending and credit laws, such as TILA/Reg Z, ECOA/Reg B, FCRA/Reg V and UDAAP, and how they apply to product design.
• Sound judgment and concise communication: you can size a legal issue, prioritize risk and give non-lawyers a clear recommendation.
• Fluency with AI tools (such as Harvey, Glean, ChatGPT or Claude) to enhance work processes and outputs, with good judgment about verifying output and protecting confidential information.
• A JD from an accredited law school and active membership in good standing of a U.S. state bar.

jobs.description:
About the Role

We’re seeking a Strategic Finance Manager to join the Strategic Finance team at Chime! Chime’s StratFin team helps leaders make better decisions about how to best use Chime’s resources to build a profitable, high-growth business that’s loved by our members nationwide. 

In this role, you’ll lead high-impact, high visibility workstreams across financial strategy, bank strategy partnerships, and new product expansion. You’ll serve as a trusted finance partner to our Banking Strategy team and collaborate with leaders across Product, Risk, Legal, Analytics, and Accounting. From evaluating partner economics and commercial terms to shaping new product opportunities, you’ll bring financial rigor and sound judgment to decisions with meaningful strategic, operational, and financial trade-offs.

We’re looking for someone who can move from analysis to action: framing key business problems, developing clear recommendations, and influencing senior stakeholders and cross-functional partners towards beneficial outcomes for Chime. In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to play a key role in some of Chime’s most important decisions.

• Develop economic frameworks and financial models to inform bank partnership strategy
• Partner with Chime’s Banking Strategy team to negotiate commercial agreements that balance strategic value, financial impact, risk, and operational feasibility
• Own the financial strategy and analysis for select new product development, with a focus on enabling and scaling unsecured consumer credit offerings
• Opportunistically support critical team workstreams in support of Chime-wide priorities
• Serve as a trusted Finance partner in cross-functional decision-making, helping teams navigate tradeoffs and drive strong financial outcomes
• Synthesize complex analyses into clear narratives and confidently communicate recommendations to Finance leadership and executive stakeholders
• Prioritize your work across a portfolio of projects, build trusted stakeholder relationships, and independently drive the highest-impact work forward

To thrive in this role, you bring:
• 6+ years of experience in strategic finance, investment banking, private equity, or other analytically rigorous finance roles
• Experience in fintech, financial services, consumer lending, banking, or other highly regulated industries is a plus
• Strong financial modeling and analytical skills, with experience framing ambiguous problems, testing key assumptions, using AI tooling for modeling and analysis, and translating model output into actionable recommendations
• Experience evaluating commercial agreements, developing partner-facing negotiation strategies, and achieving favorable negotiated outcomes
• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to influence senior executives

• A low-ego, roll-up-your-sleeves approach, a willingness to operate at both the strategic and tactical levels, and the ability to handle tight deadlines and a fast-moving team culture

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - AI Experiences
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
In 1965, an engineer in Scotland was given a mundane task with a tricky problem to it - banks wanted to close on Saturdays and still serve customers, but they didn’t know how to solve the authentication of the right user. James Goodfellow, working at Smiths Industries, uncovered the insights that you needed something you have (a card) and something you know (a PIN). Because someone told him they could only remember 4 digits instead of his proposed 6, today over 3 million ATMs use a card+4 digit PIN over 60 years later. 

Like the ATM, Mercury is building technology that pushes forward financial interfaces for the long term. Command is Mercury's LLM-powered financial assistant, launched to all customers in June
2026. It lets users understand their finances and take action in plain language, from asking about cash flow to sending payments, issuing cards, and managing invoices. With the product now in customers' hands, the work is to evolve it, extend its capabilities, and find new ways to leverage LLMs to give Mercury customers a more powerful banking* experience.

What you'll do

Ship new capabilities users love:
• Design and ship new Command skills, the domain-specific instruction sets that teach the model how to handle workflows like sending money, managing invoices, and understanding cash flow
• Design and build agentic workflows in Command, defining the architecture for how multi-step agent interactions should work as we extend what the product can do on a customer's behalf
• Work with backend teams to define tool schemas for new capabilities, shaping the data contracts between Mercury's business logic and the model
• Own new capabilities end to end, from the system prompt to the frontend component that renders the response

Own the LLM layer:
• Maintain and evolve Command's prompt architecture: the system prompt, skill loading system, session context, and the policy and compliance layers underneath
• Tune model behavior: reasoning effort, prompt caching strategy, fallback chains, and the streaming patterns that make the product feel fast
• Stay current with how models are evolving and bring that knowledge back to how Command is built

Build quality in:
• Write and expand Command's eval harness, adding cases that cover new capabilities and scoring rubrics that detect regressions before users do
• Partner with product and compliance teams to define what "working correctly" means for each new capability, then build the tests that prove it
• Own the reliability and quality of what you ship, from initial design through post-launch monitoring

This list is illustrative. Command is a product in motion and priorities will shift as we learn. The right person will help choose the next highest-leverage work.

The ideal candidate
• Has 7 or more years of software engineering experience, with deep technical expertise building and scaling LLM-powered applications in production
• Has gone beyond shipping a first version: you have scaled an LLM-powered product, dealt with the reliability and performance problems that come with real usage, and made it better over time
• Has experience designing agentic systems and has opinions about how to architect multi-step workflows that are reliable, explainable, and safe to run on behalf of real users
• Has built eval infrastructure and can write cases that actually measure whether the product works, not just whether the model outputs something plausible
• Understands the real tradeoffs in LLM deployments: latency, cost, compliance, and what breaks in production that doesn't show up in demos
• Has opinions about what makes an AI product trustworthy, not just impressive, and can build toward that bar
• Is comfortable with TypeScript and willing to learn Haskell for backend tool work, or already comfortable with both
• Can work across the full stack of an AI product, from the system prompt to the streaming frontend
• Has a track record of mentoring engineers and raising the technical bar of their team

If this role interests you, we invite you to explore our public demo at demo.mercury.com.

jobs.title: State Inventory Officer (Lagos)
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month.

As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually.

Job Title: State Inventory Officer

Reports to: State Coordinator

Employment Type: Outsourced

Work Mode: Onsite

About this role:

The State Inventory Officer is responsible for managing the inventory of POS devices across the region, ensuring accurate tracking, secure storage, and efficient distribution. This role plays a critical part in operational success by validating serial numbers, monitoring stock levels, resolving inventory discrepancies, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to maintain seamless supply chain execution.

Responsibilities:
• Inventory Management: Maintain accurate, up-to-date records of POS devices, including stock levels, locations, and serial numbers; monitor inventory to identify stock shortages and coordinate timely replenishment; conduct regular stock counts and audits to reconcile physical stock with logical inventory.
• Serial Validation: Verify serial number accuracy for all received POS devices against corresponding records, promptly communicate discrepancies to relevant stakeholders, execute corrective actions, and maintain detailed documentation.
• Discrepancy Management: Investigate and resolve discrepancies between physical and logical inventory, implementing corrective measures to prevent future errors and improve overall accuracy.
• Collaboration Communication: Partner with procurement, sales, and warehouse teams to optimize inventory operations and communicate inventory status, availability, and concerns effectively with internal stakeholders.
• Additional Duties: Perform additional operational tasks as delegated and assigned by the State Coordinator. 

Experience Background:
• OND/HND or Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business Administration, or a related field preferred.
• Proven, similar experience in inventory management or related operational roles. 

Skills Competencies:
• Analytical Problem-Solving: Strong capability to reconcile inventory discrepancies and identify process improvements.
• Technical Proficiency: Skilled in using inventory management software and Microsoft Office applications.
• Detail Orientation: Exceptional accuracy in data entry, record-keeping, and serial tracking.
• Organization Time Management: Ability to prioritize tasks, handle multiple operational demands, and meet deadlines.
• Communication: Effective written and verbal communication skills across teams. 

What Success Looks Like

in This Role:
• 100% accuracy in POS device serial tracking and inventory records.
• Zero downtime in distribution caused by unmanaged stock shortages.
• Rapid, thorough resolution of physical vs. logical inventory discrepancies.
• Seamless alignment and clear communication with sales, procurement, and warehouse teams.

Why Join Us?
• Competitive compensation, benefits, and career growth opportunities.
• Vibrant work culture and support for continuous professional development.
