jobs.title: Brand Design Manager, Growth
jobs.description:
Why join us

Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.

Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

Design at Brex

Design at Brex creates the experiences that make complex systems feel effortless through thoughtful, scalable design. Whether crafting interfaces, shaping product strategy, or harnessing AI to empower our users, we obsess over quality and clarity. This is a team where creativity meets high craft, and where designers grow by building for ambitious customers.

What you'll do

Brex is looking for a Manager, Brand Design (Growth) to join the Design team, a cross-disciplinary group of creatives including product designers, brand designers, content design, operations, and marketing strategists. Our team’s mission is to build a category-defining brand and meaningfully move key business metrics by delivering world-class creative.

Reporting into the Executive Creative Director, you’ll lead the designers responsible for Brex’s growth creative across paid social, digital marketing, email and lifecycle marketing (LCM), industry and growth marketing events, and account-based marketing (ABM) campaigns. You’ll bring exceptional brand craft to work that attracts new customers and deepens engagement, using growth experiments and creative testing to learn what works.

This is a hands-on creative leadership role for someone who leads through the work — not around it. We’re looking for a highly conceptual and craft-driven designer who remains deeply involved in execution while mentoring and guiding other designers along the way. Success in this role means influencing both the “what” and the “how”: shaping creative direction and strategy early with marketing partners, while also elevating the quality and rigor of the final output.

You’ll partner closely with producers, channel owners, and marketing leads to proactively shape briefs, prioritize workstreams, and guide projects from concept through execution. The ideal candidate is energized by building something larger than themselves, thrives in highly collaborative environments, and knows how to push creative quality while balancing business goals and team growth.

Where you’ll work

This role will be based in our San Francisco, Seattle, or New York office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require three days per week in office - Monday, Wednesday and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

Responsibilities
• Lead creative direction and execution across growth campaigns, paid social, digital experiences, email and lifecycle journeys, industry and growth marketing events, and account-based marketing.
• Manage and mentor the designers responsible for growth creative within the Brand Design team through active creative partnership, hands-on feedback, and close involvement in the work.
• Partner directly with producers to prioritize, resource, and balance work across designers and projects.
• Collaborate closely with growth, lifecycle, events, and account-based marketing partners to shape briefs and influence creative strategy from the earliest stages.
• Contribute to defining the “what” alongside stakeholders — not just executing the “how.”
• Help evolve and steward Brex’s visual identity and brand expression across channels and touchpoints.
• Translate complex business concepts into clear, compelling, and emotionally resonant visual storytelling.
• Maintain a high bar for craft across typography, layout, systems thinking, and visual execution.
• Present work confidently to stakeholders and articulate creative rationale in a thoughtful and persuasive way.
• Push creative boundaries through growth experiments and creative testing, using performance insights to guide iterations while keeping work strategically grounded and operationally effective.

Requirements
• 8+ years of experience in brand design within agency and/or in-house creative teams.
• Experience leading high-impact creative work while remaining deeply hands-on in execution and craft.
• Portfolio demonstrating exceptional concept-driven design work across campaigns, storytelling, brand systems, experiential, and digital experiences.
• Strong leadership and collaboration skills with experience coaching, mentoring, or guiding designers through the work.
• Ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders and contribute strategically to creative direction and brand development.
• High level of craft across typography, layout, visual systems, art direction, and storytelling.
• Strong communication and presentation skills with the ability to clearly articulate creative decisions and rationale.
• Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment.
• Proficient in Figma.

Bonus Points
• Experience with AI visual creation tools (Nano Banana, Midjourney, etc.)
• Experience with motion and animation tools (After Effects, Jitter, etc.)
• Experience working on both B2B and B2C brands
• Experience leading integrated campaign or experiential work across multiple channels and audiences

Compensation

The expected salary range for this role is $248,000 - $311,000. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package.

jobs.title: Sr. Brand Manager
jobs.description:
About the Role

Brand Strategy Activations is the brand steward at Chime. We own the integrated campaigns that carry the brand, from brief through production to the readout on how the work performed. Outside of campaigns, we run the social-led work, partnerships, and talent that put Chime into culture. Teams across the company rely on Brand every day, and we’re accountable for being the glue that gets great work out the door.

The Head of Brand generates a large volume of ideas and direction. This role is the person who catches it and turns it into work the company can actually execute: a goal, an owner, a brief, a schedule, and a result. If you’ve ever sat in a room and known exactly how a loose idea becomes a shipped campaign, this is that job.

You’ll work across Creative, Media, Social, Partnerships, Insights, Product Marketing, Legal, and Compliance, plus our external agency partners. You’ll be trusted with getting the brand’s biggest moments through a complicated system.

In this role, you can expect to
• Turning vision into workstreams. Take direction from the Head of Brand and define it as goals with scope, owners, success measures, and a timeline. Bring structure to ideas that arrive without it.
• Cross-functional alignment. Secure what each workstream needs from the functions that touch it, and keep every partner team clear on what they owe and when.
• Briefing. Write and own the briefs for your workstreams, following the team’s briefing process so the quality bar is consistent across everything we produce.
• Work-back schedules. Build the work-back for your workstreams, hold the dates, and flag slippage before it becomes a problem.
• Talent and partnerships. Help choose the talent and brand partners who fit Chime, and own how those relationships are set up and run.
• Social. Own how your workstreams come together on social, where most of this work is seen.
• Calendar alignment. Keep the brand calendar coherent against the team’s goals so moments land in the right order and don’t collide.
• Results. Close every workstream with a readout on what it achieved, and carry the learnings into the next brief.

To thrive in this role, you have
• 8+ years experience on both the agency side and the brand side, roughly two to three years in each. You know what it’s like to receive a bad brief and what it’s like to write one.
• A track record of taking an idea that existed only in someone’s head and turning it into a campaign that shipped.
• Strong writing. Briefs, goals, and recaps are the output of this job, and vague writing produces vague work.
• Comfort running several workstreams at once without losing the detail on any of them.
• Experience working with talent, creators, or brand partners, and judgment about which ones are right for a brand.
• Fluency in social, including what performs and why.

jobs.title: Staff Data Scientist, Marketing Analytics
jobs.description:
About the role

When people sign up for Chime, we want to know which marketing efforts brought them in and which ones brought in members who stay and use their account. You will set the direction for how Chime answers that question.

You will be the senior analytics leader for paid marketing. You will co-own and help decide how we measure a 9 figure plus paid media budget and how that measurement turns into optimization and allocation decisions. This is a high-visibility role. Marketing, Growth, Finance and executive leaders will treat your work as the main reference for how marketing performs. You will join the Marketing Analytics team and work across Marketing, Finance, Data Engineering and Data Science/ML.

In this role, you can expect to
• Own the paid performance story. Track spend and results across channels every week. Explain why numbers moved, in plain words that a non-analyst can act on.
• Measure new-member offers. Show whether our introductory new member offers bring in better members and whether they are worth the cost. Compare offer groups against fair, matched groups.
• Set the bar for experiments and offers. Define how tests are designed and read, and how we decide whether sign-up offers are worth the cost.
• Improve how we credit marketing channels. Find where our attribution rules fall short, propose better ones, and work with Data Engineering to build and maintain them.
• Turn marketing mix modeling into budget advice. Use the output of our Marketing Mix Model to advise Marketing on how to allocate budget across channels.
• Be a proactive business partner. Work with Marketing, Growth and Finance leaders as a trusted partner. Share insights and recommendations before they ask, and help them decide what to do next.
• Help plan the work ahead. Estimate the likely impact of new marketing ideas so the team can prioritize.
• Use AI to work faster and go deeper. Use AI tools to speed up analysis, check your work, and build things others can reuse.
• Raise the level of the team. Coach senior data scientists, guide contractors and set the quality bar for high-stakes work.

To thrive in this role, you have
• A Bachelor’s degree and 8+ years of experience in analytics or data science, with deep experience in marketing, growth or consumer products
• A track record of setting measurement strategy across several teams, not only delivering analyses within one team
• Deep expertise in marketing measurement: attribution, incrementality, MMM, cost per acquisition and LTV:CAC, including designing these systems from scratch
• Expert-level experimentation and causal inference skills, including knowing when standard methods don’t fit and building approaches that do
• Strong SQL and experience shaping data models and pipelines in large data warehouses (we use Snowflake)
• Advanced Python or a similar language for analysis
• Experience using Marketing Mix Model output to guide budget decisions at significant scale
• Hands-on experience bringing AI tools into analytics work for a team, and good judgment about their limits
• A history of influencing VP-level and executive decisions without formal authority, including settling disagreements between competing stakeholders
• Clear writing and speaking for senior, non-technical audiences
• A track record of growing other senior data scientists’ skills through mentorship, frameworks and shared tools
• Comfort with problems that have no precedent, where you have to define both the question and the approach

Coinbase is building the future of finance for people, institutions and their agents, with one place to trade crypto, equities, derivatives and prediction markets, use stablecoins, and connect AI agents with clear controls. jobs.title: Staff Strategic Operations Program Manager - GTM
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
Until November 18, 1883, American railroads ran on dozens of local times. Noon in Chicago was 12:31 in Pittsburgh, and every railroad kept its own clock, so schedules collided and connections failed. That day the railroads agreed on four time zones, and clocks across the country stopped and restarted on a shared standard. Nothing about the trains changed. What changed was that everyone could finally plan against the same clock.

That is the job of the Staff Strategic Operations Program Manager for Go-to-Market (“GTM”) at Mercury.

Mercury builds the financial stack for ambitious businesses: banking*, cards, payments, credit, and the financial workflows that run on top of them. Our go-to-market organization spans Revenue, Marketing, Growth Product, and GTM Data, more than 200 people who acquire customers and help them use more of Mercury. 

To do that, the four teams are building a shared GTM Engine: one view of the customer, every touchpoint logged, attribution everyone trusts, and Campaigns that share targeting and rules across channels. This role owns the whole program end to end. You would be that person, sitting on Mercury’s Strategic Operations team and embedded with GTM leadership.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

What you’ll do:

Own the program
• Build and run the integrated plan for the GTM Engine across Growth Product, Growth Marketing, Revenue, and GTM Data: milestones, dependencies, critical path, and the handoffs between teams that no single team owns.
• Keep a living RAID log and decision log with clear owners. When a data signal slips and a campaign depends on it, you know first and arrive with options.

Drive decisions
• Drive decisions through ambiguity: clarify ownership, force tradeoffs into the open, and use productive conflict to get to the right answer
• Prepare GTM Review so leaders spend their time deciding rather than reconstructing status. 

Build the operating system
• Design the planning cycles, reviews, and launch-readiness checks that let four teams work the same customer at the same time.
• Make the engine legible: dashboards, written updates, and a single source of truth that a marketer, a sales leader, and a data scientist can all read.
• Build automation and agentic flows to run programs with efficiency and high quality

What we’re looking for:
• 7+ years running cross-functional programs, ideally in B2B SaaS or fintech.
• GTM systems fluency. You have worked inside a CRM, lifecycle, CDP, or attribution stack (Salesforce, Customer.io, Segment, or equivalents) closely enough to know what is hard about getting a new signal into a rep’s or a marketer’s workflow.
• Structured thinking. You take disparate inputs (four leaders, three functions, dozens of docs) and turn them into one picture of what is happening and what needs deciding.
• Strong structured communication
• Bias to action. You pick up the unowned next step, you do not let ambiguity sit, and you go talk to whoever has the answer.
• Low ego. This is a behind-the-scenes role.
• AI fluency. You have already automated some of your own work and can show the before and after.

jobs.title: Performance Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
Who we are:

Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial ecosystem, helping 10 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, and business management tools since
2019. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, it powers most of the country’s Point of Sale (POS) transactions. Through its subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes $22 billion monthly for its customers while operating profitably.

Curious about what makes Moniepoint an incredible place to work? Check out posts on how we cultivate a culture of innovation, teamwork, and growth.

About

the role:

We are hiring for a dedicated Google Acquisition function to drive scalable customer growth across both our personal and business banking products. This Senior Manager will own the end-to-end Google performance channel — from campaign architecture and technical infrastructure to economic modelling and channel governance.

This is not an execution role dressed up as a leadership role. We need someone who thinks in systems, works from first principles, and has the depth to make credible judgements on strategy, technology, and economics simultaneously.

Responsibilities
• Campaign Architecture Execution
• Design and own the full Google channel strategy across UAC / App Campaigns, Performance Max, and Search for both personal and business banking acquisition
• Build and maintain campaign structures optimised for Moniepoint's dual-product funnel — separating signals, audiences, and bidding logic appropriately across segments
• Set bidding strategies, budget allocation frameworks, and creative testing cycles that reduce dependence on any single signal or format
• Own campaign performance end-to-end: from brief to launch to optimisation to reporting
• Tracking, Attribution Technical Infrastructure
• Architect and own the full measurement stack: Firebase / GA4 event taxonomy, Google Tag Manager configuration, and server-side event pipelines
• Lead the implementation and ongoing integrity of Conversion APIs and enhanced conversions to maximise signal quality sent back to Google
• Define the attribution model — evaluate last-click, data-driven, and custom models against Moniepoint's funnel reality, and own the decision with clear reasoning
• Partner with engineering and data teams to ensure event data flowing to Google is accurate, complete, and timely — treating signal quality as a competitive asset
• Build audit protocols for tracking coverage and attribution consistency; surface gaps before they distort decisions
• LTV/CAC Economics
• Own the economic model for Google acquisition: define CAC targets by product, segment, and channel variant; set the inputs, assumptions, and review cadence
• Understand the LTV/CAC relationship at a structural level — not just as a ratio to optimise, but as a function of product retention, monetisation curves, and cohort behaviour
• Build and iterate on payback period models that account for Moniepoint's emerging market context: irregular income patterns, higher churn risk, and longer monetisation timelines
• Design bidding and budget logic that reflects true LTV signals rather than proxy metrics, working closely with data science to enrich Google's Smart Bidding with offline conversion data
• Proactively identify when CAC is drifting against LTV thresholds and lead the diagnosis — channel mix, audience quality, creative fatigue, product-market fit — before it becomes a financial problem
• Governance Reporting
• Build a channel reporting system that surfaces reality clearly — not dashboards that flatter performance, but views that drive better decisions
• Establish review cadences with clear owners, metrics, and follow-through mechanisms
• Translate channel performance into business language for senior stakeholders: what is the cost of growth, is it sustainable, and what would change the trajectory
• Emerging Market Fintech Context
• Adapt Google acquisition strategy for the realities of emerging market users: variable device penetration, low-bandwidth environments, trust barriers to financial services, and diverse
• language/literacy contexts
• Navigate platform constraints specific to fintech advertising on Google: financial services policies, verification requirements, and creative compliance
• Bring genuine insight into what acquisition patterns distinguish sustainable fintech growth from subsidised growth in markets like Nigeria

To succeed in this role, you should have:
• 6+ years of hands-on paid acquisition experience, with the majority of that time spent on Google UAC / App Campaigns at meaningful scale
• Deep, demonstrable technical knowledge of Google's campaign infrastructure: bidding algorithms, audience signals, creative specs, and the mechanics of Smart Bidding
• Proven ability to architect and own the full measurement stack — Firebase, GA4, GTM, Conversion APIs — not just configure it but understand why each component matters
• Fluency in LTV/CAC modelling: you have built the models, owned the assumptions, and used them to make real budgeting and bidding decisions
• Experience operating in a fintech or financial services context, with direct knowledge of the acquisition compliance and trust dynamics unique to financial products
• Strongly Preferred
• Experience managing budgets larger that 10 Million USD annually
• Experience running Google acquisition in Sub-Saharan Africa or comparable emerging markets — Nigeria specifically is a significant advantage
• Familiarity with server-side conversion APIs, offline conversion imports, and enhanced conversions as mechanisms for improving signal quality in cookieless or app-first environments
• Experience working with data science or analytics teams to build custom bidding signals and offline LTV imports into Google's systems
• Prior work on dual-product or dual-segment acquisition (e.g., consumer and SME / business) with separate funnel logic

What Success Looks Like

In the first 90 days
• Full audit of existing Google campaign structure, tracking integrity, and attribution model completed — with a written assessment and prioritised improvement plan
• Measurement stack gaps identified and remediation underway with engineering
• LTV/CAC baseline model built with documented assumptions, reviewed with Growth and Finance
• First governance cadence established — weekly performance review with clear owner, metrics, and follow-through log

In the first year
• Google channel operating as a reliable, scalable growth engine with predictable CAC across both personal and business banking segments
• Signal quality measurably improved — higher match rates, cleaner conversion data, reduced reliance on last-click proxies
• Attribution model validated against actual cohort data and actively used in budget allocation decisions
• Playbook documented: campaign architecture, bidding logic, audience strategy, and economic model all institutionalised — not living in one person's head
• A team (or foundations for one) built with clear ownership, development paths, and no single point of failure

What to expect in the hiring process
• A preliminary phone call with the recruiter
• A technical interview with the hiring manager
• A Case Study
• A behavioural and technical interview with a member of the Executive team
• All interview stages are virtual

• Governance Reporting
• Build a channel reporting system that surfaces reality clearly — not dashboards that flatter performance, but views that drive better decisions
• Establish review cadences with clear owners, metrics, and follow-through mechanisms
• Translate channel performance into business language for senior stakeholders: what is the cost of growth, is it sustainable, and what would change the trajectory
• Emerging Market Fintech Context
• Adapt Google acquisition strategy for the realities of emerging market users: variable device penetration, low-bandwidth environments, trust barriers to financial services, and diverse
• language/literacy contexts
• Navigate platform constraints specific to fintech advertising on Google: financial services policies, verification requirements, and creative compliance
• Bring genuine insight into what acquisition patterns distinguish sustainable fintech growth from subsidised growth in markets like Nigeria

To succeed in this role, you should have:
• 6+ years of hands-on paid acquisition experience, with the majority of that time spent on Google UAC / App Campaigns at meaningful scale
• Deep, demonstrable technical knowledge of Google's campaign infrastructure: bidding algorithms, audience signals, creative specs, and the mechanics of Smart Bidding
• Proven ability to architect and own the full measurement stack — Firebase, GA4, GTM, Conversion APIs — not just configure it but understand why each component matters
• Fluency in LTV/CAC modelling: you have built the models, owned the assumptions, and used them to make real budgeting and bidding decisions
• Experience operating in a fintech or financial services context, with direct knowledge of the acquisition compliance and trust dynamics unique to financial products
• Experience managing budgets larger that 10 Million USD annually
• Strongly Preferred
• Experience running Google acquisition in Sub-Saharan Africa or comparable emerging markets — Nigeria specifically is a significant advantage
• Familiarity with server-side conversion APIs, offline conversion imports, and enhanced conversions as mechanisms for improving signal quality in cookieless or app-first environments
• Experience working with data science or analytics teams to build custom bidding signals and offline LTV imports into Google's systems
• Prior work on dual-product or dual-segment acquisition (e.g., consumer and SME / business) with separate funnel logic

What Success Looks Like

In the first 90 days
• Full audit of existing Google campaign structure, tracking integrity, and attribution model completed — with a written assessment and prioritised improvement plan
• Measurement stack gaps identified and remediation underway with engineering
• LTV/CAC baseline model built with documented assumptions, reviewed with Growth and Finance
• First governance cadence established — weekly performance review with clear owner, metrics, and follow-through log

In the first year
• Google channel operating as a reliable, scalable growth engine with predictable CAC across both personal and business banking segments
• Signal quality measurably improved — higher match rates, cleaner conversion data, reduced reliance on last-click proxies
• Attribution model validated against actual cohort data and actively used in budget allocation decisions
• Playbook documented: campaign architecture, bidding logic, audience strategy, and economic model all institutionalised — not living in one person's head
• A team (or foundations for one) built with clear ownership, development paths, and no single point of failure

jobs.title: Deputy Money Laundering Reporting Officer - Malta
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At OKX, we believe crypto will help reshape the future and contribute to greater individual freedom.

OKX is a leading crypto exchange and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions of customers access to crypto trading and decentralised applications. OKX is also trusted by institutions seeking secure access to crypto markets and is supported by its Proof of Reserves programme.

Across our global offices, we are united by three core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These values shape how we work and help us create a collaborative, rewarding and diverse environment for every OK-er.

About the Team

The Compliance function is responsible for promoting a strong compliance culture and supporting the safe, sustainable growth of OKX. We are a team of risk-minded problem solvers who advise the business on regulatory obligations, conduct expectations and enterprise risks.

About the Opportunity

We are looking for a Deputy Money Laundering Reporting Officer (Deputy MLRO) to support the MLRO in overseeing and further developing the organisation’s AML/CFT and financial crime compliance framework within a MiCA-regulated crypto-asset environment. The role will provide exposure to a broad range of financial crime matters, including customer due diligence, transaction and blockchain monitoring, investigations, suspicious activity reporting and regulatory engagement.

The Deputy MLRO will act as a key AML/CFT subject-matter expert across the organisation, providing oversight, advice and challenge to ensure that financial crime risks are appropriately identified, assessed and managed. The role will also support the continuous enhancement of AML/CFT systems and controls, ensuring that they remain effective, proportionate and aligned with the organisation’s evolving products, customer base and risk profile.

Working closely with the MLRO and stakeholders across Compliance, KYC, Transaction Monitoring, Operations, Product, Legal and Risk, the successful candidate will play an important role in maintaining a strong financial crime compliance framework while supporting an efficient and risk-based customer experience.

What You’ll Be Doing
• Support and deputise for the MLRO, including assisting with AML/CFT governance, management and Board reporting, regulatory matters and oversight of the organisation’s financial crime compliance framework.
• Oversee complex AML/CFT investigations and escalations, including transaction monitoring alerts, blockchain activity, higher-risk customer relationships and internal suspicious activity reports, ensuring decisions and rationale are appropriately documented.
• Support suspicious activity reporting processes, including assessment of potential suspicion, preparation and review of external reports where appropriate, and maintenance of appropriate confidentiality and controls against tipping off.
• Provide second-line oversight of KYC, CDD and EDD, including higher-risk customers, Source of Funds and Source of Wealth assessments, customer risk classification, ongoing monitoring and periodic or trigger-based reviews.
• Oversee and enhance transaction and blockchain monitoring controls, including scenario and threshold calibration, effectiveness testing, identification of emerging typologies and initiatives to improve detection quality and reduce unnecessary false positives.
• Provide AML/CFT expertise on crypto-specific risks, including self-hosted wallets, cross-chain activity, DeFi, mixers, privacy-enhancing technologies and other emerging risks, as well as applicable Travel Rule requirements.
• Support regulatory engagement and continuous improvement, including regulatory inspections and information requests, audits, remediation programmes, new product and service risk assessments, AML/CFT training and implementation of relevant regulatory developments.

What We’re Looking For
• Relevant AML/CFT and financial crime experience, preferably gained within a regulated CASP/VASP, crypto exchange, fintech, payments business or financial institution, with experience in a senior AML, financial crime or compliance role considered an advantage.
• Strong knowledge of EU AML/CFT requirements and the risk-based approach, together with a good understanding of the regulatory framework applicable to CASPs, including MiCA and the EU Transfer of Funds Regulation/Travel Rule.
• Practical experience across core AML/CFT disciplines, including CDD/EDD, Source of Funds and Source of Wealth, customer risk assessment, transaction monitoring, investigations and suspicious activity reporting.
• Strong understanding of crypto-assets and blockchain-related financial crime risks, with experience using or interpreting blockchain analytics and transaction monitoring tools considered a strong advantage.
• Strong analytical and investigative skills, with the ability to assess complex customer and transactional activity, distinguish unusual but legitimate behaviour from genuine financial crime concerns, and reach well-reasoned and defensible decisions.
• Excellent judgement, communication and stakeholder-management skills, including the confidence to provide independent challenge, escalate material concerns and communicate effectively with senior management, operational teams, auditors and regulatory authorities.
• Relevant academic or professional qualifications, with a degree in law, finance, economics, compliance, risk or a related field and/or recognised AML/financial crime qualifications such as CAMS, ICA or equivalent considered an advantage.

• Wellness and meal allowances.
• Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants.
• Additional benefits that we would be pleased to discuss during the recruitment process.

• Ability to oversee daily process management and streamline legal support workflows for the paralegal team.
• Proven track record of supporting in-house counsel with responding to complex legal requests.

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience; paralegal certification is a plus.
• 4+ years of experience as a paralegal, in either a law firm or in-house legal department. At least 2 years experience as a paralegal in a law firm is strongly preferred.
• Strong experience with litigation tracking and case management platforms (e.g., Legal Tracker, CounselLink, or similar).
• Strong knowledge of the subpoena and litigation and arbitration processes.
• Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously while meeting multiple, and often short, deadlines.

• Comfort working cross-functionally with attorneys, cross-functional partners, and external service providers.

jobs.title: Customer Experience Specialist
jobs.description:

jobs.title: Senior Product Analyst - Grow  - Scalable Platform
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

You’ll be joining the Grow Squad. We manage a complex, multi-product portfolio including Current Accounts, Savings, Investments, and Digital Assets. While other teams focus on acquiring customers, your mission is to ensure we serve them safely, sustainably, and profitably.

jobs.title: Senior Presales Consultant
jobs.description:
We’ll look to you to help drive our growth objectives while consulting closely with our product, sales, and delivery teams to design solutions that we can deliver efficiently and with quality.

• Travel to work with our teams and meet with prospects around the world.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Risk Intelligence Platform
jobs.description:
Wise moves billions every year for millions of people and businesses across multiple countries and currencies. At that scale, financial crime is constantly evolving — from scams and account takeovers to money laundering and mule networks. Staying ahead of these threats means our automated controls and machine learning models need high-quality, timely insights.

The Risk Intelligence Platform team, part of Risk Machine Learning, builds the tools and automation that help Wise's FinCrime teams develop and improve those models. Our work covers areas such as model experimentation, bias and fairness, automated training-set maintenance, and threshold analysis.

Our main users are Data Scientists and Product Managers across Fraud Prevention, AML and Sanctions. We build the platform and tooling that removes repetitive Engineering work and enables these teams to focus on what matters most: identifying and preventing financial crime effectively at scale.

As part of the team, you'll work at the intersection of Backend Engineering, data and machine learning, solving complex Engineering problems that directly support Wise's FinCrime prevention capabilities.

jobs.title: Internal Audit Senior Manager (Fincrime)
jobs.description:
Are you a Financial Crime assurance leader looking to move away from legacy, manual audit routines and build data-driven, tech-enabled audit practices?

We are looking for an Internal Audit Senior Manager (FinCrime) to join our growing EU Internal Audit team in Brussels. In this role, you won't just run audits, you will directly shape how Internal Audit operates at Wise globally.

You will lead complex FinCrime audit engagements, manage internal and external partner teams, and influence key stakeholders across governance, risk, and control functions.

If you thrive in a fast-paced fintech setting where technology, continuous monitoring, and autonomy take centre stage, this role is built for you.

What You’ll Be Doing (Your Mission)
• Automate & Innovate: Advance our internal audit framework by developing continuous monitoring tools and automated audit routines.
• Shape Strategy: Drive the annual audit plan—defining the audit universe, risk assessment models, and resource budgeting.
• Deliver High-Impact Audits: Lead end-to-end FinCrime audits per the annual plan, turning complex findings into actionable, business-critical insights.
• Align Assurance: Lead strategic cross-functional projects to create a unified, seamless assurance model across Wise.
• Build & Mentor: Empower and guide a high-performing, self-sufficient internal audit team.
• Track Real Progress: Oversee the implementation of audit recommendations and measure the real-world impact of control enhancements.

What We’re Looking For

We know great candidates don’t always tick every single box. If you hold strong assurance experience in financial services and a passion for technology, we want to hear from you!

Core Experience & Expertise
• FinCrime Specialisation: Deep expertise across key financial crime domains (FinCrime risk management, KYC/KYB, EDD, Transaction Monitoring, Screening, and Reporting). Experience with sanctions and financial crime models is a strong plus.
• Regulatory Context: Strong understanding of EU Money Laundering Directives, FATF, and Wolfsberg guidance.
• Assurance & Controls: Proven track record in risk, control, or internal audit roles within Fintech, Tech, or Financial Services.
• Data & Tech Drive: Enthusiasm for leveraging technology, data analytics, and continuous monitoring in audit workflows (hands-on data analytics experience preferred).
• Execution & Leadership: Demonstrated ability to scope audits, lead risk-based testing, manage cross-functional projects, and mentor junior team members.
• Communication: Ability to distill complex risk topics into concise, clear insights for stakeholders at all levels.

Qualifications (Preferred, Not Mandatory)
• Relevant professional certification: CAMS, CFE, ICA (Diploma/Cert), or CIA (or equivalent practical experience).

Why Apply?
• Hybrid Working: Flexible balance between home and our Brussels office.
• Modern Fintech Culture: Less red tape, higher autonomy, and an emphasis on data-driven decision-making over manual paperwork.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Cloud Platform
jobs.description:
You are a Senior Software Engineer who will be joining the team of world class DevOps Engineers. The team maintains, supports and grows Wise’s Kubernetes based Compute Platform. Your mission will be to lead, design and implement automation around Kubernetes installation, maintenance and monitoring. That includes building microservices, API-s, workflows and documentation. jobs.title: Accountant
Lead Product Manager, DeFi
jobs.description:
Who we are 

We simplify wealth creation. Founded in 2014 in Vienna, Austria by Eric Demuth, Paul Klanschek and Christian Trummer, we’re here to help people trust themselves enough to build their financial freedom — for now and the future. Our user-friendly, trade-everything platform empowers both first-time investors and seasoned experts to invest in the cryptocurrencies, crypto indices, stocks*, precious metals and commodities* they want — with any sized budget, 24/7. Our global team works across different cultures and time zones, bringing our products to more than 7 million customers, making us one of Europe’s safest and most secure platforms that powers modern investing.

 

Headquartered in Austria but operating across Europe, our products are built by fast-moving, talented, “roll-up-your-sleeves-and-make-it-happen” kind of people. It’s these diverse perspectives and innovative minds operating as ONE TEAM that keep Bitpanda at the cutting edge of our industry. So if you’re someone who thinks big, moves fast and wants to make an impact right from day one, then get ready to join our industry-changing team. Let’s go!

 

Your mission

Bitpanda serves millions of investors across Europe, and we're bringing regulated finance onchain with Vision Chain, our own OP Stack L2 blockchain. We are looking for a Lead Product Manager, DeFi to build Bitpanda’s DeFi ecosystem from the ground up, creating the world’s premier Euro-denominated DeFi ecosystem while making it safe, accessible, and intuitive for our customers. 

The first use case is crypto-backed borrowing and lending in the Bitpanda app, with an eye to then build more sophisticated products and use cases leveraging tokenized commodities, securities, funds, and structured products. You’ll decide which protocols and partners come to Vision Chain, and work collaboratively to bring DeFi to Bitpanda customers in a way that feels as simple as the app they already trust. You'll work in a small, senior team with our smart contract engineers and Bitpanda's Legal, Compliance and Risk teams, as an individual contributor reporting to the Head of Web3 Product.

 

What you’ll do
• Design and run the lending markets: set loan-to-value and liquidation thresholds, interest rate curves, caps, and oracles, while also owning monitoring and incident playbooks.
• Bring liquidity and users to permissioned markets and assets: set supply targets, bring in euro liquidity from stablecoin issuers, institutional lenders, curated vaults and market makers, and work out how verified customers reach these markets, without paying for volume.
• Make sure the right DeFi infrastructure is in place, particularly for permissioned tokenized assets: DEX liquidity deep enough for swaps and liquidations, liquidators, oracles and the other building blocks the markets depend on.
• Shape what customers see, sign, and own in the Bitpanda app, including how liquidation and risk are explained, and measure real use: borrowers who come back, bad debt and revenue, not total value locked alone.
• Recommend which protocols and partners come to Vision Chain, backed by a business case, and work with Legal, Compliance and Risk from day one on EU consumer credit rules and MiCA.

Who you are
• 6+ years of Product Management experience, with at least 3+ years focused specifically on building and scaling DeFi or crypto products.
• You know lending markets in depth: collateral and liquidation mechanics, interest rate models, oracles and how they fail, curation and bad debt. You're at home with the EVM and can read Solidity smart contract code well enough to question engineers about it.
• Demonstrated experience bringing DeFi applications into regulated consumer products and successfully bridging the gap between decentralized and centralized finance.
• Ability to lead through influence, build clear business cases, and write excellent documentation in English. This includes a strong working knowledge of EU crypto regulations (e.g., MiCA) to effectively partner with Risk, Legal, and Compliance teams.
• Nice to haves:
• hands-on experience scaling onchain ecosystem liquidity from scratch
• knowledge of and/or work experience in traditional financial markets

** This position is available in all of our Hubs.

What’s in it for you
• Flexibility to work where you thrive – Enjoy the freedom of our Hybrid working model, combining onsite collaboration and remote work, with an additional 25 days per year to work from a city or country of your choice.
• Reward for your impact – Receive a competitive total compensation package aligned with Bitpanda’s pay-for-impact policy, including participation in our stock option plan.
• Support for your mental wellbeing – Access confidential coaching, counselling, and mental health resources whenever you need them through OpenUP.
• Time to recharge – On top of your standard annual leave, prioritise your wellbeing in 2027 with 3 additional days of paid time off to rest, reset, and recharge, available once you’ve been with us for 6 months.
• Continuous learning and growth – Grow your skills and stay ahead in your career with unlimited access to Udemy’s library of online courses at your own pace.
• Exclusive perks and rewards – Enjoy discounts, rewards, and perks from partners worldwide across lifestyle, wellness, tech, and travel.
• Support during life milestones – Take advantage of up to 8 additional weeks of gender-neutral new parent leave to welcome and bond with your new addition to the family.
• Fuel and focus on-site – Pandas in Vienna, Bucharest, Barcelona, and Berlin can enjoy free onsite dining, with freshly prepared lunches and snacks to keep you fueled and focused all day long.
• Recognition for your contributions – Celebrate milestones and achievements with recognition and rewards for your Tenure at Bitpanda.
• Show your Bitpanda pride – Access exclusive Bitpanda-branded merchandise and gear to represent.
• Connect and celebrate with your team – Join unforgettable company events, from our Winter Party in Vienna to gatherings worldwide, fostering fun, connection, and celebration

 .…and even more location-specific benefits designed to make life at Bitpanda even more rewarding wherever you are.

 

Above all, you will have the opportunity to learn and grow as part of Bitpanda’s incredible journey towards being Europe’s future #1 investment platform.

Bitpanda is committed to fostering a fair and equal environment based on trust and mutual respect. We believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace is paramount to our success and we are committed to building a team that represents a wide variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills.

* These benefits may be adjusted at Bitpanda’s discretion and do not apply to our internships and exceptions to our Hybrid Working policy apply to teams with shift schedules or for folks whose roles require them to be in-office (think: Workplaces team or IT).

We simplify wealth creation. Founded in 2014 in Vienna, Austria by Eric Demuth, Paul Klanschek and Christian Trummer, we’re here to help people trust themselves enough to build their financial freedom — for now and the future. Our user-friendly, trade-everything platform empowers both first-time investors and seasoned experts to invest in the cryptocurrencies, crypto indices, stocks*, precious metals and commodities* they want — with any sized budget, 24/7. Our global team works across different cultures and time zones, bringing our products to more than 7 million customers, making us one of Europe’s safest and most secure platforms that powers modern investing.

 

Headquartered in Austria but operating across Europe, our products are built by fast-moving, talented, “roll-up-your-sleeves-and-make-it-happen” kind of people. It’s these diverse perspectives and innovative minds operating as ONE TEAM that keep Bitpanda at the cutting edge of our industry. So if you’re someone who thinks big, moves fast and wants to make an impact right from day one, then get ready to join our industry-changing team. Let’s go!

 

Your mission

Bitpanda serves millions of investors across Europe, and we're bringing regulated finance onchain with Vision Chain, our own OP Stack L2 blockchain. We are building the premier ecosystem for European financial institutions to issue and distribute euro-denominated tokenized assets. We're hiring a Lead Technical Product Manager to own Vision Chain as a product: the foundation that Bitpanda's onchain products run on.

You'll own how the chain works and evolves, covering topics spanning proof systems, core protocol modifications, selecting the infrastructure providers, and more. You'll design and implement compliance, identity and privacy solutions into and on the chain, to satisfy the requirements of both financial institutions and developers. You'll work on this in collaboration with both internal and external product and engineering teams, as well as Bitpanda's Compliance, Legal and Data Protection teams, as an individual contributor reporting to the Head of Web3 Product within a small, senior team.

 

What you’ll do
• Own Vision Chain at the infrastructure level, managing configuration choices (fee mechanism, block building logic, etc.), and modifications to the OP Stack, in collaboration with the OP Labs team.
• Manage infrastructure partnerships, owning the technical relationship with providers (RPC nodes, indexing, oracles, etc.).
• Collaborate with Compliance and Legal to implement regulatorily-compliant onchain transaction screening, identity, and privacy solutions.
• Run reliability, incidents and cost, and own developer documentation and partner technical onboarding until a developer relations lead joins.
• Coordinate with the other Vision Web3 product leads to ensure the chain’s technical roadmap supports the product roadmap being built on top of it.

Who you are
• 6+ years of product or engineering experience, with 3+ years focused on blockchain infrastructure (e.g., L1/L2, rollup-as-a-service, node infrastructure provider, account abstraction, or an exchange protocol team).

jobs.title: Senior Design Recruiter
jobs.location: New York, New York, United States
jobs.description:
Why join us

Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.

Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

Recruiting at Brex

Recruiting is where every career at Brex begins. We are the first point of connection for future builders and leaders, helping candidates see what is possible. We partner with leaders across the company to find exceptional talent and build high-performing teams. We move quickly, think strategically, and take pride in a thoughtful, welcoming candidate experience from the first contact. We shape the culture at Brex by hiring the designers who define how our products look, feel and function.

What you'll do

This role is responsible for partnering with hiring managers and design leadership to define team needs and role requirements, ensuring alignment on hiring goals across Product Design, Brand Design, and Design Leadership.

You’ll source, engage, and assess world-class design talent through diverse channels, while managing the full recruitment lifecycle from outreach to onboarding. You will develop strategies to attract and retain diverse design talent, proactively building pipelines for both immediate and long-term hiring needs.

You’ll track and analyze key hiring metrics to improve recruiting effectiveness, collaborate cross-functionally to ensure fair and consistent evaluation practices, and champion Brex’s employer brand within the design community. This includes representing Brex at design events, portfolio reviews, and on relevant social platforms

Where you'll work

This role will be based in our New York office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week, Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work.

Responsibilities
• Lead sourcing and outreach for design roles, using recruiting platforms, creative communities, portfolio sites and social networks.
• Recruit across Product Design, Brand/Visual Design and Design Leadership.
• Screen and evaluate portfolios, craft quality, systems thinking and collaboration skills.
• Partner with design leaders to calibrate on craft standards, hiring bar and team composition.
• Coordinate and facilitate interview processes, including portfolio reviews and design exercises, with a high-quality candidate experience.
• Give hiring managers and stakeholders regular updates on pipeline health and progress.
• Keep candidate data accurate in recruiting systems and dashboards.
• Contribute to continuous improvement of recruiting processes, inclusive hiring and candidate experience.
• Help shape and promote Brex's design employer brand.

Requirements
• Proven experience recruiting for design roles (Product Design and Brand Design) in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
• Strong sourcing skills and familiarity with AI tools, recruiting platforms and creative talent networks.
• Ability to assess design portfolios and understand craft, systems thinking and user-centered methods.
• Excellent communication, relationship-building and stakeholder management.
• Data-driven mindset: interprets recruiting metrics and drives process improvements.
• Manages multiple searches and priorities at once.

Bonus points
• Experience recruiting design leaders or building design teams from the ground up.
• Familiarity with compensation strategy and market analysis for design roles.
• Employer branding or talent marketing experience focused on the design community.
• Hiring across multiple geographies (US, Canada, LATAM).

Compensation

The expected salary range for this role is $126,550 - $158,200. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package.

Brex LLC is a wholly owned subsidiary of Capital One, N.A.

Please be aware, job-seekers may be at risk of targeting by malicious actors looking for personal data. Brex recruiters will only reach out via LinkedIn or email with a brex.com domain. Any outreach claiming to be from Brex via other sources should be ignored.

Engineering at Brex

Engineering at Brex is about building systems that scale with speed and intention. Our teams span Software, Data, Security, and IT, and operate with high autonomy and deep collaboration. We tackle hard technical problems, own our outcomes, and push for excellence at every level — from architecture to deployment. It’s an environment where engineering is a craft, and builders become leaders.

What you'll do
Brex's AI strategy has three pillars: Product AI builds AI into the products our customers use, Corporate AI gives every employee AI tools to work faster, and Operational AI builds the AI that runs the company. The Operational AI team owns the AI systems and internal platforms that make Brex's operations AI-native, from onboarding and KYC automation to AI-powered customer support. We're a small team with a large surface area, and our work directly shapes how fast Brex can onboard, serve, and grow its customers.
As a Senior Software Engineer on the team, you'll focus on Agents Platform, Brex's internal platform for building, evaluating, and running AI agents in production. It already powers critical automations in customer onboarding and AI tools for our sales and customer success teams. You'll own its technical direction, help it evolve from simple workflows into agents that take action, and make it the default way Brex ships AI into its operations.

Where you'll work

This role will be based in our São Paulo office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require a minimum of three coordinated days in the office per week: Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work.

Responsibilities
• Own the technical direction and roadmap of Agents Platform, partnering with Operational AI leadership and the teams that build on it to decide what the platform should do next.
• Design and build new platform capabilities, including tool calling, multi-step agent loops, multi-turn and conversational execution, and secure access to internal Brex data and services.
• Evolve the evaluation and quality system, from datasets and labeling to run comparison and regression testing, so teams can measure and improve non-deterministic systems with production-grade rigor.
• Strengthen the reliability, security, and observability of systems in business-critical flows like customer onboarding, including durable async and batch execution, authorization, cost attribution, and incident response.
• Partner with engineering, operations, and go-to-market teams to launch and scale high-impact agents, translating how they work into clear platform requirements.
• Drive adoption by making the platform easy to build on through clear contracts, paved roads, documentation, and AI-native developer workflows.
• Mentor engineers on the team and across Brex through design reviews, code reviews, and pairing, and help grow the team's technical bench.

Requirements
• 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a track record of designing, building, and operating reliable production backend systems.
• Deep, hands-on experience using AI coding tools like Claude Code or Cursor in your daily work, with the judgment to ship faster without lowering the quality bar.
• Hands-on experience shipping LLM-powered systems to production, beyond prototypes: orchestrating model calls, enforcing structured outputs, and evaluating quality over time.
• Experience with distributed and asynchronous systems and the reliability concerns that come with them, such as retries, idempotency, backpressure, and observability.
• A platform mindset: you've built shared infrastructure, developer tooling, or paved roads that other engineers adopt, and you care about developer experience and secure-by-default design.
• High ownership and operational excellence, including on-call, incident response, and owning systems end to end.
• Strong written and verbal communication, and the judgment to prioritize across many internal customers, including non-engineers. English proficiency is required, as interviews will be conducted in English.

Bonus points
• Experience building eval frameworks, LLM gateways, or agent platforms used by other teams.
• Experience with Temporal or another durable workflow engine.
• Experience with service and agent authorization, such as RBAC, scoped credentials, or agents acting on behalf of users.
• Production experience with tool use, MCP, retrieval, or agentic loops.
• A background in ML engineering, MLOps, or data infrastructure.
• Experience in fintech or another regulated environment, where auditability and model governance matter.

jobs.description:
About the role

We are hiring a Product Manager to join Chime’s Growth team, focused on Marketing Technology. You’ll sit at the intersection of Product, Engineering, Marketing, Analytics, and Data, building the platforms and capabilities that help Chime reach members with more relevant experiences and make smarter growth decisions.

This is a role for a PM who can move comfortably between growth strategy and the technical details underneath it. You’ll identify high-value opportunities, translate marketing and member needs into scalable product capabilities, and use data and experimentation to understand what actually drives incremental growth.

In this role, you can expect to
• Own product strategy and roadmap for marketing technology capabilities that support Chime’s growth.
• Partner closely with Marketing to understand growth opportunities and translate them into scalable product and platform capabilities.
• Work deeply with Engineering to define technical requirements, make thoughtful tradeoffs, and build reliable systems that can scale across channels and use cases.
• Partner with Analytics and Data to define success metrics, understand member behavior, and measure the incremental impact of product investments.
• Build and evolve capabilities across areas such as audience segmentation, lifecycle orchestration, personalization, experimentation, measurement, and marketing data activation.
• Develop hypotheses and experiments that help the team learn quickly, improve growth outcomes, and inform longer-term platform investments.
• Bring structure to ambiguous problems, balancing near-term growth opportunities with the foundational technology needed to unlock future growth.

To thrive in this role, you have
• 7+ years of product management experience owning and shipping technology products with measurable business or customer outcomes.
• Experience working on marketing technology, growth platforms, lifecycle products, customer data, personalization, experimentation, or adjacent data-intensive products.
• Enough technical depth to partner closely with engineers on system design, integrations, APIs, data flows, architecture tradeoffs, and platform reliability.
• Strong analytical fluency, including defining metrics, interpreting behavioral and funnel data, and using quantitative insights to make product decisions.
• Experience designing, evaluating, or using controlled experiments to determine incremental impact and guide product strategy.
• Experience partnering with Marketing or Growth teams and understanding how technology enables targeting, activation, measurement, and optimization.
• A track record of turning ambiguous cross-functional problems into clear product strategy, priorities, and shipped outcomes.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Product and Brand Communications
jobs.description:
About the role

Chime is at an inflection point. We're the leader in consumer financial technology, trusted by more than 10 million members. Our next chapter will be built on the strength of our brand, our technology, and our products. 

This role tells that story end to end. You'll lead Product Brand Communications with a clear mandate: make Chime a household name, establish us as the innovator in consumer finance for the AI era, and show mainstream America the full breadth of what we've built for them. You'll drive a step change in our consumer and technology brand and scale the team that gets us there.

You're equally formidable dreaming up a brand campaign that gets the country talking and orchestrating an integrated product launch that makes a splash. You partner closely with Brand Marketing and Product Marketing leadership from the start, shaping campaigns and launches into one cohesive narrative and amplify it across channels. You bring sharp brand and product comms chops, bold ideas, and a bias for action. 

As a member of the Communications leadership team, you'll report to the VP of External Communications and work closely with Marketing, Product, and Engineering leaders.

In this role, you can expect to:
• Set the strategy: Own an integrated product and brand communications strategy that drives the business and wins over consumers and the tech community alike.
• Mainstream the Chime brand: In close collaboration with Brand Marketing, turn brand partnerships, consumer insights, original research, and cultural moments into campaigns that generate sustained coverage.
• Own the product narrative: Work hand in hand with Product Marketing to drive 360-degree product launches, from messaging to media, influencer relations, and the owned and paid surround sound that turns each one into a buzzy moment.
• Build the team: Lead and develop a high-performing team and raise the bar for the function. Product and Brand Communications is a growth driver for Chime, and there's a lot of runway.
• Lead cross-functionally: Partner with Product Management, Engineering, Brand Marketing, Product Marketing, Content, and others, so every launch and campaign tells a clear story.
• Expand the spokesperson bench: Prepare Chime's product, technology, and marketing leaders for external communications opportunities, working closely with our Chief Technology Officer, Chief Product Officer, and Chief Marketing and Growth Officer and their teams.
• Keep Chime in the conversation: Cultivate relationships across national and local consumer, lifestyle, business, technology, and trade outlets. Direct external agencies to drive consistent coverage and bring campaigns to life.

To thrive in this role, you have:
• 12+ years of experience in product, consumer, or brand communications, or related marketing roles, preferably in consumer technology.
• A track record of leading product and brand communications functions, from large-scale consumer campaigns to major product launches.
• Deep media and influencer relationships across consumer, business, and technology outlets, with a history of landing stories that strengthen brand positioning.
• Experience partnering with creators, celebrities, or brands to generate earned media for consumer, corporate, or social impact campaigns.
• Proven leadership: you've developed high-performing teams, led cross-functional initiatives, and managed agency partners in fast-paced environments.
• Fluency in fintech and consumer technology, including how AI is changing products, consumer behavior, and communications.
• Exceptional writing, editing, and verbal communication skills. You write with personality and know how to make complex ideas clear and compelling.
• Experience advising C-suite executives and building effective partnerships with Marketing, Product, and Engineering teams.
• A degree in Communications, Public Relations, Marketing, Business, or a related field.

• Partner with Business Development and external bank and processor partners on commercial terms, integrations, and the next wave of payment capabilities.

jobs.title: Emerging Talent & Onboarding Program Manager
jobs.description:
Beginnings matter. Whether someone is starting their career or joining a new company, their early experiences shape how quickly they find their footing and how far they can go. A great beginning gives people the context, skills, and confidence to do their best work.

As our Emerging Talent Onboarding Program Manager, you’ll own that moment for nearly everyone who joins Mercury, across new hire onboarding, internships, and a new apprenticeship program. You’ll think as deeply about the experience people have as the systems behind the scenes that make it all work, and you’ll be a visible face of Mercury when people need support most. You’ll build programs that feel distinctly Mercury, using AI and your creativity to rethink how they work from the ground up.

*Mercury is a financial technology company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

Here are some things you’ll do on the job:
• Run new hire onboarding. Own the program end to end: the learning arc, facilitator coordination, cohort communications, and feedback. Partner with People Operations on preboarding so the experience starts before day one and every new hire’s first weeks feel useful and welcoming.
• Launch our new apprenticeship program. Design and own program operations and the apprentice

experience:

cohort programming, exec exposure, check-ins at each rotation, and partnerships with host teams.
• Strengthen our internship program. Build on what teams already run with a shared company-wide experience for interns, including onboarding, community, regular check-ins, and a clear point of contact.
• Support managers and mentors. Give the people hosting new hires, interns, and apprentices clear expectations and the resources to do it well.
• Build the systems behind the programs. Use AI, automation, and tooling to reimagine what each program can do, keep quality high as hiring grows, and adapt as the technology evolves. Use feedback and data to see what’s working and improve it.
• Tell the story of emerging talent. Partner with Recruiting, People Operations, and leaders across Mercury to show how we invest in people early in their careers.

You should:
• Have 3–5 years of experience building and running programs, ideally in Learning Development, People programs, early-career talent, or onboarding.
• Be an excellent program manager. You turn ideas into plans, keep many moving pieces organized, and follow through from launch to iteration.
• Be a skilled facilitator. You’ve led sessions or trainings and can turn what people need to know into something they learn.
• Be hands-on with AI. You experiment with new tools, know when they help, and use them to rethink what our programs can do.
• Think in systems. You spot themes across pain points, trace them back to how the program is designed, and solve them systematically.
• Be creative and comfortable with ambiguity. Some programs are established, some are new, and you’re energized by figuring out what fits Mercury.
• Be a clear, warm communicator. You can welcome someone on day one, run a room, and write a crisp message. You own the details, ask good questions, and stay open to changing your mind.

Experience with early-career, university, internship, apprenticeship, or employee onboarding programs is a strong plus.

Location and on-site expectations

jobs.title: Group Creative Director - Brand Narrative
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
In 1977, Charles and Ray Eames began a film with a picnic beside Chicago’s lakefront. Over the next nine minutes, Powers of Ten traveled out toward distant galaxies and back into the microscopic world inside a human hand. An enormous subject became a journey you could follow, built around a simple change in perspective. Images, language, movement, and sound brought the idea to life together. 

That’s the kind of creative thinking we’re looking for at Mercury: finding a compelling idea inside something complex, then bringing together the people and crafts that make it unforgettable.

We’re looking for a Group Creative Director to build and lead Brand Narrative, a new team within Brand Creative. You’ll turn company strategy, product truths, customer insight, and cultural observations into original concepts for our most important launches, campaigns, and brand moments. You’ll originate ideas yourself and stay closely involved as they become finished work.

Your background might be in art direction, design, or copywriting. What matters is your ability to develop exceptional concepts, recognize the best idea wherever it comes from, and bring the whole creative studio together to make it real. Whatever your starting discipline, you’ll bring deep experience in film-led storytelling.

You’ll lead Brand Narrative in close creative partnership with your peers leading Brand Design and Writing. Together, you’ll shape concepts, language, and visual expression from the beginning, bringing distinct perspectives and shared ownership to the work. You’ll contribute strong ideas of your own, invite others to challenge and improve them, and build on theirs. This is a role for someone who enjoys making work together, not developing ideas in isolation and handing them off.

You’ll also shape what Brand Narrative becomes. That means building its culture, developing its people, and establishing ways of working that make the entire studio more creatively ambitious. The opportunity is to make great work while building a team that can keep making it.

What you’ll do

In your first year, your focus will be roughly 70% leading creative development for our highest-priority launches and campaigns, and 30% building the Brand Narrative function.
• Originate and lead big creative ideas. Partner with Product Marketing and Brand Marketing on the brief, then turn the agreed audience, opportunity, and product proof into original creative concepts. Develop ideas that can take distinctive forms across film, social, out-of-home, digital, experiences, and partnerships.
• Bring ambitious concepts to life with your creative peers and the full studio. Work side by side with the Brand Design and Writing leads and their teams from the earliest explorations through delivery. Develop ideas together, exchange thoughtful critique, and make creative choices that draw on each discipline’s expertise. Stay hands-on, contribute through your own craft, and partner closely with Motion and Production throughout. For film, remain closely involved through scripts, visual development, production, and the final edit.
• Build audience and distribution thinking into the idea. Shape concepts around how people will discover, watch, and share the work. Work with marketing partners to consider channels and viewing contexts from the beginning, so the work belongs where people encounter it rather than simply being resized to fit.
• Push beyond the first good answer, and learn quickly. Lead thoughtful concept development and critique. Use rough scripts, prototypes, and AI tools to test ideas quickly, learn, and move the strongest work forward. Know when to keep exploring and when to commit, then protect what makes an idea interesting through feedback and production.
• Find opportunities before a brief arrives. Bring curiosity about Mercury’s products, customers, and the wider world. Develop proactive ideas and cultural opportunities that give the brand something meaningful to say or do.
• Help decide where creative ambition matters most. Partner early with Product Marketing, Brand Marketing, Product Design, Comms, and Insights. Help identify which moments deserve our largest creative investment, present recommendations to senior leadership, and use results from marketing and insights partners to inform what comes next.
• Build and lead Brand Narrative. Define the team’s purpose, priorities, creative standards, and ways of working. Help hire and develop the team, shaping its structure and capabilities. Set clear expectations, and coach people to grow their judgment and conceptual strength.
• Create a culture where the best idea wins. Make room for experimentation, honest feedback, and contributions across disciplines. Lead with generosity and conviction, share ownership of the work, and help people challenge one another without making creativity a competition for credit.
• Build practices that strengthen the work. Establish a clear path from insight and an agreed brief to concept and execution, with useful critique and close collaboration throughout. Develop relationships with external creatives and agencies who can add a distinctive perspective or capability when needed.

What you’ll bring
• A strong creative foundation in art direction, design, or copywriting. Your portfolio shows original concepts developed into ambitious, well-crafted work across multiple formats. You can explain what you contributed, how the idea evolved, and how collaboration made it better.
• Deep film experience. You’ve developed film-led ideas from concept through production, with strong instincts for story, scripts, performance, pacing, and sound. You understand how these choices work together to make an audience feel something, not just make a film look good.
• A track record of deep creative collaboration with design and writing peers. You’ve led ambitious multidisciplinary work from concept through production by building trusted partnerships. You bring a clear point of view, listen closely, work through creative disagreements constructively, and recognize when someone else’s approach makes the work stronger. You can show how your collaborators shaped the outcome, not just what you personally originated.
• Strong taste, cultural awareness, and product curiosity. You can get close to a complex business or product, find the human truth within it, and turn that understanding into something clear, surprising, and memorable.
• Experience developing creative people and shaping how a team works. You give specific, useful feedback, set a high bar with care, and create an environment where people can take creative risks. You’re excited to build a new function, including the everyday practices that give it a culture.
• Clear communication and sound judgment. You can rally people around an ambitious concept, explain why it deserves investment, and navigate competing perspectives without losing the idea. You take ownership in ambiguous situations and balance creative ambition with the need to move work forward.

What success looks like

A year in, you’ll have led major launches and film-led campaigns from original concept through finished work, with Brand Design and Writing as creative partners from the beginning. The studio’s disciplines will have shaped the work together, with audience and distribution informing the creative approach.

Brand Narrative will have a clear identity, shared creative standards, and working practices that help people test and develop stronger ideas together. Alongside planned launches, you’ll have established a pipeline of proactive opportunities that gives Mercury more ways to express its product ambition with originality and cultural relevance.

Please include a portfolio featuring film-led work and broader campaign concepts. We’d love to understand your role in developing the ideas, the choices you made through production, and how you brought the work to life with others.

jobs.description:
Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.

OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps).
