jobs.title: Senior II/Lead Software Engineer - Global KYC and Onboarding
jobs.description:
We are the Global KYC and Onboarding squad in the Servicing department and we have a mission: to enable teams at Wise to expand and fine-tune the business in a "config change" manner all across the globe, while remaining compliant and safe for the customers. There are three teams in the squad: Business Onboarding Verification, Personal Onboarding Verification and Wise Platform Verification (our B2B platform).

 

The scale we operate at: In FY2025, 15.6 million people and businesses used Wise, we onboarded over 5.9 million new customers (~500k/month), and moved £145.2bn across borders (~£400m/day) across 160+ countries and 40+ currencies. Our verification systems aren't supporting tools — they're core production infrastructure that protects customers, enables growth, and must stay reliable under constant change in regulations, policies, and evolving threat patterns.

 

 All of the teams are diverse, cross-functional groups passionate about solving complex problems with elegant solutions. We bring together backend and frontend engineers, mobile developers, designers, data analysts, and product managers who collaborate closely to deliver exceptional customer experiences. Our teams are responsible for the critical verification journeys that business and personal customers complete before using Wise's products. We own the entire verification lifecycle – from document collection flows and automated review systems to agent tooling and compliance monitoring. We operate with high ownership in a bottom-up, transparent culture, make data-driven decisions, and celebrate both technical excellence and customer impact. Right now we're focused on building KYC/FinCrime as a configuration-driven product, refactoring and building new scalable microservice systems, and increasing automation using ML/AI where it genuinely improves decisioning, review quality, and operational efficiency — with safe fallbacks and clear observability. 

As IC4, you'll shape architecture across the squad's services, lead the technical direction on initiatives like the configuration-driven KYC platform, and raise the engineering bar through mentorship and cross-team influence. As a team that touches both regulatory requirements and customer experience, we have unique opportunities to innovate in a space traditionally resistant to change.

 

By joining one of our teams, you'll directly impact these customers by transforming a traditionally frustrating experience into one that's fast, intuitive, and fair. Your code will help individuals and small businesses access global banking faster, enable entrepreneurs to pay international employees on time, and allow people like you and your teammates support their families across borders without friction. We're not just building verification systems – we're removing barriers that stand between our customers and their financial freedom.

We need like-minded engineers in all the teams in the squad, so we'll use the interview process to discover where your unique skills shine brightest. Ultimately, we want to match you with the team that perfectly aligns with your experience and sets you up for success!

jobs.title: Senior Analytics Manager - Compliance
jobs.description:
We are looking for a Senior Analytics Manager to lead the EMEA Compliance Analytics branch of the Compliance & Internal Audit Analytics team at Wise.

You’ll partner with 2nd line Compliance in Europe, the UK and MEA to ensure they can execute against the Compliance regulatory reporting schedule, as well as leveraging data to proactively monitor risks. You’ll lead a team of 3-4 analysts, so your time will be split between hands-on work (40%) and leadership responsibilities (60%).

The Compliance Analytics team supports Compliance by using analytics to provide more coverage, efficiency and accuracy to testing and monitoring, as well as building innovative tools and using automation to support regulatory reporting and other Compliance activities.

This is an AL2 role. For more information on our Analytics Career Map and levelling structure, click here.

WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING
• Partnering with stakeholders across the Compliance function covering all regions, products and domains of the business (including Financial Crime, Ops, Risk, Finance and IT)
• Taking ownership of the engagement model between analytics and Compliance for delivering regulatory reporting and moving towards building automated pipelines for recurring reports
• Identifying & implementing opportunities to do the most impactful analytics within testing projects and influencing and upskilling your partners in Compliance to do the same
• Defining and tracking KPIs to measure the team’s success and impact
• Championing innovation and data-driven insights across all Compliance activities where analytics can add value
• Leading automation and tooling projects to increase efficiency across Compliance

jobs.title: Privacy and AI Counsel
jobs.description:
As a valued member of our group privacy team, based in London, you will provide legal advice and guidance on privacy matters, ensuring compliance with relevant laws and regulations.

Reporting to the UK & EMEA privacy lead you will work with various business units and stakeholders to ensure privacy is embedded in new initiatives and projects, including several AI projects.

Our group privacy team is part of the legal tribe and works with other privacy and data protection stakeholders at Wise, including engineering teams, risk, operations and the business teams that develop and manage financial products and services.

jobs.title: Finance Systems Change Programme Lead
jobs.description:
The role

Wise is investing significantly in its finance systems, processes and controls to support the next stage of growth as a dual-listed global technology company.

We are looking for an experienced Finance Systems Change Programme Lead to establish, mobilise and lead our Finance Systems Change programme.

This role will be responsible for creating the structure, governance and delivery model required to successfully execute a multi-year finance systems change agenda, including finance systems modernisation, ERP transformation, finance data architecture, process standardisation and control automation.

Working across Finance, Product, Engineering, Data and external partners, the Programme Lead will ensure that strategic objectives are translated into an executable programme with clear ownership, governance and measurable outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Programme Mobilisation & Governance
• Establish and lead the Finance Systems Change Programme.
• Define programme governance, workstreams, decision forums and reporting structures.
• Create and manage executive reporting for Steering Committees, Finance Leadership and other stakeholders
• Ensure alignment across Finance, Product, Engineering, Data and Controls functions.

Change Delivery
• Coordinate delivery across multiple change workstreams including:
• ERP transformation
• Finance systems modernisation
• Finance data architecture
• Reporting transformation
• Process standardisation
• Control automation
• AI usage
• Drive execution against agreed milestones, timelines and budgets.
• Manage interdependencies across programmes including SOX remediation, data initiatives and operational change programmes.

Vendor & Implementation Management
• Lead programme mobilisation activities for ERP and finance systems implementation.
• Support RFP processes, vendor selection and implementation planning.
• Manage relationships with implementation partners, system integrators and external advisors.
• Ensure vendors deliver against agreed outcomes and programme objectives.

Business Change & Adoption
• Partner with Finance leaders to prepare the organisation for large-scale systems change.
• Coordinate change management, communications and stakeholder engagement activities.
• Ensure business readiness for new systems, processes and operating models.
• Drive adoption and benefit realisation across Finance teams.

Programme Planning & Risk Management
• Develop programme plans and take active role in resource modeling and operating budgets.
• Identify delivery risks, dependencies and mitigation plans.
• Track programme outcomes against agreed success measures.
• Escalate critical issues and decision points to executive leadership.
• Support recruitment and mobilisation of specialist finance systems, ERP, data and change resources.

Candidate Profile

Experience
• 10+ years leading large-scale finance transformation programmes.
• Proven experience delivering ERP or major finance systems implementations.
• Experience managing complex, multi-workstream transformation programmes.
• Experience working with executive stakeholders including CFOs, Finance Directors and Engineering leaders.
• Experience working with system integrators, consulting partners and software vendors.

Leadership
• Exceptional stakeholder management and influencing skills.
• Ability to align diverse stakeholder groups around a common vision.
• Strong communication and executive presentation skills.
• Comfortable operating in ambiguity and building structure where none exists.

Transformation Expertise
• Deep understanding of finance transformation programmes.
• Strong knowledge of programme governance and delivery frameworks.
• Experience building business cases and transformation roadmaps.
• Experience managing organisational change and adoption.

jobs.title: Influencer Senior Manager (NorthAm)
jobs.description:
We are looking for an ambitious and commercially minded Senior Manager to lead Wise’s influencer strategy across North America. Based in our Austin office alongside the North American regional team, you will report to the Global Influencer Team in London and connect global strategy with strong regional execution.

You will be accountable for the overall direction and performance of the North American influencer channel. Your remit will span three core priorities: owning the overarching strategy for North America, supporting our US Influencer Manager; directly leading and scaling our influencer activity in Canada; and developing our influencer strategy for Wise Business.

Responsibilities

North America Strategy and Leadership
• Own the North American influencer strategy, setting clear priorities across the US and Canada.
• Build annual and quarterly plans covering audiences, creators, channels and investment.
• Own regional forecasting and budget recommendations, using performance insights to scale opportunities, improve efficiency and redirect investment.
• Represent influencer marketing in regional planning and bring North American insights into our global strategy.

Market Growth
• Directly own and scale Wise’s influencer strategy in Canada, from market planning and creator identification through to execution and optimisation.
• Support the existing US Influencer Manager with strategic direction and opportunity sizing while they retain ownership of market execution.
• Build a locally relevant Canadian programme and test new propositions, formats and partnerships to define the market’s long-term growth roadmap.
• Ensure all North American influencer activity follows applicable regulatory, disclosure, brand-safety and procurement requirements.
• Manage senior relationships with relevant agencies, creator partners, platforms and tools to improve programme quality and scale.

Wise Business Influencer Strategy
• Develop and lead the global influencer strategy for Wise Business, beginning in North America and defining the role creators can play in reaching and converting business customers.
• Identify priority audiences and creator segments, and partner with the Wise Business team on positioning and messaging.
• Run structured tests to determine which creators, messages, formats and commercial models drive qualified customers, using the results to build a scalable roadmap.

jobs.title: Global Complaints Senior Lead
jobs.description:
As the Global Complaints Senior Lead, you will oversee the resolution of customer complaints on a global scale, ensuring fairness, regulatory compliance, and a better experience for our users. In this senior role, you will drive the overarching complaints strategy, address systemic issues, and empower a geographically dispersed leadership team.

Key Responsibilities
• Strategy & Leadership: Define long-term domain strategies, support the Head of Complaints, and lead high-impact, cross-functional projects that aligns with Wise’s broader business objectives and improves operational efficiency.
• Team & Capacity Building: Mentor team leads (across multiple geographies) to build independent, highly capable teams while managing global staffing, skills, and training requirements.
• Risk & Compliance: Foster a risk-aware culture, ensuring operations comply with diverse regional regulations while prioritizing customer fairness. Identify and address systemic root causes of complaints to mitigate risk and enhance customer trust.
• Operations & Financials: Oversee resource allocation and budgets, optimize team performance, evolve KPIs, and uphold rigorous QA in reporting and auditing.
• Cross-Functional Stakeholder Collaboration: Partner with Product, PR, Finance, and Risk to share critical insights and drive organizational decision-making. Build strong relationships with internal teams and external arbitration/regulatory bodies to resolve issues and leverage regional insights.
• Continuous Improvement: Leverage data and root cause analysis to identify complaint trends, collaborating across teams to resolve underlying issues and reduce future complaints.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Java - AML Handling
jobs.description:
The team you will join: AML Handling within the AML Squad in the FinCrime Chapter

 

Why this team exists

 

Regulatory expectations demand that we review more users, monitor additional typologies, and continuously elevate decision quality each year. Without technical leverage, our AML Investigations unit would keep growing - an expensive route that makes maintaining high quality difficult.

 

The AML Handling team exists to scale operational growth maintaining high quality. We craft back-office tooling that enables agents to work in a unified space, enhance their daily workflow with Artificial Intelligence, and automatically resolve high-confidence cases. 

 

What will you be working on? 

AML Handling team is looking for an experienced Product Engineer to help us build the tools and systems that enable Wise to investigate and resolve financial crime cases effectively. In AML Handling, we improve how operational teams work, using automation and AI to support better decisions, reduce manual effort, and minimise unnecessary friction for customers.

 

What will you be doing?
• Design and build scalable systems for AML case handling and investigation workflows.
• Own substantial technical initiatives end to end, from understanding the problem and shaping the technical approach to delivery and operation in production.
• Partner with Product, Operations, Data Scientists, and Data Analysts to identify opportunities, shape product decisions, and measure the impact of your work.
• Build automation and bring AI capabilities into production, with attention to quality, evaluation, traceability, and appropriate human oversight.
• Improve reliability, security, and technical quality through thoughtful system design, testing, code reviews, and knowledge sharing.

 

The technology you’ll work with

Our primary technology stack is Java, Spring Boot, and Kafka, with SQL databases. You’ll work with distributed services, asynchronous processing, and data at scale.

We design for scalability, observability, privacy, security, reliability, and cost.

jobs.title: Safeguarding Controller - APAC
jobs.description:
Job Description

Working alongside an existing team of Safeguarding specialists and reporting to the Global Safeguarding Accountable Owner, your role is to assist each of the existing controllers and product managers in ensuring the APAC safeguarding control framework runs smoothly. The role will span across both safeguarding for payments and e-money and investment business and offers a fantastic opportunity to learn about the handovers between the regimes. You will also be joining at an exciting time of product growth and expansion..

Your Mission
• You will play a crucial role in ensuring that new product launches are compliant with safeguarding regulations and controlled in a proportionate manner
• You will be responsible for ensuring completeness of our policies and procedures and coordinate with individual controllers to obtain attestations of the controls operation and alignment to the controls framework
• You will be responsible for coordinating and implementing a first line of defence assurance for APAC safeguarding controls
• You will be responsible for maintaining the APAC safeguarding risk and controls matrix for the APAC entities
• You will be the first point of escalation of discrepancies identified by the Reconciliations team for safeguarding reconciliations and provide SME advise on their resolution and treatment
• You will be involved in the incidents management process and link incidents to control failures, which will enable senior management to see themes within the control environment
• You will be responsible for MAS regulatory reporting and other safeguarding regulatory reporting preparation
• You will be responsible for the annual safeguarding audit coordination
• You will help document, challenge and build an end-to-end view of our internal control environment to illustrate key risks, controls and processes. This will all be done within our internal risk management software

Opportunities
• Own your own path of success - You’ll have a high level of autonomy and responsibility.
• Grow with the role - You will have the exposure and opportunity to speak to key senior members of the organisation getting into the details of remediation steps. You will be able to develop your technical skills and knowledge by being involved in several change management programmes relating to regulatory uplifts across different territories as well as related to implementing new products or features working with our engineering team to ensure these are safeguarding compliant.
• Stepping stone - This role provides an excellent platform for someone looking to step into the safeguarding function of a fast-growing Fintech.
• Develop an in-depth knowledge of Wise’s business - Get to know many teams across the business as you partner with them as part of day-to-day activities.

jobs.title: Associate, Transaction Monitoring
jobs.description:
YouTrip is the leading and fastest-growing multi-currency payment platform in Asia Pacific. In 2018, we pioneered the region's first multi-currency digital wallet. Now, YouTrip is the #1 multi-currency digital wallet trusted by millions across the region, processing over US$15 billion in total payment value annually. 

Our consumer and business propositions – YouTrip and YouBiz – empower individuals and businesses with inclusive, accessible, and affordable financial solutions. YouTrip has raised over US$110 million to date, including its recent Series B round led by global venture capital firm Lightspeed Venture Partners—underscoring strong investor confidence in its mission to transform digital financial services across the Asia Pacific. 

Recognised as World Economic Forum’s Global Innovator 2025, CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies (2025, 2024), and LinkedIn’s Top Startup (2024, 2023), YouTrip is dedicated to creating the next generation of digital finance services for consumers and businesses.

Valuing an entrepreneurial culture of diversity and inclusion, we are seeking driven individuals to join our fast-growing regional team as we push the boundaries of innovative fintech solutions. 

You Will
• Conduct end-to-end transaction investigations from the detection of unusual activities, to the analysis and documentation and submission of Suspicious Matter Reports (“SMR”) for lodgment to the relevant authorities.
• Have a strong knowledge of AML/CTF, KYC, Sanctions and apply a broader financial crime lens to assess and mitigate the relevant risks
• Review and assess alerts generated by our transaction monitoring and screening systems. Require a good level of analytical skill to detect unusual or suspicious transactions and escalate potential hits. Analysts may also be required to send requests for further information from customers.
• Analyse transaction data to identify trends & patterns in transactions that may signify suspicious or fraudulent activities, using data and transaction monitoring tools.
• Collaborate with other key business functions to ensure a smooth end-to-end internal process to achieve customer satisfaction and safeguard the company’s and users’ interests.
• Perform any other ad-hoc legal/compliance duties.

You Are
• Compliance & Risk enthusiast – you have racked up at least 2 - 3 years of experience in a Financial Crime, AML/CTF or Fraud Risk role, ideally within the financial services or payment industry. Relevant knowledge on payments-related regulations in Malaysia will be a plus.
• Analytical & detail-oriented thinker – you possess excellent problem-solving skills with demonstrated experience in solving complex business problems with analytical thinking. You have the natural tendency to always focus on details and hate to miss out on specifics.
• Travel enthusiast – you are a passionate traveller and understand the psychology of travellers, in particular when it comes to overseas spending behaviour and its associated risks.
• Fearless self-starter – you are not afraid to suggest and implement new initiatives to tackle complex business issues, as long as the rationale is logical and sound. You do not mind getting your hands dirty in order to get things done on a tight timeline.

jobs.title: SOC Analyst, Security Operations
jobs.description:
Who we are 

We simplify wealth creation. Founded in 2014 in Vienna, Austria by Eric Demuth, Paul Klanschek and Christian Trummer, we’re here to help people trust themselves enough to build their financial freedom — for now and the future. Our user-friendly, trade-everything platform empowers both first-time investors and seasoned experts to invest in the cryptocurrencies, crypto indices, stocks*, precious metals and commodities* they want — with any sized budget, 24/7. Our global team works across different cultures and time zones, bringing our products to more than 7 million customers, making us one of Europe’s safest and most secure platforms that powers modern investing.

 

Headquartered in Austria but operating across Europe, our products are built by fast-moving, talented, “roll-up-your-sleeves-and-make-it-happen” kind of people. It’s these diverse perspectives and innovative minds operating as ONE TEAM that keep Bitpanda at the cutting edge of our industry. So if you’re someone who thinks big, moves fast and wants to make an impact right from day one, then get ready to join our industry-changing team. Let’s go!

 

Your mission

Security is fundamental to the trust millions of customers place in Bitpanda every day. As an Cyber Security Engineer, you'll help protect our platform by detecting threats, responding to incidents and continuously improving the security of our cloud-native environment. Working alongside experienced security engineers, you'll build detections, automate repetitive tasks and investigate security events that help keep our infrastructure, applications and customers safe.

What you'll do
• Build and improve detections. Develop, test and tune detection rules in Elastic Security (ES|QL/KQL), helping improve detection coverage, reduce false positives and ensure meaningful threats are identified quickly.
• Investigate security events and hunt for threats. Respond to security alerts, participate in incident response, perform proactive threat hunting across AWS, Elastic and Datadog, and contribute to improving investigation and response processes.
• Automate security operations. Build scripts, API integrations and SOAR workflows that reduce manual effort, improve investigation quality and help the Security team operate more efficiently.
• Help secure our cloud platform. Monitor AWS security events, investigate suspicious activity, contribute to system hardening and security tooling improvements, and support initiatives that strengthen Bitpanda's overall security posture.
• Contribute to a strong security culture. Work closely with engineers across the business, support compliance activities including ISO 27001, PCI DSS and DORA, and help promote security best practices throughout the organisation.
• Keep millions of users safe, no matter the time of day. As part of this commitment, you'll participate in a weekly rotating on-call schedule alongside the rest of the team.

Who you are
• You have 2–4 years of experience in information security, security engineering or security operations, with exposure to incident response, SIEM, threat hunting or cloud security.
• You enjoy solving technical security problems and have experience writing scripts or automating workflows using APIs or security tooling.
• You have a solid understanding of AWS or another major cloud platform, networking fundamentals, system hardening and security monitoring. Experience with Elastic Security, ES|QL or KQL is a big plus!
• You're curious, proactive and eager to learn, taking ownership of your work while seeking opportunities to improve both security and operational efficiency.
• You're passionate about keeping millions of users safe, no matter the time of day; This role has on call responsibilities that rotate through the team on a weekly basis.

What’s in it for you
• Flexibility to work where you thrive – Enjoy the freedom of our Hybrid working model, combining onsite collaboration and remote work, with an additional 25 days per year to work from a city or country of your choice.
• Reward for your impact – Receive a competitive total compensation package aligned with Bitpanda’s pay-for-impact policy, including participation in our stock option plan.
• Support for your mental wellbeing – Access confidential coaching, counselling, and mental health resources whenever you need them through OpenUP.
• Time to recharge – On top of your standard annual leave, prioritise your wellbeing in 2027 with 3 additional days of paid time off to rest, reset, and recharge, available once you’ve been with us for 6 months.
• Continuous learning and growth – Grow your skills and stay ahead in your career with unlimited access to Udemy’s library of online courses at your own pace.
• Exclusive perks and rewards – Enjoy discounts, rewards, and perks from partners worldwide across lifestyle, wellness, tech, and travel.
• Support during life milestones – Take advantage of up to 8 additional weeks of gender-neutral new parent leave to welcome and bond with your new addition to the family.
• Fuel and focus on-site – Pandas in Vienna, Bucharest, Barcelona, and Berlin can enjoy free onsite dining, with freshly prepared lunches and snacks to keep you fueled and focused all day long.
• Recognition for your contributions – Celebrate milestones and achievements with recognition and rewards for your Tenure at Bitpanda.
• Show your Bitpanda pride – Access exclusive Bitpanda-branded merchandise and gear to represent.
• Connect and celebrate with your team – Join unforgettable company events, from our Winter Party in Vienna to gatherings worldwide, fostering fun, connection, and celebration

 .…and even more location-specific benefits designed to make life at Bitpanda even more rewarding wherever you are.

 

Above all, you will have the opportunity to learn and grow as part of Bitpanda’s incredible journey towards being Europe’s future #1 investment platform.

Bitpanda is committed to fostering a fair and equal environment based on trust and mutual respect. We believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace is paramount to our success and we are committed to building a team that represents a wide variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills.

* These benefits may be adjusted at Bitpanda’s discretion and do not apply to our internships and exceptions to our Hybrid Working policy apply to teams with shift schedules or for folks whose roles require them to be in-office (think: Workplaces team or IT).

jobs.title: Data Scientist II, Applied ML
jobs.description:
Why join us

Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Tens of thousands of the world's best companies run on Brex, including DoorDash, Coinbase, Robinhood, Zoom, Plaid, Reddit, and SeatGeek.

Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We’re committed to building a diverse team and inclusive culture and believe your potential should only be limited by how big you can dream. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

Data at Brex

The Data organization develops infrastructure, statistical models, and products using financial data. Our Scientists and Engineers work together to make data —and insights derived from data — a core asset across the company. Our work is ingrained in Brex’s decision-making process, in the efficiency of our operations, in our risk management policies, and in the second-to-none experience we provide our consumers.

What You’ll Do

Our Data Scientists are responsible for the entire model development lifecycle, from conception with stakeholders, through model development and productionization, to following through to see that the desired business impact is achieved — including circling back with stakeholders to make product or strategic decisions.

Responsibilities
• Drive Data AI solutions from inception to deployment to efficiently manage risk and/or improve customer experience.
• Be responsible for the full machine learning lifecycle — problem identification, model design, training, productionization, and monitoring.
• Partner with cross-functional teams (Ops, Engineering, Product, Fraud, Compliance, and Credit).

Requirements
• 3+ years of experience in Data Science/ML roles, or 2+ years with a PhD in a quantitative field
• Demonstrated ability to own end-to-end model development, including productionization
• Expertise in Python programming, SQL queries, and ML-related frameworks
• Ability to apply statistical techniques such as hypothesis testing and A/B testing, and to approach problems with a statistical mindset
• Strong software engineering fundamentals, including experience with API development and integrating ML systems into production services
• Strong communication skills and the ability to collaborate with various stakeholders, both technical and non-technical

Nice to Have
• Experience working with real-time models
• Advanced degree (MSc/PhD) or published research in Machine Learning or a related field
• Previous experience in the risk domain (fraud, AML, and/or credit) or building customer-facing ML models (suggestions/automations)
• Experience in the fintech industry

Compensation

The expected salary range for this role is $152,000 - $190,000 + equity. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. 

Brex LLC is a wholly owned subsidiary of Capital One, N.A.

Please be aware, job-seekers may be at risk of targeting by malicious actors looking for personal data. Brex recruiters will only reach out via LinkedIn or email with a brex.com domain. Any outreach claiming to be from Brex via other sources should be ignored.

jobs.description:
Why join us

Engineering at Brex

Engineering at Brex is about building systems that scale with speed and intention. Our teams operate with high autonomy and deep collaboration, own outcomes end to end, and push for excellence from architecture to deployment. It’s an environment where engineering is a craft and builders grow by solving meaningful technical problems.

What you’ll do

The Identity and Access Management team builds and maintains secure, user-friendly authentication and authorization systems that protect users, safeguard company assets, and provide a seamless access experience for developers. The team owns critical platform capabilities including login methods, step-up authentication, our custom authorization platform, account delegation flows like Copilot, Pro Access login, embedded partnerships authentication, and core vendor integrations.

As a Staff Engineer on IAM, you will lead projects and initiatives to improve the security, reliability, and developer experience of our authentication, authorization, and identity platforms for customers, partners, and internal systems. You will scope and drive projects with clear impact, work cross-functionally with the broader engineering organization, help define the team’s technical quality, and help evolve the identity platform as Brex invests in signed identity propagation, delegated and agent identity, fine-grained authorization, stronger auditability, and enterprise-ready customer authentication experiences.

Where you’ll work

This role will be based in our San Francisco office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. We currently require Monday, Wednesday and Thursday to be designated in office days. As a perk, we also have up to four weeks per year of fully remote work!

Responsibilities
• Design, build, and operate backend systems and APIs for authentication, authorization, identity context, and audit-related workflows.
• Lead engineers across the organization on initiatives end to end, from technical design and implementation through rollout, measurement, and operational support.
• Improve login and access experiences across SSO, MFA, step-up authentication, delegated access, and enterprise identity flows.
• Build and extend authorization systems that support custom roles, resource-aware access control, and secure defaults for product teams.
• Lead creation of durable, identity-aware audit trails and attribution for user, service, delegated, and agent-driven actions.
• Partner closely with engineers across Brex to make IAM integrations secure by default and easier to adopt through clear patterns, tooling, and shared libraries.
• Mentor engineers on the team to deliver high-quality code and produce operational improvements that raise the bar for reliability and maintainability across the team’s systems.

Requirements
• You have strong software engineering fundamentals and experience building reliable production backend systems.
• You have experience leading complex projects and mentoring other engineers.
• You have strong API design fundamentals, rigor around testing, code quality, and documentation.
• You understand core IAM concepts such as authentication, authorization, sessions, tokens, MFA, SSO, OAuth, SAML, OIDC, or RBAC.
• You communicate clearly, collaborate well across teams, and are effective in cross-functional technical discussions.
• You care about operational excellence and know how to improve system reliability, reduce toil, and maintain high-quality services over time.
• You have strong product and engineering judgment and can balance security, usability, and developer experience.

Bonus points
• You have worked on identity and access management, authentication, authorization, or audit systems in a production environment.
• You have hands-on experience with Okta, Oso, SSO, SAML, OIDC, OAuth, or WebAuthn.
• You have experience building enterprise-facing admin controls, authorization platforms, delegated access flows, or audit trails.
• You have worked on platform teams that provide shared infrastructure, paved roads, or secure-by-default frameworks for other engineering teams.

Compensation:

The expected salary range for this role is $240,000 - $300,000. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors, including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package.

This role will be based in our Seattle office. We are a hybrid environment that combines the energy and connections of being in the office with the benefits and flexibility of working from home. Responsibilities
• Design, build, and operate backend systems and APIs for authentication, authorization, identity context, and audit-related workflows.
• Lead engineers across the organization on initiatives end to end, from technical design and implementation through rollout, measurement, and operational support.

• Build and extend authorization systems that support custom roles, resource-aware access control, and secure defaults for product teams.
• Lead creation of durable, identity-aware audit trails and attribution for user, service, delegated, and agent-driven actions.
• Partner closely with engineers across Brex to make IAM integrations secure by default and easier to adopt through clear patterns, tooling, and shared libraries.

Requirements
• You have strong software engineering fundamentals and experience building reliable production backend systems.
• You have experience leading complex projects and mentoring other engineers.
• You have strong API design fundamentals, rigor around testing, code quality, and documentation.
• You understand core IAM concepts such as authentication, authorization, sessions, tokens, MFA, SSO, OAuth, SAML, OIDC, or RBAC.
• You communicate clearly, collaborate well across teams, and are effective in cross-functional technical discussions.
• You care about operational excellence and know how to improve system reliability, reduce toil, and maintain high-quality services over time.
• You have strong product and engineering judgment and can balance security, usability, and developer experience.

Bonus points
• You have worked on identity and access management, authentication, authorization, or audit systems in a production environment.
• You have hands-on experience with Okta, Oso, SSO, SAML, OIDC, OAuth, or WebAuthn.
• You have experience building enterprise-facing admin controls, authorization platforms, delegated access flows, or audit trails.
• You have worked on platform teams that provide shared infrastructure, paved roads, or secure-by-default frameworks for other engineering teams.

Compensation:

The expected salary range for this role is $240,000 - $300,000. However, the starting base pay will depend on a number of factors, including the candidate’s location, skills, experience, market demands, and internal pay parity. Depending on the position offered, equity and other forms of compensation may be provided as part of a total compensation package.

jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer, Tooling (Product)
jobs.description:
About the Company

Gemini is a global crypto and Web3 platform founded by Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss in 2014, offering a wide range of simple, reliable, and secure crypto products and services to individuals and institutions in over 70 countries. Our mission is to unlock the next era of financial, creative, and personal freedom by providing trusted access to the decentralized future. We envision a world where crypto reshapes the global financial system, internet, and money to create greater choice, independence, and opportunity for all — bridging traditional finance with the emerging cryptoeconomy in a way that is more open, fair, and secure. As a publicly traded company, Gemini is poised to accelerate this vision with greater scale, reach, and impact.

The Department: Tooling

The Role:

Principal Software Engineer (Product)

As a Principal Product Engineer, you'll set technical direction for the customer-facing platform that defines how millions of users experience Gemini — onboarding, compliance, customer support, and the systems that hold the customer journey together. This is a role for an engineer who operates at the level of the technology itself: someone accountable for company-level initiatives, who drives the hardest technical challenges across organizational boundaries, and who creates the architectural vision that other teams build against. 

You'll work across backend, web, and mobile, but your leverage comes less from what you build directly than from the direction you set, the leaders you grow, and the frontier you push. We treat AI-assisted development and automation as first-class — an agentic SDLC pipeline where agents plan, implement, and review work through our harness under human gates. As a Principal, you're expected to shape where that frontier goes, define the patterns and operational guidelines other engineers adopt, and advance how the whole organization builds. If you're energized by owning ambiguous, company-critical technical bets and multiplying the engineers around you, we'd love to talk.

This role is required to be in person twice a week at our New York City, NY office.

Responsibilities:
• Own the technical vision and architecture for the customer-facing platform, designing for scale and reliability with a multi-year horizon and anticipating needs before they arrive.
• Review critical designs across organizations and drive the designs for projects involving the hardest technical challenges at the company; act as a key driver of demos and technical direction beyond your own team.
• Be accountable for one or more core company initiatives spanning onboarding, compliance (KYC/identity), and customer support — carrying them from ambiguity through production and long-term operation.
• Identify strategic direction in technology and product, proposing and adopting architecture and platform approaches that advance it; tie technical bets clearly to company objectives.
• Plan and deliver large, complex, cross-org programs with interdependencies across teams and systems, spanning months to years; identify the problems worth solving and advocate for their prioritization.
• Define patterns, operational guidelines, and engineering practices for your vertical(s), and extend process improvements across teams and command pilot units.
• Provide critical technical guidance proactively — raising the security, reliability, and quality bar across the organization, and debugging or contributing to the most complex parts of a system when needed.
• Act as a technical multiplier: mentor and develop engineers and future leaders, share knowledge, delegate to grow others, and lead initiatives across domains, including outside your core area of expertise.
• Drive the organization toward a strategic vision for strong systems, sustainable practice, and healthy engineering culture; play a critical role in recruiting and bar-raising.

Minimum

Qualifications:
• 12+ years of software engineering experience building and operating complex production systems at scale.
• Recognized expertise in one or two core technical domains, with a track record of being accountable for company-level systems or initiatives end to end.
• A history of driving architecture and design for the hardest technical challenges across multiple teams or organizations.
• Demonstrated ability to set technical vision with company-level impact and to bring an increasingly strategic mindset to engineering decisions.
• Fluency across multiple layers of the stack (backend services plus web and/or mobile) and willingness to go deep wherever a problem requires.
• Proficiency in a typed language (e.g., TypeScript, Scala, Java, Go) and comfort with JavaScript/TypeScript on web and mobile surfaces.
• Experience building consumer-facing applications with strong product and UX sensibility.
• Fluency in using AI coding tools and automation, and a point of view on how to advance an agentic development practice.
• A record of acting as a technical multiplier — developing engineers and leaders, influencing prioritization across teams, and leading cross-domain initiatives.
• Excellent communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex technical issues to diverse audiences and build alignment across organizations.

Preferred

Qualifications:
• Experience in the crypto or fintech industry, or as a user of crypto products.
• Deep experience with onboarding, identity/KYC, compliance, or customer support tooling.
• Experience architecting and operating AI agents or agentic workflows in production at scale.
• Familiarity with React/React Native and cloud/microservices architecture.
• A record of driving product and technical strategy with data and experimentation.
• Experience representing engineering externally (talks, writing) or in cross-company technical collaboration.

It Pays to Work Here

 

The compensation benefits package for this role includes:
• Competitive starting pay
• A discretionary annual bonus
• Long-term incentive in the form of a new hire equity grant
• Comprehensive health plans
• 401K with company matching
• Paid Parental Leave
• Flexible time off

Salary Range: The base salary range for this role is between $192,500 - $275,000 in the State of New York. This range is not inclusive of our discretionary bonus or equity package. When determining a candidate’s compensation, we consider a number of factors including skillset, experience, job scope, and current market data.

In the United States, we offer a hybrid work approach at our hub offices, balancing the benefits of in-person collaboration with the flexibility of remote work. Expectations may vary by location and role, so candidates are encouraged to connect with their recruiter to learn more about the specific policy for the role. Employees who do not live near one of our hubs are part of our remote workforce. All employees, however, are required to onboard in-person at one of our office locations.

At Gemini, we strive to build diverse teams that reflect the people we want to empower through our products, and we are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. jobs.title: Business Continuity Management Lead
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
About the Role

Mercury is seeking a Business Continuity Management (BCM) Lead to build and lead an enterprise-wide continuity program as we prepare to become a bank. As part of the Risk team, this leader will establish practical standards, clear accountability, and tested capabilities to maintain critical services and recover effectively from disruptions, with direct visibility to the CRO and senior leadership.

This role fills the need for a dedicated leader to coordinate BCM across the organization. The ideal candidate combines deep continuity and resilience expertise with the judgment to build a proportionate program in a fast-moving environment, working effectively with Engineering, Operations, Product, Information Security, Legal, Compliance, and business teams.

The BCM Lead will own the enterprise framework, coordination, oversight, and reporting. Business and technology owners will remain accountable for their continuity plans and recovery execution.Because this is a new program, the Lead will be hands-on in the initial build: facilitating the first round of BIAs and plans side by side with owners, running exercises, and driving identified gaps through remediation. This leader will also work closely with Engineering on technology disaster recovery and with relevant teams on incident response, crisis management, and third-party resilience.

Key Responsibilities
• Develop and implement Mercury’s enterprise BCM framework, policies, standards, governance, and operating model, with a prioritized implementation roadmap aligned to bank-launch readiness and critical services.
• Partner with business owners to identify critical services, conduct business impact analyses (customer, financial, operational, and regulatory), and map dependencies across people, processes, technology, facilities, and third parties, including single points of failure.
• Establish recovery time objectives (RTOs) and recovery point objectives (RPOs), where applicable, with business and technology owners; challenge gaps between objectives and recovery capabilities.
• Set standards for continuity plans and recovery procedures, and facilitate and support accountable owners in developing actionable plans and alternative operating arrangements.
• Coordinate business continuity with technology disaster recovery, incident response, and crisis management, with clear activation criteria, escalation paths, and communications responsibilities.
• Design and lead a risk-based exercise program, from tabletop simulations to end-to-end recovery tests, and drive lessons learned, remediation tracking, and verification that gaps are closed.
• Partner with Third-Party Risk Management and vendor owners to assess critical provider recovery capabilities, contingency arrangements, and concentration dependencies.
• Embed continuity considerations into new products, material business changes, and technology implementations.
• Establish metrics and reporting that give management and relevant committees visibility into readiness, testing outcomes, material gaps, and overdue remediation.
• Build and lead a growing BCM team, including hiring and developing analysts as the program scales over the next year.
• Deliver role-based training and promote awareness of continuity responsibilities across the organization.
• Support regulatory examinations and bank-launch readiness reviews with accurate documentation and evidence of recovery capability.

Qualifications
• 10+ years of experience in business continuity management, operational resilience, disaster recovery, or a related discipline within a fintech, financial institution, technology company, or other highly regulated environment.
• Demonstrated experience building or materially enhancing an enterprise BCM program, including governance, implementation, testing, and reporting.
• Strong skills in business impact analysis, critical-service identification, dependency mapping, and recovery objective development.
• Experience developing actionable continuity plans and leading exercises that test recovery assumptions and expose gaps.
• Sufficient technical fluency to work with Engineering on cloud services, system dependencies, data recovery, and technology disaster recovery.
• Working knowledge of third-party risk management, including assessing critical vendor recovery capabilities, contingency arrangements and concentration risk.
• Proven ability to drive cross-functional remediation through influence, with a clear view of where BCM oversight ends and business or technology ownership begins.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain readiness gaps and tradeoffs to senior leadership.
• Experience managing a team of Business Continuity analysts.

About

the role:

Mercury is looking for a Model Risk Manager to help build and operate a practical, risk-based Model Risk Management program as we continue to scale and prepare for life as a regulated bank. 

Models support an increasingly broad range of decisions across Mercury, including credit underwriting, portfolio management, fraud prevention, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational processes. This role will provide independent review and effective challenge throughout the model lifecycle while helping Mercury apply governance proportionate to the actual risk of each model.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can move comfortably between technical analysis, regulatory expectations, and business context. You will conduct model validations, challenge assumptions and limitations, improve our model inventory and monitoring practices, and work closely with teams across Risk Ops, Data, Engineering, Product, Finance, Compliance, and Internal Audit. 

Showing up as a true collaborator, advisor and partner to the business will be key as we continue to build out this function and work towards our collective goals at Mercury. You should be comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where the objective is not governance for its own sake, but helping Mercury use models safely, responsibly, and effectively.

What you’ll do:
• Perform independent validations and reviews of internally developed and third-party models across areas such as credit, fraud, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational risk.
• Evaluate each model’s methodology, assumptions, data quality and lineage, implementation, and performance through reviews and testings such as outcomes analysis, benchmarking, back-testing, and sensitivity testing scaled to its risk and materiality.
• Provide credible and constructive challenges to model developers, owners, and users while maintaining effective working relationships with 1LOD.
• Assess model risk and materiality based on a model’s inherent risk, purpose, exposure, use, and potential impact.
• Help maintain a complete and accurate model inventory, including model ownership, risk rating, dependencies, limitations, validation status, monitoring requirements, and open issues.

• Develop clear reporting on model risk, validation coverage, performance concerns, concentrations, dependencies, exceptions, and overdue remediation for management and governance committees.
• Help improve Mercury’s Model Risk Management Policy, standards, procedures, and templates.
• Use automation and analytical tools to make model inventory management, testing, monitoring, and reporting more efficient.
• Partner with Mercury’s Data and AI Governance teams to establish clear boundaries and handoffs between traditional model risk management and the governance of generative AI, agentic AI, and other analytical systems outside the formal model definition.

• High ownership, intellectual curiosity, and comfort building processes in a fast evolving environment, where priorities evolve quickly, new ad hoc requests emerge regularly, and role boundaries are intentionally broad. You can operate effectively without tightly-defined scope, find the highest-leverage work, and get it done.

In 1973 at Xerox PARC, Bob Metcalfe sketched a way for many computers to share a single wire — borrowing the throughput math from his study of Hawaii's ALOHAnet — and he and David Boggs built it and measured it until it held. Behind Ethernet was a two-person team that turned a contested idea into the measured standard now carrying almost all the world's wired traffic.

At Mercury, we’re looking to accelerate several of our AI products that our customers love like Command, CLI, and MCP. We’re building for ambitious people of all kinds, and are a company made of founders and small technical teams trying to change the world - as part of that, we’re taking open applications for founders or small technical teams (Eng+) that want to work together on building the AI products of the future. This isn't a fixed role. We expect the nature of work is changing, and small teams of people paired with AI product surface and autonomy to build can create 10x outcomes. Apply as a small team or as an individual 

Here are some things you’ll do on the job:
• Find the problem. Work close enough to customers that you spot what matters before anyone assigns it to you — then decide it's worth building.
• Build and automate the workflow end to end using Command, CLI, MCP, and the rest of our AI stack.
• Ship to customers fast — quick understanding, tight iteration, deploy.
• Measure the impact honestly, then do the next one. Kill what didn't move; double down on what did.
• Run as an autonomous team — pick the target, ship the thing, own the outcome.

You should:
• Have shipped something real - a product, a tool, a company, or an open-source project people actually use.

jobs.title: Senior Customer Support Service Delivery Program Manager
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
In 1931, electrical draftsman Harry Beck looked at London’s Underground map and saw a system that had become too complicated to understand.

The maps at the time tried to represent the city geographically. Beck realized that wasn’t what riders actually needed. What mattered was how the system connected: which lines went where, where you could transfer, and the simplest way to get from one place to another. So he redrew the network around those relationships instead. His design became the foundation for the modern Tube map and changed how people navigated London.

Mercury’s Customer Experience organization has its own increasingly complex network.

As Mercury grows, the right place for support work will keep changing. Some new or complex work may benefit from starting in an incubation team before we know how it should scale. From there, it might move into Core Support, remain specialized, transition to an outsourced partner, or become increasingly supported by AI-powered tooling. The challenge is knowing where work belongs at each stage of its lifecycle, when it’s ready to move, and how to make those transitions without compromising the customer experience.

For the first 9–12 months, a significant majority of your work will focus on our growing BPO partnership. You’ll identify opportunities to expand the work we deliver through that partnership, build the operational and financial case for doing so, align CX leadership around those recommendations, and lead approved transitions from initial scoping through stabilization.

Over time, the scope will broaden. You’ll apply the same thinking across our wider service delivery ecosystem, helping us evaluate when work should enter an incubation model, when it is ready to graduate, and whether its next home should be Core Support, a specialized team, an outsourced partner, AI-powered tooling, or another model as our capabilities evolve.

You won’t be the sole decision-maker on where work lives. Your role is to develop the recommendation: bring together the data, customer impact, operational realities, and tradeoffs; build a compelling case; and help CX leadership reach a well-informed decision. Once a direction is approved, you’ll own the program that turns it into reality.

This is a role for someone who can move fluidly between strategy and execution. You should be equally energized by building a strong argument for how our service delivery model should evolve and by working through the operational details required to make that change succeed.

In this role, you will:
• Lead high-impact programs that evolve how CX delivers support, with the first 9–12 months heavily focused on expanding and optimizing our BPO partnership.
• Identify opportunities to move work to a different service delivery model and build the case for change using customer, operational, and financial data. This could include recommending that emerging or complex work move into incubation, as well as determining when incubated work is mature enough to transition into Core Support, a specialized team, or our BPO partnership.
• Help define what makes work ready to move. Develop clear criteria for when a workflow needs incubation, when it has reached sufficient maturity and stability to graduate, and which delivery model is best positioned to own it next.
• Evaluate where AI-powered tooling could take on, augment, or reshape support work, and partner with the right teams to build a clear case for when automation creates a better customer and business outcome.
• Lead approved service delivery transitions end to end, whether work is moving into incubation, graduating from incubation, transitioning between internal teams, or moving to an outsourced partner. Own the program from initial scoping and business case through readiness, migration, ramp, stabilization, and handoff into long-term operations.
• Partner across Workforce Management, Enablement, QA, Support, and other teams to build transition plans that account for capacity, training, knowledge transfer, quality, tooling, and operational readiness.
• Define success before a transition begins and measure whether the change actually delivered the intended customer, quality, capacity, and cost outcomes.
• Establish clear readiness and stabilization criteria so transitions are judged by whether they work, not simply whether they launched on time.
• Bring structure to complex, ambiguous service delivery questions, identifying the right analysis, stakeholders, dependencies, and tradeoffs required to move from uncertainty to a clear recommendation.
• Build repeatable frameworks and approaches that make future service delivery decisions faster, clearer, and more consistent.
• Use what we learn from each transition to continuously improve how Support evaluates where work should live and how changes should be executed.

We’re looking for someone who:
• Has 6+ years of experience in strategic program management, customer experience operations, service delivery, outsourcing, support operations, or a related field.
• Has deep experience with outsourced service delivery and has personally led significant transitions of operational work into a BPO or similar partner environment.
• Understands the operational machinery behind successful BPO transitions, including workforce planning, forecasting, training, knowledge transfer, quality management, ramp planning, and stabilization.
• Can build a strong recommendation without needing to own the final decision. You know how to gather the right evidence, frame tradeoffs clearly, anticipate objections, and create alignment among senior stakeholders.
• Thinks in systems. You naturally look beyond the performance of an individual team to understand how the broader service delivery model works and where changing it could produce a better outcome.
• Is analytically rigorous and commercially minded. You’re comfortable working with operational and financial data, testing assumptions, building business cases, and making recommendations when the answer isn’t obvious.
• Exercises strong judgment in ambiguous environments. You can take a question like “Is this still the right place for this work?” and determine what evidence, tradeoffs, and perspectives are needed to answer it well.
• Can move seamlessly from recommendation to execution. You’re as comfortable developing the case for a service delivery change as you are working through the details required to make it successful.
• Influences effectively without relying on formal authority. You know how to align teams with different priorities and constraints around a shared outcome.
• Communicates complex decisions with clarity. You can explain the customer impact, operational implications, economics, and tradeoffs behind a recommendation without burying the decision in the analysis.
• Holds a high bar for outcomes, not just completion. You care whether a transition delivered what we expected and are willing to revisit assumptions when the data tells us otherwise.

The ideal candidate may also have:
• Experience designing or evolving a multi-tier customer support service delivery model.
• Experience with BPO expansions, outsourced operations, vendor launches, or team and site stand-ups.
• Experience moving work between different internal delivery models, such as from incubation to Core Support or between specialized and scaled support teams.
• Experience evaluating how automation and AI-assisted support change the economics, complexity, or appropriate placement of customer support work.
• Experience with incubation or pilot operating models, including determining when new or complex work should be isolated for learning and when it is ready to graduate into a scaled delivery environment.
• Experience using SQL, Google Sheets, or business intelligence tools to evaluate operational performance and build business cases.

In 1954, architect Eero Saarinen designed a radically modern bank branch for Irwin Union in Columbus, Indiana. The building was surrounded by trees, furnished by Herman Miller, and featured rustic brick flooring. Today, that space is a conference center, and that spirit of design-forward thinking in banking* feels all but extinct.

Mercury believes that level of care and craft in design has been lost in modern finance, and we’re building products that bring it back. Cards and credit are built on complicated systems and inherited conventions, but our customers shouldn’t have to experience that complexity. We believe thoughtful design can turn something traditionally transactional into an experience that feels simple, intuitive, and distinctly Mercury.

We’re looking for a Senior Product Designer to join our Cards Credit team. You’ll tackle complex product problems, question inherited assumptions, and shape experiences that help startups spend less time banking and more time building.

In this role, you’ll:
• Own meaningful Cards Credit product problems from initial framing through shipped experience, partnering closely with Product and Engineering to understand the problem and shape what we should build.
• Turn complicated systems, requirements, and edge cases into experiences that feel remarkably simple and intuitive.
• Work across the entire design stack, from framing problems and exploring concepts to workflows, detailed interactions, visual design, prototyping, and final implementation.
• Explore broadly and design from first principles, questioning inherited patterns and assumptions when a better answer may exist.
• Bring a high level of interaction and visual craft to the Cards Credit experience, from the structure of a workflow to the details of hierarchy, typography, motion, and state.
• Collaborate with Mercury’s Brand team on physical cards and related products, creating a cohesive experience between the objects our customers hold and the product experiences surrounding them.
• Develop a deep understanding of our customers, communicate the reasoning behind your decisions clearly, and work through tradeoffs with your partners to arrive at the strongest solution.

What you’ll bring:
• A strong portfolio of product work demonstrating exceptional product thinking, interaction design, and visual craft.
• An ability to understand complicated systems and turn them into simple, thoughtful product experiences.
• Deep curiosity about why a problem exists before deciding how to solve it, with a willingness to question assumptions and work from first principles.
• Real ambition for the work itself. You want to do the best work of your career here, and you’re energized by being surrounded by people who hold themselves to the same bar.

You don’t need a background in banking, fintech, cards, or credit. We care much more about whether you’ve demonstrated the ability to understand complicated problems and turn them into simple, thoughtful product experiences.

jobs.location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
jobs.description:
"Start where you are. Use what you have. Do what you can." – Arthur Ashe

There's a version of investment products legal work that's mostly about maintaining what already exists. Reviewing disclosures that haven't changed in years, advising on products whose architecture was set long before you arrived. This isn't that. Mercury Treasury and Mercury Invest* are in some ways still taking shape and must continually rise to the occasion to meet evolving customer needs. The regulatory frameworks are complex, the product roadmap is ambitious, and the person in this role will have a direct hand in the high quality customer experience we deliver to Mercury users.

Who we are:

Since 2019, Mercury has been on a mission to reinvent banking** for the modern age. We blend elegant design and cutting-edge technology to offer checking and savings accounts, debit cards, payment services, credit products, cash management tools, and sophisticated analytics. Everything we build reflects our belief that finance should be thoughtfully crafted, fast, transparent, and frictionless.

About the team:

Our Product Regulatory Legal team operates like the rest of Mercury: with urgency, curiosity, and a bias toward action. We embed with product teams from early ideation through launch, working alongside engineers, designers, and compliance partners to get products right. We move fast, we take ownership, and we don't wait to be asked: If something needs figuring out, we’re up to the task.

What you'll do:
• Own the investment products portfolio: Serve as the primary legal advisor for Mercury Treasury and Mercury Invest, the products through which Mercury's business and consumer customers access non-deposit investment products. You'll advise across the full product life cycle, including everything from supporting new feature development, drafting disclosures, calibrating on content for marketing and customer communications, and advising on operational matters with regulatory impacts.
• Work across the company: This role sits at the intersection of product, compliance, risk, engineering, and operations. You'll build relationships across all of these functions and bring legal perspective into conversations early; not as a checkpoint, but as a low ego, high ownership thought partner.
• Advise and support compliance: You'll work closely with Mercury's compliance team on regulatory matters affecting investment products, interpreting requirements, pressure-testing approaches, and supporting examination readiness with FINRA and the SEC.
• Flex and grow: While investment products are your home base, you'll also have opportunities to contribute across Legal on other product areas, gaining new experiences and broadening your expertise over time.
• Use AI intentionally: Bring a working knowledge of AI tools in legal workflows and a genuine interest in finding new ways to drive efficiency. We're building a legal team that works smarter, not just harder.
• Be a storyteller: Translate dense regulatory concepts into straightforward, energizing narratives for product teams and other stakeholders as well as external audiences.
• Stay curious and agile: Embrace each new regulation, market shift, or product pivot as a learning opportunity. Mercury's regulatory landscape is evolving quickly, and the scope of this role will grow with it. This is not a maintenance-only role.

What you should have:
• 6+ years of legal experience, with at least 2 of those years focused on non-deposit investment products.
• Familiarity with the Investment Advisers Act, Securities Act, Investment Company Act, Regulation Best Interest, Form CRS/ADV, FINRA rules, and related regulatory frameworks.
• Some in-house experience is preferred but not required. Bonus points for exposure to regulatory agencies relevant to these products, whether as a member of agency staff or as part of an industry role.
• Exceptional communication skills. You know your audience and you tailor accordingly. You're as precise in a Slack thread as you are in a regulatory filing, and you know the value of a well-selected emoji in one versus the other.
• A proactive sense of ownership. You're never afraid to say "I don't know, but I'll find out."
• Strong working knowledge of AI use cases within legal roles and/or financial services generally and genuine interest in using AI to drive efficiency in your work.
• Some additional experience outside the investments/brokerage space. The right candidate brings a broader foundation in financial services, payments, or fintech.

What will make you successful here:

Mercury is a place where legal counsel are expected to have a point of view. Not just about what the regulation requires, but about how the product can meet that bar in a way that's elegant, scalable, and good for customers. The people who thrive on this team treat ambiguity as an invitation rather than a reason to pause. They read a regulation and think about what it permits, not just what it prohibits. 

You'll also spend a meaningful amount of your time on work that doesn't look like traditional legal practice: scoping cross-functional projects, pressure-testing product designs, building operational processes alongside compliance and ops partners. If you're someone who gets energy from that kind of work, and who measures their own impact by whether the product got better and not just whether the memo was airtight, you'll do well here.

When the Tarr Steps, a footbridge assembled of heavy stones in Exmoor National Park in England, washed away in a flood in 1942, the Royal Engineers rebuilt it. Then it washed away again in
1952. So the Royal Engineers heaved in more stones: on and on, like a Sisyphean lesson in absurdity.

Of course, they do this because the Tarr Steps are a historical monument, believed to be built during the Bronze Age. Modern bridge building looks a lot different and generally requires less upkeep. While we appreciate the charm of ancient things, Mercury is engineering the future of banking*. "Quaint" and "archaic" are not values we seek in our systems. Rebooting a tumbling server and hoping a flood of requests doesn't wash it away can be an emergency tactic, but we actively seek out durable solutions over monotonous ops work. You'll bring this ethos and teach others how to live it too.

Up to this point, the Stability team at Mercury has primarily built platform-level constructs that product teams adopt. However, those teams are asking for us to work more closely with them to mature their implementations and practices. We are creating an SRE team that will rotate through product teams. You will understand the team's domain, identify opportunities for improvements in reliability/observability/performance/preparedness and create self-reinforcing, virtuous cycles.

• Embed with product teams, helping them improve their operational maturity by setting up and refining practices around on-call, monitoring, alerting, and run books

In 1954, Eero Saarinen designed a branch office with glass walls, no offices, and a completely open floor plan in Columbus, Indiana. It was surrounded by trees; the furniture was made by Herman Miller; the lobby flooring was thick, rustic brick. It was built with transparency and community at its core. Since then, a lot of things have happened — Saarinen's branch is now a conference center, people increasingly live on the internet, and it's hard to think of a single financial institution that still applies design thinking to their company.

Mercury is on a mission to defy those expectations. We're a financial technology company that helps startups spend less time banking* and more time building. We believe that the key to our success revolves around thoughtful design — and we hold the craft of that design to an exceptionally high standard. We're looking for a Staff Brand Designer who sets that bar: someone whose eye is so precise, and whose execution is so considered, that the work around them gets better just by virtue of their presence.

This is a role for a designer who sweats the details that most people don't notice — the type hierarchy, the negative space, the grid, the crop. Someone who has developed a genuine aesthetic philosophy over years of doing hard work at a high level, and who brings that philosophy to everything they touch. You'll own the most technically complex brand design work at Mercury, provide craft oversight across the Brand Studio, and help define what visual excellence looks like as our brand continues to evolve.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

In this role, you’ll:

jobs.title: Workplace Experience Specialist - NYC
jobs.description:
This is an in-office position, where you are expected to be in the office 5 days a week, from 9:00am - 5:00pm, with 2 days a month remote. 

Mercury is looking for a Workplace Experience Specialist to bring our culture to life in our New York office through the operations of daily life in the space. This role owns the day-to-day office experience for our NYC team, ensuring that the environment people walk into each day reflects Mercury's thoughtful approach to design, quality, and connection. Our offices are where teams build relationships, solve difficult problems together, and experience the culture that makes working here meaningful. 

In addition to running the daily experience, this role will support the cultural moments that punctuate the year: monthly office events, onsites hosted in NYC, and annual celebrations. • Support the planning and execution of onsites and company events hosted in the NYC space, as well as broader employee experience initiatives — from All Hands and virtual events to merch production and cultural programs.
• Identify and lead improvements to office spaces, systems, and services to meet the evolving needs of a growing team.
• Communicate office updates, event invitations, and reminders clearly to the local team.

• Excited to be in office M-F, 9:00am - 5:00pm

jobs.description:

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.

OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). What You’ll Be Doing
