jobs.title: Senior Analyst, Lending Models
jobs.description:
About Allica Bank

Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.

Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers.

Department Description

The Modelling team sits within the Credit Portfolio Management (CPM) function and is at the heart of building the measurement and decisioning models behind Allica’s lending products. The team builds and owns the bank’s IFRS9 model estate (including PD, LGD, SICR and economic response models), the statistical and machine learning models and credit policy rules used for automated underwriting, and the credit-linked GenAI solutions used to automate processes.

Role Description

This role will be part of the team building, implementing, monitoring and optimising two sets of models: the IFRS9 impairment models that measure our credit risk and support accurate reporting to auditors and investors, and the decisioning models and policy rules behind automated lending, which are critical to delivering fast, consistent and well-controlled credit decisions and a better customer journey as the bank grows.

The role requires the technical ability and practical mindset to take models and decisioning changes from initial problem definition through data identification, cleansing and analysis to model development, implementation and ongoing monitoring. The successful candidate will be comfortable moving between structured model development and fast-paced ad-hoc analysis, working closely with Finance, Credit Risk, Underwriting, Collections, Product, Data, Engineering, Capital Markets and Model Risk colleagues. They will communicate complex concepts clearly to stakeholders with different levels of technical expertise and work with third-party suppliers where required. We are looking for a hands-on modeller who can turn data into reliable, scalable solutions, and help make data a key strength for the bank.

Principal Accountabilities

 - Take a hands-on role in the design, build, implementation and continuous refinement of the bank’s credit risk models, spanning the full suite of IFRS9 impairment models (PD, LGD, SICR and economic response) and the statistical and machine learning models that support automated lending decisions.

 - Develop and deploy models in Python across the full model lifecycle, including data preparation, feature engineering, model fitting, validation, implementation and ongoing performance assessment.

 - Perform ad-hoc analysis to optimise credit policy rules and decisioning flows, using rule-firing, decision and outcome data to identify redundant, overlapping or mis-calibrated rules.

 - Produce regular monitoring, covering population stability, discriminatory power, calibration, and segment and vintage performance, as well as decision rates and alignment with underwriting outcomes for decisioning models.

 - Recalibrate or redevelop models as portfolio experience matures, comparing predicted and actual outcomes and adjusting model scaling, score cut-offs or policy thresholds where evidence of drift or mis-calibration exists.

 - Lead root-cause investigations into model, rule or decisioning-flow underperformance by tracing issues through decision logs, data lineage, feature calculations, production pipelines and implementation logic.

 - Build well-controlled, reproducible modelling processes and drive improvements to the data, tooling and infrastructure required for future model development and deployment.

 - Document models, rules, assumptions, limitations and changes to a high standard, supporting governance, independent review and validation, and stakeholder review.

 - Work closely with Credit Risk, Finance, Underwriting, Collections, Product, Data and Engineering teams to track model requirements and translate business needs into practical solutions, while complying with all mandatory policies and maintaining a strong internal control environment.
 
 

Personal Attributes & Experience

 - You have at least 5 years’ hands-on risk modelling experience, applying statistical modelling techniques such as logistic and linear regression, as well as machine learning models, to solve practical business problems.

 - You are comfortable with large data sets, and data extraction and manipulation using Excel, SQL, Python & BI tools.

 - You have a proven track record with Python coding, and are comfortable using GenAI tools to increase coding productivity.

 - You have a good understanding of IFRS9, credit and lending concepts, preferably in commercial lending.

 - You are driven, self-motivated and passionate about building great solutions for the bank.

 - You can work independently and are flexible to adapt quickly to changing priorities within a very dynamic environment.

 - You work well with stakeholders across the business, and collaboratively within the team.

 - You have strong skills in writing technical documents as well as business-focused documents to get buy-in from various stakeholders.

 - Experience of implementation of models into software applications is highly desirable.

Prior experience in this area matters for this role. If you believe you are a strong fit for the role, but don’t quite meet one of the requirements above – if you think you can suitably overcome that, then please apply anyway.

jobs.description:
About Allica Bank

Allica is the UK’s fastest growing company - and the fastest-growing financial technology (Fintech) firm ever. Our purpose is to help established SMEs, one of the last major underserved opportunities in Fintech.

Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers.

Department Description 

The Bridging Department at Allica Bank is a high-energy, specialist lending team supporting established SMEs and professional property investors with fast, flexible short-term finance. Operating within a true challenger-bank environment, the team combines strong credit discipline with pragmatic decision-making, relationship-led lending, and a clear focus on delivering the right outcomes for customers. 

This is a fast-paced and constantly evolving department where no two days are the same. Deals are time-critical, varied, and often bespoke, requiring commercial thinking, sound judgement, and a willingness to take ownership from day one. As the Bridging proposition continues to grow, the role and the department evolve week by week.

The team is lively, proactive, and highly collaborative. People are trusted to act like owners, take responsibility for their decisions, and work closely with colleagues across Distribution, Credit, Operations, and external partners to keep things moving. There is a strong emphasis on keeping things clear and simple, working at pace, and removing unnecessary barriers to getting good deals done.

True to Allica’s values, the Bridging Department is built on teamwork, transparency, and doing the right thing for customers and the Bank. Ideas are welcomed, expertise is respected, and individuals are encouraged to challenge constructively, improve processes, and contribute to the continued success of a growing SME-focused lender. 

Role Description 

The Client Services – Team Lead is responsible for leading, coaching, and developing a team of Client Services Associates and Managers, driving high performance, accountability, and strong credit outcomes. The role plays a key part in building capability across the team, supporting individual development plans and succession planning, and fostering a culture where the team feel confident to challenge, escalate, and continuously improve. 

Alongside people leadership, the role holds responsibility for packaging and structuring complex bridging transactions, ensuring lending decisions align with the Bank’s Credit Policy, risk appetite, and asset strategy, while delivering fast, high quality outcomes for SME and professional property clients. 

The Client Services -Team Lead plays a critical role within Allica Bank’s Bridging proposition, supporting the delivery of fast, flexible lending solutions to SME and professional property clients. 

Client Services are responsible for working with the BDMs in increasing originations, structuring Indicative Terms and carrying out an initial assessment of borrowing requests to evaluate feasibility and alignment with the Bank’s credit appetite. Acting as the first point of “triage”, the role determines whether enquiries are suitable to progress, ensuring only well-structured, viable applications are submitted to Credit. This early intervention is fundamental to maintaining pace, quality, and conversion through the lending journey. 

The role works closely alongside Business Development Managers and the Credit team, supporting the effective transition of enquiries into fully packaged applications. Client Services Associates prepare high-quality files for submission, ensuring key information is captured accurately and efficiently to support timely credit decisioning. 

The Client Services – Team Lead may also be involved in originating, structuring, and progressing bridging applications from Introducers and Borrowers, from initial enquiry through to completion. 

Client Services act as a trusted point of contact for brokers, providing clarity, guidance, and responsiveness throughout the early stages of the process. The role also involves liaising with third parties such as surveyors and solicitors, coordinating activity to help drive cases smoothly towards completion.

jobs.title: Head of Marketing
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Dakota is a stablecoin infrastructure platform powering modern financial products through regulated money movement, stablecoin orchestration, and cross-border settlement. We serve institutional clients — fintechs, payment service providers, marketplaces, and enterprises — through an API-first platform that abstracts the complexity of custody, compliance, settlement, and banking partnerships. Dakota has raised $16.5M from CoinFund, 6th Man Ventures, and Triton Ventures.

We are a remote first team across North America and Europe. We value high quality work, clear thinking and ownership.

Please note: Dakota is a remote-only, equal-opportunity employer. At this time, we are able to hire within the U.S., United Kingdom, Spain and Portugal.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Dakota is at a stage where how we explain the product and how it shows up in real customer conversations matters as much as what we build. This role exists to make that repeatable.

We’re hiring a Head of Marketing to take ownership of how Dakota goes to market — defining positioning, shaping messaging, and building the foundations of a GTM motion that works in practice, not just on paper.

This is a founding marketing leadership role. You’ll work closely with the CEO and GTM leadership to set direction, make tradeoffs, and execute in a hands-on way. We’re not looking for someone to manage a large team or scale channels immediately. We’re looking for a leader who can decide what matters, test it, refine it, and then scale what’s working over time.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Define how Dakota is explained to customers

 - Define and evolve positioning, messaging and use cases that stand up in real sales conversations.

 - Clarify how Dakota’s products are differentiated and when they’re the right solution for a customer.

Build a content led GTM engine

 - Own what content is worth producing, why it exists, and how it supports customer understanding and conversion.

 - Create and iterate key assets while also using leverage- AI, contractors and partners- to increase speed and quality.

 - Set the bar for quality and relevance rather than sheer output volume.

Improve conversion and GTM effectiveness

 - Partner closely with sales and product to understand objections, stalled deals and increase buyer clarity.

 - Adjust messaging, use cases, and campaigns based on feedback from the field.

 - Scale activity once fundamentals are working, prioritizing signal before volume.

Lay foundations for scale

 - Establish lightweight workflows, metrics, and operating cadence so marketing can scale responsibly over time.

 - Use modern tools, including AI, to increase leverage without adding unnecessary processes.

WHO YOU ARE

You’re a strategic builder with strong judgment.

You likely:

 - Have been the first or early marketing hire at a startup, or owned a 0–1 GTM effort inside a larger company.

 - Have strong product marketing instincts and can operate across content, messaging, and GTM execution.

 - Are comfortable making decisions without perfect information and adjusting quickly when something isn’t working.

 - Have worked closely with sales and understand how marketing impacts real conversations and outcomes.

 - Can balance hands-on execution with setting direction and leading through influence.

 - Have managed a small team or led others before and can see yourself growing and developing people over time, without needing a large org or heavy process.

You don’t need fintech experience, but you should be comfortable marketing complex, trust sensitive, or regulated products.

HOW WE WORK

At Dakota, we value people who:

 - Strive for excellence

 - Practice extreme ownership.

 - Experiment fearlessly and learn quickly.

 - Stay close to customers.

 - Communicate clearly and directly.

WHAT WE OFFER

 - Engaging problems that increase economic freedom globally

 - Competitive salary and equity

 - Employee-friendly equity terms (extended exercise)

 - Remote work, no commuting to the office

 - Paid co-working space/desk at an office

 - Health, dental, and vision insurance

 - Regular team events and off-sites

THE ROLE

You’ll run fraud operations across everything we move: cards, ACH, wire, and stablecoin on- and off-ramps, with cards as the immediate focus while we launch our card programs. You’ll manage the daily fraud workflows, strengthen the policy and controls behind them, and work with our bank partners on fraud and dispute reporting.

It’s a high-ownership role at a company moving quickly. You’ll run the operation day to day while helping build the processes and tooling that let it scale with Dakota.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Maintain and improve Dakota’s anti-fraud policy, controls, and thresholds, and produce the fraud metrics that go to leadership.

 - Run day-to-day fraud operations: triage, investigate, and decide on alerts and cases across cards, ACH, wire, and stablecoin transfers, and lead the post-mortem when something gets through.

 - Serve as the primary point of contact for fraud escalations from our banking and processing partners, and from internal teams including customer support.

 - Own card disputes and chargebacks once customer support hands them off: provisional credit, representment, network deadlines, and Regulation E timelines.

 - Prepare fraud and dispute reporting for our bank partners, and respond to their oversight requests.

 - Design fraud management processes that scale, using AI tools to minimize manual work.

 - Tune our anti-fraud rules as typologies evolve: hunt emerging patterns before they surface as alerts or losses, measure rules against false-positive rates and alert-to-case conversion, and partner with Compliance and Engineering to ship changes.

 - Help shape the fraud operations roadmap and tooling decisions: what we configure, what we build, what we buy.

 - Experience working directly with bank partners on fraud and dispute reporting, oversight requests, and exam or audit support.

 - Hands-on experience in manual review operations: running queues, making case decisions, and hitting SLAs.

 - Card fraud fundamentals: authorization signals, card testing, and account takeover.

jobs.title: Lead Machine Learning Scientist
jobs.description:
DAVE VS. GOLIATH. WE’RE DAVE.

Dave is a financial app on a mission to build products that level the financial playing field. It is redefining the financial landscape by leveraging technology to create an affordable, transparent, and user-centric access to liquidity for millions of Americans. As a leading innovator in the U.S. financial services sector, Dave’s digital financial platform offers products designed to meet the credit needs of those underserved by traditional financial institutions. Dave’s offerings include its flagship ExtraCash product, providing members up to $500 within minutes. The company is on track to launch several new product offerings in 2026, including a Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) option.

Dave is focused on serving Americans who are financially vulnerable or living paycheck to paycheck. Dave is leading the charge in creating a new era of credit products that prioritizes speed, affordability, and accessibility, making it the go-to financial partner for those who need it most.

THE OPPORTUNITY

We're looking for a Lead Machine Learning Scientist to develop and deploy advanced machine learning solutions that help Dave detect fraud, protect our members, and responsibly expand access to credit.

This is a deeply hands-on role for someone who loves solving complex problems through data, experimentation, and modeling. You'll work across the full machine learning lifecycle, from exploring large datasets and developing predictive models to deploying solutions, evaluating performance, and continuously improving results.

You'll have meaningful ownership of technically challenging problems, with opportunities to influence how we approach fraud detection and risk decisioning. You'll collaborate closely with Product, Engineering, and Risk Operations while remaining actively involved in the modeling and technical execution that drives our business forward.

WHAT YOU'LL BUILD & OWN

 - Build and deploy advanced fraud detection models. Personally develop, train, validate, and optimize machine learning models that identify synthetic identities, first-party fraud, account takeover, and emerging fraud patterns.

 - Solve complex problems through data and experimentation. Explore large, diverse datasets, engineer predictive features, evaluate modeling approaches, and translate findings into production-ready fraud solutions.

 - Own the end-to-end ML lifecycle. Take models from initial research and prototyping through testing, deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement, ensuring solutions deliver measurable business results.

 - Apply AI to accelerate machine learning development. Use modern AI tools and techniques to improve research, coding, feature development, experimentation, validation, and modeling workflows while maintaining strong technical rigor.

 - Optimize fraud decisioning through measurable results. Analyze model performance, fraud trends, approval rates, and portfolio outcomes to identify opportunities to improve detection accuracy, reduce losses, and support responsible growth.

 - Collaborate and contribute technical expertise. Partner with Engineering, Product, and Risk Operations to integrate models into production systems, solve implementation challenges, and share technical knowledge that strengthens the broader team.

THE IMPACT YOU'LL MAKE

Your models will help Dave make smarter, more responsible fraud and credit decisions. You'll directly contribute to reducing fraud losses, improving decision accuracy, and helping more members access the financial tools they need.

Flex card is Dave's newest and most ambitious product, a pay-in-4 card built for the millions of members living paycheck to paycheck who've never had fair access to credit. Behind every purchase it makes is the system that turns a balance into a loan, casts it into installments, services it, and collects it. That system is the loan management system (LMS), and it's what this role owns.

This is a senior individual-contributor role at the foundation of Flex and every loan product that comes after it. You'll own the LMS and the systems of record end-to-end: the ledger, loan casting, servicing, collections, and the compliance tooling around them. And you'll take it from a single-product build to a scalable platform, so that when Dave launches its next loan product, it runs on what you've built instead of starting over.

If you like real ownership, hard systems problems, and building the infrastructure that makes fair credit possible at scale, this role is for you.

WHAT YOU'LL BUILD & OWN

 - Own the loan management system: Lead the LMS and core systems of record: the ledger, loan casting at billing, the pay-in-4 installment structure, participation and installment fees, repayment, and collections.

 - Build the platform, not just the product: Lead the build-vs-buy decision and the migration off our current loan-servicing platform onto a foundation that makes Flex faster, more reliable, and easier to iterate on. From there, evolve it from a single-product integration into a multi-product platform that future loan products reuse instead of rebuild.

 - Ship the mechanics members feel: installment schedules aligned to paycheck dates, early payoff, and decline and failure handling.

 - Own the numbers: Define and track system health, payoff rates, and loss performance, and use them to prioritize where to invest.

 - Enable flawless execution: Work closely with Risk, Legal/Compliance (LECO), Data Science, Engineering, and Operations, and coordinate external partners (Coastal, LoanPro) on anything that touches casting, collections, or compliance.

THE IMPACT

The LMS is where Flex's unit economics are won or lost. Payoff rates, loss performance, and whether members can repay on a schedule that fits their paycheck all run through the system you'll own and small improvements compound across every loan.

You'll be building this foundation at its most formative stage. Get it right and Dave launches its next loan product in a fraction of the time, on infrastructure that's already compliant, auditable, and proven. The problems are real, the stakes are high, and your fingerprints will be all over how Dave lends for years to come.

jobs.title: Security Engineer
jobs.description:
About

the Role:

We're looking for a Security Engineer who is equally at home hardening a CI/CD pipeline, reviewing a change to the authentication system on the backend, and triaging a bug bounty submission before lunch.This is a hands-on, builder-first role - not a governance checkbox. You'll own security operations end-to-end, embedded directly into the engineering team and working closely with infrastructure, protocol and platform.

If you treat threat modeling as a design conversation and not a compliance exercise, you're our kind of person. You should only apply for this role if you are ready to come into the office every day and work in person with our team!

What You'll Do:

Security Operations

 - Own day-to-day security operations: monitoring, alerting, triage, and response

 - Manage and monitor endpoint security via an EDR system - tune detections, investigate alerts, and drive incidents to resolution

 - Lead identity lifecycle management, including employee onboarding and off boarding (access provisioning, key rotation, deprovisioning)

Bug Bounty & Vulnerability Management

 - Be the primary owner of our ImmuneFi program - triaging, reproducing, and responding to incoming submissions daily

 - Prioritize and track vulnerabilities through to remediation in close collaboration with protocol and engineering teams

 - Develop internal tooling and processes to make the bounty workflow faster and more consistent

DevSecOps & Pipeline Hardening

 - Audit and harden CI/CD pipelines - secrets management, supply chain integrity, SAST/DAST integration, build provenance

 - Own dependency security: identify and remediate vulnerable packages across repositories (yes, including the npm dependency hell)

 - Establish and enforce security standards across the SDLC

Infrastructure Security

 - Partner with the infrastructure team to review and harden cloud environments (access controls, network segmentation, least privilege, logging)

 - Contribute to threat modeling for new systems and architectural changes

 - Drive implementation of security tooling across the stack

Vendor & External Partner Management

 - Own relationships with external security vendors and service providers — holding them accountable toSLAs, managing scope, and ensuring findings are actioned

 - Evaluate and onboard new security tooling as the team and threat landscape evolve

What We're Looking For:

- 5+ years of experience in software and security engineering, with meaningful time in a DevSecOps or security operations context

 - Strong software engineering fundamentals - you're a builder who writes code, not just policy

 - Hands-on experience hardening CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, CircleCI, or similar) and cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or equivalent)

 - Proficiency with endpoint security tooling (CrowdStrike or equivalent EDR)

 - Comfort owning identity and access management processes, including onboarding/offboarding workflows

 - Strong communication skills - you can write a clear triage report, give direct feedback to a developer and explain risk to a non-technical stakeholder

Nice to Have:

- You were a traditional software engineer before specializing in security

 - Prior experience at a DeFi protocol, crypto exchange, or blockchain infrastructure company

 - CTF/security competition background

 - Contributions to open-source security tooling

What Success Looks Like:

In your first 90 days, you've mapped our attack surface, established a daily rhythm on ImmuneFi, and shipped at least a few meaningful PRs across the full stack. Within six months, you've built enough trust in the team that engineers come to you before shipping sensitive PRs, not after.

jobs.description:
About ether.fi http://ether.fi

ether.fi http://ether.fi is one of the largest DeFi protocols on Ethereum. We started with weETH, a liquid staking token that now secures billions of dollars of staked ETH, and built outward from there: the Liquid vault range, which runs automated yield strategies across ETH, stablecoins and BTC, and ether.fi http://ether.fi Cash, a Visa card and neobank product that lets users spend directly against their on-chain balances.

Behind the protocol is a group of operating companies in Cayman, Brazil, the US, Canada and the UAE, including a regulated investment manager and a licensed VASP. We are continuing to open new markets and add additional regulated products, with finance playing a key role in this expansion.

The role

We're hiring a Head of Finance to run the finance function. Today finance sits with the COO/CFO and financial controller. We are looking for someone to own the following: month end, audits, budget, tax, treasury operations, fund NAV, payments and payroll. The CFO will set policy and sign off. You own everything else.

It's a small team. You'll have one accountant reporting to you and can hire as we grow, but you need to be comfortable doing the work yourself. We're based across several time zones and you'll be working with legal, compliance, ops and the product teams every week.

What you'll do

 - Run month end across all entities. Management accounts within 15 business days, quarterly reporting within 45 days.

 - Balance sheet recs, including wallets, exchange and custody balances against the ledger.

 - Revenue recognition for protocol fees, vault fees, card interchange and treasury income.

 - Lead our statutory audits.

 - Own the annual budget and monthly budget vs actuals. Every material assumption needs to be documented and something you can defend.

 - Cash forecasting.

 - Daily liquidity monitoring across fiat, stables and crypto. Weekly portfolio review and rebalancing to targets set by the CFO. Moving funds for payroll and payments.

 - Put intercompany agreements and a transfer pricing model in place with our advisers.

 - Tax and regulatory finance filings across Cayman, Brazil, US, Canada and UAE (economic substance, US information returns, CRA).

 - Weekly payment run, vendors, payroll and contractors in several countries, token vesting and payouts, expenses.

 - Card inventory and cost tracking with Ops.

 - Own the finance systems (QuickBooks, crypto sub-ledger, AP tool, payroll, cap table) and cut down the manual recs.

 - Work with Compliance, Ecosystem and Product on fee models and new launches. Help HR with comp budgets, relocations and payroll.

What we're looking for

 - Qualified accountant (CA, CPA, ACCA). Big 4 audit background preferred.

 - 8+ years post-qualification, at least 4 of them in-house at a crypto, fintech or asset management business.

 - Has run a finance function before, as controller or head of finance, across multiple entities and currencies.

 - Has owned audits end to end.

 - Hands-on with intercompany agreements and transfer pricing.

 - Comfortable with crypto: wallet recs, token accounting, staking rewards, NAV for crypto funds.

 - Organised and direct. Flags problems early rather than at month end.

 - Able to work in Cayman (right to work or eligible for a permit). Relocation support is available.

Nice to have

 - Cayman funds: CIMA registration, investment manager entities, working with administrators.

 - VASP, payments or card program experience, including interchange.

 - US and Canadian tax.

 - Multi-country payroll and token compensation.

 - QuickBooks Online, a crypto sub-ledger, AP automation.

The budgeted salary range for this role is $70,000-80,000 CAD / year.

Dans ce rôle, vous contribuerez à la réalisation de communications de marque et publicitaires percutantes, en formats statiques et animés. ABOUT THE ROLE

Lifecycle and Organic Growth own two things at KOHO: how Canadians find us without paid media, and every message they get from us after they sign up. As Director, Lifecycle & Organic Growth, you'll set the strategy for both and lead the teams that deliver it. On the Lifecycle side that means email, push, in-app, and SMS. On the Organic side it means koho.ca http://koho.ca, SEO, GEO, the App Store and Google Play, and content marketing.

 

You won't be starting from scratch. Lifecycle already measures its impact with a randomized global control group, tied to company KPIs like activation, power users, retention and contribution margin rather than open rates. It has a documented operating model, two-part peer QA on every send, a tiered legal review process, and an incident and continuity framework designed for a regulated financial institution. Your job is to scale what's working: grow incremental impact, bring the same measurement rigour to Organic, and connect the two into one owned-channel growth engine.

 

You'll report to the Chief Growth Officer and lead a team of seven. You'll work closely with Product, Data, Legal & Compliance, Creative, Integrated Marketing, Performance Marketing and Engineering.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Strategy and outcomes

 - Own the strategy, roadmap and targets for Lifecycle and Organic Growth. You're accountable for business outcomes (registrations, activation, engagement, retention and contribution margin).

 - Lead lifecycle programs across the whole customer journey: onboarding, activation, cross-sell and upsell, reactivation, retention and servicing.

 - Set direction for organic acquisition across koho.ca http://koho.ca, SEO, GEO (visibility in AI-powered search), app store optimization and content, alongside the senior domain lead who runs it day to day.

 - Bring Lifecycle-grade measurement to Organic: clear definitions, metrics anyone can reproduce, and reporting that connects organic presence to registrations and activation.

 - Connect owned channels with Paid, Affiliates and Product so the customer journey works end to end, not just channel by channel.

 

Measurement and experimentation

 - Steward the global control group and the incrementality program. Make sure every result the team reports is causal and holds up to scrutiny.

 - Own the experimentation roadmap (A/B tests, holdouts, multivariate journeys) and turn results into decisions.

 - Present performance and strategy to the executive team in regular business reviews.

 

Operations, governance and risk

 - Own the Lifecycle operating model: intake, prioritization, spec, peer QA, legal review tiering, launch and post-launch measurement.

 - Partner with Legal and Compliance so every customer communication is accurate, compliant and auditable, in both English and French.

 - Own incident response and business continuity for customer messaging, including fallback sending and escalation paths.

 - Own website governance: who can publish, how changes are reviewed, and how releases are protected.

 - Own the owned-channel martech stack and its vendors, with Braze as the core platform. That covers contracts, renewals and platform health.

 

People

 - Lead, develop and retain a team of senior managers and specialists, and hire as the team grows.

 - Keep the career ladder clear, and keep the team's engagement and growth high.

 

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

 - 10+ years in lifecycle, CRM or retention marketing at a B2C consumer tech, fintech or subscription business, including 4+ years leading managers.

 - A track record of moving business metrics through owned channels, backed by incrementality evidence (holdouts, control groups) and not just engagement rates.

 - Deep, hands-on fluency with a modern customer engagement platform (Braze strongly preferred): journey architecture, segmentation, Liquid personalization, and data integration through a CDP such as Segment.

 - Working fluency in organic growth: SEO and technical SEO fundamentals, ASO, content strategy, and how AI search is changing discovery. You don't need to be a career SEO, but you do need to set strategy and challenge how results are measured.

 - Strong analytical judgment. You're comfortable in SQL or working closely with Data, and you can tell when a number doesn't hold up.

 - Experience in a regulated industry (financial services, insurance, health or telecom) where marketing goes through legal and compliance review.

 - An operator's instinct: you've written the playbook, not just followed it.

 - Executive communication that's clear and concise, and you raise bad news early.

 - A record as a manager people want to work for, with the retention and engagement to show it.

 - You're already using AI in your day-to-day work.

 - Experience with Canadian financial services regulation and CASL.

 - Experience with predictive or ML-driven personalization (churn, propensity, send-time).

 

NICE TO HAVE

 - Professional working proficiency in French

 - Experience with a headless CMS (e.g. Sanity) and on-site experimentation

 

The posted salary range for this role is $175,000 – $210,000 CAD / year.

At KOHO, we are dedicated to providing pay transparency to all candidates. Compensation at KOHO is determined through various factors including but not limited to: comparable salary market data within Canada, technical skill assessment, a holistic view of previous work history, and internal pay equity with other KOHO team members.

 

DESCRIPTION DE POSTE EN FRANÇAIS

 

DIRECTEUR(TRICE), CYCLE DE VIE CLIENT ET CROISSANCE ORGANIQUE

 

À PROPOS DU POSTE

Chez KOHO, les équipes Cycle de vie et Croissance organique sont responsables de deux choses : la façon dont les Canadiens nous découvrent sans médias payants, et chacun des messages qu'ils reçoivent de notre part après leur inscription. À titre de directeur(trice), Cycle de vie client et croissance organique, vous définirez la stratégie de ces deux volets et dirigerez les équipes qui la mettent en œuvre. Du côté Cycle de vie, cela comprend les courriels, les notifications push, les messages intégrés à l'application et les textos. Du côté Croissance organique, cela comprend koho.ca http://koho.ca, le référencement naturel (SEO), l'optimisation pour les moteurs génératifs (GEO), l'App Store et Google Play, ainsi que le marketing de contenu.

 

Vous ne partirez pas de zéro. L'équipe Cycle de vie mesure déjà son impact au moyen d'un groupe témoin global randomisé, lié aux indicateurs clés de l'entreprise comme l'activation, les utilisateurs assidus, la rétention et la marge de contribution plutôt qu'aux taux d'ouverture. Votre rôle sera de faire croître ce qui fonctionne : augmenter l'impact incrémental, appliquer la même rigueur de mesure à la croissance organique et réunir les deux volets en un seul moteur de croissance par les canaux détenus.

 

Vous relèverez du chef de la croissance et dirigerez une équipe de sept personnes. Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes Produits, Données, Affaires juridiques et Conformité, Création, Marketing intégré, Marketing de performance et Ingénierie.

 

CE QUE VOUS FEREZ

 

STRATÉGIE ET RÉSULTATS

 - Piloter la feuille de route d'expérimentation (tests A/B, groupes de contrôle, parcours multivariés) et transformer les résultats en décisions.

GESTION DES PERSONNES

CE DONT VOUS AUREZ BESOIN

We’re looking for a Senior Purple Team Engineer to join our team for a role to work remotely based in Canada. Are you someone that has been doing incident response but would like to also have a technical component to your job? Or vice-versa?

You are the coach. You build company-wide preparedness for a cyber incident, starting with the security team and extending across KOHO. When an incident hits, you're part of the response team, stepping in as incident commander or supporting, depending on context and what the situation requires.

In addition to incident response, this role is responsible for building KOHO's deception engineering program from the ground up. This covers both internal detection assets (honeypots, canary tokens, decoy users, breadcrumbs) and external-facing deception (fake credentials, canary tokens embedded in customer-facing surfaces, and decoy infrastructure seeded in attacker-accessible surfaces). The program generates threat intelligence that feeds back into detection logic, playbooks, and KOHO's broader threat model.

Reporting to our Senior Manager, Product Security you’re going to be a part of a team that does.

WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

 - Own and lead incident response readiness across KOHO. Starting with the security team, conduct regular tabletop exercises and playbook reviews.

 - Document lessons learned, operational improvements, and playbook updates. Execute all improvements.

 - Design and deploy internal deception assets to detect lateral movement, insider threats, and unauthorized access across KOHO's environment.

 - Instrument deception assets to generate actionable threat intelligence and feed findings back into detection logic, playbooks, and the broader threat model.

 - Build the triage and response workflow for deception-triggered alerts into existing SOC operations, from signal to investigation to lessons learned.
 

WHO YOU ARE

 - Bachelor’s degree in computer science, technology management, or related technical or management field.

 - Hands-on experience planning and executing adversarial simulations, including scoping engagements, defining rules of engagement, and delivering post-engagement reporting.

 - Lead the end-to-end management of regulatory examinations, reviews, and information requests, including planning, evidence collection, response quality control, and issue tracking.

 - Own KOHO’s enterprise complaints management program, including policy, procedures, escalation pathways, and service standards.

 - Oversee handling of escalated and designated complaints, ensuring fair, timely, well-reasoned outcomes and clear written responses to customers.

 - Manage case flow with the external complaints body and oversee reporting to the FCAC and other applicable authorities.

 - Deliver complaints reporting and root cause analysis, converting complaint themes into product, process, and disclosure improvements that advance fair treatment of customers.

COMPLIANCE TESTING

 - Own the design and delivery of KOHO’s independent Compliance Testing Program, including methodology, quality standards, and reporting.

 - Develop the annual risk-based testing plan, scoped and prioritized from the regulatory obligations inventory and known risk concentrations; Collaborate with Operational Risk Management (ORM) on the selection of compliance controls.

 - Maintain a quality assurance process over testing outputs, including work performed by co-source or business process outsourcing partners, and report results and thematic conclusions into senior management and/or Board-level reporting.

TEAM LEADERSHIP AND INDUSTRY ENGAGEMENT

 - Lead, coach, and develop a multi-disciplinary team across financial crime, testing, and complaints, building bench strength and clear career paths.

 - Partner with Compliance Advisory and Privacy, Operational Risk, Internal Audit, Legal, and FIU to ensure integrated risk oversight.

 - Represent KOHO externally in industry associations, peer forums, and financial crime intelligence networks, staying ahead of emerging typologies, fraud trends, and regulatory developments.

 - Prepare and present decision-ready reporting to senior management and applicable Board-level committees.

AI, AUTOMATION AND INNOVATION

 - Apply AI, machine learning, RPA, and advanced analytics to transaction monitoring tuning, alert triage, complaints classification, and compliance testing.

 - Lead the development of automated testing scripts, intelligent workflows, and advanced reporting to increase coverage.

 - Evaluate and implement emerging RegTech and financial crime technology, and maintain model governance and tuning documentation for detection systems.

WHO YOU ARE

 - You have 10+ years of experience across AML and financial crime, compliance testing or audit, regulatory relations, or complaints within financial services.

 - You have deep working knowledge of Canadian consumer protection, AML, retail banking or payments, and privacy legislation.

 - You have direct experience managing regulatory examinations or information requests, and you’re composed under that kind of scrutiny.

As Senior Product Design Manager, you will lead design across a complex portfolio that combines two very different but deeply connected challenges: helping teams create and grow new customer experiences, and building the systems that allow excellent design to scale across KOHO.

You will lead and develop product designers working across zero-to-one, growth, onboarding, and other high-leverage product opportunities. At the same time, you will provide strategic leadership and support to the KOHO Design System team, helping the system evolve as a practical, adopted, high-quality foundation across app and web.

This is a role for a design leader who can move fluidly between ambiguity and scale. You will help teams turn uncertain opportunities into clear product directions, design experiments that create real learning, and make thoughtful trade-offs between velocity, quality, customer trust, and long-term experience coherence. You will also understand when a solution should be explored as a local experiment and when it needs to become a reusable pattern that improves the whole product.

You will work closely with Product managers, Engineering, Data, Research, Marketing, and other functional teams. As part of KOHO’s Product, Design, and Engineering partnership, you will shape strategy, create clarity across multiple teams, and raise the quality of the experience without making teams dependent on process or central approval.

What You’ll Do

 - Lead and develop product designers across multiple teams or a large, complex area, creating the conditions for people to grow, make decisions with confidence, and do exceptional work.

 - Set a clear design direction across zero-to-one and growth initiatives, helping teams move from ambiguous opportunities to compelling product experiences and measurable learning to accelerate KOHO in its mission to be the bank of choice for all Canadians, across app and web.

 - Coach teams through experimentation, using customer insight, research, data, prototypes, and product outcomes to decide what to build, what to test, and what to change next.

 - Balance growth velocity and unit economics with customer value, craft quality, trust, accessibility, and long-term experience health; know when to move quickly and when Coll or clarity cannot be compromised.

 - Collaborate with Product, Engineering, Data, Research, Marketing, and other teams to shape strategy, scope initiatives, make trade-offs, and deliver customer value. Respect, understand and incorporate varying perspectives in the work outputs.

 - Represent Design in roadmap, resourcing, timeline, and quality discussions, ensuring design has a meaningful voice from the beginning.

 - Support the KOHO Design System team through strategic direction, prioritization, critique, coaching, and cross-functional partnership, helping the system serve real product needs across app and web.

 - Build the operating practices, feedback loops, and decision frameworks that help teams move quickly, learn continuously, and scale quality.

 - Identify the capabilities KOHO needs as the organization grows and help attract, hire, onboard, and develop the designers and design leaders who will build them.

 - Use AI-enabled tools responsibly to accelerate exploration, synthesis, prototyping, design-system maintenance, communication, and decision-making while applying strong human judgment.
 

WHO YOU ARE

 - You have 8+ years experience designing and shipping consumer-facing digital products, ideally across mobile and web, in fintech, financial services, or another complex domain.

 - You bring significant experience leading and developing product design teams (4+ years), including designers working on ambiguous, high-impact, or consequential problems.

 - You have meaningful zero-to-one and/or growth experience. You have helped teams discover opportunities, launch new experiences, improve acquisition or activation, and learn through experimentation rather than relying only on intuition or incremental optimization.

 - You understand growth as a product and design problem, not simply a funnel or conversion problem. You can connect customer motivation, product value, trust, behavior, and business outcomes.

 - You have deep design-systems expertise and have helped build, scale, govern, adopt, or materially evolve a design system used by multiple teams.

 - You operate with strong agency and sound judgment. You can create clarity without waiting for perfect information, make decisions with appropriate context, and know when to involve others.

 - You have expertise influencing product strategy, roadmap decisions, scope, and prioritization through clear communication and customer-centered reasoning.

 - You build strong, trust-based relationships with Product, Engineering, Data, Research, Marketing, and other cross-functional partners.

 - You are an excellent communicator who can create alignment across designers, Product, Engineering, Data, Research, Marketing, and senior leadership.

 - You are comfortable using modern AI tools to accelerate workflows, explore more possibilities, prototype, and increase the scale of your impact while applying sound judgment around privacy and quality.

 - You scale your impact of craft, quality, judgement, AI-leveage, and elevate those you lead and those around you

The budgeted salary range for this role is $170,000 - 220,000 CAD / year. 

At KOHO, we are dedicated to providing pay transparency to all candidates. Compensation at KOHO is determined through various factors including but not limited to: comparable salary market data within Canada, technical skill assessment, a holistic view of previous work history, and internal pay equity with other KOHO team members.

DESCRIPTION DE POSTE EN FRANÇAIS

À PROPOS DU RÔLE

À titre de gestionnaire principal(e) du design de produit, vous dirigerez le design au sein d’un portefeuille complexe qui réunit deux défis très différents, mais profondément liés : aider les équipes à créer et à développer de nouvelles expériences client, et bâtir les systèmes qui permettent de déployer un design de grande qualité à l’échelle de KOHO.

Vous dirigerez et développerez des designers de produit œuvrant dans la création d'expériences de toutes pièces (« zero-to-one »), la croissance, l’accueil (« onboarding ») et d’autres occasions de produit à fort impact. En parallèle, vous assurerez un leadership stratégique auprès de l’équipe du système de design de KOHO pour l'aider à évoluer en tant que fondation pratique, adoptée et de haute qualité sur l'application web et mobile.

Ce rôle s’adresse à un(e) leader en design capable de naviguer aisément entre l’ambiguïté et la mise à l’échelle. Vous aiderez les équipes à transformer des occasions incertaines en orientations de produit claires, à concevoir des expériences générant de vrais apprentissages et à faire des compromis judicieux entre rapidité d'exécution, qualité, confiance des clients et cohérence de l’expérience à long terme. Vous saurez également reconnaître quand une solution doit être testée localement et quand elle doit devenir un modèle réutilisable qui améliore l’ensemble du produit.

Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec la gestion de produit, l'ingénierie, les données, la recherche, le marketing et d’autres équipes fonctionnelles. Dans le cadre du partenariat entre les équipes de produit, de design et d’ingénierie de KOHO, vous façonneza la stratégie, apporterez de la clarté entre plusieurs équipes et réhausserez la qualité de l’expérience sans rendre les équipes dépendantes de processus rigides ou d’approbation centrale.

VOS RESPONSABILITÉS

 - Diriger et développer des designers de produit au sein de plusieurs équipes ou d’un sous-ensemble vaste et complexe, en créant les conditions propices à leur épanouissement, à une prise de décision confiante et à la réalisation d’un travail d’exception.

 - Établir une direction de design claire pour les initiatives de création (« zero-to-one ») et de croissance, en aidant les équipes à passer d’occasions ambiguës à des expériences de produit attrayantes et à des apprentissages mesurables, afin d'accélérer la mission de KOHO de devenir la banque de choix pour tous les Canadiens, sur l'application web et mobile.

 - Encadrer les équipes à travers l’expérimentation, en utilisant les informations client, la recherche, les données, les prototypes et les résultats produit pour déterminer quoi bâtir, quoi tester et quoi modifier ensuite.

 - Équilibrer la rapidité de la croissance et la rentabilité unitaire avec la valeur client, la qualité de réalisation, la confiance, l’accessibilité et la pérennité de l’expérience; savoir quand agir rapidement et quand la clarté ou la qualité ne peuvent être compromises.

 - Collaborer avec les équipes de produit, d'ingénierie, de données, de recherche, de marketing et d’autres équipes pour façonner la stratégie, définir la portée des initiatives, faire des compromis et offrir de la valeur aux clients. Respecter, comprendre et intégrer des perspectives variées dans les livrables.

 - Représenter l’équipe de design lors des discussions sur la feuille de route, le recrutement, les échéanciers et la qualité, en veillant à ce que le design ait une voix influente dès le départ.

 - Soutenir l’équipe du système de design de KOHO par le biais d'orientations stratégiques, de priorisation, de critiques constructives, de mentorat et de partenariats transversaux, afin que le système réponde aux besoins réels des produits sur le web et l’application.

 - Établir les pratiques opérationnelles, les boucles de rétroaction et les cadres décisionnels qui aident les équipes à avancer rapidement, à apprendre en continu et à maintenir la qualité à grande échelle.

 - Identifier les compétences dont KOHO aura besoin au fur et à mesure que l’organisation grandit, et participer à l'attraction, à l'embauche, à l'intégration et au développement des designers et des leaders en design qui les bâtiront.

 - Utiliser les outils basés sur l’intelligence artificielle de manière responsable pour accélérer l’exploration, la synthèse, le prototypage, la maintenance du système de design, la communication et la prise de décision, tout en appliquant un jugement humain rigoureux.
 
 

VOTRE PROFIL

 - Vous possédez plus de 8+ ans d’expérience dans la conception et le lancement de produits numériques destinés aux consommateurs (idéalement sur mobile et web) dans le secteur des technologies financières (fintech), des services financiers ou un autre domaine complexe.

 - Vous comptez une expérience significative dans la gestion et le développement d’équipes de design de produit (4 ans et plus), incluant le soutien à des designers travaillant sur des enjeux ambigus, à fort impact ou déterminants.

 - Vous avez une solide expérience dans la création de produits (« zero-to-one ») ou en croissance. Vous avez aidé des équipes à découvrir des occasions, à lancer de nouvelles expériences, à améliorer l’acquisition ou l’activation, et à apprendre par l’expérimentation plutôt que de vous fier uniquement à l’intuition ou à l’optimisation incrémentale.

 - Vous percevez la croissance comme un défi de produit et de design, et pas simplement comme un problème de tunnel de conversion. Vous savez lier la motivation des clients, la valeur du produit, la confiance, le comportement et les résultats d'affaires.

 - Vous détenez une expertise approfondie des systèmes de design et avez contribué à bâtir, mettre à l'échelle, régir, faire adopter ou faire évoluer de manière tangible un système utilisé par plusieurs équipes.

 - Vous faites preuve d’une grande autonomie et d’un jugement sûr. Vous savez apporter de la clarté sans attendre d'avoir une information parfaite, prendre des décisions avec le contexte approprié et savoir quand impliquer les autres.

 - Vous avez l'habitude d'influencer la stratégie de produit, les décisions relatives à la feuille de route, la portée des projets et la priorisation grâce à une communication claire et un raisonnement centré sur le client.

 - Vous bâtissez des relations solides et fondées sur la confiance avec vos partenaires interfonctionnels des équipes de produit, d'ingénierie, de données, de recherche et de marketing.

 - Vous êtes un(e) excellent(e) communicateur(trice) capable de rassembler et d'aligner les designers, la gestion de produit, l'ingénierie, les données, la recherche, le marketing et la haute direction.

 - Vous êtes à l’aise avec l’utilisation des outils modernes d’IA pour accélérer vos flux de travail, explorer davantage de possibilités, prototyper et amplifier votre impact, tout en appliquant un sens aigu du jugement concernant la confidentialité et la qualité.

 - Vous démultipliez l'impact de votre savoir-faire, de votre exigence de qualité, de votre jugement et de votre utilisation de l'IA, tout en élevant les membres de votre équipe et les collègues qui vous entourent.

jobs.title: Senior Legal Counsel, Commercial & Corporate
jobs.description:
ABOUT KOHO

We’re on a mission to make financial services better for every Canadian. That means no hidden fees, no predatory interest rates - just financial products designed to help our users spend smart, save more, and build real wealth. We’re a performance organization with a strong heart: we care deeply about outcomes, and everything ties back to our mission - to financially empower a generation of Canadians.

At KOHO, we’re not your average 9-5. We believe real impact comes from people who are trusted, empowered, and supported to do their best work - without sacrificing their lives to do it. We prioritize work-life integration, not just work-life balance. That means asynchronous collaboration, flexible hours, and a remote-first setup built around autonomy and high trust.

KOHO is entering its next chapter - leaner, smarter, more AI-integrated. We’re building for impact, not bureaucracy. If you thrive in environments that value clarity, ownership, and bold thinking, you’ll fit right in.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As Senior Legal Counsel, Commercial & Corporate, you will provide legal support for across both KOHO Tech and KOHO Bank (letters patent pending).

You will work closely with all areas of the business and in particular, Procurement, Partnerships, and People & Culture teams to provide practical legal advice..

This role is ideal for a lawyer who enjoys rolling up the sleeves and building new things, solving complex regulatory questions, and taking ownership of outcomes in a fast-moving, flat organization.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Draft, review, and negotiate commercial agreements, including complex arrangements with banking, processing and technology partners / vendors

 - Support our product and partnerships teams on structuring and documenting strategic partnerships

 - Use AI to build legal workflows including contract templates and contract lifecycle management

 - Provide support to Enterprise and Third-Party Risk Management initiatives

 - Support employment law matters

 - Support general corporate matters including equity fundraises and corporate debt transactions
 
 

 WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - 6-8+ years post-call experience as a lawyer practicing in Canada (in-house and/or at a law firm)

 - Contract negotiation and drafting skills

 - Experience in tech procurement
 
 

WAYS OF WORKING

 - High-agency and entrepreneurial: You take ownership, figure things out, and move problems forward without waiting for perfect instructions or established processes.

 - Commercial and pragmatic: You understand that Legal’s job is to help the business achieve its goals while making smart, risk-calibrated decisions (not simply identify what could go wrong).

 - Curious and solutions-oriented: You enjoy getting into the weeds of how products and technology actually work, asking the right questions, and finding creative paths through ambiguity.

 - A builder: You don’t just solve the problem in front of you. You also look for ways to turn recurring problems into better processes, playbooks, tools, and systems.

 - Low-ego, high self-awareness: You’re confident in your judgment but genuinely open to being challenged, changing your mind, and learning from others.

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and speed: You can make progress with incomplete information, prioritize effectively, and operate calmly when the roadmap changes.

 - Technically curious: You’re excited by technology and AI and look for ways to use them to make legal work and business processes more effective.
 
 

NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience working at both a large bank and a smaller tech startup or fintech, ideally through a bank charter or launch process.

 - Familiarity with OSFI B10 guideline

The posted salary range for this role is $180,000 - $210,000 CAD / year.

At KOHO, we are dedicated to providing pay transparency to all candidates. Compensation at KOHO is determined through various factors including but not limited to: comparable salary market data within Canada, technical skill assessment, a holistic view of previous work history, and internal pay equity with other KOHO team members.

DESCRIPTION DE POSTE EN FRANÇAIS

À PROPOS DU POSTE

À titre de conseiller(ère) juridique principal(e), Commercial et corporatif, vous fournirez un soutien juridique à KOHO Tech et à KOHO Bank (lettres patentes en attente).

Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec l’ensemble des secteurs de l’entreprise, et plus particulièrement avec les équipes Approvisionnement, Partenariats et Personnes et culture, afin de fournir des conseils juridiques pratiques.

Ce poste est idéal pour un(e) avocat(e) qui aime retrousser ses manches et bâtir de nouvelles choses, résoudre des questions réglementaires complexes et prendre en charge les résultats au sein d’une organisation agile et horizontale.

CE QUE VOUS FEREZ

 - Rédiger, réviser et négocier des contrats commerciaux, notamment des ententes complexes avec des partenaires et fournisseurs bancaires, de traitement et technologiques

 - Soutenir nos équipes Produits et Partenariats dans la structuration et la documentation de partenariats stratégiques

 - Utiliser l’IA pour bâtir des flux de travail juridiques, notamment des modèles de contrats et la gestion du cycle de vie des contrats

 - Soutenir les initiatives de gestion des risques d’entreprise et des risques liés aux tiers

 - Soutenir les dossiers en droit de l’emploi

 - Soutenir les dossiers corporatifs généraux, notamment les financements par capitaux propres et les opérations de financement par emprunt

CE QUE VOUS APPORTEREZ

 - De 6 à 8 ans ou plus d’expérience après l’admission au Barreau à titre d’avocat(e) pratiquant au Canada (en entreprise et/ou en cabinet)

 - Compétences en négociation et en rédaction de contrats

 - Expérience en approvisionnement technologique

FAÇON DE TRAVAILLER

 - Autonome et entrepreneurial(e) : Vous prenez les choses en main, trouvez des solutions et faites avancer les dossiers sans attendre des instructions parfaites ou des processus établis.

 - Sens des affaires et pragmatisme : Vous comprenez que le rôle du service juridique est d’aider l’entreprise à atteindre ses objectifs en prenant des décisions judicieuses et calibrées en fonction des risques (et non simplement de relever ce qui pourrait mal tourner).

 - Curieux(se) et axé(e) sur les solutions : Vous aimez comprendre en profondeur le fonctionnement réel des produits et des technologies, poser les bonnes questions et trouver des voies créatives dans l’ambiguïté.

 - Bâtisseur(se) : Vous ne vous contentez pas de régler le problème immédiat. Vous cherchez aussi à transformer les problèmes récurrents en meilleurs processus, guides, outils et systèmes.

 - Peu d’ego, grande conscience de soi : Vous avez confiance en votre jugement, tout en restant sincèrement ouvert(e) à la remise en question, au changement d’avis et à l’apprentissage auprès des autres.

 - À l’aise avec l’ambiguïté et la rapidité : Vous savez progresser avec des renseignements incomplets, établir les priorités efficacement et garder votre calme lorsque la feuille de route change.

 - Curiosité technologique : La technologie et l’IA vous passionnent et vous cherchez des façons de les utiliser pour rendre le travail juridique et les processus d’affaires plus efficaces.

ATOUTS

 - Expérience au sein d’une grande banque et d’une plus petite entreprise technologique en démarrage ou fintech, idéalement dans le cadre d’un processus d’obtention de charte bancaire ou de lancement de banque

 - Connaissance de la ligne directrice B-10 du BSIF

RÉMUNÉRATION

L’échelle salariale affichée pour ce poste se situe entre 180 000 $ et 210 000 $ CA par année.

Chez KOHO, nous nous engageons à offrir une transparence salariale à tous les candidats. La rémunération est déterminée en fonction de plusieurs facteurs, notamment les données comparatives du marché canadien, l’évaluation des compétences techniques, l’expérience professionnelle globale du candidat ainsi que l’équité salariale interne au sein de l’équipe KOHO.

KOHO is for builders.

If you’re energized by challenge, motivated by mission, and want to be part of a team that punches above its weight - we want to hear from you.

 

The KOHO culture is one of collaboration, creativity, and diverse perspectives. We are committed to building and fostering an inclusive, accessible environment for everyone. If you have any questions, concerns, or requests regarding accessibility needs, please contact peopleaccessibility@koho.ca and the People and Culture team will be happy to help.

 

AI Disclosure: KOHO uses artificial intelligence (AI) in certain aspects of its recruitment process to screen, assess, or select applicants. For any questions or concerns, please contact us at talent@koho.ca.

Note: this posting is for an existing vacancy that we are seeking to fill.

jobs.description:
ABOUT KOHO

We’re on a mission to make financial services better for every Canadian. That means no hidden fees, no predatory interest rates - just financial products designed to help our users spend smart, save more, and build real wealth. We’re a performance organization with a strong heart: we care deeply about outcomes, and everything ties back to our mission - to financially empower a generation of Canadians.

KOHO is entering its next chapter - leaner, smarter, more AI-integrated. We’re building for impact, not bureaucracy. If you thrive in environments that value clarity, ownership, and bold thinking, you’ll fit right in.

🎯 ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a Sr. Product Manager, Repayments & Recoveries to join our team for a role to work remotely based in Canada. Reporting to the Group Product Manager of Credit, you'll join a fast-paced, cross-functional team that drives KOHO's credit product strategy.

You'll own the roadmap and execution across KOHO's repayments and recoveries service, which includes both revolving and instalment credit products. You'll scale and optimize the services we have for existing credit products and launch services for new credit products that help Canadians borrow on fair, transparent terms. KOHO is building toward becoming a full-service bank, and this role will shape how millions of Canadians access credit. That means helping users borrow responsibly when they need it, and giving them a real path back to good standing when they fall behind.

🚧 WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - You'll be owning the end-to-end product lifecycle for KOHO's installment lending products, from valuations, strategy and PRDs through STO, launch, and ongoing optimization.

 - You'll be creating consistent repayments & recoveries processes across our suite of revolving (Cover, CB, SCB) and installment (Pay Later) credit products

 - You'll be building new lending products from 0 to 1, including Hardship and Settlement loans, to give delinquent users a structured payment plan, reduce losses, and keep the customer relationship intact.

 - You’ll be running experiments and measuring the impact on gross profit from credit products, such as turning on/off on-load collections and pay-date-aligned due dates

 - You'll be working with Lifecycle, Engineering, Design, and Data Science on loan servicing, adjudication models, and decisioning logic, so that borrowing at KOHO is simple, fast, and transparent.

 - You'll be partnering closely with Credit Strategy, Financial Risk, Finance, Compliance, and Legal so that lending products meet regulatory requirements and land on a sound P&L

🧩 WHO YOU ARE

 - You have 5+ years of product management experience, including direct ownership of consumer lending products (e.g. overdraft, lines of credit, personal loans, BNPL, debt consolidation loans).

 - You are highly analytical and commercially minded. You're comfortable pulling your own data in SQL, dbt, or Redshift, and you can build a business case around unit economics, loss rates, and portfolio performance.

 - You have a deep understanding of credit risk and the regulatory landscape for lending in Canada, such as cost of borrowing disclosure, FCAC and OSFI expectations, and credit bureau reporting.

 - You have a strong track record of execution in complex, regulated environments. You break ambiguous problems into clear plans and ship on time with many stakeholders involved.

 - You are AI-native. You use AI tools every day to move faster on analysis, writing, and prototyping, and you bring that mindset to your team.

The budgeted salary range for this role is $160,000 - 190,000 CAD / year. 

At KOHO, we are dedicated to providing pay transparency to all candidates. Compensation at KOHO is determined through various factors including but not limited to: comparable salary market data within Canada, technical skill assessment, a holistic view of previous work history, and internal pay equity with other KOHO team members.

DESCRIPTION DE POSTE EN FRANÇAIS

🎯 À PROPOS DU RÔLE

Nous sommes à la recherche d’un(e) gestionnaire de produit sénior, Recouvrement et perception pour joindre notre équipe dans un rôle en télétravail basé au Canada. Relevant du gestionnaire de produit de groupe - Crédit, vous vous joindrez à une équipe multidisciplinaire dynamique qui façonne la stratégie des produits de crédit de KOHO.

Vous serez responsable de la feuille de route et de l'exécution pour l'ensemble des services de recouvrement et de perception de KOHO, ce qui inclut les produits de crédit renouvelable et de prêt à terme. Vous optimiserez et porterez à l'échelle nos services actuels pour les produits de crédit existants, tout en lançant des services pour de nouveaux produits de crédit qui aident les Canadiens à emprunter à des conditions justes et transparentes. KOHO travaille à devenir une banque de services complets, et ce rôle contribuera à définir la façon dont des millions de Canadiens accèdent au crédit. Cela signifie aider les utilisateurs à emprunter de manière responsable lorsqu'ils en ont besoin, et leur offrir un véritable chemin vers le rétablissement de leur dossier lorsqu'ils accumulent du retard.

🚧 CE QUE VOUS FERIEZ DANS CE RÔLE

 - Vous prendrez en charge l'ensemble du cycle de vie des produits de prêts à terme de KOHO, allant des évaluations, de la stratégie et des documents d'exigences de produit (PRD) jusqu'à l'enregistrement (STO), au lancement et à l'optimisation continue.

 - Vous créerez des processus harmonisés de recouvrement et de perception pour toute notre gamme de produits de crédit renouvelable (Cover, CB, SCB) et de prêt à terme (Pay Later), incluant un centre de recouvrement directement dans l'application.

 - Vous concevrez de nouveaux produits de prêt de A à Z (de 0 à 1), comme des prêts pour difficultés financières ou pour règlement de dette, afin d'offrir aux utilisateurs en souffrance un plan de remboursement structuré, de réduire les pertes et de préserver la relation client.

 - Vous réaliserez des expérimentations et mesurerez l'impact sur le profit brut généré par les produits de crédit (ex. : activer ou désactiver le recouvrement lors du chargement de fonds, ou aligner les dates d'échéance sur les jours de paie).

 - Vous travaillerez en collaboration avec les équipes de gestion du cycle de vie client, de génie logiciel, de design et de science des données sur la gestion des prêts, les modèles d'octroi et la logique de décision, afin d'assurer que l'expérience d'emprunt chez KOHO demeure simple, rapide et transparente.

 - Vous travaillerez en partenariat étroit avec les équipes de stratégie de crédit, de risque financier, de finances, de conformité et des affaires juridiques pour veiller à ce que les produits de prêt respectent les exigences réglementaires tout en appuyant des états financiers (P&L) solides.
 
 

🧩 VOTRE PROFIL

 - Vous cumulez plus de 5 ans d'expérience en gestion de produits, incluant la responsabilité directe de produits de prêt aux consommateurs (ex. : marges d'emboursement/découvert, lignes de crédit, prêts personnels, prêt à l'achat à versements/BNPL, prêts de consolidation de dettes).

 - Vous avez un esprit hautement analytique et commercial. Vous êtes à l'aise d'extraire vos propres données avec SQL, dbt ou Redshift, et vous savez bâtir une étude d'opportunité (business case) axée sur la rentabilité unitaire, les taux de perte et la performance du portefeuille.

 - Vous possédez une compréhension approfondie du risque de crédit et du cadre réglementaire du secteur des prêts au Canada, notamment en ce qui a trait à la divulgation du coût du crédit, aux exigences de l'ACFC et du BSIF, ainsi qu'à la transmission de renseignements aux bureaux de crédit.

 - Vous avez de solides antécédents en matière d'exécution au sein d'environnements complexes et réglementés. Vous savez structurer des problèmes ambigus en plans clairs et livrer dans les délais en coordonnant de nombreuses parties prenantes.

 - Vous maîtrisez naturellement l'IA (AI-native). Vous utilisez au quotidien les outils d'IA pour accélérer vos analyses, la rédaction et le prototypage, et vous transmettez cette mentalité à votre équipe.
