jobs.title: Loss Mitigation Analysis Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT KOHO

We’re on a mission to make financial services better for every Canadian. That means no hidden fees, no predatory interest rates - just financial products designed to help our users spend smart, save more, and build real wealth. We’re a performance organization with a strong heart: we care deeply about outcomes, and everything ties back to our mission - to financially empower a generation of Canadians.

At KOHO, we’re not your average 9-5. We believe real impact comes from people who are trusted, empowered, and supported to do their best work - without sacrificing their lives to do it. We prioritize work-life integration, not just work-life balance. That means asynchronous collaboration, flexible hours, and a remote-first setup built around autonomy and high trust.

KOHO is entering its next chapter - leaner, smarter, more AI-integrated. We’re building for impact, not bureaucracy. If you thrive in environments that value clarity, ownership, and bold thinking, you’ll fit right in.

ABOUT THE ROLE

KOHO is looking for a Loss Mitigation Analysis Manager to build and own our collections and recoveries strategy across KOHO's lending portfolio.

This is a rare opportunity to design a collections program at a company transitioning to a full-service bank — one where you'll set the collections and recovery strategy, define the operating model, and directly influence how we treat customers at their most financially vulnerable moments.

The role's primary mandate is end-to-end collections and recoveries, from early-stage delinquency intervention through post-charge-off recovery and customer rehabilitation. As part of KOHO's broader Credit Strategy team, you will work closely with Credit Strategy and underwriting analysts to connect underwriting insights with observed repayment, delinquency, loss, and recovery outcomes.

You'll work closely with Operations and Product to design contact strategies, payment programs, and customer-first recovery experiences that reduce losses while treating customers with dignity and respect.

In addition to its collections and recoveries mandate, the role provides analytical support for fraud and merchant disputes and performance analytics oversight for third party-supported operational queues outside collections and recoveries. This role sits at the intersection of collections, credit risk, analytics, and operations. The right person is comfortable in the data, decisive under ambiguity, and motivated by the idea that collections done well is a form of customer care.

 

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

COLLECTIONS STRATEGY & CUSTOMER TREATMENT

 - Own the monitoring and analysis of KOHO's delinquency and loss trends across all lending products — flow rates, vintage performance, and charge-off trajectories.

 - Build and maintain dashboards and reporting frameworks that give leadership clear visibility into portfolio health and collections performance; define and track key measures including contact rates, collections by delinquency stage and recovery rates.

 - Identify early warning signals of credit deterioration and propose proactive intervention strategies.

 - Design and continuously optimize contact strategies across the delinquency lifecycle, including timing, channels, messaging, and frequency; develop customer segments and treatments based on delinquency stage, risk profile, payment behaviour, and responsiveness.

 - Partner with Product to design payment arrangements — including hardship plans, instalment options, fee suppression, and settlement / partial forgiveness offers — and define eligibility criteria, discount frameworks, and authorization protocols.

 - Ensure contact strategies comply with applicable regulations, including FCAC guidelines on debt collection conduct and OSFI expectations for a federally regulated lender.

RECOVERIES & CUSTOMER REHABILITATION

 - Develop the strategy for post-charge-off debt recovery, including internal recovery and potential third-party debt placement

 - Design the customer rehabilitation (win-back) program — defining the criteria and pathway for customers who have previously defaulted to re-engage with KOHO's products, and the risk controls required to manage that re-entry.

 - Collaborate with Credit Strategy on the policy framework for re-qualifying defaulted customers for new credit products.

OPERATIONS, BPO & DISPUTES ANALYTICS

 - Lead the strategy for KOHO's future third-party collections partners, including scope by delinquency stage, channel coverage (chat, dialling), performance standards, and escalation frameworks.

 - Work with Operations to develop performance scorecards and review quality, compliance, and outcomes; help design the internal versus external collections model, including which segments to manage in-house and when to place accounts with external third parties.

 - Provide analytical support for fraud and merchant disputes, helping the accountable teams assess trends, outcomes, and operational performance.

 - Use queue and vendor performance analysis to surface emerging issues and support operational improvements, while keeping accountability for dispute decisions and non-collections operations with their respective owners.

CREDIT STRATEGY PARTNERSHIP

 - Work closely with underwriting analysts to interpret portfolio performance across the customer lifecycle, connecting underwriting and segmentation characteristics with observed repayment, delinquency, loss, and recovery outcomes.

 - Share collections and recoveries findings — including emerging risk trends, changes in borrower behaviour, and segment-level performance — to inform portfolio analysis and periodic credit policy reviews.

 - Partner across Credit Strategy, Product, Engineering, Data, and Risk teams to support well-documented analysis and implementation of changes affecting the credit lifecycle.

 

WHAT YOU BRING

Required

 - 3–5+ years of experience in collections strategy, recoveries, or credit risk management at a consumer lender, bank, fintech, or credit card company

 - Deep knowledge of the consumer collections lifecycle — from early delinquency through charge-off, third-party placement, and recovery

 - Hands-on experience designing contact strategies, payment arrangement programs, and/or settlement frameworks

 - Experience working with third party vendors, including setting performance standards

 - Strong analytical skills — comfortable building financial models, cohort analyses, and cost-benefit frameworks; SQL proficiency is highly valued

 - Familiarity with Canadian consumer protection and debt collection regulations

 - Excellent communication skills; able to translate analytical findings into operational recommendations and present to senior leadership

Nice to Have

 - Experience at a company building a collections function from scratch or in a high-growth / early-stage environment

 - Familiarity with digital-first collections channels (in-app, chat, push) as a primary contact mechanism — rather than traditional dialling-first models

 - Background in IFRS 9 provisioning and how collections performance feeds into credit loss modelling

 - Experience designing customer hardship or financial wellness programs, particularly within a mandate of treating customers fairly

The budgeted salary range for this role is $130,000-150,000 CAD / year. 

At KOHO, we are dedicated to providing pay transparency to all candidates. Compensation at KOHO is determined through various factors including but not limited to: comparable salary market data within Canada, technical skill assessment, a holistic view of previous work history, and internal pay equity with other KOHO team members.

DESCRIPTION DE POSTE EN FRANÇAIS
À PROPOS DU POSTE

KOHO est à la recherche d'une ou d'un gestionnaire, Analyse de l'atténuation des pertes, pour bâtir et piloter notre stratégie de recouvrement et de récupération pour l'ensemble du portefeuille de prêts de KOHO.

C'est une occasion rare de concevoir un programme de recouvrement au sein d'une entreprise qui devient une banque à service complet. Vous définirez la stratégie de recouvrement et de récupération ainsi que le modèle opérationnel, et vous aurez une influence directe sur la façon dont nous traitons notre clientèle dans ses moments de plus grande vulnérabilité financière.

Le mandat principal du poste couvre le recouvrement et la récupération de bout en bout : de l'intervention dès les premiers retards de paiement jusqu'à la récupération après radiation et à la réhabilitation de la clientèle. En tant que membre de l'équipe Stratégie de crédit de KOHO, vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les analystes en stratégie de crédit et en souscription afin de relier les constats de souscription aux résultats observés en matière de remboursement, de retards de paiement, de pertes et de récupération.

Vous collaborerez étroitement avec les équipes Opérations et Produit pour concevoir des stratégies de contact, des programmes de paiement et des expériences de récupération centrées sur la clientèle, qui réduisent les pertes tout en traitant chaque personne avec dignité et respect.

En plus de son mandat de recouvrement et de récupération, le poste offre un soutien analytique pour la fraude et les litiges marchands, ainsi qu'une supervision de l'analyse de performance des files de travail opérationnelles soutenues par des tiers, hors recouvrement et récupération. Ce rôle se situe au croisement du recouvrement, du risque de crédit, de l'analytique et des opérations. La personne idéale est à l'aise dans les données, sait trancher dans l'ambiguïté et est motivée par l'idée qu'un recouvrement bien fait est une forme de soin envers la clientèle.

CE QUE VOUS FEREZ

Stratégie de recouvrement et traitement de la clientèle

 - Assurer le suivi et l'analyse des tendances de retards de paiement et de pertes pour l'ensemble des produits de prêt de KOHO : taux de migration, performance par cohorte (millésime) et trajectoires de radiation.

 - Concevoir et tenir à jour des tableaux de bord et des cadres de reddition de comptes qui donnent à la direction une vision claire de la santé du portefeuille et de la performance du recouvrement; définir et suivre les indicateurs clés, notamment les taux de contact, les montants recouvrés par stade de retard et les taux de récupération.

 - Repérer les signaux précurseurs de détérioration du crédit et proposer des stratégies d'intervention proactives.

 - Concevoir et optimiser en continu les stratégies de contact tout au long du cycle de retard de paiement, y compris le moment, les canaux, les messages et la fréquence; développer des segments de clientèle et des traitements selon le stade de retard, le profil de risque, le comportement de paiement et la réceptivité.

 - Collaborer avec l'équipe Produit pour concevoir des ententes de paiement, notamment des plans pour difficultés financières, des options de versements, la suspension de frais et des offres de règlement ou de remise partielle, et définir les critères d'admissibilité, les cadres d'escompte et les protocoles d'autorisation.

 - Veiller à ce que les stratégies de contact respectent la réglementation applicable, y compris les lignes directrices de l'ACFC sur les pratiques de recouvrement et les attentes du BSIF envers un prêteur sous réglementation fédérale.

Récupération et réhabilitation de la clientèle

 - Élaborer la stratégie de récupération des créances après radiation, y compris la récupération à l'interne et le placement éventuel auprès d'agences de recouvrement tierces.

 - Concevoir le programme de réhabilitation (reconquête) de la clientèle, en définissant les critères et le parcours permettant aux clients ayant déjà été en défaut de paiement de revenir vers les produits de KOHO, ainsi que les contrôles de risque nécessaires pour encadrer ce retour.

 - Collaborer avec l'équipe Stratégie de crédit à l'élaboration du cadre de politique visant la requalification des clients en défaut pour de nouveaux produits de crédit.

Opérations, impartition (BPO) et analytique des litiges

 - Diriger la stratégie relative aux futurs partenaires de recouvrement tiers de KOHO, y compris la portée selon le stade de retard, la couverture des canaux (clavardage, appels), les normes de performance et les cadres d'escalade.

 - Travailler avec l'équipe Opérations pour élaborer des fiches de performance et évaluer la qualité, la conformité et les résultats; contribuer à la conception du modèle de recouvrement interne et externe, notamment quels segments gérer à l'interne et à quel moment confier des comptes à des tiers.

 - Offrir un soutien analytique pour la fraude et les litiges marchands, en aidant les équipes responsables à évaluer les tendances, les résultats et la performance opérationnelle.

 - S'appuyer sur l'analyse de la performance des files de travail et des fournisseurs pour faire ressortir les enjeux émergents et soutenir l'amélioration des opérations, tout en laissant la responsabilité des décisions sur les litiges et des opérations hors recouvrement à leurs responsables respectifs.

Partenariat avec la Stratégie de crédit

 - Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les analystes en souscription pour interpréter la performance du portefeuille tout au long du cycle de vie client, en reliant les caractéristiques de souscription et de segmentation aux résultats observés en matière de remboursement, de retards de paiement, de pertes et de récupération.

 - Partager les constats en matière de recouvrement et de récupération, notamment les tendances de risque émergentes, l'évolution du comportement des emprunteurs et la performance par segment, afin d'alimenter l'analyse du portefeuille et les révisions périodiques de la politique de crédit.

 - Collaborer avec les équipes Stratégie de crédit, Produit, Ingénierie, Données et Risque pour soutenir une analyse bien documentée et la mise en œuvre des changements touchant le cycle de vie du crédit.

jobs.title: Senior Analytics Engineer - Finance
jobs.description:
BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

 

We’re looking for a Senior Analytics Engineer to join Kraken’s Finance Data Eng & Analytics team within Data Platform. You’ll build trusted financial data products, using automation and AI to reduce manual work and improve the close process.

Working at the intersection of data engineering and accounting, you’ll turn complex financial data into reliable pipelines, models and automated reconciliations. You’ll use AI-assisted tools to accelerate development and investigations, keeping financial outputs tested and traceable.

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - You’ll work closely with Data Engineers, Finance and Platform Accounting to improve reporting and decision-making. Clear communication and collaboration will help you agree priorities, explain findings and drive adoption.

 - Partner with Finance to understand workflows, identify pain points and translate business needs into practical data and automation solutions.

 - Build and maintain automated workflows for data preparation, reconciliations, reporting and follow-ups, with clear controls, monitoring and exception handling.

 - Build intuitive dashboards and visualizations that help stakeholders understand performance, investigate issues and make decisions.

 - Resolve finance data issues and reconciliation breaks with Finance, Product and Engineering, addressing root causes and communicating progress.

 - Build scalable, reliable pipelines to collect, transform and curate data from internal platforms and external systems.

 - Support the design and rollout of a trusted finance data lake, with clear definitions, ownership and quality checks.

 - Improve data timeliness, enabling near-real-time insights where they add business value.

 - Evaluate new technologies, including AI-assisted automation, and prototype solutions to Finance needs that can be reliably supported in production.

 

WHAT YOU BRING

 - 7+ years of experience in data analytics and data management within financial services or a regulated industry, working directly with Finance teams.

 - Strong SQL and Python skills, including writing, debugging and maintaining production code.

 - Solid experience with Git, merge requests, and code reviews, supported by strong software engineering practices, including testing and documentation.

 - Hands-on experience building and operating pipelines and models using dbt, Spark, Airflow or comparable tools.

 - Direct experience with finance or accounting data, such as reconciliations, subledgers, cost basis or month-end close, including investigating discrepancies and validating outputs with accounting stakeholders.

 - A track record of owning pipelines end to end, making sound technical decisions and improving reliability as requirements and systems evolve.

 - Judgment and autonomy to lead complex work, navigate ambiguity and remain accountable for production outcomes.

 - Experience supporting recurring financial close activities, combined with a proactive approach to identifying manual processes and replacing them with reliable, sustainable automation.

 - Excellent communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across Engineering and Finance, explain complex technical issues, articulate financial implications, and recommend actionable solutions.

 

NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience with cryptocurrency transaction data and how digital-asset activity flows into financial records and reconciliations.

 - Experience processing large volumes of financial transactions using distributed frameworks such as Spark or PySpark.

Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

OUR COMMITMENT

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto.

We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision.

As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

You’re going to fix that.

THE OPPORTUNITY

We’re seeking a hands-on Head of Organic Growth to own how Kraken Pro gets discovered and how curious traders become active ones. At Kraken, understanding our brand ethos, mission, and the traders we serve is essential. Organic is where brand and acquisition meet.

We’re looking for a player-coach who moves fast but thinks long-term, gets in the weeds while leading from the front, and knows that traffic means nothing if it doesn’t convert. This role demands sharp B2C acquisition instincts, a product-first mindset, an obsession with UX, and a self-starter attitude.

 - Own organic acquisition. Build and run the strategy across SEO, content, social, community, referrals, and partnerships to bring high-intent traders to Kraken Pro.

 - Find out if people convert. Map the funnel from first touch to first trade, report on it clearly, and figure out where traders drop off and how to win them back.

 - Make UX your edge. Work with Product and Design to audit and improve landing pages, sign-up flows, onboarding, and in-product moments. Great acquisition dies in bad UX, and you know it.

 - Acquire through brand. Make every growth channel a brand-building one. Reach is easy to buy; trust is what makes traders stay.

 - Know the product cold. Use Kraken Pro like a trader would, understand what makes it better, and turn those strengths into growth levers.

 - Lead a lean, scrappy team. Set direction, coach, and unblock a small team, while staying hands-on enough to ship, test, and fix things yourself.

 - Test and learn. Run experiments across channels and funnel steps, double down on what works, and kill what doesn’t.

 - Report what matters. Build clear dashboards and insights that show leadership what’s driving growth, what isn’t, and what to do next.

 - Ship responsibly. Partner with Legal/Comms to ensure compliant, accurate, and aligned messaging across regions and platforms.
 
 

WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - 5+ years in B2C acquisition or growth marketing, ideally in fintech, crypto, trading or gaming with experience in a player-coach role leading a small team.

 - Product savvy. You understand how products work, why people use them, and how to turn features into growth.

 - UX instinct. You can spot friction in a flow from a mile away and brief Product and Design on how to fix it.

 - High AI competency. Enabling you to multiply your impact and keep up with demand.

 - Analytical rigor. Comfortable with funnels, cohorts, attribution, and experimentation, and able to turn data into decisions and clear stories.

 - Speed under pressure. Markets don’t wait for approval cycles and neither do you.

 - Range as a marketer. SEO, content, social, lifecycle, partnerships. You know enough about each to direct the work, and you can roll up your sleeves when needed.

 - Taste. Knowing which channels and tactics not to pursue is as valuable as knowing which to scale.

 - Familiarity trading culture, and the language traders use.

 - Strong communication and leadership skills, with the ability to align cross-functional teams around a shared growth goal.

jobs.description:

This role sits within SOX Compliance and is the senior technical authority for IT controls in the SOX program. You will set the strategy for ITGCs, IT application controls, and the controls over private key management and digital asset custody. Internal Audit independently tests the controls you own.

You will own the ITGC SOX program, building the control framework, testing approach, and evidence standards from the ground up. This is a hands-on role with real program ownership at a crypto exchange. The technology stack spans blockchain-native infrastructure, digital asset custody systems, and on-chain and off-chain processing, and engineering changes at a pace most companies never see. The systems are complex, the deployments are frequent, and the controls are consequential.

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Strategy & program ownership
 
 - Own the enterprise IT SOX strategy and roadmap, covering ITGC, ITAC, and digital asset and key management controls across all in-scope entities and jurisdictions.
 
 - Define the scoping methodology and risk assessment for IT SOX, including in-scope applications, infrastructure, wallet and custody systems, and third-party and service-organization dependencies.
 
 - Set control design standards and own the control framework. Design controls that fit modern engineering practices (CI/CD, infrastructure as code, cloud) and don’t slow them down.
 
 - Set the standard for management testing and evidence. Direct co-sourced and matrixed resources, and review the quality of their work.
 
 - Use AI-enabled workflows, continuous controls monitoring, and data analytics to move IT SOX from periodic testing toward scalable, automated assurance.
 
 Private key management & digital asset controls
 
 - Own SOX control design and coverage for the full private key lifecycle: generation, storage, access, signing and approval workflows, rotation, backup and recovery, and retirement.
 
 - Assess controls over key custody architectures, such as HSMs, MPC, multi-signature, and hot/warm/cold wallet structures, including segregation of duties, quorum and approval controls, and privileged access.
 
 - Evaluate how key management and custody controls support the existence, completeness, and safeguarding of customer and corporate digital assets and their financial reporting implications.
 
 - Assess controls over on-chain and off-chain transaction processing, reconciliation of wallets to ledgers, and reliance on blockchain data and third-party custodians or service organizations.
 
 - Be the SOX authority on emerging digital asset risks and decide how the control framework should respond as products, chains, and custody models evolve.
 
 Deficiency evaluation & remediation
 
 - Lead evaluation of control deficiencies, including root cause analysis and severity and pervasiveness assessments, and recommend classification (control deficiency, significant deficiency, or material weakness).
 
 - Own remediation strategy for open ITGC and key management findings. Drive executive-level accountability with Engineering, Security, and Infrastructure leaders.
 
 - Escalate gaps and delays directly to senior leadership. Report status to the Audit Committee as required.
 
 - Coordinate with Internal Audit so remediated controls are ready for independent validation.
 
 Executive & external stakeholder engagement
 
 - Be the senior SOX voice to the CFO, CISO, CTO, Controller, and the Audit Committee on IT control posture, risks, and remediation.
 
 - Lead the external auditor relationship on IT matters: audit strategy, reliance and scoping decisions, walkthroughs, and resolution of disagreements.
 
 - Serve as a trusted advisor to engineering and security leaders, translating audit and control requirements into practical engineering decisions.
 
 - Partner with Internal Audit, ERM, the business process SOX lead, and co-sourced providers to align coverage across the full assurance program.
 
 - Mentor SOX and risk team members and raise the technical bar across the function.

 

WHAT YOU BRING

 - 10+ years in SOX compliance, IT audit, internal audit, or external audit, with deep ITGC experience and a record of owning programs at enterprise scale.

 - Direct, hands-on experience with crypto and private key management controls, including designing, assessing, or auditing controls over key custody, wallet infrastructure, signing, and digital asset safeguarding. This is a must-have.

 - Experience in a crypto exchange, custodian, fintech, or payments company with complex, rapidly evolving infrastructure.

 - CISA and CPA certifications required. Candidates with one who are actively pursuing the other will be considered.

 - Expert knowledge of ITGC frameworks, SOX 404, COSO, COBIT, and PCAOB standards, with the judgment to make and defend scoping, reliance, and deficiency-classification decisions.

 - Strong technical fluency in how systems, databases, cloud infrastructure, and deployment pipelines work.

 - Proven ability to connect an ITGC or key management failure to its impact on business process controls and the financial statements.

 - Experience working with external auditors (Big 4 preferred) and presenting to Audit Committees and senior executives.

 - Experience across multi-entity structures or multiple jurisdictions.

 - Exceptional communicator who earns credibility with both engineers and finance executives.

NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience building or scaling an IT SOX program in a growth-stage or first-year SOX company.

 - Familiarity with CI/CD, GitLab or similar version control, and cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP).

 - Familiarity with SOC 1/SOC 2 reliance for custodians and service providers, and with proof-of-reserves or similar attestations.

 - Familiarity with audit and GRC platforms such as AuditBoard or Workiva.

 - Familiarity with AI-assisted compliance tools and willingness to adopt new technologies.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager - Payments Platform
jobs.description:
BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

THE TEAM

Payward Services is an enterprise infrastructure platform that enables companies to seamlessly integrate trading, payments, funding, and digital asset services through a single unified system. It provides coordinated liquidity, custody, compliance, risk management, and settlement capabilities, reducing operational complexity for fintechs, banks, brokerages, and payment providers.

Payward's Payments & Blockchain team owns the first and last mile of every dollar that moves in or out of its products. That means dozens of banking partners, PSPs and local rails powering deposits and withdrawals for millions of users.

The team is looking for a product manager to shape the future of this platform, from the architecture underneath to the API layer internal clients build on. At the center is Payward's in-house PSP: a scalable, multi-tenant payments backend with hosted pages, SDKs, embedded components and direct APIs, so any Payward business can plug in and reach pay-in and payout rails worldwide.

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Own the product vision and roadmap for the Payward payments platform, covering both the shared backend and the integration surfaces internal clients build on (hosted pages, SDKs, embedded components and direct APIs)

 - Map requirements across internal clients and use them to evolve the platform's vision and capabilities so it serves a growing range of use cases

 - Partner with engineering to turn the target vision into a sequenced, high-impact roadmap, with milestones every client team can plan against

 - Prioritize across competing client needs, make the trade-offs visible, and say no with a clear rationale

 - Shape the client experience end to end, from first conversation to go-live, so teams can adopt the platform without heavy hand-holding

 - Work with the banking and partnerships teams so each new PSP or bank integration is built once on the platform and reaches every Payward business

 - Bring compliance, risk and legal requirements across Payward's entities and jurisdictions into the roadmap early, before they become launch blockers

 - Set and track platform success metrics, such as time to launch a rail for an existing client, time for a new client to go live, share of rails available through the platform, and payment success rates

 
 

WHAT YOU BRING

 - 5+ years of product management experience, ideally in a platform, API or infrastructure role where your customers were other internal teams or developers

 - Working knowledge of payments: pay-ins and payouts, PSPs and acquirers, bank rails (ACH, SEPA, Faster Payments, SWIFT and local methods), and how money flows between them

 - Strong technical fluency. You can read an RFC, challenge an architecture decision, and write an API spec that engineers respect

 - Experience shipping developer-facing products such as APIs, SDKs, or embeddable UI components

 - Clear, structured writing. You turn complex system designs into docs that product, compliance and business stakeholders can all act on

 - Skill at managing many stakeholders with different priorities, and building alignment without direct authority

 - Comfort working with data to set goals and measure platform adoption and performance

 
 

NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience at a PSP, payment orchestrator or payments infrastructure company, or building one in-house

 - Background with multi-tenant SaaS or B2B2C platforms

 - Familiarity with crypto, stablecoins or on/off-ramps

 - Experience working across multiple regulated legal entities or licensing regimes

Kraken's Market Surveillance function is responsible for detecting, investigating and reporting market abuse across our regulated trading venues, spanning spot crypto markets, crypto futures, tokenised equities, OTC markets, and consumer trading. As our licensing footprint and product range grow, so does the scale and complexity of the surveillance programme behind them.

We're hiring a Principal Compliance Associate to take on the function's most complex casework, and help shape how we detect and cover market abuse as the business scales.

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Own complex investigations end to end, writing findings up to a standard a regulator can rely on, and present conclusions to a range of stakeholders.

 - Lead or contribute to periodic threshold and model reviews, recalibrating surveillance rules and alert thresholds as trading behaviour, products and market structure evolve.

 - Support the design, build-out and integration of surveillance platform capability, including onboarding new products, venues and data sources onto the surveillance system.

 - Contribute to market abuse risk assessments, helping identify and score risk across products, jurisdictions and entities, and translate findings into surveillance coverage.

 - Use AI and automation tools responsibly to speed up evidence-gathering, case reconstruction and detection-model development, always with human judgement over the final call.

 - Support conflicts of interest, information barrier, and personal account dealing matters across Markets Compliance, extending beyond surveillance casework where buy-side or asset management experience is directly relevant.

 
 

WHAT YOU BRING

 - Experience investigating market abuse or trading conduct inside a firm subject to market conduct regulation, such as an exchange, broker-dealer, trading venue, or comparable regulated trading business.

 - A track record running investigations end to end, including writing findings up to a standard a regulator can rely on and presenting conclusions to stakeholders.

 - Working knowledge of core market abuse typologies e.g. spoofing, wash trading, insider trading, front running, ramping.

 - Experience with, or strong working knowledge of, threshold and model calibration, surveillance platform integration, market abuse risk assessments, and audit remediation.

 - Comfort using generative AI and other automation tools to improve the speed and quality of investigative work, while maintaining the human oversight regulated casework requires.

 - Familiarity with a surveillance platform (such as Scila, Nasdaq SMARTS, Eventus, or NICE Actimize) and comfort with SQL or a similar query tool for evidence-gathering.

 - Clear, evidence-first written communication - your case files, escalations and regulatory drafts will sometimes be read by auditors and regulators without you in the room to explain them.

jobs.description:
BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

 

THE TEAM

Kraken's Consumer Creative & Design team owns end-to-end creative execution for Kraken Consumer and Krak. Our disciplines cover performance ad creative, brand design, motion design, AI video creative and web design. We turn growth strategy into creative that converts across paid, owned and organic surfaces. We work closely with Product Marketing, Performance Marketing, Content & Social, Lifecycle and our regional leads, and we hold the line on brand and messaging quality on everything that ships.

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

As our Staff Brand Designer, you come to the table with a strong design vision and set the visual standard for Kraken. You design static work for launches, campaigns and always-on activity, and you make sure it looks like one brand wherever someone meets it. You can take a brief or proactive idea to a finished, approved asset set, and you're comfortable building a clean, systemized layout in Figma. If you can also model and render a hero 3D asset in Cinema 4D, that's a real bonus.

You report to the Creative Lead, Consumer Creative & Design, who gives you direction, feedback and cover in reviews. This is a senior individual contributor role with no direct reports. Senior here means craft and ownership: you set the bar for brand quality on the team, you build systems others can work from, and you're the person colleagues come to with design questions.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design static creative for Kraken across product launches, campaigns, promotions and always-on activity.

 - Apply and extend the Kraken Consumer brand across surfaces, from organic social, lifecycle and web to illustration and foundational projects like key visual updates, keeping everything cohesive and recognizable without making it repetitive.

 - Design initiative-specific work, including a distinct look and partner-branded assets for launches, and purpose-built illustration for go-to-market and product moments.

 - Build scalable systems: Figma component libraries, marketing templates and modular campaign kits with localization-ready layouts, so other designers, other teams and our automated workflows can produce on-brand work quickly.

 - Use AI-assisted production as a core part of how the brand gets made, and know when it speeds the work up and when it doesn't.

 - Bring ideas to briefs rather than executing them literally. Push back with a point of view when a brief is unclear or the idea can be stronger.

 - Version and localize work across markets, languages and formats, with layouts that hold up under translation and market-specific requirements.

 - Partner with Product Marketing, compliance and regional teams to get work approved without losing the idea.

 - Collaborate closely with our motion, web, performance and AI video designers so work travels well across formats.

 - Hold a high craft bar on your own work and give clear, constructive feedback on others'.

 

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 7+ years of brand and static design experience at a high-volume in-house team or agency, ideally in fintech, crypto or another regulated category (a competitor or similar company is a big plus).

 - A portfolio that proves it, submitted with your application. Include the brief or objective alongside the work and the result where you're able to share it. We'd like to see brand and static work, an example of work you adapted for multiple formats or markets, and an example of a system or template set that other people built from. If you have 3D work, include a piece with a short note on your process.

 - Expert-level Figma: components, auto layout, variables, and files that are easy to hand off and build on.

 - Strong layout, hierarchy, type and composition that hold up at small sizes and in multiple languages.

 - Hands-on experience with AI-assisted production tools, and good judgment about where they belong in a workflow.

 - Comfort working inside regulatory constraints, including layouts that accommodate risk warnings, disclaimers and market-specific requirements without compromising the design.

 - Working fluency in Adobe CC (Photoshop, Illustrator, and After Effects for light motion).

 - Speed without sloppiness. You're comfortable with fast turnarounds, several review rounds and late changes.

 - A solid instinct for plain language and clear communication: value first, no hype, no jargon.

 - Curious about investing and crypto at a minimum, and able to make the space legible to others.

We are looking for a Head of VIP, Asia to lead and grow Payward VIP presence across the region. This is a player-coach role: you will build and lead a small, high-performing team while personally owning strategic client relationships, originating new business, and shaping the regional growth playbook.

You will set the standard for how Kraken serves, retains, and grows its most valuable private clients in Asia. That means testing new ideas, learning fast, dropping what doesn’t work, and scaling what does. If you’re bold, comfortable with ambiguity, and humble enough to fail fast and move on, this is your seat.

 
 

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Lead, coach, and develop VIP relationship managers in Asia; establish clear standards for client coverage, pipeline management, service quality, and commercial performance.

jobs.description:
BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

 

Kraken's Compliance Operations teams, including the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU), investigations and enhanced due diligence, are the front line of how Kraken detects and responds to financial crime. The systems they run on sit within Core Services Product, alongside the engineering teams who build them. That covers alert ingestion, case management, investigator tooling and a growing set of automation and AI tools.

 

This role owns the product for that investigation platform. That means how an alert is created, enriched, grouped and suppressed. How it becomes a case. How an investigator reaches and documents a decision. And how every step is evidenced to a regulator or auditor. You'll start with the FIU, where the workflows are most complex and the audit bar is highest, then extend the platform across Compliance Operations.

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Own the investigation-platform roadmap end to end. Sequence it and defend it, and re-sequence it when a regulator or the RCO raises a P0.

 - Define "done" before build starts. Write phased deliverables and acceptance criteria that Compliance signs off, and hold the line when scope moves.

 - Get requirements in before engineering starts. Build the intake between Compliance policy, monitoring rules and case management so that changes don't reach investigators before their workflows are ready.

 - Understand the process before building. Reconcile policy and SOPs against what investigators actually do and what the system actually does. Know the difference between a process fix and a technical one, and say which requests are in scope for engineering.

 - Understand the pipeline well enough to challenge it: ingestion, profile and transaction resolution, suppression and grouping logic, and reconciliation between vendor output and case management. Be able to walk an auditor through it with live examples.

 - Make auditability a first-class requirement: audit trail, data lineage, evidence retention, reviewer attribution, change-management controls, and validation of filtering and suppression logic.

 - Ship automation and AI into regulated workflows with controls that hold up in Compliance, IT and privacy audits. That means human-in-the-loop design, explainability and ongoing monitoring.

 - Run the operating rhythm: a shared forum with engineering and adjacent product managers, a regular stakeholder update, and one delivery status that everyone reads the same way.

 

WHAT YOU BRING

 - 4+ years of product management, including 2+ years on financial-crime systems such as transaction monitoring, investigations, case management, KYC/EDD or sanctions screening.

 - Working knowledge of how an AML programme is examined, including the questions regulators, internal audit and model validation ask about monitoring, filing and control systems.

 - The technical fluency to go deep on data flows and system design with engineers, and to spot when a design won't meet the requirement.

 - A track record of shipping internal tools or operational platforms that measurably changed how an operations team works.

 - Clear, concise writing, from PRDs and phase plans to audit walkthroughs and executive updates.

 - The judgement to tell a senior stakeholder a timeline isn't realistic because the requirements aren't written yet, and to keep the relationship intact.

 
 

NICE TO HAVES

 - Direct FIU experience, such as alert disposition, SAR/STR filing or leading investigators.

 - Crypto or digital-asset experience, such as blockchain analytics, wallet-level transaction analysis or focal vs counterparty logic.

 - Experience shipping AI or ML into a regulated investigative workflow, including the control design.

 - Build-vs-buy and vendor evaluation for monitoring or case-management tooling.

 - Experience with programmes that span jurisdictions (UK, EU/MiCA, US).

jobs.description:
BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

 

Kraken’s Consumer Creative & Design team owns end-to-end creative execution for Kraken. Our disciplines cover performance ad creative, 2D and 3D design, motion design, AI video creative and web design, turning growth strategy into creative that converts across paid, owned and organic surfaces. We work closely with Product Marketing, Performance Marketing, Content & Social, Lifecycle and our regional leads, holding the line on brand and messaging quality on everything that ships.

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

Great creative starts with a sharp idea, and the earlier it arrives, the better the work gets. As our Creative Strategist & Copywriter, you bring ideas in at the start of a campaign to define the creative challenge, develop the brief and write the messaging that carries it across channels.

 

You’ll turn audience insights, business goals and performance data into concept-led briefs for paid static and motion, landing pages, organic social and partnerships content, then write the headlines, scripts and copy that carry each concept across the customer journey. You’ll also help Product Marketing and Performance Marketing sharpen their own briefs.

 

This role is for a proactive self-starter. Nobody will hand you the idea: you go and find it, pitch it, write it and help get it made.

 

You report to the Creative Director, who gives you direction, feedback and cover in reviews. This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports. jobs.title: Senior Product Manager - Social Networking
jobs.description:
BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

We’re hiring a Product Manager with deep UX and interaction design expertise to build social experiences around investing and trading at Kraken.

You should be comfortable designing flows yourself, building interactive prototypes, and working through interaction details with designers and engineers. You’ll also own the product decisions: which customer problem to solve, what to ship first, and how to measure whether the experience improved.

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Design complete social journeys. Work through how someone discovers a person, decides to follow them, shares an idea or trade, receives a response, and returns. Connect these interactions into an experience users understand without explanation.

 - Make the interaction details work. Shape navigation, information hierarchy, copy, defaults, gestures, and feedback. Specify what happens when a feed is empty, a post fails, content loads slowly, or someone changes their mind.

 - Prototype before committing to a build. Turn ideas into interactive prototypes that communicate the intended behavior. Explore alternatives, test the uncertain parts, and give engineering clear flows, states, and acceptance criteria.

 - Use psychology to improve participation. Understand why people hesitate to post, seek recognition, follow strangers, or respond to others. Translate those motivations into decisions about audience visibility, prompts, reputation, feedback, and the effort required to contribute.

 - Observe users and fix what gets in their way. Run usability sessions, watch people complete tasks, and combine those observations with funnel data. Identify where people misunderstand the product, lose confidence, or abandon an action.

 - Design for first use and repeated use. Make the experience useful before someone has connections. Keep sharing lightweight during an active trading session, with clear control over what becomes public. Test the twentieth interaction as carefully as the first.

 - Connect design decisions to measurable outcomes. For each significant change, define the expected behavior and how to test it. Track task completion, abandonment, first follows, first contributions, responses, and subsequent retention. Work with data science to evaluate experiments and effects on both contributors and their audiences.

 - Take the experience through launch. Choose a focused initial scope, resolve trade-offs with engineering, review the implementation against the intended design, and use post-launch evidence to decide what to improve next.

WHAT YOU BRING

 - Has designed and shipped consumer social experiences. Your portfolio shows your contribution to feeds, profiles, sharing, messaging, discovery, or communities—and how the experience changed after launch.

 - Has strong interaction design craft. You can explain why a flow is structured a particular way, what users will notice first, what they need to understand, and which decisions or steps can be removed.

 - Can build realistic interactive prototypes. You use Figma, code, AI tools, or a combination to make behavior tangible and testable, including transitions, empty states, and failure states.

 - Understands behavior through evidence. You can show where user research challenged your assumptions and changed a design.

 - Can own product outcomes. You can prioritize a problem, define success, interpret funnel and cohort data, and explain whether an experiment produced a meaningful improvement.

 - Understands the context of social finance. You account for how credibility, incentives, reputation, and visibility of financial activity affect what people trust and choose to share.

xStocks brings real-world assets on-chain as tokenized securities that are regulated, fully-backed, and tradable across multiple blockchains. Built within Payward, the xStocks team runs the infrastructure that issues, custodies, and settles these instruments across EVM, Solana, TON, Tron, and more. The platform moves real value, so security is not a feature bolted on at the end. It is a property of everything the team ships. This is a hybrid engineering and security seat built for someone who is genuinely both: you ship products alongside the engineering team when the security queue is quiet, and you own security work end to end when it lands. You report into engineering and partner closely with the Payward security, CISO, and compliance functions.

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Own security deliverables end to end. Coordinate and review smart-contract audits, respond to security questionnaires and due-diligence requests, support CISO and compliance initiatives, and turn findings into tracked, closed-out fixes.

 - Run offensive assessments against our own platforms. Pentest the web apps, APIs, backend services, and on-chain components, and build the tooling to do it repeatedly rather than once.

 - Continuously assess posture. Threat-model new and existing systems, review architecture and key-management flows, and maintain a living view of the risks and their mitigations.

 - Review code for security. Be a default reviewer on changes touching auth, cryptography, custody, signing, and fund movement across our chains.

 - Harden the platform. Improve secrets handling, IAM and least-privilege, dependency and supply-chain hygiene, and detection and logging for security-relevant events.

 - Secure custody and signing workflows. Review and harden transaction signing flows, MPC and HSM integrations, signer permissions, admin roles, approval policies, and break-glass procedures.

 - Contribute to product engineering. Pick up regular backlog work in TypeScript so you stay close to the codebase you are defending.

 - Support incidents. Help with detection, triage, response, and post-mortems, and feed the lessons back into the program.

WHAT YOU BRING

 - An engineer first. You write and review production code comfortably, TypeScript and Node.js in our stack, and you understand systems deeply enough to break them.

 - Strong application and infrastructure security fundamentals. The OWASP-class vulnerability landscape, authn and authz, injection, SSRF, supply-chain risk, and secure design. You have done real offensive work in pentesting, vuln research, or red-team.

 - Applied cryptography and blockchain security. Symmetric and asymmetric primitives, hashing, signatures, and key management, plus the security model of EVM, Solana, and ideally TON or Tron. You can read a smart contract and reason about how it fails.

 - Ownership. You can take an ambiguous security item, an audit, a questionnaire, or an incident, and drive it to closure without being managed through it.

 - Clear communication. You can explain a risk to engineers, to a CISO, and to an auditor, and tailor the message to each.

 - An automation instinct. You do not want to catch the same issue manually twice, so you turn findings into tests, alerts, controls, documentation, or platform improvements.

 - Risk judgment. You can tell a theoretical issue from a material one, and communicate severity, likelihood, impact, and remediation tradeoffs clearly.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience commissioning or remediating third-party smart-contract audits.

 - Familiarity with custody and signing infrastructure such as HSMs, MPC, and ForDefi-style providers, and with on-chain transaction security.

 - Cloud security depth in GCP or AWS, IAM, and container and runtime hardening.

 - Detection engineering and security observability, including SIEM and log-based detections.

 - Relevant certifications such as OSCP, OSWE, or GWAPT.

 - Prior work in a regulated fintech or tokenization/DeFi environment.

You will own the trade operating model, the end-to-end order and settlement flow, cash flows, corporate actions, reconciliations, and regulatory readiness across the business.

This is a hands-on leadership role in a regulated entity. You will be a registered principal of Kraken Securities LLC, named on Form BD, and accountable for the operational side of the firm’s regulatory obligations. It extends well beyond day-to-day management and requires genuine fluency in both traditional market plumbing and the operational realities of a digital-asset business.

You will stay close to company strategy and cross-functional initiatives so the global executive team’s goals translate into clear operating priorities. As a trusted partner, you will work across Compliance, Legal, Finance, Product, Engineering, and Marketing to drive key initiatives forward, and build the team that scales the business as the firm grows.

The opportunity

 - Own the end-to-end US equities order flow, from inception through clearing and settlement, including reconciliation, corporate actions, and exception management.

 - Own equities operations, including token issuance and redemption, inventory and liquidity management, movement of client and firm assets, and settlement across exchange, custodian, and on-chain venues.

 - Serve as a named principal of Kraken Securities LLC and as an operational control point, providing dual-approval (“four eyes”) sign-off on transactions and asset movements, with coverage across time zones.

 - Design and implement the operating model for Kraken Securities aligned to strategic goals, and contribute to strategy and growth planning to help build a sustainable business.

 - Build and run the operating systems for the business (policies, written supervisory procedures, controls, books and records, and business continuity), translating C-suite goals into clear targets for each business unit, then setting performance targets, tracking progress, and reporting KPIs and costs transparently to leadership.

 - Own launch readiness for new products and markets by preparing systems, policies, and procedures, and testing them end to end with clearing, custody, exchange, and R&D partners to ensure US regulatory compliance.

 - Ensure desk coverage, settlement and reconciliation controls, and staffing are in place to support 24x5 and the transition to 24x7, and own severity-1 escalation and incident response for the US entities, including root-cause review and remediation.

 - Partner with Finance on controls around bank payments, customer funds, and reserve requirements, and own vendor and partner operations (clearing, custody, market data, liquidity providers, and technology), including onboarding, SLAs, and ongoing oversight.

 - Hire and develop a high-performing operations team, build the licensing bench and succession plan, and design the organizational structure to scale.

 - Partner with Marketing, Compliance, Product, Engineering, and Operations to keep initiatives aligned and moving, and support HR and IT in building procedures that link to corporate strategy.

What you bring

 - 12+ years in brokerage, fintech, or operations consulting, including time inside a FINRA-registered broker-dealer, and experience in crypto, brokerage, advisory, fintech, or another highly regulated industry.

 - In-depth knowledge of traditional markets: execution, clearing, settlement, custody, margin, securities lending, and corporate actions.

 - Working understanding of digital assets and tokenized securities, including custody models, on-chain settlement, and the controls they demand.

 - Direct experience under SEC and FINRA rules: books and records, supervisory procedures, trade reporting, and examination response.

 - Experience standing up or scaling operations for a new regulated product or entity, including launch readiness and regulatory approvals.

The primary goal of this role is to elevate decision-making by uncovering emerging trends and root causes, and by driving insights and actions that provide full visibility into business performance and operational efficiency.

Beyond technical expertise, success in this role depends on being a true business partner who combines data-driven insights with strategic thinking to deliver actionable recommendations, guide decision-making, and drive measurable impact across the organization.

In this role, you'll own end-to-end data management, from building and maintaining datasets and pipelines to designing dashboards and delivering insights for the Compliance team. A core part of this role is owning the logic and rule-setting behind transaction monitoring across deposits and withdrawals. You'll also contribute to experimentation infrastructure, laying the groundwork for future ML and intelligence initiatives.

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Own the logic and rule-setting behind transaction monitoring across deposits and withdrawals, partnering closely with Compliance to study patterns and refine detection logic

 - Translate compliance requirements into production detection logic, preserving correctness across alert eligibility, thresholds, customer segmentation, date windows, and deduplication

 - Develop and maintain Python and SQL pipelines for transaction data preparation, feature engineering, and detection workflows

 - Evaluate detection rules and analytical models across coverage, alert quality, threshold sensitivity, and the impact of proposed changes

 - Design reproducible evaluations on historical data that account for limited labels, class imbalance, and shifts in customer behaviour over time

 - Own testing, deployment, scheduling, monitoring, and operational support for detection workflows, including investigating data quality issues, pipeline failures, and unexpected changes in detection results

 - Execute historical backfills with clear validation and traceability, and maintain reliable downstream alert delivery and integrations with compliance systems

 - Be at the forefront of data innovation by experimenting, testing hypotheses, and translating insights into action, while incorporating software engineering best practices into pipelines and dashboards.

 

WHAT YOU BRING

 - 7+ years of experience in data analysis, data science, and data management within the fintech, crypto, financial services, or gambling industry, gained in a fast-paced, high-growth environment

 - Experience working with compliance, fraud, funding, finance, and customer support teams and analyzing large datasets, engineering features, and applying statistical methods to practical business problems

 - Strong Python and SQL skills, with experience building and supporting production data or analytical systems

 - Hands-on experience using dbt or similar tooling to model and organize high-fidelity data for reporting and decision-making

 - Experience setting up and managing data pipelines with a strong understanding of workflow orchestration, plus strong software engineering practices including version control, automated testing, code review, and CI/CD

 - Solid statistical foundation; ML exposure is a strong plus

 - Proficiency with BI and data visualization tools (e.g., Hex, Tableau, Power BI, or similar) to build executive-facing dashboards

 - Ability to investigate production issues independently and communicate technical findings and uncertainty to non-technical stakeholders

 - You believe wholeheartedly in the values outlined in Kraken's Tentaclements document

 - A degree in a field emphasizing analytical rigor, such as analytics, software engineering, statistics, or economics

 - Based in Canada, the US, or Brazil, and fluent in English

 

NICE TO HAVES

 - Fraud detection, AML, anomaly detection, or other risk applications

 - Experience with Athena, Trino, Kafka, and Kubernetes alongside the core Airflow/dbt/S3 stack

 - Transaction pattern analysis, customer segmentation, and detection threshold tuning

 - Working with sparse or delayed feedback from investigations to evaluate and improve detection

jobs.description:
BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Kraken is on a mission to build the most trusted bridge between crypto and traditional finance. The Financial Systems Engineering team connects activity across products, payments, banking, and digital assets to the data, ledgers, controls, and applications Finance relies on. Our engineers bring expertise in data engineering, complex transaction flows, financial systems, and reconciliation. We partner with Treasury, Accounting, Tax, FP&A, Product, Risk, Security, Compliance, and platform engineering to make financial data reliable, explainable, and auditable.

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Report to the CFO and lead the engineering vision for Kraken’s financial systems, translating Finance priorities into a clear technical strategy and delivery roadmap

 - Assess the current landscape, including fragmented data, processes, and technical debt. Define a target architecture and phased transformation plan based on evidence, business needs, and sound engineering judgment

 - Lead, coach, and grow a team of specialists across financial systems, data engineering, integrations, and ledger-related services. Establish clear ownership and develop technical leaders

 - Set standards for the completeness, quality, lineage, and ownership of financial data, from source events through transaction and balance records, reconciliation, accounting, and reporting

 - Contribute to architecture decisions for ledgers, subledgers, financial data models, APIs, and integrations across fiat and crypto activity. Determine what should be standardized and where distinct product flows need governed treatment

 - Partner with Accounting and Treasury to improve account and legal entity attribution, financial controls, reconciliation, exception handling, and the traceability of records across internal and external systems

 - Lead modernization and migration without disrupting close, reporting, fund movements, or other critical Finance operations. Define validation checkpoints and criteria for retiring legacy processes and systems

 - Establish end-to-end testing, documentation, observability, release controls, and incident response practices that account for the financial impact of upstream changes

 - Partner with Product, platform engineering, Risk, Security, Compliance, Tax, and Legal on system boundaries, access controls, resilience, regulatory needs, and auditability

 - Evaluate build, buy, and integration options; review consequential designs; and communicate architectural decisions, sequencing, risks, and tradeoffs clearly to Finance and Engineering leaders

WHAT YOU WILL TACKLE FIRST

In your first year, you’ll build the foundations for a more reliable, scalable Finance architecture:

 - Move key reconciliations from a monthly to a daily cadence, with clear ownership and a process for resolving exceptions

 - Reduce the time needed to find the root cause of reconciliation breaks from weeks to days

 - Map and validate the source tables and transformations that actually feed financial statements, establishing lineage and ownership

 - Complete the UAT data lake connections needed to test financial data flows end to end before changes reach production

WHAT YOU BRING

 - Significant software engineering and technical leadership experience, including leading experienced teams through complex financial systems or data architecture change

 - A strong track record of hiring, coaching, and developing specialists while creating clear ownership, high engineering standards, and effective cross-functional partnerships

 - Deep understanding of ledgers, subledgers, double-entry concepts, reconciliation, settlement, and the path from an operational event to an auditable financial record

 - Experience with crypto or digital asset infrastructure and the challenges of connecting on-chain activity, internal balances, custody or wallet flows, and traditional financial systems

 - Strong technical judgment in distributed systems, data engineering, APIs, event-driven processing, and integrations across complex platforms

 - Experience defining a target architecture and delivering a transformation roadmap across fragmented or legacy systems while sustaining production reliability

 - Experience designing for data completeness, accuracy, lineage, reconciliation, access control, and auditability

 - Sound judgment in production operations, including incident response, monitoring, debugging, change management, and reliability improvements

 - Ability to partner with senior Finance and Engineering leaders and translate financial, operational, and control needs into a practical engineering roadmap

 - Ability to lead experts and make informed architecture decisions without needing to be the deepest specialist in every domain; clear communication of priorities and tradeoffs to executives and technical teams

 - Experience with Rust, TypeScript/Node.js, or Python; finance applications such as NetSuite, Kyriba, or BlackLine; and SOX or SOC control environments is valuable

Running this well is a problem few companies have solved, and it's the job.
 
 - Own the reliability of the platform engineers depend on: the AI Gateway, the agent runtime and the connections to internal tools. Set the SLOs, own the error budgets and decide what happens when they're spent.
 
 - Design resilience across model providers: routing, failover, retries, rate limiting and graceful degradation when a provider is slow, throttling or down.
 
 - Make LLM traffic legible. Build observability that shows latency, errors, token usage and cost by team, model and use case, so engineers can see what their workloads cost and where they're spending their time waiting.
 
 - Treat capacity and cost as one problem. Routing decisions affect both latency and spend, and you'll own the tradeoff directly.
 
 - Work with Security, Finance and AI governance to put access controls, budgets, audit logging and data handling into the platform, not into a spreadsheet next to it.
 
 - Lead incident response and blameless post-incident reviews. Turn what breaks into fixes that stay fixed.
 
 - Automate operations with infrastructure as code, safe deployments and progressive rollouts, so the platform gets more reliable as it grows rather than more fragile.
 
 - Mentor engineers and raise the operating standard across the team.
 
 This is a Staff role. You'll set the technical direction for how the platform runs, not just keep it running. The platform is small enough that your decisions shape it directly, and used broadly enough that they affect every engineering team at Kraken.
 
 

SKILLS YOU SHOULD HODL

 - Extensive experience in site reliability, infrastructure or platform engineering, with a track record of owning high-traffic, business-critical services in production

jobs.title: Principal Database Engineer
jobs.description:
BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Kraken’s Core Infrastructure Engineering team builds and operates the shared data systems behind critical production services. Our estate spans on-premises and cloud infrastructure, with MariaDB at its centre and Kafka, Redis and Elasticsearch across the wider platform.

We’re hiring a Principal Database Engineer to bring long-term experience and technical judgment to this estate. You’ll assess it, set the goals and direction, and work hands-on with the team to deliver measurable improvements. This is an individual contributor role with influence across teams and several quarters of work.

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Review the estate against business needs and production evidence. Judge reliability, scale, cost and operational complexity, identifying what should be preserved and where investment or simplification would make a difference.

 - Define the target architecture and measurable goals. Agree a prioritised roadmap with engineering leads and dependent teams, explaining the trade-offs and sequencing work around delivery risks.

 - Execute that roadmap with the team through design, implementation and adoption. Stay personally involved in difficult migrations and scaling decisions, with representative benchmarks, data-integrity checks and credible cutover and rollback plans. Adapt the plan as evidence changes and verify the results in production before calling the work complete.

 - Investigate difficult MariaDB failures and performance limits through the engine, storage and application behaviour. Improve fleet reliability through useful observability, safer changes and tested backup, restore and disaster recovery procedures. Set recovery objectives with service owners and prove them through exercises.

 - Build and maintain production software for database provisioning, upgrades and routine maintenance. Make self-service workflows safe and auditable, incorporating access controls and change evidence with Security and Compliance.

 - Work with application teams on schemas, transaction boundaries, queries and data-store choices. Make the operational consequences clear and resolve dependencies that span teams.

 - Mentor engineers across the team through design reviews, pairing and incident analysis. Help them deepen their database expertise and take ownership of technical decisions.

 - Participate in on-call and incident response, leaving clear operational ownership and following through on lessons from production.

 

WHAT YOU BRING

jobs.description:
BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

We are looking for a Security GRC Lead to own security governance, risk, and compliance across Payward's acquisitions. You will be the accountable owner for bringing each acquired company from its own control environment into ours, working with the M&A Technology Team from diligence through to either full platform migration or steady-state coverage under our central program.

Payward acquires and integrates companies continuously, across multiple jurisdictions and regulatory regimes. Every target arrives with its own controls, its own maturity level and its own audit history, and every one enters our financial statement audit scope on a timeline set by the deal rather than by readiness. Today that work competes for the same people who run controls for the parent company. This role exists so that it has a dedicated owner.

This is a build role to uphold the repeatable process for assessing an acquired company against our security baseline, mapping its controls into our compliance frameworks,and setting remediation milestones a newly acquired team can realistically hit. You will then run it, deal after deal, and you are accountable for the work getting done.

 

THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Assess each acquisition target against Payward's security baseline, during diligence where deal timelines allow and immediately post-close otherwise
