jobs.description:
ABOUT NU

Nu serves more than 143 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page https://www.nu.com/2026-en

ABOUT THE TEAM

At Nubank, Compliance is a strategic partner—not a tollgate. We view effective Risk Management & Compliance as the engine that maintains agility and empowers rapid, responsible growth across multiple global markets. Our team partners directly with internal clients using a targeted friction approach: we focus on the most relevant regulatory risks and embed compliance directly into product design rather than distributing rules after the fact.

The Global Compliance function serves as the Second Line of Defense, responsible for the full regulatory lifecycle: tracking new regulations, advising product and technology teams, testing controls, coordinating regulatory inspections, and monitoring remediation of regulatory issues.

This role is positioned at a pivotal moment. Nubank has received conditional approval for a US National Bank Charter. Should the charter be approved, this person will help build and operationalize the compliance and Community Reinvestment Act (CRA) infrastructure for a de novo national bank. In the near term, the role focuses on charter readiness—including supporting the development of the organizing bank's proposed CRA strategy—and on strengthening Nubank's consumer compliance posture under its current US operating model. The role requires someone who can build from scratch, own outcomes, and operate with an entrepreneurial mindset in a highly regulated environment.

JOB SUMMARY

We are seeking an experienced Compliance Analyst with dedicated compliance, risk, or audit experience at a regulated US financial institution or bank. This role carries primary ownership of Community Reinvestment Act (CRA) support and consumer protection compliance across Nubank's US deposit and unsecured lending products (personal loans and credit cards).

The CRA dimension of this role is central. Working within the Second Line of Defense, this person supports the oversight of CRA program execution and engages directly with community stakeholders to help assess local credit and community development needs. In the near term, and as part of charter readiness, this person will help drive the development of the proposed CRA Strategic Plan for the organizing bank.

This person reports to the Head of US Compliance, who is expected to serve as the bank's CRA Officer upon charter approval. The role provides direct support to that function.

The ideal candidate independently interprets and applies complex regulatory frameworks, translates regulatory requirements for cross-functional and business audiences, and develops proactive strategies to mitigate compliance risk. This person does not wait for direction—they identify issues, propose solutions, and drive them to completion.

Please note: This is a consumer compliance and CRA role. It is not a BSA/AML role. While a general awareness of the broader regulatory environment is useful, this position does not focus on anti-money laundering, sanctions, or financial crimes compliance. Candidates whose primary experience is in BSA/AML should review the focus areas below carefully before applying.

 

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Community Reinvestment Act (CRA)

 - Support the development of the proposed CRA Strategic Plan for the organizing bank as part of charter readiness, including helping define assessment areas, measurable performance goals, and community development objectives appropriate to a digital banking model.

 - Engage directly with community organizations, nonprofits, local stakeholders, and community development practitioners to assess local credit and community development needs, and document those needs to inform the bank's CRA strategy.

 - Support the Second Line oversight of CRA program execution, including monitoring and providing effective challenge to the First Line on the adequacy of CRA-related activities, controls, and documentation.

 - Support the public engagement and comment process associated with the CRA Strategic Plan, should the bank pursue the strategic plan evaluation option.

 - Establish and maintain CRA records, data, and documentation to support performance evaluation readiness and examination preparedness.

 - Monitor CRA-related regulatory developments and supervisory expectations, and advise on implications for the bank's strategy and operations.

Compliance Advisory

 - Independently advise business partners on new product initiatives, marketing campaigns, servicing processes, and system implementations to identify and mitigate compliance risk before deployment.

 - Provide effective challenge to the First Line of Defense (Business Operations, Marketing, Product) on the design and adequacy of compliance controls, policies, and procedures.

 - Interpret and apply federal and state consumer protection laws to diverse and complex business scenarios, offering actionable compliance solutions—not just risk flags.

 - Assess the compliance and regulatory impact of internal operational events, audit findings, and external regulatory changes; develop and drive remediation plans in coordination with the First and Third Lines of Defense.

 - Translate complex regulatory requirements into plain-language guidance for cross-functional teams, business leadership, and where applicable, external stakeholders (e.g., partner banks, regulators).

 - Monitor emerging consumer banking trends, proposed rulemaking, and enforcement actions to proactively identify risks and advise the business on implications.

Charter Readiness & Compliance Infrastructure

 - Support the build-out of compliance and CRA infrastructure appropriate for a de novo national bank under OCC supervision, including policies, procedures, monitoring, testing, training, and recordkeeping. Activities are conducted in preparation for potential operations as a national bank, subject to charter approval.

 - Identify gaps in current compliance processes that would require enhancement or replacement under direct charter operations.

 - Conduct and contribute to compliance gap analyses comparing current processes, policies, and controls against OCC supervisory expectations for a de novo national bank; support the development of remediation roadmaps to close identified gaps.

 - Partner with Legal, Risk, and Operations to support readiness for potential OCC examinations and supervisory expectations, as well as potential examinations or inquiries from other regulators (e.g., CFPB, state regulators).

 - Execute compliance activities in alignment with Nubank's Global Compliance standards, frameworks, and methodologies, adapting them as needed for US regulatory requirements.

Mentoring & Knowledge Sharing

 - Mentor junior compliance team members and cross-functional partners on evolving regulatory landscapes, sharing insights and best practices.

 - Create and maintain compliance training materials, reference guides, and knowledge-base documentation to build institutional regulatory knowledge.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

REQUIRED

 - Dedicated compliance, risk, or audit experience within a US financial institution or bank.

 - Direct working experience with the Community Reinvestment Act (CRA), including familiarity with assessment area definition, community development activities, performance evaluation, recordkeeping, and—ideally—the CRA strategic plan option.

 - Experience engaging with community organizations, community development practitioners, or local stakeholders to identify and respond to community credit needs.

 - Bachelor's degree in Finance, Law, Business Administration, or a related field.

 - Deep working knowledge of US consumer compliance regulations, including ECOA/Reg B, TILA/Reg Z, UDAAP (Section 5 FTC Act / Dodd-Frank §1031), and EFTA/Reg E. Familiarity with FCRA/Reg V, GLBA/Reg P, and broader US banking regulations is a plus.

 - Demonstrated ability to independently interpret regulatory requirements and apply them to complex, ambiguous business scenarios—not just follow established playbooks.

 - Experience providing compliance advisory to product, technology, or business teams in a fast-paced environment.

 - Track record of building or materially improving compliance processes, controls, or monitoring programs (not just operating within existing ones).

 - Strong judgment, integrity, and discretion in handling sensitive and confidential matters.

 - Ability to communicate complex regulatory topics clearly to non-compliance audiences.

 - Comfort operating with a high level of autonomy while knowing when to escalate.

Preferred

 - Experience with Fair Lending compliance, including ECOA/Reg B monitoring, fair lending risk assessments, or disparate impact / disparate treatment analysis.

 - Experience with consumer complaints oversight, including complaint program design, root cause analysis, and trend reporting.

 - Experience with compliance testing, monitoring, or quality assurance for deposit, credit card, or personal loan products.

 - Experience at a de novo bank, BaaS arrangement, or fintech-bank partnership where compliance or CRA infrastructure was being built or materially enhanced.

 - Familiarity with OCC supervisory expectations, examination processes, and heightened standards for de novo institutions.

 - Understanding of how banking technology, automated decisioning, and data practices intersect with consumer protection requirements.

 - Professional certification: CRCM, CCEP, or similar.

HEAD OF DESIGN, AI PRIVATE BANKER

Nu | Palo Alto, CA

ABOUT THE AI PRIVATE BANKER

The AI Private Banker is Nu's intelligent financial partner—an AI-powered advisor that helps millions of customers understand their finances, make confident decisions, and take action seamlessly. It is built on Nu's proprietary foundation models and data infrastructure, developed by the AI Core team that joined Nu through the Hyperplane acquisition. This is not a chatbot bolted onto a banking app. It is a fundamental reimagining of how people relate to their money, powered by conversational AI, recommendation engines, and real-time personalization across mobile and web.

The AI Private Banker represents Nu's next chapter and one of the company's highest-priority strategic bets. It sits at the intersection of banking and frontier AI, and every design decision here directly shapes how millions of people experience financial guidance.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a Senior Design Manager (M4) to lead the design organization for the AI Private Banker team in Palo Alto.

As Sr Design Manager, you will lead a multidisciplinary team of product designers and content designers (6+) crafting the AI Private Banker experience—shaping how customers interact with our AI advisor, how trust is earned, and how complex insights become simple, actionable, and human.

But you are no longer just building for the AI Private Banker vertical. You are establishing the foundational experience systems that will power AI across all of Nu, while ensuring alignment with the broader Magic App vision (Nu's next-generation unified app experience). In this context, you will help define the design vision, systems, cultural anchors, and rituals that make this product feel unmistakably Nu: clear, kind, and empowering—bridging product-specific excellence with company-wide coherence.

You will partner closely with Rohan Ramanath (GM, AI Core) and the broader product, data science, and engineering leadership to translate AI capabilities into trusted, explainable human experiences. This is a high-visibility role with senior stakeholder exposure across the US and Brazil, requiring someone who can navigate ambiguity, align teams across borders and time zones, and find structure in an emerging space.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead and inspire a multidisciplinary team of product designers and content designers (6+) working on conversational, visual, and systemic layers of the AI experience

 - Define and evolve the design north star for the AI Private Banker—how it looks, feels, and behaves across touchpoints

 - Partner with product, data science, and engineering to translate AI capabilities into trusted, explainable human experiences

 - Build and scale design systems for AI interaction patterns (voice, confidence levels, error recovery, transparency)

 - Coach and grow the team—helping them balance craft excellence with experimentation and speed

 - Drive cross-functional alignment, ensuring the design voice stays consistent from early prototypes to production

 - Create frameworks for evaluating AI experience quality—usability, emotion, trust, and value perception

 - Establish the cultural anchors and rituals that make the design team operate with clarity, purpose, and velocity

 - Represent design to senior leadership across the US and Brazil, navigating complex cross-functional and cross-cultural dynamics

WHAT GREAT LOOKS LIKE

 - You have built or led design teams working on AI- or data-powered experiences (e.g., personalization, recommendations, chat, insights)

 - You think systemically but care deeply about detail and tone

 - You are a natural coach—you know how to elevate others' craft and clarity

 - You balance strategic thinking with the ability to dive deep into design problems

 - You are comfortable working with uncertainty and helping teams find structure in emerging spaces

 - You advocate for human values in AI—fairness, clarity, empathy—not as slogans but as design principles

 - You thrive in high-growth, high-change environments and can adapt as the company, team structures, and priorities evolve

 - Experience in fintech, banking, or regulated industries is a plus but not required

WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

The AI Private Banker represents Nu's next chapter: helping people feel in control of their financial journey through intelligence that listens, learns, and guides. Design leadership here means more than building interfaces—it means shaping how AI meets humanity, every day, at the scale of 100 million+ customers.

About the team

As Nu expands its footprint into the US, we are seeking a visionary, highly specialized US Chief Information Security Officer (CISO).

This is not a traditional operational CISO role. You will serve as the executive pillar for Nu’s US strategy, bridging the gap between traditional financial regulations and modern, hyper-scalable crypto and AI technology platforms. You will act as the point of accountability for US regulatory bodies, lead governance transformations, and oversee critical cross-functional security domain leadership.

We are looking for a security leader who balances deep traditional banking compliance expertise with a forward-looking understanding of cryptocurrency protocols and artificial intelligence security.

About the role

As the US CISO, you will architect, establish, and operationalize a unified US security and compliance posture. You will protect customer trust, satisfy strict US regulatory frameworks (e.g., OCC compliance), and secure frontier technology initiatives ensuring Nu’s platform remains resilient, future-proof, and compliant as we scale globally.

Key responsibilities and Expectations

 - US Regulatory & Regulatory Agency Liaison: Serve as the primary US security authority and point of contact for regulators (e.g. OCC). Oversee all mandatory statutory disclosures, including financial and IBFR background reviews.

 - Crypto & Web3 Product Defense: Partner with crypto product and infrastructure teams to secure future-proof financial technologies, translating complex blockchain architectures into compliant, enterprise-grade risk frameworks.

 - Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) Transformation: Uplevel Nu’s GRC program to support multi-geography scaling.

 - AI Security Frameworks: Lead the strategic security response for AI initiatives—from developer workflows and engineering toolsets to model integrity and deployment risks.

 - Insider Threat Program Development: Design, build, and deploy an end-to-end enterprise Insider Threat program across first and second lines of defense in close partnership with Risk and Legal teams.

Qualifications 

 Professional Experience & Education:

 - Executive Leadership

Experience:

15+ years in Information Security, with significant experience operating at an executive, director, or CISO level within FinTech, Banking, or Digital Assets.

 - US Financial Regulatory Expertise: Deep hands-on experience navigating US regulatory environments, specifically working with the OCC, statutory disclosure processes, and financial institution compliance.

 - Cryptocurrency & Blockchain Security: Demonstrated domain expertise in cryptocurrency security, decentralized finance, or digital asset platforms. Experience at leading crypto-native institutions or hyper-growth FinTechs is highly valued.

 - AI Security Strategy: Familiarity with modern AI security risks, LLM integrations, safe code generation tools, and model security.

 - GRC Upleveling: Proven track record of rebuilding or scaling GRC frameworks within complex, multi-national organizations.

 - Executive Communication: Exceptional communication skills needed to interface effectively with regulatory examiners, executive leadership, and board members.

Competencies & Attributes:

 - Fluency in English is required; Portuguese and/or Spanish are a plus.

 - Strong people leadership at scale, including developing managers and leading teams of differing maturity through change and ambiguity.

 - Excellent stakeholder management and communication, with maturity in negotiation and conflict resolution across senior cross-functional partners.

 - A pragmatic, hybrid profile, balanced across people leadership, product sensibility, and technical depth rather than weighted to any single one. A genuine product mindset focused on customer and agent outcomes, with the technical depth to raise the bar in architectural discussions.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As the Community-Led Growth Senior Specialist, you'll build acquisition inside communities Nu doesn't own — WhatsApp and Telegram groups, Reddit threads, diaspora forums — where access is earned, not bought, and where most channels have no native attribution. You will work as the marketing counterpart to a Growth Product Manager. You own community strategy, native content, and channel activation, particularly in social and other hard-to-track spaces where the audience already lives.

YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

jobs.title: Head of Design, Digital Assets
jobs.description:
ABOUT NU

Nu serves more than 143 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page https://www.nu.com/2026-en

HEAD OF DESIGN (HANDS-ON), DIGITAL ASSETS

We are building open money and open financial services — not "crypto."

The Digital Assets team at Nu is reimagining how a financial services platform can use blockchain technology to solve real problems for real people — without ever making customers think about the blockchain at all. We have deliberately renamed ourselves from Crypto to Digital Assets, and we have effectively banned the word "crypto" internally. We do not do crypto for crypto's sake. We do blockchain banking.

The reference point is Apple Pay. It runs on cryptography, public and private keys, and secure tokenization inside a secure enclave. Apple never says any of that. It says "on device," and "it just works." That is the standard for everything we ship.

THE ROLE

We are looking for a hands-on design leader to join the Digital Assets team in Palo Alto. You will be the lead design voice for a genuinely new category: making digital assets — Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and stablecoins — as simple, accessible, and trusted as a debit card swipe.

This role sits at the intersection of consumer product design, financial innovation, and zero-to-one invention. Much of what you will design has never existed in consumer form before. You will not be asked to study what the incumbents did; the explicit instruction is to carve a new path.

WHAT YOU WILL DESIGN

 - The buy, hold, and sell experience for Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Digital Dollars, etc. — designed to feel intuitive, familiar, and clear from the first interaction.

 - Earning, also known as staking: an experience that lets customers put eligible digital assets to work and earn rewards with clarity, control, and trust — without exposing the protocol mechanics underneath.

 - Onchain transfers and payments: sending, receiving, and using digital assets in ways that feel as simple and dependable as moving money today, while the underlying blockchain complexity stays out of the customer’s way.

 - The invisible infrastructure layer that powers core functionality across the entire company, including the US build.

 - Both the customer experience and the platform that other teams will draw on for future launches.

 - New ways for people to own, move, use, and grow value across financial products and borders — shaping a flexible foundation for what open money can become without being constrained by today’s conventions.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

 - Consumer instincts over crypto fluency. Deep domain experience in crypto is not the point here — and can even work against you. If your instinct is to explain custody models or gas fees to a customer, this is not the seat.

 - Mobile expertise is a must-have. There is no desktop app in Brazil; effectively no web. Strong recent mobile work is non-negotiable, and a primarily B2B or enterprise background is a hard fit.

 - Zero-to-one experience. You have designed products that did not exist before, where there were no references to copy, and you thrived in the ambiguity.

 - A product marketing mindset. You care about the words, the positioning, and how it feels — not just the design elements. Our touchstone is "a thousand songs in your pocket," decided before the product was designed.

 - The ability to hide complexity. You have made something complicated feel obvious and delightful. Products that resonate with us: Cash App, Apple, the Tesla app, Duolingo, Wise, Revolut.

 - Fintech experience is a plus, never a requirement. We will teach you the compliance, legal, and regulatory ropes. What we cannot teach is the instinct to dream a magical experience first.

 - A short line to the business. The design team reports directly to the GM of the business unit. For a senior designer, that means unusual room to shape strategy rather than receive it.

HOW WE WORK

 - Dream first. The hiring manager's framing is: "Dream the magical experience first. We'll tell you afterwards what's not allowed."

 - No desktop-first. Everything is mobile-first, consumer-first.

 - No copy-and-paste. No copying from Coinbase or Robinhood. We are deliberately different.

 - The US is part of the trajectory. You will be shaping work that serves the next phase of global growth.

THE TEAM

You will report directly to Michael Rihani, GM of the Digital Assets business unit. Michael is a product leader with close to twenty years of experience, including four years at Apple on Apple Pay, leading Bitcoin and consumer financial services at Cash App and Coinbase, and directing Supercharging UX and Bitcoin payments at Tesla. He believes the biggest thing the industry is missing is storytellers and design people who can make the technology disappear.

INTERVIEW PROCESS
1. Portfolio review with Ethan Eismann (CDO, Nu) — asynchronous
2. Live portfolio presentation with 2-3 design leaders and/or senior designers (~1 hour)
3. Hiring manager interview with Michael Rihani
4. Possible additional interviews. This interview process is subject to change, and may evolve with the hiring process. We appreciate your flexibility.

* A system-level collaborator. You know how to operate within a mature design organization — influencing the global system, contributing patterns, and partnering with central teams rather than working around them.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Nu is building a global Software Asset Management (SAM) capability to govern how software is requested, acquired, secured, provisioned, optimized, renewed, and retired across the company. Software is one of our largest and fastest-growing technology spend categories, and it carries real security, privacy, and audit exposure — every tool we buy creates licenses to optimize, access to control, contracts to honor, and data to protect.

We are looking for a senior individual contributor to lead this transformation globally. This role owns the design and implementation of Nu SAM operating model, working across Enterprise Technology Services (ETS), Information Security, IAM, Procurement, Finance, Legal, Data Protection, and business areas.

This is an IC6 role: you will lead through deep expertise, influence, and execution across multiple functions and geographies. You will not be expected to manage a large team directly; instead, you will set the technical and operational direction for SAM and enable partner teams to execute consistently.

You own a clear goal: a trusted, governed, and cost-efficient global software portfolio — with complete inventory, right-sized licenses, controlled access, audit-ready evidence, and measurable savings.

YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Leading the global implementation of Nu Software Asset Management framework, from intake through acquisition, lifecycle management, renewal, and decommissioning.

 - Establishing ETS as the operational owner of the software portfolio and creating clear interfaces with ITSec, IAM, Procurement, Legal, DPO, Finance, and business owners.

 - Implementing an intake-first operating model in which software needs are assessed for catalog fit, duplication, build-vs-buy, security, open source governance, and data-protection requirements before commercial negotiation begins.

 - Defining and operationalizing the Software Catalog as the single source of truth for software assets, owners, licenses, spend, contracts, renewals, usage, risk classification, and access posture.

 - Driving the separation of license management from access management, partnering with IAM to ensure least-privilege access, automated provisioning/deprovisioning, and reliable license reclamation.

 - Designing risk-tiered workflows for SaaS, AI tools, FOSS, browser extensions, connectors, pilots, and exceptions.

 - Establishing lifecycle automation, including renewal alerts, inactivity-based reclamation, ownership reassignment, offboarding workflows, and Shadow IT detection/remediation.

 - Leading the Software Asset Selection Committee and defining decision criteria, escalation paths, exception handling, and governance cadence.

 - Building global SAM standards, policies, RACI, controls, SLAs, playbooks, and reporting practices that meet Nu security, regulatory, and audit needs.

ABOUT THE TEAM 

The Credit Risk Squad is part of the 2nd line of Defense, responsible for managing and overseeing the credit risk function of our organization by providing independent oversight and challenge to the first line of defense. 
As a second line Credit Risk team, we are responsible for creating Expected Credit Loss (ECL) models used to calculate loss allowances, making sure the company's credit risk is managed correctly and efficiently — participating end-to-end in the model development process, including implementation, monitoring, ensuring operational quality of the data, and supporting Finance accounting teams. 
Our team's models feed the financial statements of the Holding under IFRS 9, and, as Nubank expands into the United States, under US GAAP as well

About the Role 
As a Credit Risk Expert focused on the US, you'll be the senior technical authority on US GAAP credit-loss and CECL (Current Expected Credit Losses) methodology within our Credit Risk team. Nubank's US expansion requires expected-credit-loss models that meet US regulatory and accounting standards.

You'll govern local US CECL models: assessing and identifying gaps, reviewing risks, and driving an implementation plan — hands-on where needed, working through the team rather than alone. It is also expected that you become the team's standing focal point for US-specific credit regulation.

This is a specialist, individual-contributor role, — but you'll be expected to share your knowledge to the rest of the team, along with senior stakeholders in Finance, Risk, and Product.

You’ll be Responsible for 

 - Own the US GAAP / CECL methodology — be the team's definitive expert on how expected credit loss should be calculated and governed under US standards.

 - Assess and close regulatory gaps — evaluate our current state against what's required for the local US regulation; identify what's missing in model methodology, documentation, and governance, and drive the plan to close it.

 - Build models for new US portfolios — as new US products launch, build their expected-credit-loss models from the ground up, hands-on, including Development, Implementation and Monitoring process.

 - Close the explanatory gap between IFRS 9 and US GAAP models — advise on main drivers for differences between IFRS 9 and US GAAP results.

 - Transfer knowledge across the team — ensure US GAAP/CECL expertise doesn't stay siloed with you; coach and upskill teammates who will implement and maintain these models day to day.

 - Be the face of credit risk with US stakeholders — represent the team with local US leadership (CFO, CRO) and act as a primary point of contact with US regulators on credit and expected-loss matters.

 

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS

Required

 - Bachelor's degree in Economics, Finance, Accounting, Engineering, Statistics, Math, or a related quantitative field.

 - Deep, hands-on experience building expected-credit-loss / provisioning models under US GAAP, specifically CECL (ASC 326).

 - Strong working knowledge of US credit risk regulatory expectations — what regulators, internal model risk teams, and external auditors scrutinize in ECL models.

 - Proven experience actually building models (not only reviewing or auditing them).

 - Strong communication skills and a demonstrated ability to transfer technical knowledge to non-specialists and teammates, rather than keeping it centralized.

ABOUT NU

Visit our Institutional Page https://www.nu.com/2026-en

ABOUT THE ROLE

Every transaction at Nubank travels across a network before it reaches a customer. As we grow across countries, accounts, regions and hybrid environments, the connectivity layer underneath has to stay fast, segmented, auditable and cheap to run — while never becoming the thing that takes the platform down.

As a Senior Software Engineer on a Cloud Network platform engineering team, you set and evolve the technical direction for how Nubank connects its cloud, hybrid and on-premises environments. You own problems whose scope spreads across several teams and business units, and you are expected to bring structure to ambiguity rather than wait for it to be resolved for you.

YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Setting and evolving the technical direction of the cloud network platform owned by your team, aligning with Nubank's canonical approaches and contributing back to the broader technical community.

 - Support complex network projects and processes end to end — working independently, coordinating across subjects and stakeholders, and escalating for managerial support in a timely way rather than reactively.

 - Proactively reducing long-term complexity through simplification, consolidation, deprecation and paved roads, explicitly balancing scalability, maintainability and cost, and considering both human and AI interaction with the platform.

 - Owning the operational health of the network platform in your team's scope: leading complex incident response (diagnosis, coordination, resolution), driving complex postmortems, and owning the short- and long-term tech debt strategy that comes out of them.

 - Promoting a culture of safe change — feature flags, gradual rollout, monitoring, fast rollback — applied to network changes, and driving simplification and cost optimization across the topology.

 - Setting and enforcing quality standards for the team's automation and infrastructure code: testing practices, code review bar, reusable modules, and anticipation of quality and maintainability needs coming from business strategy.

 - Defining observability for the platform — robust monitoring, controls and SLAs that surface issues proactively rather than after customer impact.

 - Bringing a strong end-to-end domain understanding: tracing a business process from product through the transactional path down to the network and data layers, and understanding how network design choices propagate through it.

 - Owning the network security posture of your scope, including PCI DSS or equivalent standards, segmentation, and controls that hold up under audit.

 - Evaluating buy vs. build options and new products and technologies, being data-driven about stability, reliability, scalability and cost before committing to a solution.

 - Participating in hiring as a core part of the role, contributing to function-wide taskforces and initiatives, and documenting decisions so that knowledge travels across teams, not just within yours.
 
 

WE ARE LOOKING FOR A PERSON WHO HAS
• Strong software engineering foundations and solid coding skills (Python, Go, Java, .NET etc.), with experience building and maintaining production-grade systems..
• Solid hands-on experience with cloud computing (AWS preferred) in production environments, including core services such as VPC, IAM, load balancing, DNS and managed connectivity services..
• Hands-on experience with infrastructure as code and automation (Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK or similar)..
• Experience designing, deploying and operating distributed systems with a focus on reliability and cost efficiency..
• Interest in specializing in cloud networking and connectivity. Prior network experience is not required; we will help you build that depth..
• An analytical profile: you go after root causes and propose solutions that hold, working in a continuous improvement environment..
• Clear communication with technical and non-technical audiences..
• English proficiency to read, write and collaborate across time zones.

Nice to have
• Experience with incident response and root cause analysis in cloud environments..
• Familiarity with cloud networking concepts (hybrid connectivity, segmentation, firewalls)..
• Experience with observability stacks and security/compliance standards (PCI DSS)..

ABOUT THE TEAM

Nu's Business Control Officers (BCOs) are the first-line risk representatives embedded in each business unit. They make sure we understand the regulations we must follow, that controls are in place, and that our systems operate as intended across operational and regulatory risk.

As Nu grows, adds bank licenses and expands into new markets, first-line risk management has to scale with it. The global BCO team sets how the function works across the company, in close partnership with the second line, which defines the risk frameworks and verifies adherence to them. 

ABOUT THE ROLE

This role will redefine what a BCO is at Nu. You will move the function from coordination to leadership: setting the standards, methodologies and training that make first-line risk management consistent, high-quality and credible with regulators, across every market.

Nu is seeking a Staff Security Engineer to contribute in the Identity and Access Management security function across a financial technology organization serving over 100 million customers in Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia. 
This is a senior individual-contributor role with organizational-level technical influence, responsible for supporting a multi-year IAM security strategy, directing its execution across multiple engineering teams, and ensuring that identity and access controls meet the security, regulatory, and operational requirements of a globally operating financial institution.

The Staff Security Engineer is expected to bring a demonstrated history of delivering consequential security programs — including programs that encountered setbacks — and the technical judgment that only sustained, hands-on experience in the domain produces. 
Critically, this role requires a security engineering philosophy grounded in business enablement: the conviction that security done well accelerates what the organization can do, not merely protects it. This means rigorously distinguishing between controls that reduce real risk and those that create the appearance of compliance without reducing exposure, taking genuine ownership of outcomes rather than delegating accountability through policy, and continuously questioning inherited assumptions about what security measures are necessary, sufficient, or proportionate.

What You’ll Be Responsible For

 - Defining, communicating, and executing a multi-year security strategy (especially in the IAM field) aligned with the organization's risk posture, regulatory obligations, and business objectives across multiple countries and regulatory jurisdictions.

 - Lead organization-wide authentication migrations that span heterogeneous surfaces — browser, operating system login, CLI tooling, and API-level integrations — across thousands of employees, multiple device ecosystems, and distributed work environments, producing measurable outcomes: authentication success rates above 99%, material reductions in per-authentication time, support exception rates below 1%, and return on investment within weeks of enforcement.

 - Designing and maintaining the core identity infrastructure with the durability and operational discipline required at organizational scale: enterprise Identity Provider, PKI and X.509 certificate lifecycle automation, mutual TLS for service-to-service authentication, and credential management systems engineered to remain sound as the organization grows.

 - Translating least-privilege access from a principle into a measurable, organization-wide program — with defined metrics, visible adoption curves, and accountability structures that allow Security and Engineering leadership to track and act on the organization's access risk posture over time.

 - Designing and maintaining a security engineering framework — comprising technical mechanisms, policies, incentives, and assurance processes — that ensures security properties are durable, verifiable, and operationally sound, rather than dependent on individual vigilance or periodic audits.

 - Leading technical incident response for identity and access security events, including critical vulnerabilities in remote access infrastructure, ensuring thorough investigation, documented root cause analysis, and structural improvements that reduce the likelihood and impact of recurrence.

 - Designing and facilitating large-scale preparedness exercises grounded in realistic attack paths — involving engineering, operations, and executive functions — to identify genuine gaps in IAM controls, not merely satisfy a compliance requirement.

 - Providing technical mentorship and coaching to senior engineers; lead innovative projects with universities and actively collaborate in hiring and career decisions in order to maintain a high technical standard throughout the safety organization.

 - Proficiency in software engineering: ability to produce, review, and reason about production-quality code in at least one general-purpose programming language.

jobs.description:
ABOUT NU

Nu serves more than 143 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page https://www.nu.com/2026-en

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for an outstanding AI Engineer with both a passion for design and experience architecting modern AI implementations.

Nu's design and research function is roughly 260 people. Over the past year they have been building their own tooling: something like 100 AI-assisted solutions and 30+ local knowledge repositories, each built inside a business unit to solve that unit's problem. Most of them work. None of them talk to each other.

The Design Center of Excellence exists to turn that kind of local invention into systems the whole function can build on. It has design ops and research ops. It does not have an engineer — which means the CoE can identify a need, specify a tool, and then has no one to build it.

This is that hire: the first engineer in the CoE, and the person who architects the systems that let design at Nu scale. You'll work directly with the designers and researchers who use what you build, and the person who scopes a system is the person who builds it.

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

NuBrain — the first priority. A global knowledge system for the design and research function, consolidating the 30+ local repositories that already exist. The hard part is not merging content; it's the context architecture — how retrieval is structured, how token consumption stays sane, and how content reaches people and agents at the moment it's useful.

New tools that enable superlative creative marketing and brand expressions at scale. As Nu scales globally, we are inventing new ways to express our brand in the product and through our marketing. Instead of hiring fleets of marketing designers in every country, we aim to build tools that enable consistent high quality creative expression to be driven centrally.

Canonicalizing what already exists. Roughly 100 AI solutions have been built locally by designers and researchers. Someone needs to understand what they are, decide what becomes standard for the function, and retire the rest before the duplication compounds.

Deciding the shape of the answer. Plugin, MCP server, agent, Claude skill, or a full platform — that call is yours to make and defend. Part of the job is telling the CoE that the tool they asked for should be something else.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Architect and build the systems design at Nu runs on — increasingly agentic ones.

- Sit with designers and researchers, understand the need underneath the request, and turn it into something scoped and buildable.

- Stand up or reuse the infrastructure, write the code, and ship it to the function.

- Instrument what you build. Metrics and observability are part of the deliverable, not a follow-up.

- Own the roadmap for CoE tooling: prioritize, sequence, say no, and keep things moving without a PM behind you.

- Be the technical voice in a design organization — make trade-offs legible to people who don't read code.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

An outstanding, deeply experienced AI engineer. This is an engineering hire first. You've spent years building systems other people build on, and recent years working with AI models on things like token consumption, rate limiting, response latency, MCP servers, and other modern AI engineering challenges.

A track record architecting UX systems. Before AI, you designed and built the foundations of user experience at scale — design systems, component platforms, UI frameworks, front-end infrastructure used by many teams.

A love for design that shows up in your work. Since AI, you've used it to build compelling examples and more sophisticated systems than were possible before. We'd like to see them.

Agentic systems that help design scale. Ideally you've built them — agents, tooling, or infrastructure that let designers do more, faster, and better. This is the strongest signal for the role.

A protagonist. You'll serve a 260-person function as a centralized hub. That means navigating stakeholders, leading projects, and pushing work through an organization that doesn't report to you. You drive the work yourself rather than relying on someone else to run the project.

Evidence you've shipped. Send us GitHub, live tools, demos, and systems you can walk us through. We are not asking for a design portfolio.

BACKGROUNDS THAT TEND TO FIT

- Design systems and UI platform engineers at design-led product companies.

- Engineers at design tooling companies.

- Engineers who have been building AI and agentic tools for designers — in their day job, in open source, or in public.

- Founders and technical leads who were the engineer behind a design-led product.

WHAT THIS ROLE IS NOT

- Not a designer who codes. The engineering bar is the bar.

- Not a generalist backend or infrastructure role. UX systems experience is core.

- Not customer-facing mobile product work. This is internal systems and tooling for the design function.

- Not a research or modeling role. (The "design modeling" profile — building the models AI consumes — is a different conversation, later.)

It went live in October 2026 with its AML/CFT and sanctions framework already in place: entity risk analysis, internal directives, customer risk classification, monitoring and screening standards, and MROS reporting. Money Boxes ("Caixinhas") is one of Nubank’s most strategic product innovations, transforming how millions of customers organize, save, and grow their money across Latin America. As Nubank expands into new geographies and financial verticals, we are looking for an exceptional Senior Staff Software Engineer to serve as the chief technical authority for our Money Boxes core platform.

In this role, you will operate at the intersection of high-concurrency distributed systems, transactional ledgering, investment asset allocation, and liquidity orchestration. You won't just maintain existing product flows—you will architect the foundational engines that enable millions of users to dynamically deposit, segment, and yield return on their savings instantly, securely, and at massive scale.

Your Mission: scale an extensible, multi-tenant Money Boxes platform that abstracts complex investment assets, yield generation mechanisms, and regulatory ledgering into simple, bulletproof platform capabilities across multiple international markets.

What You Will Own & Build

 - Money Boxes Platform Architecture: Define and execute the multi-year technical vision for Money Boxes backend architecture, ensuring high extensibility to support diverse underlying assets (e.g., fixed income, yield-bearing accounts, money market funds) across different countries.

 - Core Ledgering & Transaction Engines: Architect high-throughput, double-entry accounting engines and balance tracking systems that guarantee exact-once delivery, deterministic reconciliation, and real-time calculation of accruals and yield.

 - Liquidity & Asset Routing Infrastructure: Design resilient execution flows for deposits, withdrawals, and auto-investments, managing real-time settlement with internal brokerages, clearinghouses, and banking rails with low latencies and zero transactional error margin.

 - Multi-Country & Multi-Currency Abstractions: Abstract regional regulatory rules, local tax logic, and currency nuances into clean platform boundaries so product squads can launch localized Money Boxes experiences in record time.

 - Technical RFC Leadership: Author comprehensive design documents (RFCs) and drive architectural consensus across Payments, Core Banking, Investments, and Security leadership.

 - Fintech, Banking, or Investments Domain Depth: Deep hands-on experience building systems in transactional environments—such as savings platforms, ledger/accounting engines, investment order management, custody, or core banking infrastructure.

 - Distributed Systems Mastery: Exceptional fluency in event-driven architectures, transactional consistency, distributed sagas, domain-driven design (DDD), and high-concurrency microservices.

 - Platform & API Mindset: Demonstrated ability to build domain-agnostic, developer-friendly platforms and APIs with explicit contracts, SLAs, and high observability that allow consuming product teams to innovate rapidly.

ABOUT THE ROLE 

We are seeking an FP&A Senior Specialist to be the finance partner for our Digital Assets organization. Today that means our crypto trading and custody business in Brazil and the digital asset products inside Nu Global, including stablecoin balances, cross-border money movement, and crypto trading. As Nubank and the Digital Assets business expands to additional geographies, you will own the finance view of this business in each market it enters.

Digital Assets is both a customer product and a set of rails. Stablecoins, FX, on and off ramps, and card spending can be a source of revenue, a cost to manage, or the reason a customer chooses us in the first place. This role is about building as the business grows, including how we model and forecast it, starting with the economics of a single customer, trade, or balance and building up to the business P&L. You will also own the position Finance takes on those numbers with Digital Assets leadership.

The scope covers every digital asset product we offer, in every market where we offer it. Economics and accounting differ by product, entity, and country, and many of the answers are still being worked out. You will decide which assumptions matter most, make them explicit, and revise them as the business learns.

You will operate with a high degree of autonomy and regular exposure to the leaders who run these businesses. You will be expected to hold a position when the analysis supports it, push back with evidence, and take direct feedback. This is a senior individual contributor role. You will stay hands-on in the models and analysis, and you will help raise the standard of work across the FP&A team around you.

 - Support expansion into new geographies with the financial analysis behind each launch, including unit economics, local rails and funding methods, and the effect of licensing and legal entity structures.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Traffic Management team keeps Nubank’s customer‑facing and internal services reachable and secure. It is the layer that routes and protects every service request, from mobile app entry points to service‑to‑service calls across all our regions and environments. This function owns the strategy and execution for our service mesh ensuring our products can scale safely as we grow and expand. In this role, you will drive the reliability, scalability and security of this critical platform, evolving our service mesh, strengthening resilience and observability, and pushing our capabilities so that product teams can ship quickly without compromising stability.

YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Deliver end‑to‑end milestones on the traffic platform, from problem definition to rollout and follow‑up, breaking complex problems into clear tasks and keeping progress and risks visible for the team and key stakeholders.

 - Take ownership of complex and sometimes ambiguous problems, analyzing options and trade‑offs, and proposing clear, pragmatic solutions that balance reliability, performance, security and effort.

 - Ensure the stability and quality of what you and the team ship: design with failure in mind, put the right tests and observability in place, and react quickly to incidents, driving follow‑ups that prevent them from happening again.

 - Collaborate with engineers, product and partner teams to understand needs, align on priorities and turn them into clear technical plans and milestones that are connected to the team’s goals.

 - Use AI and agents in an AI‑first way in your routine to investigate issues, write and review code, explore solution options and automate repetitive work, helping the squad adopt safe, effective AI workflows rather than just individual usage.

 - Create and maintain clear technical documentation and runbooks that help other engineers understand, use and operate the traffic platform with confidence, and share knowledge through reviews, sessions and participation in function‑level initiatives.

 - Help other engineers grow by giving and receiving feedback through code reviews, design discussions, pairing and day‑to‑day collaboration, acting as a reference for good engineering practices inside the team.

 - Participate in support and on‑call routines for the area, using incidents, tickets and metrics as input to suggest and drive medium‑term improvements to the platform and to how we work.

WE ARE LOOKING FOR A PERSON WHO HAS

 - Operated large-scale, high-performance synchronous distributed systems in the cloud, working directly with load balancers, reverse proxies, TLS/mTLS and routing, and using metrics, logs and traces to debug issues, optimize performance and improve overall reliability.

 - Worked hands-on with Kubernetes-based infrastructure and Infrastructure-as-Code tooling — defining and evolving manifests, routing and deployment strategies, and managing DNS configuration — with a solid understanding of how these pieces fit together to deliver resilient traffic paths in production.

 - Uses AI as part of their daily engineering workflow, leveraging AI tools and agents to investigate issues, write and review code, explore solutions and automate repetitive work, while consistently validating outputs and holding quality and safety as non-negotiable standards.

 - Led end-to-end infrastructure platform projects from design to production go-live, breaking work into clear milestones, coordinating across stakeholders, managing risks and trade-offs, and following through post-rollout to stabilize and evolve the solution.

 - Experience with Istio or other service-mesh technologies such as Linkerd or Envoy-based solutions — or legacy stacks like Finagle — designing and evolving traffic policies, resilience features and observability for service-to-service communication.

 - Worked with AWS networking and compute primitives (ALB/NLB, security groups, VPC, Route 53, IAM) in production environments, with an understanding of how these layers interact with application traffic.

 - Hands-on experience using Infrastructure-as-Code tools such as Pulumi or Terraform to design, version and roll out changes to cloud and Kubernetes infrastructure in a safe, repeatable way.

 - Previously built platform capabilities or shared libraries for other engineers — abstractions, SDKs or internal tooling — that make it easier and safer for product teams to consume traffic and networking capabilities at scale.

 - Analyzing the transactional AML Alerts generated by the AML transaction monitoring system, to identify suspicious situations, contributing to a more ethical and fair society, truly understanding that it is also a key driving force for the solid growth and development of Nubank and Brazil & Mexico;

Being diligent, flexible and resilient, according to Nu's principles!

In order to achieve that, our Operational Squad - AML Ops - is responsible for protecting Nu against criminal activities and helping stop the laundering of ‘dirty’ money into the Mexican economy, complying with the necessary regulations, and ensuring the continuity of our business.

WHAT DOES A REGULATORY SOLUTIONS ANALYST FOR AML OPS DO…

 - Analyze AML Alerts, financial transactions, accounts, and data from the alerts generated by the AML transaction monitoring system, to identify suspicious situations and provide detailed recommendations (Report to UIF, Cancel, etc.)

 - Prepare all the investigation files to escalate it to the AML Forum (Comité de Comunicación y Control).

 - Provide advice on sanctions and other screening processes such as KYC. 

 - Collaborate with cross-functional areas (including legal, compliance, and risk management, among others) to minimize money-laundering risks to the business

 - Support the discard operation in binding lists.

 - Apply FIU typologies.

 - Involvement in the implementation of the regulatory framework that will contribute to Nu Mexico's growth plan.

 - Stay current with AML/FT laws, regulations, and industry standards to ensure our practices remain compliant.

QUALIFICATIONS:

- You are detail-oriented, diligent, organized and enjoy operational activities. 

 - You have excellent reporting skills, particularly for regulatory reporting.

 - You are a proactive, autonomous person and have an interest in owning your operational routines and creating processes and improving them, but at the same time, understand that there are bureaucracies in the regulatory activities that need to be followed. 

 - You are able to meet deadlines and to be flexible to adapt to changing conditions.

 - You can communicate clearly, succinctly and effectively. 

 - You feel good to be constantly challenged to learn and do more. 

 - You are good with oral and written communication in Spanish and/or English. 

 - You believe in a more just and ethical society and Nubank's values and culture.

 - You have a strong sense of integrity and responsibility handling sensitive information.

 - You understand that we can contribute within Nubank to the construction of this society, guaranteeing the application of all the rules and regulatory aspects inherent to the Client's Registration.

 - You can easily turn numbers into complex strategies, proposals and effective action plans.

IT WILL BE A DIFFERENTIAL IF YOU..

 - Have a Bachelor’s Degree in Law, Administration, Finance, Economic Sciences or related;

 - Have CNBV certification is a plus, or strong experience in AML Regulations;

 - Have previous experience in monitoring transactional AML alerts for the different banking products (Credit Card, Savings, Remittances, Investments, etc.) and-or in compliance areas in processes related to AML;

 - Have knowledge of sanctions and KYC processes related to AML;

 - Have knowledge in sending the suspicious activity reports (SAR, ROI);

Nu serves more than 143 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

SENIOR COUNSEL, REGULATORY LEGAL – LATIN AMERICA (PAYMENTS & DIGITAL ASSETS)

ABOUT US

Nu is one of the largest digital financial platforms in the world, with more than 127 million customers across Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia. Guided by our mission to fight complexity and empower people, we are redefining financial services in Latin America and this is still just the beginning of the purple future we're building.

Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: NU), we combine proprietary technology, data intelligence, and an efficient operating model to deliver financial products that are simple, accessible, and human.

Our impact has been recognized by global rankings such as Time 100 Companies, Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies, and Forbes World’s Best Bank. Visit our institutional page https://international.nubank.com.br/careers/

ABOUT THE ROLE

As Senior Counsel, Regulatory Legal – Latin America, you will be the legal voice on how Nu's payments and digital-assets products can operate, launch and scale across the region. You will define where licenses, registrations or regulated entities are required, and turn that analysis into a clear recommendation the business can act on.

This is a legal and regulatory strategy role, not a compliance operations role. You will work with Product, Compliance, Public Policy, Risk, Treasury and business leaders on new products and new markets, in an environment where regulation is moving faster than the product. You will own the regulatory path for what we build next, and you will be expected to say "here is the path I recommend", not just "here are the risks".

YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Advising on regulatory legal strategy for payments, money movement, wallets, stored value, digital assets, stablecoins and related products across Latin America.

 - Building and maintaining a country-by-country view of the regulatory perimeter: which activities require licenses, registrations, approvals or local regulated entities.

 - Leading the legal analysis for entry into new markets and for the launch of new products, features and business models.

 - Working with Product and business teams to structure products in line with applicable law, and proposing alternative structures when the initial model hits a regulatory obstacle.

 - Coordinating license and registration applications (payments, financial services, virtual assets) and supporting engagement with regulators, central banks and other authorities, including on novel issues.

 - Managing local external counsel while remaining accountable for synthesizing their input into a practical recommendation.

 - Creating scalable frameworks, playbooks and decision trees so recurring questions are answered consistently across markets.

 - Monitoring regulatory developments and separating what materially affects our strategy from general noise, and anticipating where regulation is heading on stablecoins, tokenized money, crypto-assets and new payment infrastructure.

 - Briefing senior legal and business leaders on complex regulatory topics in clear, concise and commercially useful terms.

 - Acting as a generalist legal business partner for new businesses in Latin America, coordinating a holistic legal approach, including support on agreements related to our products.

WE ARE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS

 - Qualified as a lawyer, holding the local bar license in the country where you will be based.

 - In-house experience at a fintech, payments, crypto/digital-assets or banking company, where you personally worked through regulatory, licensing and market-entry questions in Latin America.

 - Hands-on experience with payments regulation and licensing, and with digital assets, crypto, stablecoins or blockchain-based financial products.

 - Experience analyzing and comparing regulatory regimes across several Latin American jurisdictions, not a single-country specialty, with familiarity with the South American regulatory landscape.

 - A solid understanding of how payments, banking, securities, FX and digital-asset regulation interact.

 - Experience taking part in obtaining or maintaining financial-services, payments or digital-asset licenses or registrations.

 - Experience breaking down complex product architectures and money flows to pinpoint the core regulatory question, and the judgment built along the way to know when to escalate, bring in external counsel or engage a regulator, and when the business can simply move forward.

 - A track record of briefing senior legal and business leaders on technical regulatory topics, turning them into clear, actionable recommendations.

 - Experience as a senior, autonomous legal partner to Product and business teams in fast-moving environments, owning ambiguous problems and finding a compliant path forward instead of only flagging risks.

 - Fluent English and Spanish.

Nice to have

 - Direct work with financial regulators or central banks, or prior experience at a financial-regulatory law firm, central bank or regulator.

 - Experience in regulatory policy for digital assets and payments.

 - Banking or credit regulatory background combined with curiosity about digital assets.

 - Familiarity with additional Latin American markets.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Nubank is scaling rapidly across Latin America, and our Mexico division is central to empowering millions of people with intuitive, transparent, and accessible financial services. To support our sustained customer growth and expand our product ecosystem reliably, we need senior technical leaders who can translate high-level business vision into resilient, scalable distributed architectures.

In this role, you will serve as a strategic technical anchor across the Mexico division, collaborating closely with engineering leadership and cross-functional teams spanning Growth, Operations, and Core Value Proposition. You will bridge local market dynamics with Nubank's global platform ecosystem, steering architectural decisions that directly impact how prospects seamlessly transition into engaged Nubank customers.

Operating with a country-wide horizontal perspective, you will guide technical roadmaps across multiple business units and squads, untangle complex domain boundaries, and elevate engineering standards across chapters. By pairing architectural vision with pragmatic delivery, you will ensure our systems remain resilient, extensible, and prepared for exponential scale.

RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Define and execute the long-term architectural vision for the Mexico division using Domain-Driven Design (DDD) principles to decouple complex systems and eliminate single points of failure.

 - Steer technical strategy across squads in Growth, Operations, and Core Value Prop, ensuring local business flows integrate seamlessly with Nubank’s global platform foundation.

 - Mentor and develop senior engineering talent across chapters, cultivating technical excellence, architectural rigor, and operational best practices.

 - Partner with engineering directors and executive leadership to translate commercial objectives into scalable system designs and actionable execution roadmaps.

 - Drive cross-team technical consensus on mission-critical initiatives, advocating for sound trade-offs between delivery velocity and platform extensibility.

 - Champion operational resilience and observability across customer acquisition funnels, proactively identifying bottlenecks to optimize conversion latency and system reliability.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Demonstrated track record of technical leadership as a Staff-level engineer (or equivalent scope) guiding distributed systems architecture across multi-team engineering organizations.

 - Deep practical expertise applying Domain-Driven Design (DDD) to design, decouple, and scale event-driven microservices.

 - Proven ability to influence cross-functional technical roadmaps across globally distributed platform and product teams without direct hierarchical authority.

 - Experience architecting mission-critical, high-throughput systems where fault tolerance, reliability, and low-latency performance are essential.

 - Professional working proficiency in English, with demonstrated success communicating complex architectural concepts to both technical and executive audiences.

ABOUT NU

HEAD OF DESIGN, GLOBAL APP PLATFORMS (CORE)

ABOUT THE ROLE

Core is the team that defines what great design means at Nu. It's a small, deliberately elite group of designers with two jobs: set the bar for design across the company today, and decide where that bar is headed next.

Core delivers the vision for the Nu app as it launches across countries. Right now that means designing the next version of the app, and the version after that. But vision alone isn't the job. Everything Core builds has to be adoptable by every market. When Core ships a new experience, it defines the guidelines, hands them to our teams in Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, and partners with them as they tailor it to their customers.

Millions of people across Latin America have never had a credit card. For many of them, Nubank is the first institution that gives them a real path to one. Credit Builder is where that path starts.

Our Credit Builder card is an entry-level credit product. Customers add money to unlock spending power, and we coach them step by step toward a full credit limit. The goal isn't to keep people on a starter product. It's to move them up and out of it, and most of our success stories do exactly that. The experience is built around gamification. A guided timeline walks customers through adding to their money box, increasing their limit, setting up autopay and building healthy habits. It has become one of the highest-NPS experiences at Nu and a model for gamification across the company.

Today Credit Builder runs in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia. Next year our scope roughly flips. We'll bring our under-18 credit product, our credit score product (NuScore) and Credit Builder into more countries, possibly including the US. We're also planning a significant revamp of the core experience.

We're hiring a Staff Product Designer to help set the craft bar for this work. You'll be one of the most senior designers in Global Credit Card, working on both the high-visibility revamp and the day-to-day product work that keeps a fast-moving, multi-country team shipping.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead design for Credit Builder and related underserved-credit products across Brazil, Mexico, Colombia and new markets, including the US.

 - Drive the upcoming revamp of the Credit Builder experience, raising the bar on visual craft, interaction design and motion.

 - Design global solutions that hold together as one system while adapting to local needs, such as regulatory requirements, cultural context and market-specific constraints.

 - Push gamification and financial-coaching patterns further, helping customers understand how credit works and how to grow it.

 - Mentor and level up the more junior designers on the team, through critiques and day-to-day collaboration.

 - A low-ego, hands-on mindset. On a lean team covering many products and markets, everyone pitches in, including senior folks.

NICE TO HAVE

WHY NUBANK

As a second line function, we challenge process and control owners so that management can sign its SOx 302/404 conclusions with confidence.

This role is built on strong accounting and financial statement skills. You should be able to define materiality and scope of accounts by reading the Group's financial statements, and apply GAAP (mainly IFRS) to design controls that prevent material misstatements on a timely basis. Your accounting and disclosure knowledge is what lets you hold deep discussions with Finance specialists and with the external auditors throughout the audit.

YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR 

 - Owning the ICFR cycle for a defined process portfolio: Risk and Control Matrix (RCM), narratives, walkthroughs, TOD and TOE.

 - Linking the risks identified in the RCM directly to the financial statement line item (FSLI).

 - Applying Nu's internal methodology and tying Risk → Assertion → Objective → Control → Evidence.

 - Determining technologies in scope and deciding when to request SOC reports (ITGC).

 - Challenging process and control owners, and treating IPE/EUC in design and testing.

 - Executing TOE according to sampling and RoMM, and independently producing audit-ready workpapers.

 - Drafting deficiency texts that size impact, magnitude and probability on the financial statements, and tracking remediation with the first line.

 - Contributing to cross-functional discussions with IT, Finance, first line and external audit counterparts on your scope.

 - Using low-code automation and AI with a risk lens, never as a substitute for professional skepticism.

 - Leading a specific pack, process or workstream, sharing what you learn and supporting teammates.

 - Contributing to cross-functional discussions with IT, first line and external audit counterparts on your scope.

 - Deal with complex and increasingly ambiguous problems that involve several stakeholders, trade-offs between speed and rigor, and a busy calendar of changes and new geographies, with no predefined path to the solution.

 

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS

 - Education: Degree in Accounting, Economics or Business Administration, around 6 years of experience in similar positions.

 - At least one of following experiences: Big 4 integrated audit; public-company Internal Audit with an annual SOX cycle; 2LoD Internal Controls / SOX office; controllership experience.

 - Fluent English (written and spoken) to document workpapers and manage stakeholders around the world.

 - Independence on scoped projects: you close SOX deliverables with light review, not constant supervision.

 - Deep understanding of accounting principles, mainly IFRS (for example, IFRS 9, IFRS 18), and of financial statement disclosure.

 - Ability to read the Group's financial statements to define materiality and scope of accounts.

 - Ability to explain which assertion a control mitigates and how its failure becomes a misstatement.

 - Working knowledge of COSO 2013 and PCAOB standards, including AS 2201.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Every transaction at Nubank travels across a network before it reaches a customer. As we grow across countries, accounts and regions, the connectivity layer underneath has to stay fast, segmented, auditable and cost-efficient, without ever becoming the thing that takes the platform down.

As a Senior Cloud Network Engineer on our Cloud Network platform engineering team, you will design, build and operate the cloud network that Nubank’s engineering teams rely on. You will treat the network as software: automated, tested and versioned. This is an IC5 role: you lead through technical depth, design quality and influence, not direct reports. You will be part of a global engineering organization and work with teammates across countries, so collaboration in English is part of everyday work.

You’ll be responsible for

 - Designing and evolving connectivity patterns across multi-account, multi-region and hybrid-cloud topologies, making sound architectural decisions in designs that span multiple teams.

 - Building and maintaining the network platform as code (Terraform or similar), with strong standards for testing, code review and reusable modules.

 - Owning the operational health of the platform in your scope: leading incident response, driving postmortems and following through on the tech debt they uncover.

 - Promoting safe change on the network: gradual rollouts, monitoring and fast rollback.

 - Defining observability for the platform, with monitoring and SLAs that surface issues before customers feel them.

 - Owning the network security posture of your scope, including segmentation and standards such as PCI DSS, with controls that hold up under audit.

 - Simplifying the topology over time through consolidation, deprecation and paved roads, balancing scalability, maintainability and cost.

 - Evaluating build vs. buy decisions with data on stability, scalability and cost.

 - Mentoring other engineers, taking part in hiring, and documenting decisions so knowledge travels across teams.

We are looking for a person who has

 - Production experience with public cloud networking, preferably AWS: Transit Gateway, VPC design, Direct Connect, PrivateLink, Route 53, NAT/egress patterns and network firewalls. Experience with Azure or GCP networking is also valued. 

 - Experience connecting cloud and on-premises environments: hybrid connectivity, BGP and dynamic routing, IP address management, load balancers and firewalls, planning, deploying and troubleshooting at scale.

 - Coding and automation skills (Python, Go, Java, .NET), using infrastructure as code (Terraform or similar), Git, CI/CD and containers to build and operate network infrastructure.

 - A background in network engineering, SRE, DevOps or software engineering. What matters is hands-on public cloud networking experience.

 - Experience leading incident response and root cause analysis for high-impact failures that cross team boundaries.
