ABOUT US

Nu is one of the largest digital financial platforms in the world, with more than 127 million customers across Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia. Guided by our mission to fight complexity and empower people, we are redefining financial services in Latin America and this is still just the beginning of the purple future we're building.

Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: NU), we combine proprietary technology, data intelligence, and an efficient operating model to deliver financial products that are simple, accessible, and human.

Our impact has been recognized by global rankings such as Time 100 Companies, Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies, and Forbes World’s Best Bank. Visit our institutional page https://international.nubank.com.br/careers/

ABOUT THE ROLE

As Product Counsel, U.S. Products, you will be the lead legal partner for the teams building and launching Nubank's U.S. consumer financial products. You will be one of the first lawyers in our new, standalone U.S. Legal function, reporting to the Head of U.S. Legal (or equivalent).

Nu is growing in the U.S., and every product we launch has to be compliant, simple for customers and fast to ship. Your work makes that possible: legal review sits inside the product lifecycle from the first idea, not at the end. Done well, our products earn the trust of customers and regulators alike.

You will own the first line of legal guidance for product squads, turning U.S. federal and state requirements into clear, practical direction they can act on. You will work closely with Compliance, Risk, Product, Engineering, Data, Security, Marketing, Operations and the global Legal team.

YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

Counseling product teams

 - Giving clear, fast and actionable legal guidance to product, engineering, data and business teams, from concept and design through launch, scaling and sunset.

 - Triaging the day-to-day legal questions that come from squads, and assessing legal and regulatory risk for new and existing U.S. products and features (deposit accounts, credit and lending, payments and cards, rewards and pricing), in line with Nubank's risk appetite.

 - Advising on the federal and state consumer financial laws behind our products, such as UDAAP, TILA/Reg Z, ECOA/Reg B, FCRA, EFTA/Reg E, TISA/Reg DD, and state licensing, lending and consumer protection laws.

 - Turning complex and changing requirements into simple guidance and design patterns that squads can use on their own, with no legal black boxes.

Customer-facing documents and marketing

 - Drafting, reviewing and approving account and credit agreements, terms and conditions, consents, notices and customer communications, and keeping them up to date.

 - Reviewing marketing, advertising, promotions and social media content against U.S. advertising, fair lending and UDAAP standards.

 - Partnering with Product Design and Operations on complaints, disputes and servicing, so customer outcomes are fair, transparent and well documented.

Partners, vendors and outside counsel

 - Drafting, reviewing and negotiating agreements with U.S. banking, program, processing, technology and other partners, flagging risk and recommending proportionate protections.

 - Supporting third-party risk management with Procurement, Compliance, Security and Risk.

 - Working with outside counsel on specialized matters, and bringing consumer credit and fair lending knowledge in-house where it makes sense.

Regulatory readiness and leadership

 - Working with Compliance and Regulatory Affairs to prepare for examinations, audits and regulator inquiries, and supporting responses and remediation when needed.

 - Being a trusted counterpart for leaders in Product, Tech, Data, Security, Risk, Compliance and Operations.

WE ARE LOOKING FOR A PERSON WHO HAS

 - Hands-on experience in financial services, fintech or regulatory law, in-house or at a leading law firm, with a significant part of that work advising on consumer-facing digital products.

 - Deep working knowledge of U.S. consumer financial services law as it applies to digital products, including UDAAP, TILA, ECOA, FCRA and EFTA, and familiarity with the bank regulatory framework and federal and state licensing.

 - A record of leading complex product matters end to end, such as launching or redesigning a consumer financial product, structuring and negotiating bank, program or fintech partnerships, or advising through regulatory examinations, inquiries or enforcement matters.

 - Experience working side by side with product, engineering and data teams, ideally as product counsel or in a compliance-by-design role.

CHIEF OF STAFF TO THE CHRO

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Chief of Staff to the CHRO is the operational and strategic backbone of the People & Culture organization. Working closely with the CHRO and the P&C Leadership Team (PLT), this person owns the team's reporting and operating rhythm and leads selected strategic initiatives. They bring independent judgment to consequential people and organizational decisions and serve as a trusted partner to P&C leaders and senior stakeholders across Nubank.

This is a broad role. It combines governance, strategic planning, and business analysis, and it is designed as an entry point to other roles in the organization. Candidates are evaluated both for the Chief of Staff role itself and for their potential to take on broader responsibilities over time.

This is an individual contributor role built on ownership and trust. We expect someone who anticipates needs, brings structure to ambiguous problems, and moves work forward with a high degree of autonomy. They build alignment across teams, challenge assumptions constructively, and know when to bring a trade-off or risk to the CHRO. The role requires sound judgment and discretion in handling sensitive people and organizational matters.

YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

 - Own the P&C operating rhythm. Connect P&C strategic priorities to planning cycles, leadership forums, business reviews, and ensures a focused CHRO agenda, continuously reassessing what deserves her attention. Define what gets reported, to whom, and at what cadence.

ABOUT NU

Nu serves more than 143 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page https://www.nu.com/2026-en

ABOUT THE TEAM

Mexico FP&A is the finance partner of the Mexico business. We sit between the product, credit, growth and marketing teams and the country leadership, and our job is to make sure every bet the business makes is sized, challenged and reflected in the P&L before it is made.

We are not a reporting team. We work hand in hand with Credit Card, Lending, Cuenta (deposits and transactional) and Growth stakeholders, as well as Treasury, Controllership, Public Policy, Second Line Risk and Investor Relations, to turn strategy into numbers and numbers into decisions.

How we work

 - We are owners: we make things happen instead of waiting for them.

 - We have a bias to output: fast, right-sized answers over months-long projects.

 - We set the finance agenda, not only serve it.

 - We embrace conflicting ideas and question the status quo, with data.

 - We work hard, with integrity and putting the team first.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As the IC7 in Mexico FP&A for credit products and strategic planning, you are the senior analytical bridge between Mexico's credit products, the P&L and the planning process. You do not run closings or own the budget calendar. You own something harder: making sure what goes into the plan is grounded, challenged and financially sound, and that leadership decides with the right numbers in front of them.

The role has three faces. You are a business partner to Credit Card, Lending, Cuenta, Growth and Core, who challenges their strategy and helps them bake initiatives into the plan. You are a first responder who quantifies, within days, anything that hits the P&L that wasn't planned. And you are a decision shaper who builds the frameworks, tools and governance leadership uses to decide.

At this level you set the finance agenda rather than wait for requests. You work directly with the country CEO, CFO and business-unit leaders, move between hands-on modeling and executive framing in the same week, and raise the analytical bar of the team around you.

WHAT YOU WILL DO
1. Partner with product teams and bake their initiatives into the plan

 - Understand the projections of Credit Card, Lending, Cuenta, Growth and Core teams and challenge the strategy behind them: assumptions, timing, certainty and whether the impact is really incremental.

 - Help teams translate initiatives into P&L impact when they don't know how, and carry them into budget, rebudget, forecast checkpoints and the 5-year plan.

 - Size initiatives with a consistent toolkit (NPV, CAC, payback, ROAS, gross profit) and apply clear inclusion criteria.

 - Push back when a plan doesn't add up and perform deep dives proactively, for example recommending not to launch a program until its economics are positive, and proposing alternatives such as phased rollouts or test budgets.
2. React fast to anything that hits the P&L unplanned

 - Be the first to quantify regulatory and market shocks.

 - Turn the impact into options: mitigation levers, owners and dates, not only a number.

 - Detect and escalate data and accounting anomalies that distort the P&L.
3. Be the analytical bridge between credit products, the P&L and planning

 - Challenge investments and strengthen how decisions are made with clear argumentation.

 - Build tools leadership can use directly that help in the decision-making process.

 - Propose and drive decision governance, especially on when Finance must be involved.
4. Communicate to executives and raise the bar of the team

 - Prepare materials for executives with a clear narrative, grounded in numbers.

 - Support regulatory deliverables.

 - Coach analysts on the team and set the bar for analytical rigor.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

Must have

 - Bachelor's degree in Economics, Finance, Industrial Engineering, Actuarial Science or a related quantitative field; a master's degree is a plus.

 - 8+ years of experience in FP&A, business analytics, strategy or credit analytics, with a significant part in consumer credit, banking or fintech.

 - Track record of changing senior leadership decisions with analysis: stopping, reshaping or accelerating initiatives based on their economics.

 - Deep unit-economics and credit knowledge: NPV, CAC and payback, ROAS and incrementality, cost of risk, provisions (IFRS 9), funds transfer pricing, interchange, and how credit policy flows into the P&L.

 - Hands-on analytical

jobs.title: Senior Director: Corporate Governance & Public Company Reporting
jobs.description:
ABOUT NU

Nu serves more than 143 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page https://www.nu.com/2026-en

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Legal team partners with Nubank's leadership, Board and regulated entities across Brazil, Mexico, Colombia and the United States. This role sits in a small, high-visibility team under the Chief Legal Officer that owns governance for the parent company and sets the standards that bank and other regulated-entity boards follow as well as advises on all public company reporting and issuer matters.

Day to day, you will work alongside the CLO, CFO and the executive team, and with Finance, Investor Relations, Treasury, Risk, Compliance, regional legal and regulatory teams, and outside counsel across several jurisdictions.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a public company, Nubank needs governance and reporting that work end to end: from the parent Board and its committees down to every regulated entity in the group. This role leads that model. You will serve as Assistant Corporate Secretary to the parent company and be a trusted partner to directors and executives, while owning the company's SEC and NYSE reporting program and the global standards for how subsidiary and bank boards operate.

You will also be the execution engine behind large, strategic corporate initiatives, turning legal requirements into clear ownership, milestones and decisions across many moving parts. This is a big remit with direct exposure to the Board and executive team.

You will:

 - Run Board and committee processes end to end, so directors receive well-prepared, decision-focused materials on time.

 - Lead SEC and NYSE reporting, with disciplined disclosure controls and timely, consistent filings.

 - Build the readiness plan, owners, controls and systems for the evolution of the company's public-company reporting and governance requirements.

 - Set a global governance baseline for regional bank and subsidiary boards, adapted to local law and supervisory expectations.

 - Drive cross-functional corporate, legal-entity and capital-markets projects from kickoff to close.

As a senior leadership role, this position is subject to Nu’s Global Statutory Officer Policy and involves appointment across applicable group entities. Final designation remains contingent upon local legal, compliance, and regulatory clearances.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND EXPECTATIONS

Board and corporate secretary support

 - Coordinate with the CLO, annual Board and committee calendar, agendas, materials, minutes, resolutions and evaluations, and attend Board meetings.

 - Manage director onboarding, committee charters, governance policies and annual shareholder meetings.

 - Help the team adopt the operating rhythms of a public company board, and prepare executives to present to directors with confidence.

Public company reporting and securities compliance

 - Lead the SEC and NYSE reporting program under the current foreign private issuer framework, including Form 20-F, Form 6-K, registration statements and related disclosure processes.

 - Coordinate drafting, review, certifications, filing calendars and approvals with Finance, Investor Relations, Treasury, Risk, Compliance and business leaders.

 - Prepare the organization for expanded reporting and governance requirements, including disclosure controls, calendars, systems and cross-functional ownership.

 - Oversee, with Compliance, insider-reporting and securities-compliance processes, including Section 16 filings, trading windows, insider lists and related policies.

Global and regulated-entity governance

 - Define global baseline standards for subsidiary and bank boards: structure, reserved matters, delegated authority, escalation, minutes, materials and records.

 - Advise on governance requirements for regulated financial institutions in the United States and Latin America, working with local legal and regulatory teams on independence, notifications and supervisory matters.

 - Make sure the parent Board understands what is happening at the local level, and that local boards align with group expectations.

Corporate projects and legal-entity management

 - Lead or support financings, capital-markets transactions, M&A, reorganizations and large legal-entity structuring initiatives, project-managing counsel across jurisdictions.

 - Own global legal-entity governance and lifecycle management: formation, maintenance, annual filings, officer and director appointments, powers of attorney, signatory authorities, reorganizations and dissolutions.

Outside counsel, process and innovation

 - Manage outside counsel and specialist providers with clear scopes, budgets and accountability.

 - Improve templates, processes, technology and governance data as the company grows, and adopt AI and automation responsibly, with confidentiality safeguards and human review.

QUALIFICATIONS

Professional Experience & Education

 - Law degree; admission to practice law in the United States (New York preferred). Brazilian qualification is a plus.

 - 10-15 years of relevant legal experience in corporate governance, securities, public-company reporting or corporate legal work, including meaningful responsibility for Board and committee matters.

 - Training at a leading U.S. law firm, advising public companies, or financial institutions.

 - In-house experience at a regulated financial institution, fintech or large regulated, international group (banking, payments, consumer finance, lending, broker-dealer or digital assets), advising across legal, regulatory, product and business teams.

 - Familiarity with banking regulation and regulated-entity governance in the United States and Latin America; depth in Brazil preferred, Mexico, Colombia or other regional markets valuable.

 - Working knowledge of SEC requirements for foreign private issuers and U.S. domestic registrants, NYSE listing standards and public-company disclosure controls.

 - Experience as a corporate secretary, assistant secretary or senior governance counsel supporting a public-company Board and committees, including drafting materials and minutes and advising directors and executives.

 - Experience coordinating multi-jurisdictional work with local and international counsel.

Competencies & Attributes

 - Ability to work comfortably with senior leaders and directors in both the United States and Brazil.

 - Has executive presence and can explain complex matters clearly and with poise.

 - Ability to influence senior leaders and directors in the U.S. and Brazil, and align stakeholders across time zones and functions.

 - Very detail-oriented and organized, able to manage many parallel workstreams, deadlines and moving parts without losing accuracy.

 - Ability to turn legal requirements into plain language for non-lawyers.

 - Ownership and urgency: delivers with limited supervision, follows through and removes obstacles.

ROLE DETAILS

Location: Brazil or the United States. The role requires travel to São Paulo and to Board meetings in the US.

Reports To: This position reports to the Chief Legal Officer, who is based in the US.

The Credit Risk Squad is part of the 2nd line of defense, responsible for managing and overseeing the credit risk function of our organization by providing independent oversight and challenge to the first line of defense. Within it, the Provisions team creates the Expected Credit Loss (ECL) models used to calculate loss allowances, participating end to end in model development, implementation, monitoring, data quality and support to Finance accounting teams. Our models feed Nubank's financial statements under IFRS 9 and local regulation, including CMN Resolution 4,966/2021 and BCB Resolution 352/2023 in Brazil.

About the Role 

As a Retail Credit Risk Senior Specialist focused on Brazil, you'll be the focal point for everything related to Res. 4966 expected credit loss provisioning. You'll proactively identify and control gaps in the models and in the processes built around them, from inputs and model implementation to closing and regulatory reporting. That means making sure models comply with regulatory expectations, produce the correct data for accounting and regulatory reports, and that ECL movements are understood, controlled and well explained.

You'll also be a primary point of contact for the local regulator (BCB) and the external auditors (KPMG) on the local models, working alongside the team's leadership. This is an individual-contributor role with high visibility among senior stakeholders in Finance, Risk and the local CRO's office.

YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

ABOUT NU

Nu serves more than 143 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

ABOUT THE ROLE 

This role leads analytics for two scopes, Contestation and Fraud Security Features, and is accountable for the analytical side of both rather than the product roadmap. The work spans fraud victim reimbursement, chargeback resolution, operations time per complaint, AI adoption in operations, regulatory reporting, new security layers for customers, and a horizontal view of how fraud frictions affect customers' lives.

The Contestation Platform team is the analytical foundation for how Nubank handles customer reports and disputes, providing the best experience possible for customers who were fraud victims or had any issues with their credit card purchases. This includes an intuitive reporting flow, transparency in the process and fairness in reimbursements decisions. The focus for 2027 is how we can increase the AI usage in the platform to decrease total costs of our complaints, including decreasing losses and operational time spent to resolve a complaint.

The Security Features team is an innovative area, with the primary goal to make Nubank customers feel safer, and we do this by creating solutions that increase customers' perception of our defenses and also create new defenses. Our best example is Safe Mode (Modo Rua), an extra security layer that protects customers' investments and cash-out when we detect they are away from home/ safe wifi networks. The focus for 2027 is to understand why customers still believe Nubank is not the safest financial institution, even though we believe we have best-in-class fraud policies/models at least in BR, and after identifying the pain points, increase safety perception.

The Customer Analytics scope was once a dedicated pack and is now held by one of the Decision Intelligence analysts. It owns horizontal fraud views, trying to solve a historical gap we have in fraud, that teams are isolated in their silos, not having proper understanding of how different squads' defenses impact customers as a whole in their real life. The focus for 2027 is to ensure fraud squads understand their defenses' impact in customers' experience, and give CX the same weight as fraud losses for decision making.

YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR

jobs.title: Associate Director – Portfolio & Restructuring
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

At OakNorth, we're on a mission to empower ambitious businesses and the communities they serve. Since 2015, we've lent over $21 billion across the UK and US, helped create more than 58,000 new homes and 36,000 new jobs, and supported hundreds of thousands of personal savers — all while driving economic growth in the markets we serve.

About the Role

OakNorth is looking for an experienced and commercially minded In-House Legal Associate Director to join our Portfolio & Restructuring Legal team (PM-TET) in the US. This is a newly created role and an amazing opportunity to be our first dedicated US portfolio lawyer, supporting our US Portfolio & Restructuring Team (PMT US) as our US lending book continues to grow.

We're dedicated to helping trailblazing businesses thrive, and our support doesn't stop at closing. PM-TET advises on everything that happens during the life of a loan, from amendments, waivers and consents through to events of default, acquisitions and facility increases, and supporting on restructurings, protecting the bank's position while giving practical and commercial legal advice.

This role offers the unique opportunity to own day-to-day US portfolio legal advice, work directly with PMT US and senior stakeholders, and shape how the function is built out in the US. You will report to the Senior Director, PM-TET in London and the Senior Director, PMT in the US, and work closely with PMT US and our Transaction Execution team in the US (TET US), as part of a wider PM-TET team across London and India. As you grow, so will your influence and responsibility, shaping not just individual matters, but the future of OakNorth's portfolio in the US.

In a nutshell, the mission of our Associate Director will be to act as the go-to legal adviser for PMT US during US business hours, providing timely, US-qualified advice on US law loan and security documents and making sure post-completion matters are executed efficiently and in line with Credit approvals. The successful candidate will have significant lender-side experience in real estate, lender finance and/or corporate lending, ideally including portfolio management work, with some exposure to workout or restructuring matters. The candidate will be able to work within tight timelines, exercise sound judgement independently, and will align with the OakNorth values of working as one team with the ambition to deliver a high-quality product to our customers.

What You'll Do

 - Act as the primary legal adviser to PMT US on all day-to-day legal matters arising during the life of the loan across the US portfolio.

 - Interpret US law finance and security documents and advise PMT US on the bank's rights, obligations and options under the documents.

 - Prepare, review and negotiate amendments, waivers, consents, extension agreements and management agreements, ensuring they accurately reflect Credit approvals.

 - Advise on potential and actual events of default, prepare reservation of rights letters and other notices, and help develop strategies that protect the bank’s position.

 - Lead the legal workstream on acquisitions, facility increases and redemptions, dealing with conditions precedent, other completion requirements and the release of security.

 - Advise on US-specific security and structures, including UCC security and filings, deposit account control agreements (DACAs), co-lends and participations, and lease reviews.

 - Instruct and manage US external counsel, controlling scope and spend and determining which matters can be handled in-house.

 - Support PMT US on US restructurings, forbearance arrangements and enforcement where required, working alongside US external counsel.

 - Develop US precedents, templates and playbooks aligned with PM-TET UK, and maintain matter trackers and records so that all standard operating procedures are complied with.

 - Work closely with PMT US, Credit, Operations, TET US and Debt Finance teams to ensure that portfolio actions are consistent with credit terms.

 - Collaborate with the PM-TET team in London and India, sharing knowledge on US law and practice and supporting team members on US matters.

 - Advise as to US lending customs and practices in the context of post-completion portfolio management and assist with expanding the US lending platform.

 - Live all OakNorth values, be a culture carrier and leverage GenAI tools to increase productivity and enhance decision-making.
 
 

YOU'LL BE A GREAT FIT IF YOU HAVE…

 - US qualification admitted and in good standing in at least one US state, with at least 4 years' post-qualification experience in lender-side real estate, lender finance and/or corporate lending, gained in private practice and/or in-house at a bank or lender.

 - Experience of day-to-day portfolio management work, such as amendments, waivers, consents and events of default, with some exposure to workout, restructuring or enforcement.

 - Strong working knowledge of US secured lending.

 - Strong communication and interpersonal skills to build trusted relationships with:
 
 - ExCo and senior stakeholders in the US and UK businesses.
 
 - PMT US and Credit, giving clear, pragmatic and commercial advice at all stages of a matter.
 
 - Wider teams including TET US, Operations, Customer Due Diligence and Finance.
 
 - External counsel, borrowers, sponsors and co-lenders.

 - The confidence to work autonomously, exercise sound judgement on risk and know when to escalate.

 - A commercial mindset, with the ability to find practical solutions that protect the bank's position.

 - High level attention to detail, project management and organisational ability, with the ability to manage a number of matters simultaneously.

 - Ability to understand and process information quickly and effectively.

 - Comfort working as part of a team spread across different time zones (US, UK and India).

 - Proactive and personal drive, results driven, team player, flexible across products and matters, and able to work outside of comfort zone and develop new areas of proficiency.

 - Ability to succeed in a culture where change and speed are part of daily work.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Credit Risk - Real Estate
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

At OakNorth, we’re on a mission to empower ambitious businesses and the communities they serve. Since 2015, we’ve lent over $21 billion across the UK and US, helped create more than 58,000 new homes and 36,000 new jobs, and supported hundreds of thousands of personal savers — all while driving economic growth in the markets we serve.

We’re an entrepreneurial, technology-led bank, combining deep lending expertise with data, technology and AI to make better decisions and deliver a different experience for our customers.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Credit Risk team plays a critical role in enabling OakNorth to support ambitious businesses while maintaining a high-quality lending portfolio. Working closely with Debt Finance Origination, Credit Analytics, Portfolio Management and Legal, we bring together technical expertise, independent judgement and commercial thinking to support lending decisions.

We’re a collaborative, fast-moving team where people are encouraged to challenge, take ownership and find solutions. You’ll be part of this team, bringing dedicated real estate expertise to the same shared portfolio and working closely with colleagues across Credit Risk and the wider business.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Senior Director, Credit Risk – Real Estate to play a senior role in shaping credit decisions across OakNorth’s UK real estate lending portfolio. You’ll lead the independent assessment and challenge of opportunities across a broad range of SME real estate businesses, from investment and development finance to operational real estate.

This is an opportunity to bring deep property credit expertise and sound commercial judgement to transactions that matter. You’ll work closely with Debt Finance Origination, Credit Analytics and Portfolio Management, influencing deals from an early stage, helping shape their structure and presenting clear, high-quality recommendations to Credit Committee.

As a senior member of the Credit Risk team, you’ll have the trust and scope to influence complex decisions, engage directly with customers and senior stakeholders, and help raise the quality of our approach to real estate lending. You’ll balance disciplined risk management with the opportunity to back ambitious businesses and the communities they serve.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Lead credit decisions: Own the independent assessment and challenge of new real estate lending opportunities, bringing clear judgement to decisions across the UK portfolio.

 - Shape transactions early: Partner with Debt Finance Origination and Credit Analytics from the outset to identify key risks, test assumptions and develop structures that work for OakNorth and its customers.

 - Set the standard for Credit Committee: Lead clear, well-reasoned recommendations and bring constructive challenge to senior credit discussions and decisions.

 - Assess complex real estate: Apply your expertise across investment and development finance in residential, office, retail and industrial property, as well as operational real estate such as PBSA, BTR and co-living.

 - Get beneath the numbers: Scrutinise cashflow models, Red Book valuations and Project Monitor reports where relevant, making sure each decision is based on reliable, relevant and robust information.

 - Work directly with customers: Join borrower discussions with the Debt Finance team, providing an early view on credit appetite, structure and the risks that need to be addressed.

 - Protect portfolio quality: Work with Portfolio Management on existing exposures, including loan increases, extensions, covenant resets, restructurings and emerging risks.

 - Support strong execution: Review term sheets, security structures and key documentation, working with Legal and Loan Execution to ensure appropriate protections and good customer outcomes.

 - Bring independent judgement: Take a balanced, pragmatic view — knowing when to support a transaction, when to challenge and when a proposal should not proceed.

 - Help shape our approach: Contribute to strategic work that strengthens real estate credit and the wider team, including thoughtful use of data, technology and AI to improve assessment and decision-making.

YOU’LL BE A GREAT FIT IF YOU HAVE…

 - At least 10 years’ experience in credit risk, with deep expertise in SME real estate lending or a strong track record of transferable experience

 - Strong knowledge of real estate investment and development finance across sectors such as residential, office, retail and industrial

 - Experience with operational real estate, including PBSA, BTR or co-living; experience in SME cashflow lending or lending at fund level would also be valuable

 - Excellent financial analysis skills and the ability to assess complex transactions, business plans, cashflows, valuations, downside scenarios and debt capacity

 - A strong track record of independent credit judgement, constructive challenge and influencing senior credit decisions

 - Confidence leading Credit Committee discussions and engaging with customers, deal teams and senior stakeholders

 - A good understanding of SME credit risk models and measures, including RWA, PD and LGD

 - Strong experience with risk and control techniques, including setting effective covenants and managing portfolio risk

 - The commercial judgement to balance disciplined risk management with backing ambitious businesses

 - Clear communication, negotiation and stakeholder skills, alongside the ability to take ownership and manage competing priorities in a fast-moving environment

NICE TO HAVE

 - A broader understanding of risk across the SME product lifecycle, from origination and optimisation through to collections and recoveries

 - Experience working directly with clients and deal teams on transaction structure and credit appetite

 - Experience contributing to strategic projects or improving credit processes and decision-making

WHY OAKNORTH?

At OakNorth, you’ll work on meaningful, complex lending transactions without the layers of bureaucracy often associated with larger institutions. You’ll be part of one Credit Risk team, with the opportunity to bring specialist real estate expertise while working closely with colleagues across the business.

We value independent thinking, commercial judgement and people who take ownership. We move quickly, challenge conventional approaches and use technology and AI to keep improving how we work. As we grow, you’ll have the opportunity to influence not only individual transactions, but how we approach real estate lending and risk management more broadly.

If you’re an experienced real estate credit professional ready for greater ownership, exposure to senior decision-makers and the chance to make a meaningful impact, we’d love to hear from you.

WHAT WE OFFER

 - Equity — we want you to have a stake in the business so our interests are aligned

 - 25 days’ holiday plus personalised benefits — opt in to what matters to you

 - Subsidised private medical insurance with Bupa

 - Enhanced maternity and paternity leave

 - Wellbeing and social events, plus an in-house Barista Bar in the London office

 - Volunteering time off to support causes that matter to you

 - Salary sacrifice schemes — cycle to work, nursery, gym and electric car scheme

THE ROLE

Working directly with OakNorth's Chief Lending Officer, you'll help grow and scale our UK and US lending businesses.

This is a commercial, analytical and hands-on role. You'll shape strategy, assess growth opportunities and work with lending leadership and teams across the business to turn plans into results.

You’ll be a trusted partner to the CLO — exercising independent judgement, anticipating what’s next and bringing structure without slowing decisions — and thrive in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

SHAPE GROWTH AND STRATEGY

 - Shape the growth strategy for UK and US lending, identifying opportunities across sectors, markets and segments and testing them with financial modelling and commercial judgement

 - Own the strategic planning rhythm — annual plans, budgets, targets and quarterly priorities — with Finance, Credit and lending leadership

TURN STRATEGY INTO EXECUTION

 - Lead high-priority strategic and operational initiatives end to end, turning priorities into clear plans with milestones and owners

 - Work across Lending, Credit, Finance, Product, Technology and People to keep initiatives moving and remove barriers

PARTNER WITH THE CLO AND BUILD FOR SCALE

 - Act as a trusted partner to the CLO — preparing analysis and materials for executive, leadership and board discussions, and coordinating MBRs, QBRs and OKRs

 - Build the operating models, structures, hiring and capabilities needed to scale, simplifying through technology, automation and AI

THE PROFILE

We are open on background. You may have worked in investment banking, private credit, commercial lending, strategy and operations, consulting, or as a Chief of Staff to a senior commercial leader. What matters most is how you think and your ability to turn strategy into results.

YOU WILL BRING:

 - Commercial and growth mindset — able to spot opportunities, size them and translate them into actionable plans

 - Strategic and operational capability — thinks strategically while getting into the detail to deliver

 - Strong executive partnership — confident with a fast-moving leader; independent judgement, clarity and constructive challenge without slowing decisions

 - Entrepreneurial approach — comfortable without a playbook, taking ownership in a high-growth environment

 - High energy, low ego and a hands-on approach

 - Financial services experience — strong preference for banking, lending, private credit or investment banking

WHAT WE OFFER

 - Equity — we want you to have a stake in the business so our interests are aligned

 - 25 days’ holiday plus personalised benefits — opt in to what matters to you

 - Subsidised private medical insurance with Bupa

 - Enhanced maternity and paternity leave

 - Wellbeing and social events, plus an in-house Barista Bar in the London office

 - Volunteering time off to support causes that matter to you

jobs.title: Industrial Training - Finance (Regulatory Reporting)
jobs.description:
OAKNORTH

Industrial Training – Regulatory Reporting

Finance · Regulatory Reporting

📍 India | 🕐 Internship (12 months) | 🏢 Onsite | 🎯 Intern

ABOUT US

At OakNorth, we're on a mission to empower ambitious businesses and the communities they serve. Since 2015, we've lent over $21 billion across the UK and US, helped create more than 58,000 new homes and 36,000 new jobs, and supported hundreds of thousands of personal savers — all while driving economic growth in the markets we serve.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Regulatory Reporting team is responsible for producing accurate, timely, and complete regulatory and management reporting across liquidity, capital, credit, and balance sheet returns for OakNorth Bank. We work closely with Treasury, Finance, and Risk to ensure the Bank meets its obligations to the PRA, Bank of England, and other regulators — while continuously improving the quality and efficiency of our reporting processes.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for an Intern to join our Regulatory Reporting and Treasury team for a 9-month placement, with an immediate start. You'll support the production of a broad range of regulatory returns — including liquidity, capital, and balance sheet-driven submissions — alongside management information and treasury ALCO packs. This is an excellent opportunity for a recently qualified finance professional to gain hands-on exposure to regulatory reporting in a fast-paced banking environment.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Support production of monthly and quarterly liquidity returns including NSFR, LCR, ALMM, and PRA110, with reconciliation to financials.

 - Assist with balance sheet-driven regulatory returns including FINREP, PRA108, and Bank of England statistical returns (BT, ELS, GT, AD, AL, BE, CC, PL).

 - Contribute to additional exposure-related returns including FSA015, PRA loan book data, asset encumbrance, and mortgage returns (MLAR).

 - Support capital and RWA reporting including own funds, credit exposure returns, leverage ratio, and large exposures.

 - Assist in the preparation of pre-defined and ad hoc management information as directed by the manager.

 - Support production of treasury ALCO packs.

 - Ensure accuracy, timeliness, and completeness of all reporting; highlight gaps or errors in processes or logic and actively contribute to improvements.

 - Support the Pillar 3 document publication process and assist with stress testing, ICAAP, and ILAAP activities.

YOU'LL BE A GREAT FIT IF YOU HAVE…

 - CA intermediate cleared and Article ship completed from a reputed firm.

 - A strong foundation in financial and accounting concepts, with an interest in regulatory reporting and treasury functions.

 - High attention to detail with a commitment to accuracy and completeness in all work produced.

 - Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple reporting deadlines simultaneously.

 - A proactive approach to identifying and resolving process gaps, with a continuous improvement mindset.

Nice to Have

 - Prior exposure to regulatory reporting frameworks such as PRA, Bank of England returns, or Basel III metrics.

 - Familiarity with liquidity and capital concepts including LCR, NSFR, or RWA calculations.

 - Experience working with financial data in Excel or other reporting tools.

jobs.title: Manager - Treasury, Capital Markets / Front Office
jobs.description:
The role

OakNorth runs an £8bn balance sheet with a small, senior Treasury team. Reporting to the Head of Treasury, you will own the execution of the bank's derivatives and FX activity and its investment portfolio, the sizing of its FX funding and liquidity positions, and support for capital and wholesale funding issuance — building the analytics behind those decisions. Treasury here is run as a measurable profit contributor rather than a cost centre, and the decisions taken on this desk are a material part of that.

This is a hands-on execution role rather than an oversight one. You will be pricing, trading, sizing and building the analysis behind your own recommendations, and presenting that work in senior forums including ALCO and to the CFO.

The role is deliberately front-office weighted, but the team is small and the remit is broad. There is genuine scope to build depth in the wider Treasury agenda — funds transfer pricing, liquidity and interest rate risk frameworks, and Board and regulatory work — for someone who wants it.

Principal responsibilities

Derivatives and FX

 - Execute interest rate swaps, cross-currency swaps and FX forwards across the bank's hedging programme. This is the most frequent trading activity on the desk and the centre of the role

 - Price, negotiate and execute with dealers across the counterparty panel, and evidence best execution

 - Own the FX risk position — including the USD lending book and intragroup exposures — and produce the exposure and hedging analysis that supports ALCO and Board reporting

 - Monitor collateral and margin flows under CSA arrangements, including the liquidity consequences of adverse mark-to-market moves. Supports expansion and onboarding with additional counterparts

 - Work with Finance on hedge designation and supporting documentation
 
 

Investment portfolio

 - Execute the gilt and HQLA investment programme against Board-approved mandates, using asset-swap spread and relative-value analysis to inform selection

 - Maintain and extend the portfolio construction tooling, including duration, maturity-ladder and concentration constraints

 - Size and roll the Treasury bill programme against deposit deployment windows

 - Support oversight of the externally managed AAA CLO portfolio, including trend and spread analytics and preparation for quarterly manager review

 - Support expansion of the investment instruments to develop the liquidity portfolio
 
 

Capital and funding issuance

 - Support the origination and execution of capital instrument issuance — Tier 2 and AT1 — working alongside the Treasurer, CFO and external advisers

 - Build and maintain the analysis behind issuance decisions, including sizing, pricing benchmarks and comparable market levels

 - Contribute to the development of wholesale funding options as the balance sheet grows, potentially spanning senior unsecured and secured issuance and securitisation
 
 

Funding and liquidity sizing

This part of the role is about sizing and direction. Operational execution and settlement sit with Treasury Operations; you set the strategy, size the transaction and steer the team.

 - Own USD liquidity end to end — determining how much liquidity is required in currency, and executing the cross-currency swaps that deliver it within Risk Appetite Limits

 - Set the sizing and collateral strategy for Bank of England repo facilities (ILTR and STR), instructing and reviewing rather than operating them

 - Steer the wider team on the analytical basis for funding and liquidity decisions, and review their output
 
 

Analytics and automation

We work extensively with AI-assisted development — Claude and Claude Code — inside a GitHub-controlled workflow. You do not need to be a software engineer, but you do need to be able to build a working analytical tool this way, or to learn to do so quickly.

 - Build, maintain and extend the desk's Python toolkit — pricing, sizing, limit monitoring and income attribution

 - Replace manual spreadsheet processes with repeatable, auditable and documented ones

 - Contribute to the Treasury Management System implementation and the Bloomberg data integration
 
 

Control, governance and reporting

 - Ensure trades are captured, confirmed and reported in line with the Treasury Trading Policy and supporting procedures

 - Monitor Risk Appetite Limits and Key Risk Indicators for front-office activity, and escalate promptly and clearly

 - Prepare and present front-office inputs to ALCO

 - Support regulatory deliverables — ILAAP, ICAAP and PRA information requests — from a front-office perspective
 
 

Essential experience and skills

 - Relevant execution experience — typically three to six years in a bank treasury front office, money markets or ALM desk, or a markets and rates role with clearly transferable execution skills.

 - Well-honed Bloomberg skills.. You should be fast and self-sufficient across money market and fixed income pricing, curve and relative-value analysis, swap and FX pricing, and the day-to-day ticket and blotter workflow.

 - Instrument knowledge — interest rate and cross-currency swaps and FX forwards first and foremost, together with gilts, Treasury bills and repo including Bank of England facilities.

 - Regulatory mechanics — a sound working understanding of LCR, NSFR and HQLA classification, as well as Capital regulation and how execution decisions move them.

 - Python literacy — sufficient to build, read and debug analytical tooling (pandas, numpy), together with real enthusiasm for AI-assisted development.

 - Communication — the ability to explain a trade, a number or a risk clearly and briefly to a senior, non-specialist audience.

Desirable

 - CFA, FRM, BTRM in progress or complete

 - Exposure to Clearing, CSA and margining mechanics, SA-CCR, or hedge accounting

 - Securitisation, CLO or structured credit experience

 - Exposure to debt capital markets — capital instrument or senior debt issuance, or securitisation — from a bank treasury, DCM or advisory seat

 - Experience in a challenger bank or another small team where breadth was required rather than optional
 
 

Who will do well here

 - You get things moving. Pace matters more than polish, and you are comfortable forming a view, making a call and owning the outcome.

 - You learn quickly and want to. The technical range here is wide, and we would rather hire someone visibly capable and eager to grow into the full breadth of it than someone with a narrow and finished skill set.

 - You are helpful by default. The team is small and nobody's job description is treated as a boundary.

 - You are comfortable being challenged, and challenging back.

You thrive in a global team. The finance team is spread across the UK and India and you're good at building trust across time zones and you don't need to be in the same room to stay aligned.

jobs.title: People Partner - US
jobs.description:
OakNorth is a leading commercial digital bank, built by entrepreneurs for entrepreneurs. Founded in 2015, we support lower mid-market businesses — those with revenues between $1m and $100m — by providing fast, flexible debt finance and personalised banking services. To date, we have lent over $16bn to businesses globally, directly contributing to the creation of 56,000 jobs and 34,000 new homes.

We began operating in the US in mid-2023 and have since lent over $700m to US businesses. In March 2025, we announced an exciting milestone: the acquisition of Community Unity Bank (CUB), an FDIC-insured community bank based in Birmingham, Michigan, which marks a significant step in our US expansion.

This is a rare opportunity to join early and have real ownership over how we build People in the US. As we establish our American operation across New York and Michigan, this is the first dedicated People hire on the ground — you won't be inheriting a playbook, you'll be writing it.

THE ROLE

We are looking for a commercially minded, hands-on People Partner to support our US business. Reporting into the Senior Director, People Partnering, based in the UK, you will be the primary HR contact for our US employee population across New York and Michigan, partnering closely with senior leaders to deliver an exceptional employee experience and drive business performance. This is a generalist role - you will need to be comfortable operating at both a strategic and operational level.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

BUSINESS PARTNERING

 - Be a genuine commercial partner to US leaders — understanding the growth agenda, embedding yourself in the business, and shaping people strategies that directly support OakNorth's US expansion.

 - Build trusted relationships quickly across New York and Michigan, becoming the go-to for leaders navigating anything from org design to team performance.

 - Use data and insight to get ahead of risks and opportunities, bringing proactive insight led recommendations.

EMPLOYEE RELATIONS & COMPLIANCE

 - Manage employee relations matters end-to-end, including performance management, investigations, and separations, in line with US employment law.

 - Maintain up-to-date knowledge of federal and state employment legislation across New York and Michigan, and ensure policies and practices are compliant.

 - Partner with legal counsel as required on complex or sensitive ER matters.

 - Maintain accurate HR records and ensure compliance with at-will employment frameworks and applicable state-specific requirements.

PERFORMANCE & TALENT

 - Support the delivery of OakNorth's performance cycle, including calibration and year-end processes, ensuring consistency across the US population.

 - Partner with managers to build capability, provide coaching on feedback and development conversations, and embed a high-performance culture.

 - Identify high-potential talent and support succession planning in partnership with the global People team.

LEARNING, DEVELOPMENT & CULTURE

 - Partner with the L&D team to embed OakNorth's learning strategy on the ground in the US — spanning Manager Capability, Performance & Growth, Employee Lifecycle, and AI & Future Capability.

 - Act as a culture carrier for OakNorth's values and ways of working as we establish our US presence, ensuring the experience in New York and Michigan feels authentically OakNorth.

 - Drive employee engagement across the US population — running listening mechanisms, interpreting data, and working with leaders to take meaningful action.

 - Champion belonging and inclusion within the US team, connecting local initiatives to the global People agenda.

ONBOARDING & OFFBOARDING

 - Help support with the onboarding experience for US hires, ensuring a smooth and engaging start.

 - Manage offboarding processes, including exit interviews, and feed insights back to the People Partners.

GLOBAL COLLABORATION

 - Work closely with People Partners in the UK and India to deliver consistent, globally aligned people practices.

 - Contribute to global People projects and initiatives, including L&D, culture, and engagement programmes.

 - Act as the US voice in global People discussions, bringing market-specific context and insight.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

ESSENTIAL

 - 5+ years of HR generalist or business partnering experience, ideally within a fast-paced financial services, fintech, or technology environment.

 - Strong knowledge of US employment law; experience navigating multi-state complexity across New York and Michigan.

 - Track record of building credible relationships with senior stakeholders and influencing without authority.

 - Experience managing complex employee relations matters independently.

 - Proactive, resourceful, and solutions-focused, with a bias for action and the confidence to build where a playbook doesn't yet exist.

 - Strong communication skills; able to flex between tactical delivery and strategic conversation.

 - Collaborative working style with the ability to operate effectively across time zones within a global team.

 - Willingness to travel between New York and Michigan as required to support both locations.

 - Comfortable using AI tools to work smarter — drafting, analysing data, spotting patterns — and acts as an advocate for AI adoption within the people function.

 - Approaches work with an AI-native mindset; not just open to new tools but actively seeks ways to leverage them to improve the employee experience and HR delivery.

DESIRABLE

 - Experience in a scale-up, growth-stage, or post-acquisition integration environment.

 - Exposure to performance management system implementation or optimisation.

 - Experience working with an international People team across multiple geographies.

LOCATION & WAYS OF WORKING

New York (5 days in office). We are a high-energy, relationship-driven business and believe strongly in the value of being present. As our first People partner hire on the ground in the US, you're building relationships and culture from the ground up, and that happens in person. You'll also travel to Michigan regularly to stay close to the CUB team.

Benefits and Perks

 - 401k plan with Principal (ON match up to 4%)

 - Medical Care (managed through Insperity) - employees can add their family to their plan if needed

 - Dental & Vision bundle

 - Insperity Health Savings Account Program - this is a tax-advantaged employee benefit which can help manage health care costs by allowing employees to set aside some of their current earnings on a pretax basis for reimbursement of qualified health care expenses during the plan year

 - EAP

 - 20 days Holiday

jobs.title: Co-Head of Credit Risk – Real Estate
jobs.description:
We are looking for a Co-Head of Credit Risk – Real Estate to help grow our real estate lending businesses working alongside our Co-Head of Credit Risk – Trading Business. Together, you will provide senior credit leadership across our real estate and trading business lending, each bringing deep expertise in your area.

Based in London, you will help shape the real estate deals we do, the people we develop and how we work across the UK market, while keeping sound credit judgement at the heart of every decision.

This is a role for someone who wants to build, not just oversee. You will work closely with our Debt Finance Originators to understand customers’ ambitions and find the right structure for their transactions, making and sanctioning credit decisions and bringing an independent view to Credit Risk Committee.

The opportunity goes beyond individual deals. You will lead our Real Estate Credit Risk teams, oversee portfolio risk and help shape how we approach real estate credit as we grow internationally.

We also want your ideas. How could AI improve our analysis? Where could better data help us spot risk sooner? What should we stop doing so the team can spend more time on the decisions that matter? You will help turn those ideas into practical changes.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

SHAPE REAL ESTATE CREDIT ACROSS OAKNORTH

 - Work with senior Lending and Credit Risk colleagues to support growth across all markets, with clear views on the opportunities we should pursue and the risks we should take.

 - Help shape our approach to real estate credit, combining consistent underwriting standards with an understanding of local markets, deal structures and regulation.

 - Stay close to transactions and the portfolio, and build the team’s capability as the business grows.

CREDIT DECISIONS AND SANCTIONING

 - Make and sanction decisions on new transactions, amendments and other material credit matters within your delegated authority.

 - Assess deal structure, leverage, cash flow, security, sponsor strength and downside risk.

 - Work with Debt Finance Originators from the early stages of a deal, helping shape terms and structures that work for the customer and meet our risk appetite. Provide clear, timely credit feedback and be direct when a transaction is not right for us.

 - Take responsibility for complex or higher-risk cases, including when information is incomplete or circumstances are changing.

 - Record decisions clearly, with a sound rationale.

CREDIT RISK COMMITTEE

 - Play an active role in Credit Risk Committee and chair where appropriate, bringing a solutions-focused, commercial mindset and independent credit judgement to UK real estate decisions. Help shape our real estate credit appetite, find workable structures for good lending opportunities and keep decisions moving at pace without compromising credit standards.

 - Challenge the key assumptions and risks, including how individual deals affect portfolio concentrations.

 - Bring a clear view and be prepared to challenge senior colleagues.

BUILD AND LEAD THE TEAM

 - Lead our Real Estate Credit Risk teams, giving people clear responsibility and expecting high standards.

 - Develop credit professionals who can think for themselves, form a view and stand behind a decision.

 - Coach colleagues through complex transactions and give future leaders the experience to take on more responsibility.

 - Bring the teams together across markets, and recruit and retain the people we need for our next stage of growth.

USE AI AND DATA TO IMPROVE CREDIT WORK

AI and technology should be part of how we do credit work, not a separate project. You will help the team:

 - spend less time gathering information and preparing credit analysis and committee papers

 - use data to identify portfolio risks earlier

 - automate repetitive tasks and test tools that improve the quality and speed of our work

You do not need a technical background. We do expect curiosity, a willingness to test new approaches and the judgement to know where they add value.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

You will have substantial experience underwriting and sanctioning complex commercial real estate transactions. Direct experience of making credit decisions is essential; policy or governance experience alone is not enough.

You will bring:

 - deep knowledge of real estate lending across different asset classes and transaction types

 - sound judgement on deal structure, sponsors, security, cash flow and downside risk, alongside an understanding of portfolio exposures

 - experience on senior Credit Risk Committees and the confidence to challenge senior Lending colleagues

 - a track record of leading and developing credit teams

 - Experience in UK or across more than one lending market, would be an advantage.

WORKING AT OAKNORTH

We were founded by entrepreneurs, for entrepreneurs. Our customers have ambitions for their businesses, and we look for ways to help them get there. That takes curiosity, commercial understanding and the willingness to look beyond the obvious answer.

You should enjoy that kind of work: getting into a complex deal, challenging assumptions and finding a structure that others may have missed. Just as importantly, you need the independence to say no when the risk is not right.

We move quickly and expect people to take ownership. You will have room to put ideas into practice, challenge established ways of working and develop your team. In return, we expect clear decisions, disciplined risk judgement and responsibility for the outcome.

If you want to help grow a lending business, develop strong credit leaders and change how credit work gets done, this is an opportunity to do all three.

Benefits & Perks 

 - Equity — we want everyone to have a stake in the business so our interests are aligned

 - 25 days holiday plus personalised benefits — opt in to what matters to you

 - Subsidised private medical insurance with Bupa

 - Enhanced maternity and paternity leave

 - Wellbeing and social events, plus in-house Barista Bar in the London office

 - Volunteering time off to support causes that matter to you

 - Salary sacrifice schemes — cycle to work, nursery, gym, and electric car scheme

You will manage a book of complex real estate and property-backed loans, owning both the customer relationship and the post-origination credit risk, including customers showing early signs of financial distress. You will work with an analyst team based in India.

THE PORTFOLIO:

Sectors: residential and commercial real estate (investment and development), student accommodation, co-living and retirement living, and property-backed hotel and healthcare loans

 - Work with the India analyst team: direct day-to-day work, review outputs ,coach analysts and work across time zones/georgaphies.

 - Professional engagement: Hands on engagement with external professional advisors legal, valuers, PMS etc.

 - Work with AI: use the Bank’s approved AI tools day to day and help find step changes in how the book is managed.
 

WHAT YOU'LL BRING
• Extensive (10-15 Years) UK real estate lending or portfolio management experience across investment and development, ideally at a bank or specialist lender and in more than one sector.
• Experience of revolving credit, loan-on-loan or lender finance facilities, or a strong working understanding of how they are structured and monitored.
• Strong credit appraisal, financial analysis and modelling skills; comfortable with LMA documentation.
• Experience of managing underperforming and distressed credits, with a working knowledge of restructuring and insolvency.
• A track record of negotiating confidently and presenting clearly, both verbally and in writing, to senior stakeholders and credit committees.
• Actively looking for opportunities to grow back book; cross selling bank offering
• Openness to AI and new ways of working.

jobs.title: Business Development Representative
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

OakNorth's lending business is scaling across the UK and US, and we need a Business Development Representative to join our growing Commercial Strategy team.

Our next good deal should not depend on who happens to find us.

As a Business Development Representative, you own the front end of our lending pipeline. That means two things.

Generating new opportunities. You work hand in hand with Marketing, turning campaign themes, target segments and ideal customer profiles into live outreach: multi-touch sequences across email, phone and LinkedIn, follow-up on the demand our campaigns generate, and the account research that makes it land. The output is qualified meetings with the right people.

Qualifying inbound leads. You own inbound enquiries end to end: researching them, screening them, and routing them, within SLA, to the right Originator.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Outbound

 - Run marketing-led outbound campaigns. Take the segments, messaging and campaign themes Marketing develops and put them into market as multi-touch, multi-channel sequences, run at a consistent cadence.

 - Research accounts and personalise. Understand a business and its situation well enough to earn a first conversation.

 - Feed back on what is working. You are closest to the response (which messages land, which segments go quiet, which objections keep recurring). Campaign design gets better because you tell Marketing what you are seeing.

Inbound

 - Work the demand Marketing generates. Content downloads, webinar and event registrations, website enquiries. You pick these up quickly, research them properly, and convert those that meet our criteria.

 - Own the inbound queue. Qualify and route every inbound lead within SLA, with the research already done before it reaches an Originator.

Across both

 - Qualify with rigour. Screen against our policies and credit appetite. Saying “this is not a good fit, and here is why” is as valuable here as saying yes.

 - Nurture over time. Most businesses worth lending to are not ready today. Keep warm, useful relationships with prospects and referrers until they are.

 - Keep the data clean. Accurate CRM records and weekly pipeline reporting. What you build gets reused in outreach across the bank.

 - Work shoulder to shoulder with Originators. Take their feedback on lead quality seriously, and adjust how you work.
 
 

WHAT THIS ROLE IS NOT

 - It is not a closing role. You will not negotiate or sign facilities. You hand over to an Originator once a prospect is properly qualified.

 - It is not a volume-dialling role. Hard-selling outreach damages our standing within the market.

 - It is not a role that pays for activity. Booking a meeting is not the finish line.
 
 

THE PROFILE

You are likely to be early in your career with some exposure to lending, credit or financial services. How you work matters more than the exact shape of your CV.

YOU'LL BRING

 - Overall 1-4 years of experience in Sales/Business Development with prior experience working in a banking/fintech industry.

 - Enough finance grounding to qualify a lead properly: you can hold a sensible conversation about how a business loan is structured and assessed, or you can learn that quickly and want to.

 - Experience working to targets in an outbound role, and the resilience that takes. Outbound means hearing “no” far more often than yes, and we need you as sharp at the end of a campaign as at the start.

 - Credibility with senior people. Originators need to take your leads seriously from early on, and prospects and advisers need to find you worth their time.

 - Real organisational discipline. You keep records accurate and current without being chased.

 - Clear, concise written English. Most of the first impressions you make will be in writing.

 - Break complex problems into incremental, shippable steps with clear domain boundaries.

 - Shape platform-wide architecture with an eye on wider business impact.

 - Coach and mentor engineers by example.

 - Use GenAI to move faster and decide better and help set the direction for how it’s embedded across the organisation.

Technology

We're pragmatic about our technology choices. These are some of the things we use now:

 - Python, NodeJS

 - TypeScript, React, styled components

 - PostgreSQL, BigQuery, MySQL

 - Jest, React Testing Library, Cypress, pytest

 - AWS, GCP

 - Docker, Terraform, GitHub, CircleCI
 

HOW WE EXPECT YOU TO WORK

We expect you to work in these ways, as well as encouraging and enabling these practices from others:

 - Collaborate - We work in cross-functional, mission driven, autonomous squads that gel over time. We pair program to work better through shared experience and knowledge.

 - Focus on outcomes over outputs - Solving a problem for users that translates to business results is our goal. Measurements focused on that goal help us to understand if we are succeeding.

 - Practice continuous improvement - We optimise for feedback now, rather than presume what might be needed in the future and introduce complexity before it will be used. This means we learn faster. We share learnings in blame-free formats, so that we do not repeat things that have failed, but still have confidence to innovate.

 - Seek to understand our users - We constantly seek understanding from data and conversations to better serve our users' needs, taking an active part in research to hear from them directly and regularly.

 - Embrace and enable continuous deployment - Seamless delivery of changes into an environment - without manual intervention - is essential for us to ensure that we are highly productive; consider resiliency; and practice security by design.

 - Test outside-in, test first - TDD keeps us confident in moving fast and deploying regularly. We want to solve user problems, and so we test with that mindset - writing scenarios first, then considering our solution; coupling tests to behaviour, rather than implementation.

 - You build it, you run it - We embrace DevOps culture and end-to-end ownership of products and features. Every engineer, regardless of their role, can lead delivery of features from start to finish.

 - Be cloud native - We leverage automation and hosted services to deliver resilient, secure services quickly and consistently.
 

HOW WE EXPECT YOU TO BEHAVE

We embrace difference and know that when we can be ourselves at work, we are happier, more motivated, and creative. We want to be able to bring our whole selves to work, have our own perspectives and know that we belong. As such, through your behaviours at work, we expect you to reflect and actively sustain a healthy engineering environment that looks like this:

 - A wide range of voices heard to the benefit of all

jobs.title: Application Security Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Application Security Engineer is a hands-on software engineering role, focused on writing and shipping fixes for the hardest application and AI security problems, particularly those that cross team boundaries or involve architecture, authentication and authorisation, and that automation cannot yet safely resolve. You will work in unfamiliar codebases, root-cause the flaw, and deliver the change through code, tests and deployment, taking remediation load off engineering teams so they can stay focused on delivery. You will work closely with the teams that detect, prioritise and track vulnerabilities. As OakNorth leans heavily into agentic systems, you will also secure how AI and coding agents are built and used, and build our internal coding agent platforms so they can fix a wider range of security issues safely and at scale.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Write and ship fixes for complex application security vulnerabilities, including architectural weaknesses and legacy technology issues that automated remediation cannot yet handle safely.

 - Lead remediation of problems that cross team and system boundaries, making and coordinating code changes across multiple services and owners and seeing them through to production.

 - Fix authentication and authorisation flaws in code, including identity, access control, session and token handling, service-to-service trust and permission models.

 - Act as a dedicated engineering resource for security remediation, taking the fix burden off product teams so they can focus on delivery.

 - Take the output of security tooling (SAST, DAST, SCA, secrets, container and IaC scanning), validate findings, root-cause them in the code and implement the fix rather than only triaging.

 - Secure agentic and AI-enabled systems in code and architecture, mitigating risks from the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications such as prompt injection, excessive agent permissions, tool misuse, insecure agent-to-agent communication and unsafe handling of agent outputs.

 - Build and improve our internal coding agent platforms, including remediation agents, by contributing specialist fixes, remediation patterns, evaluation cases and feedback on where agents succeed or fail.

 - Engineer guardrails for agent-generated and human-written changes, such as least-privilege agent access, human approval points, secure defaults, shared libraries, pipeline checks and policy-as-code, so vulnerabilities do not recur.

 - Build and harden GitHub workflows and release pipelines, including GitHub Actions hardening, secrets and token handling, branch protection, dependency and supply chain controls, and security gates in CI/CD.

 - Deliver higher-risk changes safely through testing, peer review, staged rollout and rollback, in partnership with the teams that own the systems.

 - Work with the teams that detect, prioritise and track vulnerabilities to take prioritised findings through to merged fixes, and automate recurring fix types where it is safe to do so.

 - Document remediation approaches, share knowledge and coach engineers on secure design, secure coding and the safe use of AI coding agents.

 - Track remediation progress, including backlog reduction, SLA performance and risk reduction, and provide evidence for audit and regulatory requirements.
 
 

YOU'LL BE A GREAT FIT IF YOU HAVE…

Engineering Skills

 - Full stack engineering experience across front end, back end and APIs, with proficiency in one or more languages (e.g., Java, Python, C#, JavaScript/TypeScript) and the ability to work in unfamiliar and legacy codebases.

 - Strong hands-on experience with GitHub (pull requests, code review, branch protection, code scanning) and GitHub Actions, including building and securing release pipelines.

 - Working knowledge of cloud platforms, containers and infrastructure as code.

 - Ability to review code, find vulnerabilities and implement practical, correct fixes.

Application Security Skills

 - Strong application security knowledge, including the OWASP Top 10 and common vulnerability classes such as injection, broken access control, insecure deserialization and cryptographic weaknesses.

 - Deep understanding of authentication and authorisation, including OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, JWT and session handling, RBAC/ABAC models and service-to-service identity.

 - Hands-on experience interpreting application security tooling output (SAST, DAST, SCA, secrets, container and IaC scanning), distinguishing true and false positives and finding root cause.

 - Understanding of CI/CD and software supply chain security, including GitHub Actions risks such as untrusted input, over-privileged tokens and third-party action pinning.

AI & Agentic Security Skills

 - Day-to-day experience using coding agents such as Claude to write, review and fix code, with sound judgement on where they are reliable and where they are not.

 - Knowledge of and informed opinions on the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications and related AI security risks, including prompt injection, tool and permission abuse, data leakage and agent identity.

 - Ability to design guardrails, permission boundaries and evaluation approaches for AI agents and agent-generated changes.

 - Ability to turn manual fixes into repeatable patterns and test cases that agent platforms can use.

Remediation & Architecture Skills

 - Experience fixing architectural and design-level security issues, and making safe changes in systems with limited tests, documentation or clear ownership.

 - Ability to plan and deliver changes that span multiple teams and services, managing dependencies and risk.

 - Sound judgement on testing, rollout and rollback for higher-risk changes.

Collaboration & Communication Skills

 - Ability to work as a trusted partner to engineering teams, explaining why a fix is needed and making it easy to adopt.

 - Influence without direct authority across teams that own the affected systems, including stakeholders in different locations and time zones.

 - Clear written and verbal communication, including documentation and progress reporting.

Mindset & Attributes

 - Ownership and a bias to action: comfortable taking on ambiguous, hard problems and seeing them through to resolution.

 - Pragmatic, risk-aware judgement when balancing speed of remediation against the risk of change.

 - Curiosity and continuous learning as threats and agentic technologies evolve

WHAT WE OFFER

 - Health & Protection: Medical cover for you, your family & parents; life and accidental cover at a multiple of your salary
