jobs.title: Director, Workout & Restructuring - Real Estate
jobs.description:
ABOUT US
At OakNorth, we’re on a mission to empower ambitious businesses and the communities they serve. Since 2015, we’ve lent over $21 billion across the UK and US, helped create more than 58,000 new homes and 36,000 new jobs, and supported hundreds of thousands of personal savers, all while driving economic growth in the markets we serve.

ABOUT THE TEAM
We manage a portfolio of complex, high-value real estate exposures where performance has deteriorated or the original business plan is no longer achievable. Our job is to protect and maximise the Bank’s recovery, taking ownership from the earliest signs of distress through to restructuring, consensual resolution or, where necessary, enforcement.

We work across a broad range of real estate assets, sponsors and capital structures. Our approach is commercially minded, analytically rigorous and decisive. We engage directly with borrowers, sponsors, investors, advisers and legal counsel, and expect our people to take control, challenge conventional thinking and deliver the best achievable outcome for the Bank.

ABOUT THE ROLE
We are looking for an exceptional real estate restructuring professional to join as a Director. You will own a portfolio of complex and often contentious distressed real estate exposures, leading recovery strategy from initial diagnosis through to final resolution.

This takes more than technical credit or restructuring knowledge. You will combine strong commercial judgement, deep real estate expertise, financial and analytical capability, and the confidence to lead difficult negotiations and decide under pressure. You will understand the property and the business, identify what has gone wrong, establish realistic recovery options and take control. That may mean resetting the business plan, restructuring the debt, securing additional equity or capital, negotiating a consensual exit, or pursuing formal enforcement where it offers the best recovery.

You will present clear, evidence-based recommendations to senior management and Credit Committee, and work closely with Portfolio Management, Credit and Legal. This is a hands-on role for someone who has personally led complex restructurings and can show a track record of successful outcomes. You will report to a Senior Director, Workout & Restructuring.

WHAT YOU’LL DO
Own and deliver recovery strategies

 - Take end-to-end ownership of a portfolio of complex distressed real estate exposures, from initial diagnosis through to resolution.

 - Develop and recommend commercially grounded recovery strategies across the full range of options: business-plan restructuring, asset repositioning, debt restructuring, new capital, sponsor solutions, consensual sale, refinance, enforcement and insolvency.

 - Understand the asset, borrower, sponsor, capital structure and realistic exit routes. Challenge assumptions and identify the true risks to recovery.

 - Continuously assess alternative strategies, balancing recovery value, risk, timing, execution certainty and cost.

 - Act decisively to protect the Bank’s position, preserve asset value and maintain leverage over borrowers and other stakeholders.

Lead complex restructurings and negotiations

 - Lead negotiations with borrowers, sponsors, shareholders, equity investors, mezzanine lenders, co-lenders and other stakeholders.

 - Structure and execute consensual restructurings, including debt amendments, maturity extensions, capitalisation, repayment arrangements, equity injections, new money and business plan changes.

 - Challenge sponsors and borrowers, hold firm on the Bank’s position and use negotiation and legal leverage effectively.

 - Recognise when consensual solutions will not deliver the best outcome and recommend enforcement or insolvency decisively.

 - Appoint and manage external advisers, including solicitors, valuers, receivers, insolvency practitioners and asset managers.

Apply rigorous financial and commercial analysis

 - Undertake and challenge detailed financial analysis, cash flows, development appraisals, investment models and recovery valuations.

 - Build and stress-test recovery scenarios, including downside cases, enforcement costs, timing, interest and cash leakage.

 - Assess complex lending and security structures, including senior, mezzanine and intercreditor arrangements, guarantees, debentures and other security.

 - Evaluate asset-level business plans, development viability, funding requirements, sales strategies and availability of additional capital.

 - Maintain an evidence-based view of expected recovery, provisioning requirements, risk grading and downside exposure.

Governance, control and leadership

 - Prepare and present high-quality credit papers to senior management and Credit Committees, setting out facts, key risks, options, recommendation and rationale.

 - Ensure appropriate governance, documentation, risk escalation and policy compliance throughout the life of each case.

 - Own actions, milestones and delivery against the agreed recovery strategy.

 - Direct, challenge and support junior colleagues, setting high standards for credit judgement, analytical rigour and stakeholder management.

 - Work with Portfolio Management, Credit, Legal and other teams to ensure a joined-up approach to the Bank’s exposures.

YOU’LL BE A GREAT FIT IF YOU HAVE…

 - A proven track record in real estate restructuring and workout. You will have personally led complex distressed real estate situations and delivered outcomes across consensual restructurings, asset repositioning, debt restructuring, disposals and enforcement. This is essential.

 - Deep real estate lending experience. Strong understanding of investment and development finance, including real estate economics, funding structures, development risk and asset-level business plans.

 - Exceptional commercial judgement. You can assess a difficult situation quickly, tell a viable recovery from a delaying tactic, identify the best route to recovery and make hard decisions with conviction.

 - Strong restructuring and negotiation skills. Experienced in leading high-stakes discussions with sponsors, borrowers, equity investors, lenders and advisers, often in contentious or time-critical situations.

 - Technical credit and financial capability. Comfortable analysing complex financial models, cash flows, valuations, security structures, legal documentation and alternative recovery scenarios. You challenge the numbers rather than simply rely on them.

 - A strong understanding of enforcement and insolvency. Familiarity with the practical application of LPA receivership, administration, security enforcement and other recovery mechanisms.

 - Excellent communication and influencing skills. You distil complex situations into clear recommendations, write high-quality credit papers and present confidently to senior stakeholders and Credit Committees.

 - Personal accountability and resilience. Comfortable operating autonomously, managing competing priorities and taking responsibility for difficult cases and their outcomes.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience within a bank, debt fund or specialist real estate lender.

 - Exposure to complex mid-market sponsor relationships, multi-lender structures, mezzanine debt and intercreditor arrangements.

 - Experience across multiple real estate sectors, including residential development, commercial investment, mixed-use and specialist assets.

 - Experience managing and developing junior restructuring or credit professionals.

WHAT WE OFFER

jobs.description:
ABOUT US

At OakNorth, we're on a mission to empower ambitious businesses and the communities they serve. Since 2015, we've lent over $21 billion across the UK and US, helped create more than 58,000 new homes and 36,000 new jobs, and supported hundreds of thousands of personal savers — all while driving economic growth in the markets we serve.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Portfolio Monitoring team is responsible for the ongoing management and surveillance of a complex, high-value lending book. We track performance, identify emerging risk and make sure the Bank has a clear, current view of its exposure. It's a hands-on team — close to the data and the clients, and expected to surface issues early and act on them.

We work across leveraged finance, real estate and corporate lending. Our approach combines rigorous credit analysis with commercial judgement and direct engagement with borrowers and other stakeholders. We work closely with Credit, Workout & Restructuring, Legal and Operations, and increasingly use technology and AI to sharpen how we monitor and report.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a commercially minded credit professional with experience in corporate or leveraged lending to join as a Director. You will take ownership of a portfolio of complex trading and leveraged finance credits, maintaining a forward-looking view of performance and acting early when risk emerges.

You will understand the borrower, its business plan, capital structure and key stakeholders; challenge financial performance and forecasts; and determine what changes mean for the Bank's position. You will lead borrower discussions, assess requests for waivers and amendments, and present clear, evidence-based recommendations to senior management and Credit Committee.

This is not a reporting role. It calls for hands-on ownership, sound credit judgement and the confidence to challenge assumptions and stand behind recommendations. You will work closely with Credit, Workout & Restructuring, Legal and Operations, including on the timely escalation and handover of deteriorating credits where appropriate.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own and actively manage the portfolio

 - Take ownership of a portfolio of complex trading and leveraged finance credits, maintaining a clear view of each borrower's performance, financial position and emerging risks

 - Lead annual credit reviews, assessing business performance, management forecasts, risk grade and appetite, and recommending any action required

 - Challenge performance against the original underwriting assumptions and understand the borrower, its management team, sponsor, capital structure and potential exit or refinancing routes

 - Manage watchlist and early warning processes, identify deterioration promptly and agree appropriate monitoring, actions and escalation

 - Work with Workout & Restructuring and other colleagues when a credit deteriorates, ensuring a clear and timely handover where appropriate

Lead borrower engagement and credit decisions

 - Lead direct discussions with borrowers, management teams and sponsors, building relationships while confidently challenging performance and protecting the Bank's position

 - Own waiver, consent and amendment requests, assess their credit implications, negotiate terms and present clear recommendations for approval

 - Engage with co-lenders, agent banks, advisers and Legal as needed, understanding stakeholder positions and the Bank's rights under the lending documentation

 - Prepare and present well-structured credit papers and portfolio updates to senior management and Credit Committee, setting out the key facts, risks, options, recommendation and rationale

 - Follow through on agreed actions, decisions and escalation, ensuring issues are addressed rather than simply reported

Apply rigorous financial and portfolio analysis

 - Analyse and challenge financial statements, trading performance, cash flow and liquidity forecasts, leverage, debt service and covenant headroom

 - Run stress tests and downside scenarios to assess the impact of changes in performance, market conditions or macroeconomic events on individual credits and the portfolio

 - Assess risk ratings, sector and borrower concentrations, maturity pressures and refinancing risk, translating analysis into timely, practical recommendations

 - Understand lending documentation, security packages and capital structures, including relevant co-lender and intercreditor arrangements, and assess how they affect the Bank's position

Governance, controls and team leadership

 - Maintain accurate, current portfolio information and ensure appropriate governance, documentation, risk escalation and policy compliance

 - Oversee the effectiveness of lender controls, including covenant testing, information undertakings and consent rights, without owning routine loan administration

 - Monitor co-lender and agent bank performance against contractual reporting and consent obligations; identify control gaps and drive remediation with the relevant owners

 - Help develop portfolio monitoring frameworks, processes and scalable controls with Credit, Risk and Operations, using data and technology where they improve outcomes

 - Support and challenge junior colleagues, sharing credit expertise and setting high standards for analysis, judgement and follow-through

NICE TO HAVE

jobs.title: Director, Workout & Restructuring - Trading
jobs.description:
ABOUT US

At OakNorth, we're on a mission to empower ambitious businesses and the communities they serve. Since 2015, we've lent over $21 billion across the UK and US, helped create more than 58,000 new homes and 36,000 new jobs, and supported hundreds of thousands of personal savers — all while driving economic growth in the markets we serve.

ABOUT THE TEAM

We manage a portfolio of complex, high-value trading and leveraged finance exposures where performance has deteriorated or the original credit thesis is no longer intact. Our job is to protect and maximise the Bank's recovery — taking ownership from the earliest signs of distress through to restructuring, consensual resolution, or where necessary, enforcement.

We work across a broad range of corporate and leveraged borrowers, sponsor-backed structures and capital arrangements. Our approach is commercially minded, analytically rigorous and decisive. We engage directly with borrowers, management teams, sponsors, co-lenders, advisers and legal counsel, and expect our people to take control, challenge conventional thinking and deliver the best achievable outcome for the Bank.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for an exceptional restructuring professional with a leveraged finance and corporate lending background to join as a Director. You will own a portfolio of complex and often contentious distressed trading and leveraged finance exposures, leading recovery strategy from initial diagnosis through to final resolution.

This takes more than technical credit or restructuring knowledge. You will combine strong commercial judgement, deep leveraged finance expertise, financial and analytical capability, and the confidence to lead difficult negotiations and decide under pressure. You will understand the business, the capital structure and the sponsor, identify what has gone wrong, establish realistic recovery options and take control. That may mean resetting the business plan, restructuring the debt, securing new money or equity, negotiating a consensual exit, or pursuing formal enforcement where it offers the best recovery.

You will present clear, evidence-based recommendations to senior management and Credit Committee, and work closely with Portfolio Management, Credit and Legal. This is a hands-on role for someone who has personally led complex restructurings and can show a track record of successful outcomes. You will report to a Senior Director, Workout & Restructuring.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own and deliver recovery strategies

 - Take end-to-end ownership of a portfolio of complex distressed trading and leveraged finance exposures, from initial diagnosis through to resolution

 - Develop and recommend commercially grounded recovery strategies across the full range of options: business plan restructuring, debt amendment, new money, sponsor solutions, management change, consensual sale, refinance, enforcement and insolvency

 - Understand the borrower, management team, sponsor, capital structure and realistic exit routes — challenge assumptions and identify the true risks to recovery

 - Continuously assess alternative strategies, balancing recovery value, risk, timing, execution certainty and cost

 - Act decisively to protect the Bank's position, preserve business value and maintain leverage over borrowers and other stakeholders

Lead complex restructurings and negotiations

 - Lead negotiations with borrowers, management teams, sponsors, equity investors, mezzanine lenders, co-lenders, and other stakeholders

 - Structure and execute consensual restructurings, including debt amendments, maturity extensions, PIK arrangements, equity injections, new money, covenant resets and business plan changes

 - Challenge sponsors and management, hold firm on the Bank's position and use negotiation and legal leverage effectively

 - Recognise when consensual solutions will not deliver the best outcome and recommend enforcement or insolvency decisively

 - Appoint and manage external advisers including solicitors, financial advisers, insolvency practitioners and business review specialists

Apply rigorous financial and commercial analysis

 - Undertake and challenge detailed financial analysis, trading forecasts, liquidity models and recovery valuations across complex corporate and leveraged structures

 - Build and stress-test recovery scenarios including downside cases, enforcement costs, timing, cash leakage and exit multiples

 - Assess complex lending and security structures including senior, unitranche, mezzanine and intercreditor arrangements, debentures, guarantees and other security

 - Evaluate business plan viability, trading performance, liquidity runway, management quality and availability of additional capital or equity

 - Maintain an evidence-based view of expected recovery, provisioning requirements, risk grading and downside exposure

Governance, control and leadership

 - Prepare and present high-quality credit papers to senior management and Credit Committees, setting out facts, key risks, options, recommendation and rationale

 - Ensure appropriate governance, documentation, risk escalation and policy compliance throughout the life of each case

 - Own actions, milestones and delivery against the agreed recovery strategy

 - Direct, challenge and support junior colleagues, setting high standards for credit judgement, analytical rigour and stakeholder management

 - Work with Portfolio Management, Credit, Legal and other teams to ensure a joined-up approach to the Bank's exposures

YOU'LL BE A GREAT FIT IF YOU HAVE…

 - A proven track record in leveraged finance or corporate restructuring and workout. You will have personally led complex distressed situations and delivered outcomes across consensual restructurings, debt amendments, new money processes, management transitions and enforcement. We're looking for someone with 9+ years of relevant experience; this is the core of the role, not a nice-to-have.

 - Deep leveraged finance and corporate lending experience. Strong understanding of sponsor-backed and corporate capital structures, including leveraged buyouts, unitranche, mezzanine, and intercreditor dynamics.

 - Exceptional commercial judgement. You can assess a difficult situation quickly, tell a viable recovery from a delaying tactic, identify the best route to full recovery and make hard decisions with conviction.

 - Strong restructuring and negotiation skills. Experienced in leading high-stakes discussions with sponsors, management teams, equity investors, co-lenders and advisers, often in contentious or time-critical situations.

 - Technical credit and financial capability. Comfortable analysing complex financial models, trading performance, liquidity positions, security structures, legal documentation and alternative recovery scenarios — you challenge the numbers rather than simply rely on them.

 - A working understanding of enforcement and insolvency. Familiarity with administration, fixed and floating charge enforcement, pre-pack processes and other formal recovery mechanisms in a UK corporate context.

 - Excellent communication and influencing skills. You distil complex situations into clear recommendations, write high-quality credit papers and present confidently to senior stakeholders and Credit Committees.

 - Personal accountability and resilience. Comfortable operating autonomously, managing competing priorities and taking responsibility for difficult cases and their outcomes.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience within a bank, debt fund, or specialist leveraged lender

 - Exposure to complex mid-market sponsor relationships, multi-lender structures and intercreditor negotiations

 - Experience across multiple sectors within a leveraged or corporate lending context

 - Experience managing and developing junior restructuring or credit professionals

WHAT WE OFFER

 - 👶 Enhanced maternity and paternity leave

jobs.title: Performance Marketing Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT PLASMA

Plasma is building the primary account for global money.

Money used to belong to a country. Increasingly, it belongs to a person or business moving through many countries. People and businesses now earn, spend, save, hire and invest across borders. Traditional banks cannot serve this new world.

Our first product, Plasma One, is a global money account: a place to receive, hold, send funds in seconds, earn yield and spend with a card in the local economy.

Underneath is the Plasma network, built from first principles for stablecoin payments. Stablecoins make dollars faster, cheaper and more reliable to move.

The opportunity is to become where all global money lands first: where income arrives, balances grow, payments move, businesses operate, and new financial products are built.

THE TEAM & OUR STORY https://x.com/Plasma/status/2067634709727719601?s=20

We are a global team of founders, operators and engineers, obsessed with building the best products. We work at the cutting edge of financial innovation, using stablecoins to create tools for consumers and businesses.

We operate with trust, clarity, and ambition: own your craft, move with urgency, contribute beyond your lane, back your teammates, debate rigorously, and keep raising the bar for what great means.

THE ROLE

 - You inherit a live product with real spend, and you own the paid engine that scales it across Plasma One and Plasma Business. Channels, budget, creative and measurement all sit with you.

 - Own the cost of acquisition of valuable users and managing our paid advertising motion end to end.

 - Deploy many variations of ads, platforms and angles to test high performing creative and formats driving users into both custom funnels and direct to app while measuring downstream events.

 - Take us beyond our crypto-native audience. Find the audiences, messages and formats on Meta, Google, TikTok and YouTube that bring in people who fund and keep spending, then scale the ones that work.

 - Run the campaigns yourself. You build them, launch them, read the results and decide where tomorrow's budget goes. New creative, new audiences and new angles every week, with a clear read on what worked and why.

 - Look past the click. Work with product and design on landing pages, onboarding, lifecycle and referrals so a new sign-up becomes a funded account and a regular user.

 - Build the paid function. The tracking, reporting and playbooks you set up become what the team runs on, and as channels prove out you help hire the specialists who scale them.

THE BAR

 - Regional market expertise. You know how to work on an acquisition strategy that differs between countries and markets

 - Deep, hands-on experience running paid acquisition at a consumer app or fintech, especially paid social and search, with real budgets and real accountability for the outcome.

 - Understand how to navigate Meta AEM, Google optimization, Apple search ads, Snapchat and other platforms, configure Appsflyer, our data warehouse and creative to achieve exceptional results.

 - A track record of structured creative testing and confident budget allocation across channels.

 - Strong measurement skills. You know attribution, incrementality and cohort analysis, and where each one can mislead you.

 - Range across the funnel. You have improved landing pages, onboarding, lifecycle or referrals, working closely with product and design.

 - Proof, not claims. Show us what you personally tested, what improved, and what it did to acquisition cost, activation and retention. Vague answers will not get through.

 - Resourceful. You find a way to get the answer or the result, with or without a big team behind you. Based in London or ready to relocate.

NICE TO HAVE

 - You were an early growth hire at a global consumer fintech

 - You know your way around mobile measurement partners such as AppsFlyer or Adjust, and the ad policies that come with financial products.

 - You are curious about stablecoins and new payment rails. Prior crypto experience is not required.

WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU

 - Above-market salary for the level of the role, with token compensation.

 - A beautiful London HQ with gym access and daily food, for those who thrive in an office environment. Visa sponsorship and relocation support if you're joining from abroad.

 - Premium health insurance for you and your family, fully covered by Plasma.

 - Monthly wellness budget, whether that's the gym, therapy, sauna, or massage.

 - All the tools and tech you need to operate at your best.

 - Real ownership and responsibility from day one, with your work shipping to hundreds of thousands of people, moving millions of dollars every day.

Data Protection & Privacy
We are committed to protecting the privacy and security of your personal data. Any personal information you provide during the recruitment process will be processed in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable local data protection laws.

We are a global team of founders, operators and engineers, obsessed with building the best products. We work at the cutting edge of financial innovation, using stablecoins to create tools for consumers and businesses.

We operate with trust, clarity, and ambition: own your craft, move with urgency, contribute beyond your lane, back your teammates, debate rigorously, and keep raising the bar for what great means.

THE ROLE

You'll report to our General Counsel and own compliance and licensing at Plasma. That means building and running our global compliance program, and leading the licensing work that gets us into new markets.

This is a hands-on role. We're looking for an operator who's ready to own more. You'll set the priorities, write the docs yourself, work directly with partners and make sure things actually ship across Legal, Product and Engineering.

GLOBAL COMPLIANCE PROGRAM

 - Build and own the global program and proportionate market implementations: AML/CFT, sanctions, KYC and KYB, transaction monitoring across fiat and on-chain flows, Travel Rule and consumer protection. Make clear which controls Plasma operates and which sit with regulated partners.

 - Own the financial crime risk assessments, company-wide and for each market, and the policies and controls that follow from them.

 - Set the compliance conditions for new products, features and markets before launch, working with Product and Engineering from the design stage. Turn requirements into practical controls, identify owners and verify readiness, escalating material risks and unresolved legal questions to the General Counsel.

 - Own the compliance relationships with our banking, card and other regulated partners. Oversee the controls they require of us, the controls we rely on them for, and their diligence requests and audits.

 - Choose and run the compliance tooling with Operations and Engineering, and automate first-line review as volume grows, with clear escalation paths and quality checks.

 - Run compliance testing, staff training and independent audit readiness.

GLOBAL LICENSING AND MARKET ENTRY

 - Work alongside Legal in setting the licensing roadmap: which markets, which license in each, if needed, and in what order.

 - For each market, recommend whether to build, buy or partner, with the cost, timeline, capital and headcount each option needs, so Leadership can decide how to appropriately enter new markets.

 - Where needed, run licensing applications end to end: draft the regulatory business plan, program of operations and policies, coordinate financial projections with Finance and fit-and-proper filings with the relevant officers, and manage the regulator's questions through to approval.

 - Lead the regulatory side of acquiring licensed entities: diligence on the target's licenses and compliance record, change-in-control filings, and integration after closing.

 - Recommend when a product or market can run on a partner’s license and when it needs our own, working with Legal to resolve the regulatory perimeter. Document the agreed position for each product and turn it into clear launch conditions, so the reasoning holds up with regulators and partners.
 

GOVERNANCE

 - Lead regulatory engagement for our licensing and compliance workstreams alongside Legal and the relevant local officers. Be Plasma's primary day-to-day contact for the compliance teams at our banking and card partners.

 - Report to Leadership on a regular cycle: license status, alerts and case backlog, suspicious activity filings, onboarding outcomes, open findings.

 - Track regulatory change in our markets and turn it into changes to the roadmap, the product and the program.

 - Work with Legal on regulatory analysis, outside counsel and consultants. Own the compliance and licensing budget within agreed priorities, and make the case for the people, tooling and specialist support needed to deliver.

 - Build the compliance and licensing function as Plasma grows, including recommending where to hire or use specialist support. Coordinate local officers and programs while preserving their jurisdiction-specific accountability and required independence.

THE BAR

 - You have 4+ years in compliance, licensing or regulatory roles in payments, e-money, neobanking or digital assets firms. You have owned substantive workstreams at a fast-moving fintech and are ready to lead a function. We care more about what you have delivered than your previous title.

 - You have personally written and implemented meaningful parts of a compliance program, and can explain how you tested the controls and supported a regulator review or partner bank audit.

 - You have played a substantial hands-on role in a licensing application, regulatory approval or market-entry process. You can show what you drafted, which issues you resolved and how you drove it forward, not just which licenses your employer holds.

 - You have strong practical knowledge of AML, sanctions and KYC, with depth in at least one relevant regulatory framework and experience adapting controls for another market or working closely with local specialists.

 - You understand how responsibilities are divided between a fintech, its banking and card partners and its technology providers. You bring relevant experience in card programs, stablecoin on- and off-ramps or wallet models, and can get up to speed on the rest.

 - You take work from an open question to a clear recommendation and completed implementation. You write well, manage dependencies and influence cross-functional teams without relying on a large team beneath you. Previous people-management experience is helpful, not required.

NICE TO HAVE

 - You have run compliance for a card issuing program with a sponsor bank.

 - You have worked directly with UAE regulators (such as VARA, the CBUAE, ADGM or DIFC) or Asian regulators (such as MAS in Singapore or the SFC and HKMA in Hong Kong).

 - You hold a Law degree, CAMS or a similar certification.
 
 
 

WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU

 - Above-market salary for the level of the role, with token compensation.

 - A beautiful London HQ with gym access and daily food, for those who thrive in an office environment. Visa sponsorship and relocation support if you're joining from abroad.

 - Premium health insurance for you and your family, fully covered by Plasma.

 - Monthly wellness budget, whether that's the gym, therapy, sauna, or massage.

 - All the tools and tech you need to operate at your best.

 - Real ownership and responsibility from day one, with your work shipping to hundreds of thousands of people, moving millions of dollars every day.

Data Protection & Privacy
We are committed to protecting the privacy and security of your personal data. Any personal information you provide during the recruitment process will be processed in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable local data protection laws.

jobs.description:
ABOUT PLASMA

Plasma is building the primary account for global money.

Money used to belong to a country. Increasingly, it belongs to a person or business moving through many countries. People and businesses now earn, spend, save, hire and invest across borders. Traditional banks cannot serve this new world.

Our first product, Plasma One, is a global money account: a place to receive, hold, send funds in seconds, earn yield and spend with a card in the local economy.

Underneath is the Plasma network, built from first principles for stablecoin payments. Stablecoins make dollars faster, cheaper and more reliable to move.

The opportunity is to become where all global money lands first: where income arrives, balances grow, payments move, businesses operate, and new financial products are built.

THE TEAM & OUR STORY https://x.com/Plasma/status/2067634709727719601?s=20

We are a global team of founders, operators and engineers, obsessed with building the best products. We work at the cutting edge of financial innovation, using stablecoins to create tools for consumers and businesses.

We operate with trust, clarity, and ambition: own your craft, move with urgency, contribute beyond your lane, back your teammates, debate rigorously, and keep raising the bar for what great means.

CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE 

Plasma is scaling its customer-facing operations across international markets, and we’re growing the Customer Experience Team to match. You’ll join an established team and take ownership of coverage for the CET time zone, making sure our customers get great support when they need it most.

You’ll work across the full customer journey, from first contact through to resolution. Because we’re still building out our playbook, your input will directly shape the processes, standards, and team culture as we grow. You won’t just follow the process; you’ll help refine it.

Some flexibility in working hours & weekend shifts will be needed to support coverage and the occasional busy period. We’re looking for a hard-working self-starter who thrives in a fast-moving startup environment and is committed to the mission alongside the rest of the team.

THE ROLE

 - Own the customer experience day-to-day: Be the first person our customers reach when something goes wrong or they need help. You will handle inbound queries across chat, email, and support tooling, and take accountability for the quality and speed of every response.

 - Be the right hand of the Ops lead: Work directly alongside the Head of Operations to build out processes, identify gaps, and support decisions as we scale the team internationally. This is not a back-office support role. You will be involved in how we think about operations.

 - Build the foundations: We are early. Many of the processes, templates, and escalation paths do not exist yet. You will create them. From response frameworks to internal guides, you will help lay the groundwork the team will rely on as we grow.

 - Support international team scaling: As we hire Ops team members in new markets, you will help onboard them, share knowledge, and maintain consistency in how we deliver for customers across regions.

 - Spot problems before they become patterns: Track issues across the customer base, flag recurring themes to Product and Engineering, and help prioritise fixes that actually move the needle for customers.

 - Work across teams: Collaborate with Compliance, KYC, and Product to make sure the customer experience is joined up, especially during onboarding and verification flows where things can go wrong quickly.

 - Represent the customer internally: Your proximity to customer feedback is valuable. Use it. Bring customer insight into internal conversations and push for improvements that matter.

 - Be Flexible with Shift Rotation: Most weeks you’ll work the normal Mon-Fri, however team members currently rotate weekend shifts which means that you may be required to work a weekend shift once every 6 weeks. You’ll then be able to take those days worked off the following week.
 
 

THE BAR

 - 1 to 3 years of experience in customer operations, customer success, or a support role, ideally within fintech, payments, or crypto. We will consider strong candidates from outside these sectors if the fit is right.

 - Someone who takes ownership. You do not wait to be told. When something is broken or missing, you fix it or flag it. You hold yourself to a high standard even when no one is watching.

 - Clear and direct in how you communicate. You can write a helpful, professional response under pressure and explain a complex situation simply. You know the difference between being thorough and overcomplicating things.

 - Competent English Language - our team communicates in english so being competent with the language is a requirement.

 - Comfortable with ambiguity. This is an early-stage company. Processes will change, priorities will shift, and some days you will be figuring things out as you go. You see that as interesting rather than frustrating. Preferably, you have worked at a fast-paced tech company.

 - Genuinely curious about crypto. You do not need deep technical knowledge, but you need to understand the basics of how stablecoins and digital assets work and be motivated to learn more. Our customers live in this space.

 - Organised under pressure. You can manage a queue, prioritise effectively, and keep quality high when things are busy.

 - Collaborative by default. You work well with people in different functions, different time zones, and different levels of seniority. Building the team abroad means working with people you may never meet in person, and you are good at that.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience in a startup or scale-up where you had to build or rebuild processes, not just follow them.

 - Exposure to Intercom, Zendesk, Freshdesk, or similar support tooling in a live production environment.

 - Any familiarity with KYC or compliance workflows as they relate to customer onboarding.

 - Experience supporting or managing a small team, even informally, or helping onboard new colleagues.

 - An interest in how stablecoin and DeFi products work and the customer challenges they create.

 - Multilingual skills that could support customer communication across our international markets.
 
 

WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU

 - Above-market salary for the level of the role, with token compensation.

 - A beautiful London HQ with gym access and daily food, for those who thrive in an office environment. Visa sponsorship and relocation support if you're joining from abroad.

 - Premium health insurance for you and your family, fully covered by Plasma.

 - Monthly wellness budget, whether that's the gym, therapy, sauna, or massage.

 - All the tools and tech you need to operate at your best.

 - Real ownership and responsibility from day one, with your work shipping to hundreds of thousands of people, moving millions of dollars every day.

experience:

 - Design for the 80 / 20: Encode judgment and complexity under the hood while keeping the default experience simple and successful for most customers.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Ramp builds software that moves real money, from bill payments and corporate cards to reimbursements, accounting integrations, and travel. Our customers rely on us to keep their operations running: invoices get paid, books get closed, and finance leaders can trust the data behind every decision.

In this role, you will be the person who spots where customers are getting stuck and drives issues to a clear resolution. You will learn a complex product deeply enough to troubleshoot across payments, bank linking, accounting syncs, and card programs, then partner with teams across Engineering, Risk, Product, and Partnerships to get problems solved. This is not script-based support. You will triage, investigate, and make high-signal judgment calls throughout the day.

You will thrive in this role if you are a systems thinker and deeply customer obsessed. Support is the baseline. How you think about improving processes, tools, and outcomes is what sets you apart.

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Be the voice of Ramp's Customer Support. You'll spend your day engaging with customers, primarily via live calls, email, and chat.

 - Diagnose across a broad product surface. Ramp isn't one product — it's payments, cards, travel, accounting integrations, and more. You'll need to understand how they connect and where they break.

 - Operate with an ownership mindset, managing escalations end-to-end. You take full accountability for every ticket you handle. When an issue crosses team boundaries — risk, engineering, product, partnerships — you route it correctly, follow up, and make sure the customer isn't left waiting. You'll work across Zendesk, internal tooling, and Slack-based escalation workflows.

 - Build and shape AI tools, not just use them. Ramp is building AI into CX operations. You'll use AI-powered research tools and proprietary tools like Glass daily, provide direct feedback on what's working, and play an active role in how these tools evolve. You're not just a user — you're a builder. We are all builders at Ramp.

 - Ship improvements, not just flag them. When you notice a process gap, a missing SOP, or a knowledge base article that's sending associates down the wrong path, you don't just raise it — you have the autonomy to roll up your sleeves and fix it. Leverage AI to solve problems, build automations, and improve the systems around you. The best people in this role make the whole team better.

 - Communicate with precision and empathy. Our customers are financially sophisticated. You need to explain what's happening, what you're doing about it, and what they should expect — clearly and without filler.

WHAT YOU NEED

 - You're a systems thinker: you don't just solve the ticket in front of you, you ask why the problem exists and how to prevent it from happening again.

 - You actively use AI tools — Claude, Notion AI, research and workflow tools — and can demonstrate how you've applied them to get real work done. This is a hard requirement.

 - You're fast-moving while holding yourself to a high bar for execution: you balance speed, accuracy, and thoroughness in every interaction.

 - You can hold a technical conversation about how systems connect (APIs, bank integrations, accounting software) even if you're not writing code.

 - You manage competing priorities without dropping things. When you have 15 open issues across 4 internal teams, nothing falls through.

 - You write clearly and concisely. You can explain a payment reconciliation issue to a CFO without jargon.

 - You're comfortable on the phone. Many interactions start there.

 - You have a demonstrated track record of exceeding key performance standards, including CSAT, QA, and speed-of-service metrics.

NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience building workflows or automations using AI tools, not just prompting

 - Familiarity with accounting workflows (AP/AR, GL, reconciliation) or ERP integrations (NetSuite, QuickBooks, Sage)

 - Background in payments infrastructure (ACH, wire transfers, card networks)

 - Track record of working somewhere that shipped product fast and expected CX to keep up

WHY BE A CX ASSOCIATE AT RAMP

 - Cross-functional exposure from day one. You work directly with Product, Engineering, and GTM teams — not siloed into a support queue.

 - AI tools and unlimited access. Unlimited tokens, proprietary AI tools like Glass, and a culture that expects you to use them to move faster and build smarter.

 - Career growth that you own. Grow within CX, explore other functions internally, or carve out a path that doesn't exist yet. If you're invested, we're invested.

 - Culture that's different from a call center. Team events, in-person offsites, and a genuine commitment to building a team people want to be part of.

You will thrive in this role if you are a systems thinker and deeply customer obsessed. Support is the baseline. How you think about improving processes, tools, and outcomes is what sets you apart.

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Be the voice of Ramp's Customer Support. You'll spend your day engaging with customers, primarily via live calls, email, and chat.

 - Diagnose across a broad product surface. Ramp isn't one product — it's payments, cards, travel, accounting integrations, and more. You'll need to understand how they connect and where they break.

 - Operate with an ownership mindset, managing escalations end-to-end. You take full accountability for every ticket you handle. When an issue crosses team boundaries — risk, engineering, product, partnerships — you route it correctly, follow up, and make sure the customer isn't left waiting. You'll work across Zendesk, internal tooling, and Slack-based escalation workflows.

 - Build and shape AI tools, not just use them. Ramp is building AI into CX operations. You'll use AI-powered research tools and proprietary tools like Glass daily, provide direct feedback on what's working, and play an active role in how these tools evolve. You're not just a user — you're a builder. We are all builders at Ramp.

 - Ship improvements, not just flag them. When you notice a process gap, a missing SOP, or a knowledge base article that's sending associates down the wrong path, you don't just raise it — you have the autonomy to roll up your sleeves and fix it. Leverage AI to solve problems, build automations, and improve the systems around you. The best people in this role make the whole team better.

 - Communicate with precision and empathy. Our customers are financially sophisticated. You need to explain what's happening, what you're doing about it, and what they should expect — clearly and without filler.

 - You're a systems thinker: you don't just solve the ticket in front of you, you ask why the problem exists and how to prevent it from happening again.

 - You actively use AI tools — Claude, Notion AI, research and workflow tools — and can demonstrate how you've applied them to get real work done. This is a hard requirement.

 - You're fast-moving while holding yourself to a high bar for execution: you balance speed, accuracy, and thoroughness in every interaction.

 - You can hold a technical conversation about how systems connect (APIs, bank integrations, accounting software) even if you're not writing code.

 - You manage competing priorities without dropping things. When you have 15 open issues across 4 internal teams, nothing falls through.

 - You write clearly and concisely. You can explain a payment reconciliation issue to a CFO without jargon.

 - You're comfortable on the phone. Many interactions start there.

 - Experience building workflows or automations using AI tools, not just prompting

 - Track record of working somewhere that shipped product fast and expected CX to keep up

jobs.description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Customer Activation Managers at Ramp drive value for customers and revenue for the business by ensuring fast, effective onboarding and activation of newly closed customers. As a Senior Scaled CAM, you’ll play a critical role in delivering high-quality outcomes at scale while helping shape the processes, playbooks, and customer strategy that fuel Ramp’s growth.

You’ll own a high-volume portfolio of micro-SMB and micro-MM customers, balancing efficiency and personalization through strong judgment, structured execution, and thoughtful use of scalable motions. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in fast-paced environments, operates with high ownership, and consistently drives customer outcomes.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the end-to-end onboarding and activation of a large portfolio of micro-SMB and micro-MM customers, driving customers to full Ramp adoption within 60 days through efficient, scalable motions.

 - Lead onboarding with strong executive presence, setting clear agendas, controlling call flow, and driving as much progress as possible in minimal touchpoints.

 - Ensure fast, thorough, and complete implementation by educating customers on Ramp functionality, best practices, and the “why” behind key workflows.

 - Confidently navigate and position Ramp’s full product suite, including Cards, Bill Pay, Travel, Treasury, and Accounting integrations, tailoring recommendations to customer workflows and business goals.

 - Deeply understand customer workflows, pain points, and blockers, and problem-solve alongside Product, Engineering, and Support when needed.

 - Drive revenue by minimizing implementation delays and reinforcing the value of Ramp as a core financial operating system.

 - Use customer data, usage signals, and patterns to prioritize outreach, identify risk, and intervene proactively.

 - Balance implementation work, follow-ups, proactive outreach, and group onboarding while maintaining a high bar for quality.

 - Partner closely with Product to surface customer feedback, identify trends, and influence roadmap priorities.

 - Identify opportunities to automate, standardize, and improve onboarding processes, contributing to playbooks, enablement materials, and scalable best practices.

 - Act as a multiplier for the team by sharing insights, patterns, and coaching peers through examples and collaboration.

 - Help maintain an industry-leading customer experience while operating at high volume and pace.
 
 

WHAT YOU’LL NEED

 - 5+ years of experience in Customer Onboarding, Implementation, Account Management, Sales, or a related customer-facing role in B2B SaaS.

 - Proven success managing a high-volume book of business while consistently driving customer outcomes.

 - Strong executive presence with the ability to lead confident, structured customer conversations and handle objections effectively.

 - Experience balancing scale and personalization through group onboarding, automation, and targeted 1:1 engagement.

 - Comfort working cross-functionally with Product and Engineering to share feedback, troubleshoot issues, and ideate solutions.

 - Data-informed mindset with experience using metrics and signals to guide decisions and assess risk.

 - Proven track record of meeting or exceeding key performance metrics in fast-paced environments.

 - High adaptability and comfort navigating ambiguity in a scaling organization.

 - Strong curiosity about product design and the ability to communicate why Ramp works the way it does.
 
 

NICE TO HAVES

 - Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university.

 - Experience with accounting or ERP systems such as NetSuite, QuickBooks, Xero, or Sage.

 - Background in financial services, fintech, or payments.

 - Experience at a high-growth startup or in a scaled Customer Success organization.

 - Prior experience contributing to enablement materials, playbooks, or process improvements.

BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO ALL FULL-TIME RAMP EMPLOYEES (GLOBAL)

 - Flexible PTO

 - Centralized home-office equipment ordering

 - Health and wellness stipend

 - Budget for intra-office travel

 - Weekly coffee stipend

UNITED STATES

 - 100% medical, dental & vision insurance coverage for you, with partial coverage for dependents

 - One Medical annual membership

 - 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

 - Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

 - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

 - Pet insurance

 - In-office perks: lunch, snacks, drinks, and more

 - Relocation expense coverage to NYC or SF (if needed)
 
 

CANADA

 - Life, AD&D, and disability coverage

UNITED KINGDOM

 - Build and evolve backend services that detect and prevent fraud across multiple surfaces, including account access and money movement.

 - Develop enforcement and response tooling that enables fast, safe actions such as identity locks, business locks, payment freezes, and other containment levers.

 - Design and operate high-signal systems with strong observability: metrics, dashboards, alerting, and playbooks for incidents and fraud campaigns.

 - Partner with UIM/Identity stakeholders to strengthen authentication and identity foundations (roles, permissions, identity state, and related platform primitives).

 - Drive end-to-end delivery: technical design, implementation, rollout strategy, and iteration based on outcome metrics.

 - 3+ years of software engineering experience (or equivalent).

 - Strong backend engineering fundamentals (APIs, distributed systems, data modeling, reliability).

 - Experience building data-informed detection or decisioning systems (rules engines, scoring, anomaly detection, or similar), or strong interest in learning in this domain.

 - Proven ability to operate production systems: debugging, incident response, and improving on-call quality through instrumentation and automation.

 - Strong cross-functional communication skills and comfort working with product and operations partners.

 - Experience in fraud, risk, identity, authentication, authorization, abuse prevention, or security engineering.

jobs.description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.

A few things that define how we operate:

 - One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle.

 - If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.

 - We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.

 - We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.

 - We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.

OUR TEAMS

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Right now, we operate across five areas:

 - Compute — the foundation for running Ramp’s services and financial workflows: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and asynchronous execution and messaging systems, including Temporal. The team owns production runtime reliability, scaling, isolation, and safe rollouts.

 - Storage — the production data foundations that underpin Ramp: databases, caching, and object storage, with ownership of reliability, performance, capacity, recovery, and safe data movement.

 - Developer Infrastructure — the shared infrastructure that helps engineers ship and understand production: CI/CD systems, observability foundations for logs, metrics, and traces, and visibility into infrastructure usage and cost.

 - Compliance Platform — the infrastructure and operational capabilities for Ramp’s government environments and compliance needs: secure access, deployment paths, environment validation, and technical controls that let product teams deliver reliably within regulatory and compliance requirements.

 - Reliability Platform — the tools and operating model for understanding and improving customer-facing reliability and performance: SLA/SLO measurement and reporting, customer-health visibility, monitoring and paging, and incident response and follow-through. The team helps product teams remain accountable for the health of what they build.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Production Engineers at Ramp are full software engineers who happen to specialize in infrastructure. You write production code, you own systems end-to-end, and you drive technical outcomes across the organization — not just within your team.

Day to day, you will:

 - Build and operate critical infrastructure across Ramp's compute, storage, messaging, and observability stack — owning the systems that handle real financial transactions at scale.

 - Drive architectural change — not just flag problems. When you surface a reliability or scalability issue, you own the path forward: you propose the solution, find the owners across engineering, and stay in until it's resolved.

 - Partner with product teams at the design phase — reviewing architectures, embedding golden paths, and making it easy to build correctly the first time.

 - Build Ramp's next level of scale — you'll be a hands-on contributor to the most consequential infrastructure shift happening right now: our move to a cellular architecture, enabling Ramp to scale, reach international markets, operate in highly regulated and constrained environments (e.g. FedRAMP), and deliver on enterprise-grade SLAs.

 - Enable AI-native engineering — as Ramp builds increasingly AI-powered products, PE is the team that makes sure the platform can support them. You'll proactively partner with product teams on AI infrastructure patterns, define the golden paths that turn one-off solutions into reusable foundations, and stay ahead of emerging challenges before they become blockers.

 - Build developer tooling and self-service infrastructure — so that other teams can answer their own questions (cost, performance, reliability) without involving PE.

 - Participate in on-call rotation — and more importantly, use every incident as a signal to eliminate the root cause, not just resolve the symptom.

 - Lead across the company — PE doesn't just review designs or show up when called. We proactively initiate cross-team architectural reviews, and we take full ownership of company-wide reliability and scalability initiatives: identifying the problem, proposing the solution, aligning the stakeholders, and staying in until it's done.

WHAT WE LOOK FOR

We don't hire for a checklist. We hire for the instincts that make someone exceptional on this team.

The mindset we're looking for:

 - You can't walk past something broken without wanting to fix it — and you don't stop at the workaround. You find the root cause and eliminate the class of problem.

 - You think in systems, not tasks. You understand that "fixing the bug" is step one; making it so the bug can't happen again is the job.

 - You move with urgency but without chaos. You know when to go fast and when to slow down and do it right.

 - You treat product teams as your users. You build for them, communicate with them proactively, and measure success by how much faster they can ship. But you're also an owner — when something is broken or blocking, you don't wait to be asked. We win when our customers win.

 - You leave things better than you found them. Every system you touch, every process you encounter — you move it forward. Not always dramatically, but always directionally. You picked it up in a certain state; you leave it in a better one.

 - You are equally comfortable reading a database query plan, reviewing a system design doc, writing a Terraform module, and jumping into an incident at 2am.

Experience profile:

 - 2+ years of software engineering experience shipping high-quality architectures for critical systems

 - Strong software engineering fundamentals — you write clean, well-tested, production-ready code

 - Hands-on experience with distributed systems at production scale

 - Experience with at least one major cloud provider (AWS preferred)

ABOUT THE ROLE

Companies are adopting AI across more teams, but most still struggle to produce real workflows, measurable outcomes, and efficient spend. Ramp’s AI Solutions team helps customers turn that spend into working systems: agents, automations, and integrations that run real finance operations, built on top of Ramp’s growing AI product stack, including Glass, Inspect, Router, and Token Spend Management.

As a software engineer on AI Solutions, you'll co-lead customer engagements with an AI Solutions Strategist while also helping turn repeated customer needs into platform capabilities across Ramp’s AI product stack. The Strategist owns business discovery, the ROI story, stakeholder alignment, and rollout planning. You own the technical side: discovery, solution design, prototyping, implementation, production readiness, and the product feedback loop back into our platform and AI primitives.

This is a deeply client-facing, hands-on building role based in New York, with occasional travel depending on engagements. You'll take projects from a customer's first workflow-discovery sessions through launch and into steady, measurable production use — then turn what you learned into reusable product patterns the next customer can adopt without starting from zero.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Ship production AI workflows for the companies we partner with — agents, automations, and integrations their teams use every day.

 - Translate customer work into platform work by identifying needs across deployments and helping improve Ramp’s AI primitives.

 - Make the next deployment easier by turning customer specific work into reusable components, product feedback, reference architectures, and playbooks.

 - Run technical discovery with customers: current workflows, systems, data quality, constraints, and what's blocking adoption.

 - Turn customer goals into concrete requirements, including security, privacy, reliability, performance, scalability, and cost.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

ABOUT THE ROLE

How we build software is changing. Designers are building tools and agents, prototyping in code, and shipping directly into the product. More people can create software than ever before. That makes design judgment more important, not less.

We’re looking for a Design Systems Lead to build that judgment into the foundations of Ramp.

This is not just about maintaining a component library. It’s about making it possible for designers, engineers, and agents to build experiences that look, feel, and work like Ramp—without a designer driving every decision or the design systems team reviewing every change.

You’re a designer first, with the technical depth to guide architecture and get into the code. You have exceptional taste and strong opinions about typography, hierarchy, interaction, and motion. Just as importantly, you know how to turn that judgment into patterns, tools, and guidance that make everyone else’s work better.

You’re deeply curious about AI and already using it to change how you work. You build, experiment, inspect the results, and push past the demo. You can imagine a different way of building software—and lead a team toward it.

This role is for you if you’re excited by:

 - Making great design reproducible. Raise the quality of Ramp’s product and encode what makes it good, so people and agents can produce coherent, usable experiences by default. The system should make excellent work easier, not make every experience look the same.

 - Reimagining what a design system can be. Build beyond components and tokens into composition, interaction patterns, agent guidance, and evaluations. Connect exploration and production so the fastest way to build is also a path to great quality.

 - Leading a team that multiplies everyone else’s impact. Create clear direction, ambitious goals, and a caring yet demanding environment. Inspire curiosity, develop people, and stay close enough to the work to help make it exceptional.

The opportunity is to raise the floor for everyone building at Ramp, while giving designers more room to make the most important experiences extraordinary.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead and develop the design systems team. Set clear priorities, ownership, and goals. Give direct, timely feedback, hold people accountable, and help them do the best work of their careers.

 - Own the system’s vision and direction. Decide what to preserve, evolve, simplify, or replace based on what builders and customers need. Turn that direction into focused work the team can deliver.

 - Elevate Ramp’s visual and interaction design. Raise the bar for typography, hierarchy, density, motion, responsive behavior, accessibility, and the states beyond the happy path.

 - Make design judgment usable by people and agents. Translate principles into reusable patterns, reference experiences, composition rules, and guidance that produce better work without you in the room.

 - Guide technical architecture with engineering. Shape everything from components and tokens to how agents discover guidance, compose interfaces, and check their work. Make sound tradeoffs between flexibility, coherence, performance, and ease of use.

 - Stay hands-on. Build prototypes, work in code, and get into implementation details to test ideas, unblock the team, and understand where the system breaks down.

 - Define and measure quality. Build repeatable evaluations grounded in real tasks. Measure whether builders can ship better work faster, with less rework—not just whether they use the tools.

 - Improve the path from idea to shipped experience. Partner with engineering and AI teams on workflows that support fast exploration, useful iteration, and appropriate production safeguards.

 - Earn adoption. Work alongside product teams, listen closely, teach through examples, and turn recurring questions and exceptions into improvements to the system.

 - Keep the team moving forward. Experiment as models and tools evolve, share what you learn, and change direction when the evidence calls for it.

WHAT YOU NEED

 - Experience leading and developing strong design or design engineering teams, with a track record of setting direction and delivering meaningful outcomes.

 - Exceptional visual and interaction design skills. Your work shows a clear point of view, attention to detail, and an ability to make complex experiences feel simple.

 - Deep systems thinking and experience building systems that other teams actually adopt. You can show how your work improved both their speed and the quality of what shipped.

 - Strong technical fluency. You can prototype and build in code, understand front-end architecture, and work through implementation tradeoffs with engineers—not just hand off specifications.

 - Active, hands-on use of AI in your design and building workflow. You understand where it helps, where it fails, and how to improve its output rather than accept it.

 - Experience turning design principles into practical guidance, reusable patterns, and quality checks that work at scale.

 - Strong product judgment and a habit of staying close to the people using what you build. You connect system decisions to real workflows and customer outcomes.

 - The ability to create clarity in ambiguity, make decisions, give difficult feedback, and maintain momentum without losing the quality bar.

 - Curiosity that borders on obsession about how AI changes software and how we build it—and the ability to ignite that curiosity in others.

NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience building agent-usable design guidance, generation workflows, or evaluations for design quality.

 - Experience building developer or designer tools that became part of other teams’ daily workflow.

 - Experience leading a major design-system migration or company-wide change in how teams build.

 - Experience evolving a system across platforms or connecting product and brand experiences.

 - Founder or early-stage startup experience.

 - Centralized home-office equipment ordering

 - Health and wellness stipend

 - Budget for intra-office travel

 - Weekly coffee stipend

 - 401(k), including employer match on contributions made while employed by Ramp

 - Fertility HRA (up to $10,000 per year)

 - Parental leave: up to 16 weeks (birthing + bonding) or 8 weeks (bonding only) at 100% pay

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Work the hardest UK onboarding cases yourself and make the final first-line (1LoD) call: complex ownership structures, EDD, PEP and adverse-media outcomes, and anything that needs judgement rather than a checklist

 - Keep the UK queue moving: spot what’s stuck, decide what matters most, and pick up cases yourself through leave and spikes in volume

 - Be the senior expert the UK team leans on: share your reasoning on hard cases, raise the bar on decisions, and help everyone get better at building as well as reviewing

 - Own escalations with our card-issuing and payments partners, including recurring failures, disputed or unnecessary requirements, and turning each fix into a repeatable playbook

 - Set the standard for customer-facing onboarding communications: clear requests, fast follow-ups, no avoidable back-and-forth

 - Build fixes, not workarounds: automate your own work with AI, and work with Product and Engineering to remove requirements customers shouldn’t have to meet twice

 - Define and track operational metrics (caseload by provider, time to close, handling time) and use them to decide what to fix next

 - Write consistent, evidenced 1LoD decision standards that hold up to partner sample reviews and second-line scrutiny
 
 

WHAT YOU NEED

 - 5+ years in KYB / onboarding / financial-crime operations at a UK fintech, EMI, PI or bank

 - Practical working knowledge of the UK regulatory framework for EMIs/PIs: MLRs 2017, JMLSG guidance, and FCA expectations for customer due diligence

 - Strong judgement on complex business customers: multi-layer ownership, overseas parents, trusts, PEPs, and knowing when to escalate

You'll design and run those systems: how work gets split, how agents coordinate, how results get deduplicated, verified and ranked, and what it all costs. The problems are general (agent swarms, agentic map-reduce, long-running fan-out workflows) and you'll own them from prototype to production.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Decide how the work gets done: how to break a problem down, what each agent sees, how many agents to run, and which model handles which step

 - Squeeze accuracy out of the models: context design, self-verification, voting and consensus across agents, and knowing when more agents stop helping

 - Measure quality without reading every trace: sampling, automated verification, and precision and recall on the final output

 - Drive down cost and latency per useful result: model routing, caching, early stopping, and smaller or fine-tuned models where they hold up

 - Turn one-off experiments into reusable workflows on our existing orchestration stack

 - Evaluate new models, inference setups and training approaches, and bring in what works

WHAT YOU NEED

 - Experience building applied AI systems and LLM applications that shipped

 - Hands-on experience with multi-agent or high-fan-out LLM workloads: parallel agents, map-reduce over models, large batch inference

 - Strong engineering in Python; you build concurrent, distributed systems that hold up in production

 - Judgment about output: you decide what the end result should look like before you scale the swarm, and you can separate signal from agent noise

 - The habit of measuring: cost, yield, false-positive rate, and whether a change actually helped

 - Ownership: you can run a roadmap and a production system with little oversight

 - Clear written communication

NICE-TO-HAVE
