jobs.description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.

A few things that define how we operate:

 - One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle.

 - If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.

 - We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.

 - We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.

 - We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.

OUR TEAMS

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Right now, we operate across five areas:

 - Compute — the foundation for running Ramp’s services and financial workflows: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and asynchronous execution and messaging systems, including Temporal. The team owns production runtime reliability, scaling, isolation, and safe rollouts.

 - Storage — the production data foundations that underpin Ramp: databases, caching, and object storage, with ownership of reliability, performance, capacity, recovery, and safe data movement.

 - Developer Infrastructure — the shared infrastructure that helps engineers ship and understand production: CI/CD systems, observability foundations for logs, metrics, and traces, and visibility into infrastructure usage and cost.

 - Compliance Platform — the infrastructure and operational capabilities for Ramp’s government environments and compliance needs: secure access, deployment paths, environment validation, and technical controls that let product teams deliver reliably within regulatory and compliance requirements.

 - Reliability Platform — the tools and operating model for understanding and improving customer-facing reliability and performance: SLA/SLO measurement and reporting, customer-health visibility, monitoring and paging, and incident response and follow-through. The team helps product teams remain accountable for the health of what they build.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

As a FinOps Specialist within Production Engineering, you’ll help Ramp make better decisions about infrastructure spend – from resource usage and cloud commitments to vendor contracts and new investments.

You’ll work closely with Production Engineering leadership, Developer Infrastructure, Finance, Procurement, and engineering teams across Ramp. You’ll bring financial depth, investigate opportunities independently, and partner with engineers to turn recommendations into measurable results.

This is a senior individual contributor role.

Day to day, you will:

 - Set direction for infrastructure cost management. Identify the highest-impact opportunities across Ramp, establish priorities with Production Engineering leadership and partner teams, and build a roadmap that balances immediate savings with lasting improvements.

 - Understand and explain our spend. Investigate costs across AWS, observability, and AI providers. Connect changes to usage, architecture, customer growth, and engineering decisions, and help teams distinguish expected investment from avoidable waste.

 - Embed with teams early. Partner with product and infrastructure teams during design and planning. Help them evaluate cost implications, model how systems will scale, and make informed tradeoffs before committing to an architecture or vendor.

 - Build forecasts we can defend. Work with engineers to understand upcoming launches, migrations, and capacity needs. Translate those plans into financial models that explain expected spend, key assumptions, and uncertainty.

 - Shape commitment and vendor strategy. Model cloud discounts, commitment levels, payment structures, and renewal scenarios. Partner with Finance, Procurement, and infrastructure leaders to develop negotiation strategies and carry them through vendor discussions.

 - Drive optimization across the company. Proactively identify opportunities that span teams, propose a path forward, align engineering owners and technical program managers, and stay involved through implementation and verified savings.

 - Make cost visible and actionable. Partner with DevInfra to build attribution, dashboards, anomaly detection, and self-service tools that let teams understand and manage their costs. Establish reusable approaches that make cost awareness part of how Ramp builds, and work toward clearer service and product unit economics.

 - Evaluate new infrastructure investments. Build models for decisions such as buying versus renting capacity, changing providers, or adopting new infrastructure. Make the financial implications and technical assumptions clear.

 - Use AI to investigate and build. Use AI tools and coding agents to analyze data, create dashboards and automations, navigate infrastructure code, and develop proposed changes with engineering partners. Help improve the tools and workflows that make cost management repeatable.

WHAT WE LOOK FOR

We don’t hire for a checklist. We hire for the judgment and ownership that make someone effective in this role.

The mindset we’re looking for:

 - You follow the question through. When a bill changes, you want to understand what happened, whether it makes sense, and what to do about it.

 - You have high agency. You identify opportunities without waiting for an assignment, investigate independently, and bring a recommendation. When progress depends on other teams, you find the right partners and drive the work forward.

 - You think in systems and tradeoffs. You connect technical decisions to financial outcomes and weigh savings against reliability, performance, engineering time, and flexibility.

 - You look for the underlying cause. When you uncover unexpected spend or an inefficient process, you investigate what allowed it to happen and improve the tooling, decisions, or practices that will prevent it from recurring.

 - You connect efficiency to customer outcomes. You partner closely with engineering teams to understand their goals and make cost tradeoffs that help Ramp serve customers reliably and scale sustainably. You pursue savings with a clear understanding of their impact on performance, reliability, and the team’s ability to deliver.

 - You make complex things understandable. You can discuss financial models with Finance and infrastructure choices with engineers, and help both make decisions together.

 - You own the outcome. You set priorities, build alignment, and follow through to implementation and measured results. You turn what you learn into tools and practices that help teams make better decisions themselves.

Experience profile:

 - Experience improving infrastructure economics in a growing technology organization, with examples of decisions you influenced and measurable results you helped deliver.

 - Strong financial modeling and forecasting skills. You can translate engineering roadmaps, customer growth, migrations, and new infrastructure investments into future spend scenarios. You make assumptions and uncertainty explicit, explain variances, and update forecasts as plans evolve.

 - Experience planning large infrastructure contracts and commitments. You can model usage over multi-year terms, compare pricing and payment structures, and balance savings against overcommitment risk and flexibility. You’ve helped shape commitment levels, renewal timing, and negotiation strategy with Finance, Procurement, and engineering leaders.

 - Working knowledge of cloud billing and pricing, including cost allocation, commitment discounts, payment structures, and the relationship between usage and cost. AWS experience is especially relevant.

 - Strong technical fluency. You can reason about compute, storage, networking, and managed services, and navigate Terraform or similar infrastructure-as-code tools to understand how systems are configured. You can investigate technical questions independently, connect infrastructure choices to cost, and work with engineers on concrete changes.

 - Experience with cost attribution and analysis. You can connect infrastructure spend to teams, services, products, and usage drivers, including shared resources. You work directly with cost and usage data, reconcile conflicting sources, and develop practical allocation methods with clear assumptions.

Relevant backgrounds include FinOps, infrastructure finance, strategic sourcing, analytics, data, and infrastructure engineering. A software engineering background is welcome, but not required.

You'll own that work end to end. For team acquisitions, that means the pipeline, the assessment, the economics, the founder and team conversations, the offers, and post-close integration with People Operations and the hiring teams. When Ramp acquires a company outright, you'll own the people side of the deal alongside Corporate Development: who stays, at what level, on what terms, and how we communicate it.

You'll report to Ramp's head of People Finance & Strategy and work day to day with Corporate Development, Legal, and the business leaders who'll take the teams.

This is a senior individual contributor role with direct exposure to our co-founders, CFO, and head of Corporate Development. You'll run the hiring process yourself, from first conversation to signed offers, and stay with the team through post-close integration, which no one owns at Ramp today. The scope will change as we do more of this, and defining it is part of the job.

This role will grow with what Ramp does. As volume grows, so does the scope: larger acquisitions alongside Corporate Development, the people side of company acquisitions, and strategy work across People Finance & Strategy. At Ramp, people who have built deep operating judgment in roles like this have gone on to lead major business areas. For the right person, this is a way to build deal judgment and talent judgment at the same time, with the company context to take on broader operating roles over time in corporate development, general management, or People leadership.

You don't need to have done this exact job before. You do need to have run deals or searches yourself and be credible with founders and with executives.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the relationships. The founder, every member of the team, and the Ramp leaders who'd take them hear from you first, and you keep those conversations moving from the first call to signed offers.

 - Price and structure the package. Use market data and our compensation framework to build an offer for each person and a budget for the team, including salary, equity, sign-on, and retention.

 - Write the recommendation. Pursue, pass, or route to Corporate Development, with the economics compared to hiring the same people individually. Present it to our co-founders, CFO, and head of Corporate Development.

 - Run the process: interviews, references, light diligence, negotiation within agreed bounds, and close.

 - Build the pipeline with Corporate Development. Keep a current view of the companies and teams in the areas Ramp is building, and of the investors, founders, and bankers who see them early. Qualify quickly and pass quickly.

 - Handle the mechanics with Legal and People Operations: confidentiality, non-solicits, immigration, the team's existing equity, and timing.

 - Own post-close integration with People Operations and the hiring teams: start dates, managers, onboarding, retention checkpoints. Track whether the people we set out to hire joined, stayed, and performed, and turn what you learn into a playbook.

 - On company acquisitions, own the people workstream with Corporate Development: team diligence, leveling, retention design, offers, and communications.

jobs.title: Senior Web Developer I
jobs.description:
Relay is a digital banking platform that gives self-made business owners the tools and know-how to be great with money—bringing clarity, confidence, and control to every dollar earned, so they can turn hard work into lasting success. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.

Web Development builds and runs relayfi.com http://relayfi.com — the pages, components, content platform, and infrastructure that turn organic search, AI-driven discovery, and paid traffic into new Relay accounts. We're a small team with a big impact, moving fast while holding a high bar for performance, accessibility, and SEO.

We're looking for a Senior Web Developer to lead complex web projects, shape technical decisions, and help scale the platform behind Relay's growth. You'll work in a modern Next.js codebase with React, TypeScript, Tailwind, and Contentful, tackling architectural challenges that directly impact site performance, scalability, and discoverability. You'll own projects from technical planning through launch, mentor other developers, and partner closely with teams across the company.

This is an ideal role for a front-end developer who thrives on ownership, enjoys solving complex technical problems, and wants to make a measurable impact. Your technical judgment will carry weight here, and you'll have the autonomy to challenge assumptions, influence priorities, and shape how we build.

Want to see what we're building? Check out relayfi.com http://relayfi.com and Telegraph https://storybook.relayfi.design/, the design system our engineers use across Relay.

What You’ll Be Doing

 - Project Ownership: Lead complex, multi-part projects end-to-end — define scope, set milestones, coordinate with cross-functional teams, and deliver high-quality work on time. Own what happens after launch by measuring performance, identifying opportunities, and iterating on improvements

 - Technical Architecture: Define the technical approach for features and projects, making thoughtful decisions around server/client boundaries, caching, revalidation, and CDN behaviour. Balance performance, scalability, and technical debt while proactively simplifying systems, improving maintainability, and addressing root causes

 - Performance, Accessibility & Technical SEO: Proactively improve site performance, accessibility, security, and technical SEO, including structured data, metadata, and semantic markup that improve discoverability across search engines and AI platforms

 - Content Platform Development: Build and optimize integrations between the headless CMS and front end, developing scalable content models and tools that empower non-technical teams to manage and publish content independently

 - AI-Driven Development: Build and integrate AI workflows and agents that improve development efficiency, from automated code reviews and performance monitoring to design-to-component generation. Establish testing and review guardrails to maintain quality and help the team adopt AI effectively

 - Measurement & Experimentation: Build and maintain analytics, event tracking, attribution, feature flags, and A/B testing infrastructure to support conversion optimization. Own integrations between the website, marketing tools, and CRM systems, including forms and lead routing

 - Code Quality & Testing: Set a high bar for maintainable, performant, and well-documented code. Define testing strategies across unit, integration, and end-to-end tests, ensuring quality and reliability are built into every project

 - Cross-Functional Leadership & Mentorship: Serve as a trusted technical partner to Marketing, Design, Product, and external agencies, translating business needs into technical solutions and driving alignment on priorities and tradeoffs. Mentor developers through pairing, code reviews, and knowledge sharing, while helping cross-functional partners navigate technical decisions

Who You Are

 - You have 4+ years of front-end development experience, ideally in a high-growth B2B SaaS or fintech environment, with a proven ability to work independently and deliver high-quality solutions

 - You're strong in React, Next.js, and Node, and you write TypeScript by default. Our repo is fully typed in strict mode with type checking enforced in CI, so strong TypeScript proficiency is essential

 - You're skilled in modern front-end architecture, with a strong understanding of server/client boundaries, caching, revalidation, and CDN behaviour. You think in systems, designing scalable solutions while anticipating downstream impacts

 - You're proficient in Tailwind and experienced working with design systems, reusable components, and headless CMS platforms. You understand content modelling and integrations, with experience in Contentful and GraphQL being valuable but not required

 - You have a strong understanding of web performance, accessibility, and technical SEO, including Core Web Vitals (LCP and CLS), image optimization, bundle analysis, WCAG 2.1 AA, semantic HTML, metadata, structured data, sitemaps, and heading hierarchy

 - You actively use AI tools and workflows to improve development efficiency, with the judgment to evaluate outputs, manage risks, and maintain code quality

 - You have strong project management and communication skills, with the ability to lead cross-functional initiatives, manage competing priorities, and translate technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders

 - You're a proactive problem-solver who thinks beyond individual tasks, understands customer needs, challenges assumptions, anticipates downstream impacts, and adapts quickly to new technologies and feedback

Bonus Points

 - You've built analytics, experimentation, and marketing integrations using tools like Segment, GTM, Statsig, and HubSpot

 - You've worked with AWS Amplify Hosting or similar CI/CD platforms and built end-to-end tests using Playwright or equivalent tools

 - You've built animations using GSAP or Framer Motion and have experience with SCSS

The Interview Process

 - Stage 1: A 30-minute Google Meet video call with a member of the Talent team

 - Stage 2: A 45-minute Google Meet video call with our Director, Web

 - Stage 3: A take-home technical challenge

 - Stage 4: A 60-minute Google Meet video call with the Web team, including a review of your take-home submission and a live exercise building on it

 - Stage 5: A 45-minute in-person interview with a member of the Leadership team

Our Compensation Approach

We believe Relayers should feel rewarded for the impact they have on our mission and growth. Compensation follows impact. As impact increases, compensation grows, and we do not limit compensation changes to a once-a-year review cycle.

The annual salary range for this role is $107,100 CAD to $130,900 CAD.

For candidates who demonstrate full readiness for the defined scope of the role, the typical starting salary is $119,000 CAD. Offers below this point reflect candidates we believe can grow into the full scope of the role with support and development. Offers above this point reflect impact that meaningfully exceeds the role’s defined expectations or an expanded scope from day one.

We encourage you to have a conversation with your recruiter and ask questions about compensation throughout the hiring process. For more information on our compensation philosophy and perks and benefits, visit our Candidate Hub https://www.notion.so/Candidate-Hub-1c7da8b7f88580a893f7d7c7852b064e?pvs=21.

Why Relay Might Be the Perfect Fit For You 

 - You push relentlessly for reinvention: You're always asking "how can this be better?" -- in your work, in your craft, in yourself. Comfort is a signal to push harder, not coast. You'd rather build something better than defend something familiar.

 - You crave autonomy: We trust our team with big challenges and the freedom to solve them. If you’re someone who takes initiative, is comfortable taking risks, and seeks input when needed, you’ll find the freedom here empowering.

 - You own your work: You take pride in your work, follow through on commitments, and feel a deep sense of responsibility for outcomes, not just tasks.

 - You build with AI, not just use it: You're actively embedding AI into how you work, pushing what's possible, and bringing your team along with you.

 - You care about impact, not noise: You care deeply about the substance of your work. You measure success by results, not recognition, and you let your work speak for itself. 

 - You’re energized by complexity and ambiguity: You enjoy tackling problems that don’t come with a playbook. You’re comfortable building from scratch, iterating as you go, and collaborating to shape the best path forward.

 - You seek out feedback: You see directness as respect, not criticism. You actively seek input, sit with hard truths, and use feedback as fuel for improvement.

 - Small businesses are why we're here: Relay exists to help them thrive -- and that mission has to resonate with you.

Join Us

We're looking for people who are relentless, curious, and care deeply about the work. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't perfectly match the job description -- your perspective and drive matter more. We welcome diverse backgrounds and people who think critically, challenge the status quo, and want to help small businesses thrive.

If you require accommodations at any stage of the hiring process, please reach out to your Talent Partner.

Disclaimer: For compliance reasons, all offers of employment at Relay are conditional upon a successful background check and employment verification through Certn.

Important Notice: Relay’s recruitment team only contacts candidates and corresponds from official corporate email addresses ending in @relayfi.com. We will never ask for sensitive personal data (such as bank account details, credit card numbers, or social security/insurance numbers) during the initial application or interview stages.

jobs.description:

Our mission is to increase the success rate of small businesses. Traditional banking has been a growth limiter rather than a growth enabler for business owners, and we're changing that. Relay is the all-in-one, collaborative money management platform. We're building for employer SMBs and their finance function, and we're focused on delivering a human-centric customer experience.

Relay processes millions of dollars in deposits, wires, checks, and card transactions every business day, and 321,000+ small business owners trust us with their money. The Transaction Monitoring team is why that trust is warranted. Every transaction we review is a decision: hold or release, investigate or clear. Good decisions mean legitimate business owners get their money fast and bad actors get stopped before they succeed.

We're looking for someone with real transaction monitoring experience who is curious, decisive, and excited to build with AI, not just work a queue.

 - Review and investigate suspicious activity across every payment channel: deposits, checks, wires, and card transactions

 - Make hold/release decisions on flagged transactions, and own them — verify the signals, check the story, make the call. Review customer documentation and verify business activity to support hold and release decisions.

 - Detect patterns that don't belong: velocity abuse, accounts moving money in ways that don't match their profile, business email compromise, altered items

 - Document your investigations clearly and completely — your case notes are read by compliance, our bank partner, and potentially examiners

 - Suggest improvements to fraud rules and controls: flag rules that are generating false positives, spot gaps that let bad activity through, and bring recommendations to Risk Strategy so your findings shape how we detect fraud

 - Collaborate with Compliance, Customer Experience, and Product to resolve cases quickly without compromising on risk

 - Use AI tools daily to investigate faster, pull data, and improve how the team works

- You have 2+ years of transaction monitoring experience at a bank, fintech, or payments company. You've made real hold/release decisions, not just escalated them.

 - You're curious and investigative. When something doesn't add up, you dig into the why instead of just flagging it and moving on.

 - You make calls and stand behind them. Holding a deposit means a business can't access their money; releasing it means betting your judgment that it's clean. You're comfortable owning both.

 - You're a problem solver with high agency. You don't just spot issues — you come with solutions and drive them forward without waiting to be asked.

 - You build with AI. You're actively using AI tools in how you work today and you're excited to push what's possible with them.

 - You communicate clearly. You document findings well and can present them to teammates, compliance, and non-risk partners like CX and Sales.

 - You thrive in a fast-paced environment. You're comfortable wearing multiple hats, handling ambiguity, and adapting as fraud patterns shift.

 - You have a growth mindset. You want to get a little better every day and you treat feedback as fuel.
 
 

Bonus Points:

 - SQL proficiency — you can pull your own data without waiting on analytics

 - Card and disputes experience, including familiarity with the relevant regulations

 - Working knowledge of compliance: BSA/AML, KYC/CIP, and how regulations shape monitoring decisions

 - CAMS, CFE, or equivalent certification

jobs.title: Risk Analyst (Onboarding)
jobs.description:
Relay is a digital banking platform that gives self-made business owners the tools and know-how to be great with money—bringing clarity, confidence, and control to every dollar earned, so they can turn hard work into lasting success. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.

Our mission is to increase the success rate of small businesses. Traditional banking has been a growth limiter rather than a growth enabler for business owners, and we're changing that. Relay is the all-in-one, collaborative money management platform. We're building for employer SMBs and their finance function, and we're focused on delivering a human-centric customer experience.

Relay processes millions of dollars in deposits, wires, checks, and card transactions every business day, and 321,000+ small business owners trust us with their money. Every one of them started in the same place: an application. The Onboarding team is Relay's front door. Every application we review is a decision: approve or decline, verify or request more. Good decisions mean legitimate business owners get banking fast and bad actors never get in.

We're looking for someone early in their career — new grads included — who is curious, decisive, and excited to build workflow improvements, not just work a queue.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Review and decision new business applications end-to-end: compliance checks, KYC/KYB, document verification, and fraud review

 - Make approve/decline calls and own them — verify the signals, check the story, make the call. Review customer documentation and verify business activity to support your decisions.

 - Detect patterns that don't belong: synthetic identities, business profiles that don't match the story, altered or fraudulent documents, signals that don't add up

 - Document your reviews clearly and completely — your decisions and case notes are read by compliance

 - Suggest improvements to onboarding rules and controls: flag rules generating false positives, spot gaps that let bad actors through, and bring recommendations to Risk Strategy and your pod lead so your findings shape how we decide

 - Balance risk and customer experience — every decision trades fraud prevention against friction for a real business trying to open an account

 - Use AI tools daily to investigate faster, pull data, and improve how the team works
 

WHO YOU ARE

 - You're a recent graduate or early in your career with strong judgment — you make sound calls on incomplete information and can explain your reasoning. (This is an entry-level role: we'll teach you the tools, KYC/KYB, and fraud investigation.)

 - Build mutual action plans that get partners to their first client referrals, and drive early activation rather than stopping at signature

 - You have strong interpersonal skills, a growth mindset, and the adaptability to thrive in a fast-scaling, evolving environment

 - You have experience in fintech, accounting software, or a neobank

 - You have sold through a channel, partner, or referral motion

Data Platform, the team you'll lead, owns the foundation underneath: infrastructure, cost, real-time data, observability, and the AI capabilities the rest of Relay builds on.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Growth
jobs.description:
Relay is a digital banking platform that gives self-made business owners the tools and know-how to be great with money—bringing clarity, confidence, and control to every dollar earned, so they can turn hard work into lasting success. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.

At Relay, product management is about outcomes, not outputs. We start with real customer problems and build solutions that move the needle for SMBs, and for our business. Our team pairs long-term vision with rapid iteration. We believe that trust is a product feature, and that usability, reliability, and polish aren't afterthoughts, they're core to how we earn the confidence of business owners.

Why this role matters

Signing up for a business bank account is the easy part. The hard part is the distance between "account opened" and "this is where I run my business." That distance is where most SMBs quietly stall; the first deposit that never lands, the payroll still running out of the old account, the bookkeeper who was never invited in. Every business owner who doesn't cross it stays on the cashflow tightrope we exist to get them off of.

As Senior Product Manager, Growth (Activation), you own that crossing. You'll own the journey from first login to funded, transacting, habitual use of Relay — and the systems, experiments, and in-product moments that get customers there faster and in greater numbers. This is a metrics-owning role: you'll be accountable for activation rate, time-to-first-deposit, and depth of product adoption in the first 90 days, and for the revenue those unlock.

In your first year, you might:

 - Rebuild the post-signup experience so a new owner reaches their first funded transaction in days, not weeks

 - Diagnose where and why customers drop between account approval, funding, and first payment, then ship the sequenced interventions that close those gaps

 - Stand up the experimentation and lifecycle infrastructure that lets Relay run activation tests continuously rather than one-off

 - Drive adoption of the products that make Relay sticky (multiple accounts, cards, bill pay, accounting integrations) by getting them in front of the right owner at the right moment

 - Partner with Risk and Operations so that friction we add for good reasons (KYC, fraud controls) costs us as few good customers as possible

 - Build the narrative and roadmap that aligns leadership, Marketing, and CX around a shared definition of an activated customer

What you'll be doing:

 - Own activation end-to-end: define the vision, set the roadmap, and deliver measurable improvements to how quickly and completely SMBs start running their money through Relay

 - Treat activation like a business: define the activation metric that actually predicts retention and revenue, instrument it, monitor it, and make decisions rooted in data and customer insight

 - Run a real experiment engine: form hypotheses, design tests, read results honestly, and kill what doesn't work, while knowing when a problem calls for a rebuild rather than an A/B test

 - Ship high-quality product from ideation to launch: partner closely with design and engineering as part of a leadership trifecta, raising the bar for usability, craft, and polish. Onboarding copy and empty states are your job, not someone else's

 - Work across the whole first-run surface: in-product experiences, lifecycle messaging, and the handoffs between Marketing, Sales, and CX that make or break a new customer's first month

 - Stay deeply connected to SMB customers: watch real owners set up their accounts, understand what makes them hesitate to move their money, and design for the trust that earns

 - Build and tell the story: create clear narratives that inspire leadership and cross-functional partners, even in ambiguous situations

 - Champion product culture at Relay: bring curiosity, ownership, and a high bar for quality that elevates the product team as a whole

Who you are

 - At least five years of product management experience, with a track record of owning and materially moving a funnel or lifecycle metric

 - Direct experience with activation, onboarding, or early-lifecycle work in a product-led business

 - Strong data competency: you self-serve your metrics, write your own SQL, and can tell a real signal from a noisy test

 - Fluent in experimentation. You know what your infrastructure can and can't support, and you're rigorous about what counts as a win

 - Excellent storytelling and communication

 - Keep credit policy current with our funding partner. Make sure what we approve stays within the policy our partner will fund, and update that policy as the portfolio grows.

 - Own charge card escalations. Be the expert Customer Experience escalates to for documentation requests, decline reasons and credit questions they can't resolve.

 - Build what isn't there yet. Find the next process, report or tool the function needs, and build it.

 - You've done manual commercial credit underwriting at a corporate or commercial card issuer, from large issuers to card-focused fintechs. US experience is not required.

 - You use AI and data tools to work faster, and you can show how they've changed the way you underwrite or monitor a portfolio.

 - You work well with sales. You can explain a decline or a smaller limit without losing the relationship.

jobs.location: Toronto, ON · Vancouver, BC · New York, NY · Kitchener-Waterloo, ON · Boston, MA
jobs.description:
Relay is a digital banking platform that gives self-made business owners the tools and know-how to be great with money—bringing clarity, confidence, and control to every dollar earned, so they can turn hard work into lasting success. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.

This is an open call, so it isn't tied to one specific job. When you apply, tell us the kind of role you're most interested in. If your submission stands out, we'll match you with roles that fit, now or as we plan our 2027 hiring.

WHY AN OPEN CALL

We want to meet people who do great work. At Relay, that means people who take ownership, hold a high bar, stay curious, adapt quickly and care about what they build. A resumé shows very little of that, and AI can now write a polished one for anyone. So we'd rather see how you think.

This open call is built around three of our values:

 - Champion the self-made. Self-made businesses are why we exist, so the challenge starts with them: a real problem a small business owner might face.

 - Run toward problems. We want people who step in when something is broken or unclear. Show us a problem you didn't wait to be handed.

 - Take big swings. We push past incremental fixes. Bold ideas, backed by clear reasoning are encouraged here.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Builders and problem solvers in any function: engineering, design, product, marketing, sales, risk, operations and more. What you have in common:

 - You run toward problems. When something is broken or unclear, you figure it out and fix it.

 - You build to find answers. A prototype, a spreadsheet model or a quick test beats a long debate.

 - You take big swings and you commit to the bets you make.

 - You care about small business owners and want to fix what makes running a business hard.

 - You get a little better every day, and you go looking for feedback.

THE CHALLENGE

Think about a problem might a small business owner face, and show us how would you solve it? It doesn't have to be about money.

Answer in whatever format shows your thinking best: writing, a voice memo, a video, or something you built. Upload documents or audio up to 50 MB, or share a link for video and anything you built, such as Loom, YouTube, Figma or GitHub. Make it as long or as short as it needs to be.

Feel free to use AI if it helps (we use it every day at Relay)! We care about how you framed the problem and what you decided to do and why. Use it not to replace your thought, but to extend or augment your abilities.

 - A person reads every submission. Nothing is scored automatically.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Growth
jobs.description:
Relay is a digital banking platform that gives self-made business owners the tools and know-how to be great with money—bringing clarity, confidence, and control to every dollar earned, so they can turn hard work into lasting success. We do this by replacing financial guesswork with real visibility, transforming cash flow from a constant source of stress into a clear signal owners can use to run stronger, more resilient businesses.

At Relay, product management is about outcomes, not outputs. We start with real customer problems and build solutions that move the needle for SMBs, and for our business. Our team pairs long-term vision with rapid iteration. We believe that trust is a product feature, and that usability, reliability, and polish aren't afterthoughts, they're core to how we earn the confidence of business owners.

Why this role matters

Signing up for a business bank account is the easy part. The hard part is the distance between "account opened" and "this is where I run my business." That distance is where most SMBs quietly stall; the first deposit that never lands, the payroll still running out of the old account, the bookkeeper who was never invited in. Every business owner who doesn't cross it stays on the cashflow tightrope we exist to get them off of.

As Senior Product Manager, Growth (Activation), you own that crossing. You'll own the journey from first login to funded, transacting, habitual use of Relay — and the systems, experiments, and in-product moments that get customers there faster and in greater numbers. This is a metrics-owning role: you'll be accountable for activation rate, time-to-first-deposit, and depth of product adoption in the first 90 days, and for the revenue those unlock.

In your first year, you might:

 - Rebuild the post-signup experience so a new owner reaches their first funded transaction in days, not weeks

 - Diagnose where and why customers drop between account approval, funding, and first payment, then ship the sequenced interventions that close those gaps

 - Stand up the experimentation and lifecycle infrastructure that lets Relay run activation tests continuously rather than one-off

 - Drive adoption of the products that make Relay sticky (multiple accounts, cards, bill pay, accounting integrations) by getting them in front of the right owner at the right moment

 - Partner with Risk and Operations so that friction we add for good reasons (KYC, fraud controls) costs us as few good customers as possible

 - Build the narrative and roadmap that aligns leadership, Marketing, and CX around a shared definition of an activated customer

What you'll be doing:

 - Own activation end-to-end: define the vision, set the roadmap, and deliver measurable improvements to how quickly and completely SMBs start running their money through Relay

 - Treat activation like a business: define the activation metric that actually predicts retention and revenue, instrument it, monitor it, and make decisions rooted in data and customer insight

 - Run a real experiment engine: form hypotheses, design tests, read results honestly, and kill what doesn't work, while knowing when a problem calls for a rebuild rather than an A/B test

 - Ship high-quality product from ideation to launch: partner closely with design and engineering as part of a leadership trifecta, raising the bar for usability, craft, and polish. Onboarding copy and empty states are your job, not someone else's

 - Work across the whole first-run surface: in-product experiences, lifecycle messaging, and the handoffs between Marketing, Sales, and CX that make or break a new customer's first month

 - Stay deeply connected to SMB customers: watch real owners set up their accounts, understand what makes them hesitate to move their money, and design for the trust that earns

 - Build and tell the story: create clear narratives that inspire leadership and cross-functional partners, even in ambiguous situations

 - Champion product culture at Relay: bring curiosity, ownership, and a high bar for quality that elevates the product team as a whole

Who you are

 - At least five years of product management experience, with a track record of owning and materially moving a funnel or lifecycle metric

 - Direct experience with activation, onboarding, or early-lifecycle work in a product-led business

 - Strong data competency: you self-serve your metrics, write your own SQL, and can tell a real signal from a noisy test

 - Fluent in experimentation. You know what your infrastructure can and can't support, and you're rigorous about what counts as a win

 - Excellent storytelling and communication

skills:

you bring clarity and inspire conviction across engineering, design, and business stakeholders

 - Experience working closely with engineering and design as part of a leadership trifecta to deliver polished, high-quality experiences

 - Demonstrated success working cross-functionally with Sales, Marketing, and Customer Experience teams to ensure effective launches and adoption

 - Comfort working in ambiguous environments while bringing structure and clarity where needed

 - A hands-on operator's instinct. You're as comfortable in the details of a UX flow or a lifecycle trigger as in a roadmap review

Bonus points

 - You've worked on activation in fintech, where compliance, funding, and risk controls sit directly in the path of the customer journey

 - You've joined a company at its early stages and seen it through scale

 - You're familiar with risk/fraud tools or KYC/onboarding frameworks and how to optimize around them without weakening them

 - You've built lifecycle or CRM systems in partnership with a marketing team

The Interview Process

 - Stage 1: A 45-minute Google Meets video call with a member of our Talent team

 - Stage 2: A 45-minute Product Deep Dive interview with the hiring manager

 - Stage 3: A 1-hour case study panel interview - a take home case study assignment will form the basis of this discussion

 - Stage 4: A 45-minute Google Meets interview with a member of our leadership team

Our Compensation Approach

 - Attend Rho-sponsored events in person to build relationships and community.

 - Ramp relationships and expand referral volume through networking.

 - Advocate for client needs to inform Rho’s roadmap.

 - Win new business in competitive sales against the industry’s incumbents and newer players.

 - Deliver comprehensive product demos and answer technical inquiries.

 - Experience working with startups.

 - A consummate team player who enjoys wearing multiple hats and inspiring everyone around you to do great work.

jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Senior Software Engineer at Rho, you'll build the financial infrastructure powering the next generation of founders. This isn't a role where you sit inside a lane. You'll move across the stack, own problems end-to-end, and talk directly to the customers using what you ship. We're hiring engineers who are restless about impact, reach for AI tools the way other people reach for documentation, and genuinely want to understand why what they're building matters.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own problems from scoping to production. Write the code, ship it, watch it land.

 - Work across the stack. You go where the problem is, not where your comfort zone ends.

 - Talk to customers. Sit in on calls, read support tickets, watch session replays. Build what people actually need.

 - Use AI in your daily workflow. Code generation, debugging, spec drafting, and spot where it changes what's possible.

 - Move fast and iterate in the open. Get something in front of users, then make it better.

 - Pick up what's falling. If something's broken, fix it.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years of software engineering experience in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

 - Genuine full-stack flexibility. You've shipped across the stack and don't treat the backend/frontend divide as a hard boundary.

 - Genuine AI fluency. You use these tools every day and think about where they raise the ceiling on what you can build.

 - A bias to ship. You'd rather get something in front of a user than perfect it in a doc.

 - Customer curiosity. You want to know the person on the other side of what you're building, and you'll go find out.

 - High agency. You make progress when things are unclear, surface problems early, and own your outcomes.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

jobs.title: Design Engineer
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

A ROLE FOR THOSE COMMITTED TO DESIGNING WITH UNCOMMON CARE.

Most of a banking product is invisible when it's done right. The transfer that confirms with a motion so clean you feel it settle. The card that materializes like it was always going to. The empty state you almost want to keep looking at. Nobody files a support ticket about these things. They just trust the product a little more, and they can't tell you why.

We're hiring a Lead or Staff Design Engineer to own exactly that layer: the feel. The motion, the microinteractions, the details most companies never get to because they're too busy shipping features. We are not too busy. We think this is the work.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

You live in the browser, in code, in the space between "it functions" and "it feels inevitable." You build the interactions, the transitions, the animations, and the components that make Rho feel like the most considered product our customers use all day. Then you write the libraries that let the rest of the team hit that bar without you in the room.

This is not a product design role. You're not writing PRDs, running discovery, or owning a roadmap. You're the person who takes something that works and makes it sing, and who builds the systems that make singing the default.

If you've ever reimplemented an animation three times because the first two were 40ms too slow and felt cheap, you already understand the job.

 - Own the feel of the product. Motion, microinteractions, transitions, gestures, the physics of how things move and respond. Every one of them earns trust or spends it.

 - Build the libraries no one else has built. Animation primitives, interaction patterns, and components that are genuinely new, not a re-skin of what's already on npm. We want work that other design engineers screenshot.

 - Ship in code. You build the real thing, in the real medium, at production quality. Figma is where a conversation starts, not where craft is decided.

 - Set the craft bar in motion. Define what "good" feels like at Rho and encode it into a system, tokens, easing curves, timing, springs, so the whole product moves with one considered voice.

 - Sweat details nobody asked you to sweat. The half-pixel. The 20ms. The focus ring. The way a number ticks up. This is the entire job, not a footnote to it.

WHO YOU ARE

You've been doing this for a while, and you have the receipts: at least 7 years building production interfaces, with a body of work that is visibly, unusually crafted. This is a lead role: you set the craft bar for the feel of the product and raise everyone around you to it, through the work itself and the systems you leave behind. We need to see it. A portfolio, a personal site, a component library, shipped work, live demos, something we can open and feel the care in.

You are the kind of person who:

 - Thinks Emil Kowalski and Josh Puckett are describing the job, not the aspiration. If those names mean nothing to you, this role probably isn't yours yet. If they make you nod, keep reading.

 - Has strong opinions about motion. You know why the default ease is wrong, when a spring beats a curve, what makes an animation feel expensive versus cheap, and when the answer is no animation at all. You can defend every one of these.

 - Writes real code. React, TypeScript, CSS at a level where you're building the hard interaction, not styling someone else's. You've probably published a library, or wanted to.

 - Is a genuine craftsperson, not a generalist who dabbles in polish. Your happiest hours are spent alone with a hard interaction problem, iterating past the point most people would call it done.

 - Has taste and can't turn it off. Sloppy motion physically bothers you. You notice the jank in other people's products. You've rebuilt things for free just because they annoyed you.

WHO THIS IS NOT FOR

 - Product designers looking to move into engineering. This is the reverse: a builder who obsesses over feel. If your portfolio is flows, journey maps, and product cases, that's a different (great) role, apply for our Product Designer opening instead.

 - Engineers who tolerate design. You have to love the pixel, not just implement it.

 - Anyone early or mid-career. This is a lead/staff craft role. You need years of taste, reps, and shipped work behind you, and the standing to set the bar for others. We'd love to meet you down the line.

 - People who think "good enough, ship it" is a virtue. It sometimes is. Not here, not on this layer.

 - Anyone who needs the interaction spec handed to them. You define what great feels like; nobody's going to define it for you.

THE BAR

We want Rho to feel like the most crafted financial product in the world, calm, confident, alive. Restraint over decoration. Motion with a reason. Details that reward the customer even when they don't consciously notice. If you've read this far and you're already thinking about how you'd rebuild one of our transitions, we should talk.

Our people are our most valuable asset. The salary range for this role is $130,000 - $300,000. Base salary may vary depending on relevant experience, skills, and business needs. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, healthcare benefits, and paid time off.

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

THE ROLE

Rho is hiring Product Managers, but what we truly seek are GMs/Product CEOs. You'll own a meaningful surface of the platform end-to-end — close enough to the work and close enough to the customer that your judgment is earned, not inherited from a roadmap. You'll know what founders need before they ask, because you've built the intuition that comes from proximity, not process.

How products get built is fundamentally changing. AI is collapsing the line between thinking about something and making it real. The best PMs right now aren't just writing specs — they're prototyping with frontier models, testing ideas the same afternoon they have them, and building product that couldn't have existed a year ago. If that's already how you work, keep reading.

Rho is rebuilding the finance stack for the innovation economy. What happens next depends on the quality of our decisions and the speed at which we make them. The PMs we hire are how we get there.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Operate like a founder. Your surface is your company: its metrics are your P&L, its problems are yours whether or not they're in your job description. Nobody assigns founders their work. Default to motion — ship the scrappy version, learn, ship again, and unblock yourself instead of waiting. The surfaces you touch move faster because you're on them.

And build for them. Develop a deep, almost unfair understanding of how early-stage companies think about money, time, and risk. Design for the workflow they don't know they want yet — the desire path, not the paved one.

Own a problem space, not a problem. Not a feature, not a ticket queue — a living territory of customer problems that shift and collide. Frame the ones that matter, sharpen the hypothesis, define success before you build, and see it through to landing in a founder's hands. The map will change under you; redraw it and keep moving.

Decide what matters most — and re-decide when the facts change. Make deliberate calls about what to do now, next, and never. Hold them loosely: when the evidence says pivot, you pivot without ego. A PM who can't say no is just a project manager with better slides.

Work at the frontier. AI is your leverage in both directions: it 10x's how you work — more ideas tested, more prototypes built, more customer insight absorbed, more shipped — and it expands what you can build, product experiences that weren't possible twelve months ago. You're expected to find both. When a new capability drops, you're the one asking what it unlocks for our customers.

Get in the weeds. You're prototyping, pressure-testing, and iterating alongside design and engineering — with opinions about the details. Bring people along while you're there: partner deeply across Engineering, Design, Operations, GTM, and leadership, and communicate the why so well the team could make your calls without you in the room.

WHO YOU ARE

 - You have 3+ years building products — as a founder, PM, or engineer or equivalent experience in a fast-paced, high-growth environment — and you've shipped work you're proud to put your name on.

 - You have frontier fluency. You work with AI daily — prototyping, analyzing, drafting, automating — and you can point to something you shipped or changed because a new capability made it possible. Not theorizing; doing.

 - You have taste. You hold your own view of what good looks like, obsess over the details, and know that in a banking product, every interaction carries trust.

 - You have discovery rigor. You can articulate the problem, the hypothesis, and how you'll know it worked before you've written a spec.

 - You build. You're not above opening a prototype, sketching a flow, or pulling the data yourself.

 - You think like a founder. You've been one, worked next to one, or operated like one — you take ownership past the edges of your role, and you pull things over the line that would die in someone else's backlog.

 - You're at home in ambiguity. You make calls on incomplete information and treat a pivot as new information, not a setback. Plans change; you're the steady one when they do.

 - You bring people with you. You build trust quickly, communicate proactively, and can align a room even when the answer is no.

 - You crave a team that pushes you — smart, ambitious people who make the work fun and help you grow faster than you thought possible.

Our people are our most valuable asset. Our target compensation range for this role is $165,000 - $320,000. Compensation will be determined by leveling and performance throughout the interview process. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, comprehensive healthcare benefits, and paid time off.

 - Assist in performing risk assessments on potential clients using established frameworks and checklists

 - Flag and escalate suspicious activity or potential compliance issues identified during onboarding to senior compliance staff

 - Coordinate with internal teams, including sales and operations, to collect outstanding client information and ensure timely onboarding

 - Maintain accurate and complete records of client onboarding files, compliance decisions, and supporting documentation in accordance with team standards

You Have

jobs.title: Staff / Principal Product Designer, Design Systems
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

Rho — New York (in person)

Rho is building the best business banking platform on earth. Not "one of." The best.

We're looking for a Staff or Principal Product Designer to own our design system, the governed, in code foundation that everything we ship stands on. This is not a role where you maintain a Figma library and file tickets. This is the role where you define the frontend layer of a financial operating system that companies trust with their money.

It's a long post on purpose. We'd rather you know exactly what this is before you apply.

What you'd actually own

Our design system is becoming the governed frontend layer of the product, components in code, rules enforced through lint and CI, documentation an AI agent can query and build against on spec. You would own that. The architecture, the tokens, the primitives, the motion language, the governance, the contribution model, and the standards that let 80 plus engineers and PMs ship on bar without a designer babysitting every pixel.

You'll partner with our frontend guild, our engineers, and the design team as genuine equals, not as a service desk. You'll decide what a component is, how it behaves, how it moves, what it enables, and where it must not bend. You'll set the craft bar for the entire org and then build the system that makes hitting that bar the path of least resistance.

Who this is for

You've been doing this for a while. We mean it, at least 7 years of product design experience, with real design systems ownership at scale. Not "contributed to a design system." Owned one. Built one. Governed one. Watched it get abused and fixed the governance so it couldn't happen again.

You are the kind of person who:

 - Designs in code, or is hungry to. You believe Figma is not the build environment, and that designing in the real medium eliminates a whole category of hidden QA cost. If the phrase "design engineer" makes you lean forward, hi.

 - Has genuine taste and a serious bar for it. Branding, typography, motion, microinteractions: you sweat all of it. You have opinions about easing curves and you can defend them. A transition that feels half a beat off bothers you until it's fixed.

 - Owns your craft, doesn't inherit it. You can point at a visual language and say "I built that," not "that was set before I got there and I adjusted the fonts."

 - Builds systems, not screens. You think in primitives, states, edge cases, and two-way doors. When something breaks at a thousand users, you already designed for it.

 - Ships, then sharpens. You move fast, you work out loud, you share the messy middle instead of disappearing for three weeks and returning with a monument. Perfect but late is a fail here.

 - Has low ego and high standards at the same time. You hold a firm craft bar and you genuinely want the critique. You defend decisions with reasoning, not with "it's my stylistic choice."

 - Gets the domain, or is dying to. Financial workflows are dense, multi-role, permission scoped, and unforgiving. You find that fun, not frightening.

Who this is NOT for

A few honest filters, to save us both time.

Do not apply to this role if you are junior. This is a Staff/Principal position. If you're earlier in your career, we'd genuinely love to meet you, we just want you in the right process. Apply for our product designer role instead: https://www.rho.co/careers/f4ece49b-3b53-4ffb-861f-9cc972c10b27

It's also probably not your fit if:

 - Your portfolio is process decks, tiny mockups, and journey maps, and the actual UI is nowhere to be found. We evaluate craft at the pixel level. If we can't see it, we can't hire it.

 - Your idea of a design system is a color palette and a component library nobody governs.

 - Motion and micro interactions are afterthoughts to you rather than part of the craft.

 - You need a fully specced ticket before you can move, and ambiguity makes you freeze.

 - You want to be handed the vision. We want someone who brings one.

 - "Move fast" reads to you as "lower the quality bar." Here it means the opposite, the bar is high AND the pace is high, and the system you build is how those two coexist.

 - You lead with an AI chatbot case study. We love AI and use it every day. But a conversational UI is not a demonstration of end-to-end product craft.

How we work

Small pods. Artifact first. Designers own their surfaces end to end, including research, QA, and the fight to get it shipped right. We use AI natively and expect you to. The design team is heads down on building the governed frontend layer this quarter, and this role is central to it.

We're in the office in New York because the best systems work happens shoulder to shoulder, obsessing over a real screen.

The bar

Restraint over decoration. Confidence over noise. Interfaces that feel calm because someone sweated every detail so the user never has to, and that feel alive because the motion is considered, not bolted on. We care about how money moving feels, how a card creation confirms, how a state transition lands. If "it looks fun, but does it do anything" is a question you ask yourself unprompted, you'll fit right in.

How to apply

If you've read this far and you're already thinking about how you'd architect our token layer, we should talk.

Come ready to do two things when we meet, walk us through a real, working file (not just the polished case study frames), and show us a design system you actually built and governed. Bring one deeply complex, systems level project and one piece you're proud of at the pixel level, and tell us plainly which decisions were yours.

jobs.title: Senior Data Engineer
jobs.description:
About Us

About the Role

Our team is looking for a Senior Data Engineer to join our data products team and help build & scale Rho's commercial banking technology.

The Data team builds data products for internal stakeholders and customers directly, maintaining a strong data driven culture across the company. This means treating data, pipelines, and ML systems as products in their own right: owned, versioned, documented, and built for other teams to discover and consume, not just infrastructure that sits behind the scenes. A key part of this role is building horizontal data products: reusable, ML-powered systems like an internal OCR pipeline, a transaction coding suggestion engine, and RAG-based and agentic systems that leverage our data to automate and augment internal workflows, that serve multiple teams and use cases across the company.

Technologies we use for data: Python, Go, Snowflake, DBT, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes, Terraform, Prometheus, Google Cloud Services, Omni, Hex

The ideal candidate is a strong software and data engineer with good taste & judgement, someone who knows what good looks like, and subscribes to a “strong opinions, weakly held” mindset.

Responsibilities:

- Design, build, and own data products, reliable, scalable, well-documented pipelines and datasets that other teams can discover, trust, and build on directly

 - Apply strong software engineering practices (clean code, testing, version control, CI/CD) to data products and ML systems, treating them with the same rigor as production software, while moving fast in AI-first world

 - Build horizontal, ML-driven data products, such as our OCR pipeline for document processing, our transaction coding suggestion system, and RAG/agentic tools, designed to be reused across multiple teams rather than built for a single use case

 - Define and uphold data product quality: implement quality checks, monitoring, alerts, and SLAs so consumers of a data product can rely on it the way they'd rely on any well-run internal API

 - Partner directly with the stakeholders who consume your data products to understand their needs, gather feedback, and iterate, treating them as customers rather than downstream requesters

 - Collaborate with business intelligence and analytics teams to turn business needs into data products that are easy to find, understand, and self-serve from

 - Lead initiatives to grow Rho's catalog of data products and improve the platform that supports them, expanding what other teams can build on top of

Requirements:

- 5+ years of experience in data engineering, software engineering, or DevOps

 - Proficiency in workflow orchestrators such as Airflow, Dagster, or Prefect

 - Experience with major data platforms including Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, or in-house HDFS-based solutions

 - Skilled at building data infrastructure using GCP, AWS, or comparable cloud providers

 - Comfortable managing and deploying services on Kubernetes

 - Practical experience with Terraform or Pulumi for automating infrastructure

 - Advanced programming abilities in Python and Go are integral to this role, along with strong SQL skills (Java experience also considered)

 - Proven experience building, owning, and iterating on data products or data pipelines based on consumer feedback, not just building infrastructure in isolation

 - Experience designing systems for reuse across multiple teams

 - Good communication skills and a team-oriented, collaborative approach, comfortable working directly with the people who consume what you build

Nice To Haves:

 - Experience building a data platform or data product suite from the ground up

 - Experience integrating or deploying ML models into production systems (e.g., classification, suggestion, or extraction models)

 - Experience with RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) systems and vector databases

 - Experience building or deploying agents

 - Experience with data modeling and data product approaches such as Data Mesh, Kimball, Inmon, Data Vault, or similar

 - Experience working with streaming data systems

 - Familiarity with Prometheus or other time-series databases used for monitoring

 - Experience with business intelligence (BI) tools such as Omni 

What we offer

Our people are our most valuable asset. Base salary may vary depending on relevant experience, skills, geographic location, and business needs.

- Top-notch Private Healthcare Insurance for you and your family members

 - Generous PTO policy

 - Lunch at work

 - Learning and development budget

 - Hybrid work environment (with old town Belgrade office)

jobs.title: Law Firm & Accounting Partnerships Lead
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Rho is looking for a Law Firm & Accounting Partnerships Lead to own two of our highest-leverage referral channels: the startup law firms that incorporate companies on day one, and the accounting, bookkeeping, and outsourced CFO firms that run their books from day two onward. These are the advisors founders trust before they ever pick a bank — and the firms that shape which financial stack a company lands on.

You'll own this channel end to end: strategy, partner sourcing, negotiation, launch, enablement, and the revenue that comes out of it. This is a builder role, not a maintenance role. You'll inherit early relationships and a real product story, and your mandate is to turn that into a repeatable, quota-carrying channel with a named partner roster, a working referral motion, and reporting leadership can trust.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

OWN THE CHANNEL STRATEGY

 - Define the segmentation and target list for both sides of the channel: startup-focused law firms (formation, emerging companies, venture practices) and accounting/bookkeeping/OCFO firms

 - Build the business case for where to invest — which firms, which geographies, which practice groups drive the most qualified client referrals

 - Set the partner tiering model and the value exchange at each tier (co-marketing, dedicated support, revenue share, product access)

 - Own the channel number: sourced pipeline, referred accounts, funded accounts, and revenue contribution

SOURCE AND CLOSE PARTNERS

 - Prospect, pitch, and close new law firm and accounting firm partnerships — this is a hunting role, not an inbound one

 - Build relationships with multiple stakeholders inside each firm: managing partners, practice group leads, business development, and the associates and staff who actually make the referral

 - Structure and negotiate partnership terms alongside Legal and Finance

 - Represent Rho at the conferences, bar association events, CPA gatherings, and founder dinners where these relationships get built (expect meaningful travel to major tech hubs)

DRIVE REFERRALS AND PARTNER REVENUE

 - Turn signed partnerships into activated ones — a logo on a page is not a partnership

 - Run onboarding and enablement so partner teams know exactly when and how to introduce Rho to a client

 - Build the co-marketing motion with Marketing: webinars, CPE-eligible content, perk pages, newsletters, and joint events

 - Run MBRs/QBRs with top partners against shared goals, and prune the partners who aren't producing

BE THE VOICE OF THE CHANNEL INTERNALLY

 - Work cross-functionally with Sales, Onboarding, Support, and Product to make sure referred clients get a white-glove handoff

 - Bring structured feedback to Product on what law firms and accounting partners need from Rho — multi-entity views, advisor access, close workflows, integrations

 - Partner with Sales leadership so channel-sourced deals are worked, tracked, and credited cleanly

BUILD THE OPERATING SYSTEM

 - Stand up the infrastructure that makes the channel scale: partner CRM hygiene, referral attribution, pipeline tracking, and a partner portal experience

 - Document the playbook — partner onboarding, referral handoff, enablement, and event workflows — so the next hires ramp fast

 - Produce clear, regular reporting on channel-sourced pipeline and revenue for leadership
 
 

WHO YOU ARE

 - 5+ years in partnerships, channel, or a closing sales role — ideally at a fintech, B2B SaaS, or professional services platform selling into or through advisors

 - You've carried a number and hit it. You're comfortable with a quota tied to partner-sourced revenue

 - You've built something from scratch. You know the difference between running a program and starting one, and you want the second

 - Credible with professionals: you can hold a real conversation with a managing partner about their book of business, not just pitch a product

 - Strong commercial instincts — you can structure a deal, run a negotiation, and know when to walk away

 - Excellent written and verbal communicator; you can present to an executive audience and write a partner email that actually gets replies

 - Data-driven: you instrument the channel, read the numbers, and reallocate effort accordingly

 - Thrives in ambiguity, moves fast, and doesn't need a playbook handed to you — you're writing it

 - Based in the Bay Area and willing to travel (~25–35%)

BONUS POINTS

 - Existing network among startup law firms and/or accounting, bookkeeping, and OCFO firms

 - Background in accounting or law (CPA, JD, or time inside a firm) — you've lived the workflow you're selling into

 - Experience launching a partner program at a fintech or spend management company

 - Familiarity with the startup ecosystem — VCs, accelerators, formation platforms, fund admins

 - Experience with partner CRM/PRM tooling and referral attribution

Why This Role

Law firms and accountants are the highest-trust distribution channel in the startup market — at comparable companies, the accounting channel alone has grown into one of the largest sources of new customers. Rho hasn't built it yet. You'd own that from the ground up, with a direct line to leadership, a clear number, and the room to build a team behind you as the channel proves out.

COMPENSATION

$150-200K OTE
Equity, health/dental/vision, 401(k), and other benefits included.

Financial Crime Analyst

We're looking for an experienced financial crime analyst to support our overall fraud and anti-money laundering (AML) strategy and operations, working alongside and supporting the Financial Crime lead as a critical member of the team. As a core member of the team, you will have a unique opportunity to learn and apply your previous experience, design and innovate financial crime detection systems, while conducting data analysis and being actively engaged cross-functionally. You will help lead efforts to build a best-in-class program that directly supports a seamless and frictionless client experience while reducing fraud and AML risk exposure and protecting against financial loss and regulatory risk.

 - Prepare and file Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs) and maintain supporting documentation in line with regulatory requirements

 - Assist customers by preparing and responding to inquiries related to fraud and financial crime investigations, and support the resolution of incidents

 - Document investigation processes and outcomes to maintain audit-ready records

 - Maintain department productivity goals and quality standards

 - Collaborate with the Financial Crime team to support and refine our operations, working cross-functionally with Client Services, Financial Operations, Compliance, and Transaction Monitoring teams

 - Maintain regular communication with team members to ensure maximum efficiency in recovery efforts and support ongoing strategy management

 - Deep dive into individual fraud and AML event vectors to perform root cause analyses

 - Support KYC/CIP and customer due diligence (CDD/EDD) reviews as needed

jobs.title: Payment Operations Associate
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the role

We're looking for a Payment Operations Associate to support Rho's day-to-day payment processing. You'll process client repayments, issue rewards and credits, resolve payment exceptions, and keep credit and card program settings up to date, working alongside Credit Risk, Client Services, Fraud, Compliance, and our partner bank. The work is deadline-driven and detail-oriented, and it feeds directly into client statements and month-end close.

What you will do

 - Process client repayments. Run recurring ACH pulls for monthly credit repayments on a fixed due-date schedule, handling non-standard accounts manually, and process interim payments as they arise. Confirm each payment is captured accurately from initiation through posting.

 - Issue rewards, credits, and incentives. Calculate and release cashback rewards on a set monthly schedule, reconcile against system-generated figures, and process statement credits, sign-up bonuses, and promotional incentives with the appropriate review and approval. Provide cashback breakdowns to clients on request.

 - Maintain credit and card program settings. Update client credit limits, payment terms, statement cycles and custom pricing, keeping records consistent across systems and documenting every change.

 - Manage wire operations. Handle wire trace requests, recalls, returns, and non-posted wires with our partner bank, and administer enrollments and limit changes for drawdown wire services.

 - Manage ACH operations. Initiate ACH returns and reversals in line with NACHA rules, applying the correct return code and meeting NACHA return/reversal timeframes that apply to each request.

 - Support fraud and credit review. Expedite settlement on transactions once Fraud or Credit has approved them, and hold transactions for review when something looks unusual. Manage RDC returns with outreach to the relevant teams, and set the appropriate settlement delay or instant release on credit repayments based on client credit risk.

 - Report on delinquency. Produce a weekly past-due report for Credit Risk, Finance, Client Services, and Fraud, monitor 30-day credit repayment returns and overdue balances daily, and escalate for client outreach.

 - Route compliance, fraud and legal escalations. jobs.description:
About Us
