About the Role

Rho ships faster than anyone in our category. Over the next year, we're entering new product categories and launching our most ambitious products yet.

Your job is to make every launch land: to take a product from "engineering says it's nearly ready" to "customers understand it, sales can sell it, and the market notices."

You'll sit at the center of go-to-market, working daily with Product, Engineering, Sales, Sales Enablement, Customer Success, Growth, Creative, and Comms. You'll see what's shipping, who needs to know, and what happens after, before anyone else does. And you'll shape the product, not just the launch: you bring customer and market evidence into decisions on who we build for, what we charge, and what ships.

The best people in this seat are a little obsessed. They read the customer transcript twice, can't leave a launch plan vague, and catch the dependency nobody else noticed. When they see an opportunity, they ask "why not today?"

You'll report to the VP of Marketing and manage a product marketer. Together you'll ship agents that extend the team's impact.

What you'll own

 - Launches, end to end. You're the single owner of the plan for every major launch: sequencing, readiness, dependencies, go/no-go criteria, and follow-through after launch. When dates move, you keep it on the rails.

 - The bridge between Product and GTM. Join the product process early and pressure-test scope and timing from the customer's view. Weigh in on pricing, positioning, and feature set so we build what we can explain, price, and sell. Carry product decisions to Sales, Marketing, and CS, and market feedback back to Product.

 - Sales. Give reps positioning, objection handling, competitive talk tracks, and demo narratives. Train the Sales Enablement team, who train the reps, and run launch kickoffs with them. Stay close enough to deals to know what's working.

 - The launch calendar and adoption. Decide what gets loud, what ships quietly, and what isn't ready. Own product content with the content team so every product gets the attention it deserves, and own the release communications and adoption programs that get customers using it. Partner with growth engineers on lifecycle marketing.

 - New category entry. Own positioning, narrative, pricing story, competitive strategy, and execution, then turn it into a playbook that makes the next launch easier.

 - Positioning and messaging. Make complex, technical products clear to customers and to a market that hasn't heard of us. Turn research into sharp ICPs and messaging in the customer's own words.

 - The website. Own rho.co http://rho.co messaging from narrative to page architecture to copy, and ship changes yourself.

 - The customer learning system. Build direct relationships with buyers and users, run structured discovery, and log the objections and product gaps you hear. Own the synthesis, so product and GTM decisions every quarter trace back to customer evidence.

 - Customer marketing. Turn customers into proof: case studies, references, testimonials, advocates. Keep the Growth team stocked with a steady flow of fresh customer stories for every channel.

Products that customers adopt, a sales team that can sell what we ship, and product, pricing, and positioning decisions that trace back to customer evidence.

 - Product, Sales, and Marketing all trust you, and you push back with evidence.

 - You've worked closely with sales and know what a rep needs five minutes before a call.

The Role

Our Product Managers operate like owners of their surface. The APM role is how we develop the next ones.

You join a senior PM's team and own a defined part of a banking product. You ship to real customers in your first quarter. You get real scope, a direct mentor, and honest feedback every week. The goal: in 18 months, you own a surface as a full PM.

In banking, every interaction carries trust. Money moves, cards get declined, payments settle or fail. You learn how a regulated financial product works from the inside, and you learn to build products that customers trust with their money.

Own a feature area end to end. Your mentor gives you a defined part of the product. You own it from the problem to the result. Frame the problem, write the spec, ship it, and measure what changed. When the data shows a better direction, bring a recommendation, not only the data.

Build with Design and Engineering every day. Sit with your designer and engineers from the first sketch to the launch. Write specs that engineers want to read. Give clear feedback on flows and edge cases, because in banking an edge case is a customer's money. Unblock the team fast, and run launches end to end. In a regulated product, this also means that you bring Compliance and Operations in early, so they do not block the launch late.

Get close to customers. Talk to founders and finance teams every week. Read support tickets. Learn how early-stage companies think about cash, spend, and risk, and bring that knowledge back to the team.

Decide with data. Define success before you build. Pull your own data. Report clearly what worked and what did not.

Build with AI. Use frontier models to test ideas, build prototypes, analyze customer feedback, and draft specs. We expect AI to make you faster, and we expect you to find new ways to use it for our customers.

WHAT YOU GET

 - Weekly 1:1s and structured reviews at 6 and 12 months.

 - A clear path to Product Manager.

Who You Are

a technical background or coding experience, work at a bank or fintech, or startup experience.

jobs.title: Staff Security Engineer
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About Us

Rho is on a mission to make finance frictionless for organizations. Our team and technology power high-performing companies with an all-in-one, end-to-end finance platform that lets organizations safely manage cash and spending across commercial-grade banking, corporate cards, treasury management, expense management, accounts payable, and more. 

Our customers run their banking, cards, and payments through Rho. We are splitting a large Python monolith into Go and Python services on GCP, and shipping a public API, agents, and MCP surfaces. Security is part of the product. 

The Team 

Security at Rho is small: a VCISO, one security engineer in Poland, and the engineers who ship. You will be the first US security engineer. We plan to grow this into a team over the next six months, and you will help pick who. 

The Role

Hands-on. You write production code most days. You own product and platform security, and you own finding queues and incident response until we hire for detection and response. 

What you'll do
Product Security

 - Threat model new systems and review designs with the teams that own them before they ship. 

 - Build the paved road: secure defaults, guardrails in CI, dependency and supply chain checks, so the safe way is the easy way. 

 - Own the vulnerability lifecycle: triage findings from Pensar, Semgrep, CodeQL, Dependabot, pentests, and inbound researcher reports; hold the SLAs; write the fix or get it written; track remediation to zero. Stand up our vulnerability disclosure program. 

Platform Security

 - Harden GCP and GKE: least-privilege IAM, workload identity, secrets, network policy, environment separation, all in Terraform. 

 - Secure our LLM, agent, and MCP surfaces: guardrails, sandboxes, agents as identities with scoped access, prompt injection detection. 
 

Detection & Response

 - Own detections in our SIEM, tune signal to noise, keep the runbooks current, stand up on the call rotation, and lead incidents end to end: triage, contain, investigate, remediate, post-mortem. 

 - Run tabletop exercises and hunt for what detections miss. 

What we're looking for

 - 6+ years in security engineering, or software engineering with a security focus. You ship code and tools, not only findings.

 - Depth in one of product security, cloud and platform security, or detection and response, and working knowledge of the other two.

 - Comfortable changing production and owning the outcome. Python or Go, Kubernetes, Terraform, one major cloud.

 - You can triage competing risks and trade security against velocity without slowing the team down.

 - Clear writer: design reviews, runbooks and incident reports engineers actually read.

NICE TO HAVE

 - Fintech, payments or another regulated industry. PCI DSS or SOC 2 evidence work.

 - Bug bounty, red team, CVEs, talks, or open source.

 - Hands-on AI security: guardrails, agent identities, prompt injection.

jobs.title: Lead Web Designer
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

About the role

Most company websites are brochures. A hero, three feature tiles, a logo wall, a demo button. They get redesigned every few years and forgotten every few weeks in between.

Ours shouldn't be. For most founders, rho.co http://rho.co is the first time they meet us. It's where they decide whether we feel like a bank they'd trust with their company's money, long before they talk to anyone. That first impression is either doing the work for us or working against us.

We're hiring a Lead Web Designer to reimagine the entire site. Not a refresh. A rebuild of how Rho shows up in the world, from the homepage to every product page, pricing, our tools, our comparisons, our blog and our careers page.

We want rho.co http://rho.co to feel like the most considered financial brand on the internet. Calm, confident and alive. Restraint over decoration. Every page earns its place. If you've read this far and you're already thinking about what you'd change about our homepage, we should talk.

What you'll do

You'll own rho.co http://rho.co end to end. The story, the structure, the visual language, the motion and the details, all the way to production.

 - Reimagine the whole site. Rethink the information architecture, the narrative and the visual system from first principles. What a founder needs to understand, in what order, and how it should feel.

 - Make the product the hero. Show what Rho actually does with real, considered product moments rather than stock illustrations and vague promises.

 - Build a system, not a set of pages. Define the layouts, type, color, components and motion that let the site scale across dozens of product, solution and comparison pages without losing its voice.

 - Design in the real medium. You work in code and in our CMS, not just in static mocks. What you design is what ships.

 - Sweat the details. Type that's set with care. Motion that has a reason. Pages that load fast and feel calm. The 404 page that somebody actually smiles at.

 - Measure it. Partner with marketing and growth on what the site needs to achieve, and judge your work on whether more of the right founders sign up.

Who you are

You've been doing this for a while: at least 6 years designing and shipping marketing sites and brand experiences, with a portfolio that is visibly, unusually crafted. We need to see it. Live sites we can open, scroll and feel.

You are the kind of person who:

 - Treats a website like a product. You think about structure, flow and outcomes, not just how a page looks in a screenshot.

 - Has real typographic and editorial taste. You can make a page of words feel beautiful, and you know when to get out of the way.

 - Brings motion with restraint. You know when an interaction makes a page feel alive and when it's just noise.

 - Builds what you design. You're comfortable in code, a modern CMS, or both, and you care how the thing behaves on a phone at 7am on a slow connection.

 - Can tell a complicated story simply. Banking, cards, treasury and bill pay are dense. You find the clear, human way to explain them.

 - Can't turn your taste off. You notice the misaligned baseline on other people's sites, and you've rebuilt your own site more times than you'd admit.

Who this is not for

 - Product designers who want a side project. This is a full time, high craft role focused entirely on the website.

 - Template designers. If your best work is a theme with the logo swapped, this isn't the one.

 - Anyone who needs the brief written for them. You'll help define what the site needs to say and do.

 - People who think "good enough, ship it" is the standard for a homepage. Not here.

Our people are our most valuable asset. The salary range for this role is $110,000 - $150,000. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, healthcare benefits and paid time off.

jobs.title: Growth Product Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

Rho is the modern banking platform built for the AI era. Startups and growth-stage companies can open accounts in minutes, issue cards, manage expenses, pay bills, and close the books – all in one connected platform backed by real human support.

The Role

The best products grow because people can't stop using them and can't help telling others about them.

We want Rho to grow because of the product. Every founder who uses Rho pays vendors, issues cards to their team, and invites people in. Every one of those moments is someone meeting Rho for the first time, and a chance to bring in the next customer. Your job is to make the most of every one.

We're hiring a Growth PM to own how Rho grows through the product itself, from the first time someone hears about us to the moment Rho becomes their bank. That means three things:
1. Get founders into the funnel. Grow the top of the funnel through referrals, network effects and every place Rho already touches.
2. Get them through sign up. Work closely with your partners across product to make getting approved fast and painless.
3. Get them fully onboarded. Make sure they actually switch banks and start using everything Rho can do, not just open an account.

What you'd own

 - The growth strategy, not just the features. Define the bets, the channels and the metrics that drive our next stage of growth, and be accountable for the number.

 - A referral engine founders love to use. Make referring Rho effortless and a little bit fun, then keep making it better.

 - Network effects across every edge. Vendors who get paid, employees who get cards, payees, and accountants all touch Rho. Turn each of those into a reason to sign up.

 - The top of the funnel, in partnership with marketing. Work hand in hand with our marketing team on acquisition, conversion and where we invest.

 - Activation, all the way through. Get founders past sign up and into the product. Get them to switch banks, issue cards, pay their first bill, and run their business all on Rho.

 - Unconventional bets. Some of the best growth ideas won't look like product work. Bring them anyway.

Who you are

You've done this before: at least 5 years in product, with real growth or product led acquisition work you can point to and a number you moved.

You are the kind of person who:

 - Thinks in loops, not funnels. You see how one customer brings in the next and design for that.

 - Has strong product judgment and taste. Growth tactics that cheapen the product aren't wins. You find the ones that make it better.

 - Lives in the data. You size the opportunity, set the metric, run the experiment and know whether it worked.

 - Moves fast. You ship something real, learn from it, and ship again.

 - Uses AI to do more with less. Not just for your own work, but to build systems that let a small team grow a big business.

 - Partners well. Marketing, design, engineering, sales, post sales and support all touch growth. You bring them along.

Who this isn't for

 - Marketers who want to stay in marketing. This is a product role. You'll be building, not running campaigns.

 - Feature PMs looking for a change of scenery. Growth is its own craft. We need someone who already loves it.

 - Anyone who needs a fully formed roadmap handed to them. You'll write it.

The bar

We're building the best business banking platform in the world for founders. If you're already thinking about how you'd get every vendor we pay to become a customer, we should talk.

Our people are our most valuable asset. Our target compensation range for this role is $165,000 - $320,000. Compensation will be determined by leveling and performance throughout the interview process. In addition to base pay, Rho offers equity, comprehensive healthcare benefits, and paid time off.

 - Represent design in client-facing settings where needed.

 - Produce polished, well-considered design work using our existing design patterns - we're not looking for someone who wants to rethink the foundations. Maintain design coherence across a product suite that serves multiple user types with meaningfully different needs.

 - Handle the full range of design needs: big new features, incremental iterations, mobile polish, and the occasional slide deck or screenshot pull for the sales team.
 

Who You Are

 - An experienced product design leader with 8+ years of product design experience, especially in lean team environments. Experience in fintech, financial services, or a regulated product environment is a plus.

 - Stellar end-to-end design chops, from early discovery and concept development through detailed interaction design and QA.

 - Excellent judgment about process. You know when to go deep and when to move fast, and you can explain why.

 - Comfortable presenting design decisions and rationale to senior stakeholders, including to external partners.

 - Grounded in existing patterns and best practices, and you are not looking to reinvent the wheel, but always looking to make it roll better.

 - Aligned with our values: humility, ambition, caring, excellence, inclusion, and a genuine belief that the work matters.

 - Familiarity with AI-powered product features and the UX considerations that come with them is a plus.

Why You’ll Love Us

 - We operate with the pace of a startup, the rigor of a financial services firm, and the mission-orientation of a company that deeply cares about the people it serves.

 - With fifty million Americans in our addressable market, we are building for the millions of people who need our products and services across the country - and we’ve got the potential to reach many more.

 - We have the privilege of providing financial protection for vulnerable members of society and partnering with expert service providers to do so. Our customers and partners love us, and we love them back. You can sleep soundly every night knowing you are doing a great thing by getting our services into more hands.

 - We treat one another like we treat our customers: with respect and dignity. Diversity, equity, and inclusion are cultural values we take very seriously, and we welcome and recruit team members of all backgrounds and identities.

 - We offer competitive wages, health, dental & vision coverage, paid parental leave, 12 paid holidays each year, your own professional development budget, and generous vacation.

If you are a high-performing person who wants to join a diverse, inclusive team and use your skills to make a real impact in people’s lives, we invite you to apply to join our team.

We're proud of what we've built — and we're just getting started. Read our Culture Manual and learn more about how we work.

About the team

The Finance team is where numbers become decisions. Within Finance, Treasury looks after the cash that moves through Wealthsimple every day — across a growing number of entities, currencies, and products. As we've expanded, so has the complexity of that job: more accounts to watch, more flows to move, more systems to keep working together. This role sits within Cash & Collateral Management and reports to the Senior Manager on that team. We're a small, high-trust group — embedded in the business, not reporting from the sidelines — and we hold ourselves to a high bar for both rigour and clarity. If you want your work to actually shape how the company operates, this is the place to do it.

About the role

Wealthsimple's cash operations have grown more complex as our product line-up has expanded — more entities, more currencies, more moving parts. This role exists to keep that complexity under control: owning the day-to-day movement and monitoring of cash, while also driving the automation work needed to make it scale. It's not a "keep the lights on" role. You'll be expected to build the tools and processes that make cash management faster and more reliable, not just operate what already exists.

This role doesn't have direct reports today, but there's real opportunity to grow into people leadership as the team scales.

What you'll do

 - Own the daily, business-critical money movements that power our products — making sure funds land where they need to, when they need to, across multiple entities and currencies

 - Manage short-term liquidity so there's always enough on hand to fund settlements and meet daily obligations, without idle cash sitting where it shouldn't

 - Analyze and forecast cash needs through detailed bank balance monitoring and flow-of-funds analysis — turning raw account data into decisions the business can act on, including intercompany funding requirements

 - Support new product launches by scoping their cash flow, settlement, and account requirements early

 - Scale and improve the systems we already use for cash management rather than just maintaining them — building automation for balance monitoring, transfers, and forecasting that lets the processes scale efficiently

 - Partner with product, engineering, and finance teams to keep cash operations in step with the business as it moves and expands

Skills you bring

 - 5+ years of experience in treasury, cash management, or corporate banking operations

 - Experience managing cash positioning and forecasting across multiple entities and currencies

 - Strong understanding of banking infrastructure — account structures, payment rails, and settlement processes

 - Experience leading or contributing to the automation of manual treasury or cash processes

 - Advanced Excel and SQL skills, with comfort working with large datasets to drive forecasting and analysis

 - Experience working cross-functionally with product, engineering, or finance teams to support new product launches

 - Clear communication skills — you can explain cash and treasury mechanics to people who don't work in treasury

Nice to have

 - Experience in fintech or a regulated financial services environment

 - Familiarity with treasury management systems (TMS) or ERP treasury modules

 - Exposure to building automation tools using scripting or low-code platforms (e.g., Python, SQL-based workflows)

 - Experience with intercompany funding structures or multi-entity treasury operations

jobs.title: Agent(e), Opérations de l'expérience client – Télétravail (CDD)
jobs.description:
BUILD SOMETHING PEOPLE LOVE

Wealthsimple is Canada’s leading financial innovator. The company offers a full suite of simple, sophisticated financial products across managed investing, do-it-yourself trading, cryptocurrency, tax filing, spending and saving. Wealthsimple currently serves more than 4 million Canadians and holds over $169 billion in assets under administration. L'équipe Opérations de l'expérience client façonne, au quotidien, l'expérience que Wealthsimple offre à sa clientèle. Nous gérons les interactions concrètes, par courriel, par clavardage et par téléphone, ainsi que les moments charnières où une personne choisit de nous confier, ou non, sa vie financière. Notre objectif est simple : offrir un soutien rapide, fluide et fiable qui dépasse les attentes des personnes que nous servons.

 - Modèle 100 % télétravail : Ce poste est entièrement à distance. Vous pouvez travailler de n'importe où au Canada.

 - Environnement de travail : Bien que le poste soit à distance, les candidats doivent disposer d'un espace de travail privé, calme et professionnel, doté d'une connexion Internet haute vitesse fiable, afin de garantir la confidentialité et la qualité de nos interactions avec les clients.

 - Date de début visée : le 4 janvier, 2027.

 - Contrat : Engagement initial de 6 mois avec possibilité de prolongation et opportunités d'évolution en interne.

Wealthsimple connaît une croissance rapide, et chaque jour, de plus en plus de Canadiennes et de Canadiens commencent à utiliser notre plateforme. Cette croissance s'accompagne d'un effort tout aussi important pour que notre clientèle ait de moins en moins besoin de nous joindre. Nous nous attaquons aux causes profondes des problèmes courants et créons de meilleurs outils en libre-service, notamment grâce à l'IA, afin que la clientèle puisse régler les questions simples de façon autonome. Notre équipe peut ainsi se concentrer sur les conversations où l'intervention humaine fait toute la différence.

Quand quelque chose ne fonctionne pas comme la cliente ou le client s'y attendait, c'est vous qui rectifiez le tir. Vous aiderez la clientèle par clavardage, au téléphone et par courriel, en prenant en charge des questions et des problèmes qui demandent une vraie réflexion, et non des réponses toutes faites. Certains jours, il s'agira de démêler une situation complexe; d'autres jours, de rassurer une personne et de l'accompagner étape par étape. C'est un travail exigeant et structuré, qui demande un bon jugement, de l'intelligence émotionnelle et le sens des responsabilités nécessaire pour mener chaque dossier à terme. Bien exercé, ce rôle est l'un des plus importants chez Wealthsimple.

CE QUE VOUS FEREZ

 - Aider la clientèle par clavardage, au téléphone et par courriel, en gérant un flux constant de conversations du début à la fin.

 - Accompagner la clientèle dans ce qui compte le plus pour elle, qu'il s'agisse de questions rapides ou de problèmes complexes liés à ses placements ou à ses services bancaires.

 - Écouter attentivement, vous mettre à la place de la clientèle et communiquer avec la clarté, la chaleur et la bienveillance auxquelles elle devrait s'attendre chaque fois qu'elle s'adresse à Wealthsimple.

 - Prendre en charge chaque dossier qui vous est confié : trouver la véritable source du problème, dénicher la réponse même face à une situation inédite et faire un suivi pour que rien ne passe entre les mailles du filet.

 - Travailler selon un horaire établi et atteindre des cibles claires en matière de qualité, de productivité et de respect de l'horaire. Ces cibles sont au cœur de l'évaluation du rendement dans ce poste.

 - Acquérir une connaissance approfondie des produits de Wealthsimple et des notions financières sur lesquelles ils reposent, et continuer d'apprendre au fil de leur évolution.

 - Tirer parti du coaching et de la rétroaction sur la qualité pour perfectionner constamment votre savoir-faire.

VOS DÉBUTS:

 - Excellente maîtrise du français et de l'anglais, avec une communication écrite et orale claire et chaleureuse dans les deux langues (exigence essentielle).

 - Expérience en service à la clientèle, que ce soit en technologie, en hôtellerie et restauration, dans le commerce de détail, dans les services financiers ou dans un autre domaine.

 - Bon jugement et capacité à prendre rapidement de bonnes décisions, même quand la réponse n'est pas évidente.

 - Grande intelligence émotionnelle, notamment la capacité à bien cerner les gens et à garder son sang-froid dans les situations tendues.

 - Débrouillardise et détermination pour trouver des réponses par vous-même.

 - Vitesse et précision au clavier, et agilité pour passer rapidement d'un outil ou d'un système à l'autre sans perdre de vue la clientèle.

 - Aisance à travailler selon un horaire établi et avec des cibles mesurables.

ATOUTS

 - De 1 à 2 ans d'expérience dans les services financiers

QUI VOUS ÊTES

Vous prenez les choses en main. Quand une cliente ou un client vous soumet un problème, ce problème devient le vôtre jusqu'à ce qu'il soit réglé. Vous ne le refilez pas à quelqu'un d'autre en espérant que tout se passe bien. La curiosité vous pousse à comprendre comment les choses fonctionnent, et vous faites preuve de débrouillardise quand la réponse ne saute pas aux yeux. Vous avez à cœur les personnes que vous aidez, et cela se voit : vous sentez quand une personne s'inquiète pour son argent, et vous savez ramener le calme dans la conversation. Enfin, vous avez la détermination nécessaire pour bien faire ce travail jour après jour, même quand la file d'attente déborde et que les problèmes sont difficiles.

Nul besoin d'une formation en finance. Les personnes qui viennent de la technologie, de l'hôtellerie et de la restauration ou du commerce de détail possèdent souvent exactement les compétences que ce poste exige. Ce qui compte le plus, c'est la curiosité, la débrouillardise, l'habitude de résoudre les problèmes par soi-même et un réel souci de la clientèle.

VOS DÉBUTS

Vous apprendrez ce que vous devez savoir une fois parmi nous. Notre programme d'intégration est conçu pour que toute personne ayant les bonnes compétences puisse réussir, peu importe son parcours.

Vous commencerez par une formation sur Wealthsimple : nos produits, notre clientèle, ainsi que les principes et les normes qui guident notre façon de la servir. Vous aurez un aperçu de tout ce que nous faisons. Vous mettrez ensuite ces apprentissages en pratique en aidant la clientèle dans un contexte réel et encadré, le temps de prendre de l'assurance. Quand le moment sera venu, vous intégrerez un secteur précis de notre équipe de soutien pour vous spécialiser, approfondir vos connaissances et développer une expertise dans un volet de nos activités.

Des possibilités d'avancement existent au-delà de ce poste, et certaines personnes accèdent à d'autres rôles chez Wealthsimple. Ce n'est toutefois pas automatique : cela se mérite en faisant bien ce travail et en prenant en main votre propre développement.

 - Congés payés (PTO) Jusqu’à 20 jours de vacances par an (selon la durée du contrat) + 1 jour de congé de maladie payé par mois.

 - Matériel informatique Nous vous fournissons le tout dernier MacBook sur le marché. De plus, vous recevrez en cadeau un écran, un clavier, une souris, un adaptateur et un casque d'écoute pour travailler avec tout le confort nécessaire.

jobs.title: Staff/Senior Product Designer, Growth
jobs.description:
BUILD SOMETHING PEOPLE LOVE

Wealthsimple is Canada’s leading financial innovator. The company offers a full suite of simple, sophisticated financial products across managed investing, do-it-yourself trading, cryptocurrency, tax filing, spending and saving. Wealthsimple currently serves more than 4 million Canadians and holds over $169 billion in assets under administration. The company was founded in 2014 by a team of financial experts and technology entrepreneurs, and is headquartered in Toronto, Canada.

We're proud of what we've built — and we're just getting started. Read our Culture Manual https://www.wealthsimple.com/en-ca/culture and learn more about how we work https://www.wealthsimple.com/en-ca/careers.

About the team

As a Product Designer on Growth, you’ll turn ambitious ideas into meaningful experiences that move the business forward. More than 4 million Canadians trust Wealthsimple with their money. Your job is to grow that number by designing the experiences that turn clients into our biggest advocates.

You’ll partner with Product, Engineering and Marketing to rethink our referral strategy, support our highest visibility campaigns, and lead 0 to 1 social features from the ground up. You'll help define and lead our entire growth domain, rethink how people discover and share Wealthsimple, and create experiences that make our products more valuable as our community grows. It’s an opportunity to shape a brand new product area, move fast, and turn great ideas into measurable impact.

What you’ll do

 - Build the loops that fuel growth. Design experiences that turn discovery into acquisition, engagement into advocacy, and happy clients into our strongest growth channel, driving new clients and net deposits.

 - Help define Social at Wealthsimple. Explore and shape new ways for people to connect with their financial lives, from profiles and discovery to creators and sharing investing activity.

 - Reinvent referrals. Rethink how people invite others to Wealthsimple, including seamless, real-world experiences like QR-based invites.

 - Make big ideas tangible. Shape high-visibility campaigns like Monthly Millionaire and Match, creating experiences that reach millions of Canadians and give people a reason to engage.

 - Experiment your way to impact. Prototype, launch, measure, learn, and iterate. Know when to double down, when to pivot, and when to move on.

 - Own the experience end-to-end. Move fluidly from discovery and strategy to interaction design, polished visuals, and thoughtful micro-interactions.

 - Shape what we build next. Partner closely with Product and Engineering to turn ambiguous problems into clear opportunities, influence roadmaps, and bring ambitious ideas to life.

Skills you bring

 - Growth design experience. You’ve designed consumer experiences across acquisition, activation, engagement, or retention, and can point to the impact your work made.

About the team:

At Wealthsimple, we aren't just managing portfolios; we're rewriting the rules of how Canadians interact with credit. The Credit Analytics team own’s Wealthsimple's lending ecosystem, operating at the intersection of high-growth tech and data-driven underwriting.

We believe that being “credit-worthy” should mean more than just a traditional score. Our mission is to challenge the status quo, building inclusive products that empower millions of Canadians and the businesses they run to lead better financial lives. We’re growing fast, moving from small data to massive scale through iteration and experimentation.

We are extending our consumer credit expertise into business lending built for Canadian small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs). This is a true green-field build — new adjudication policy, new underwriting signals, and new risk infrastructure, informed by everything we've learned scaling our consumer card portfolio.

About

the role:

We are looking for a Senior Associate to own credit policy for our business lending products, starting with a business credit card — from adjudication through the full account lifecycle. You will design and implement the underwriting framework that determines who qualifies and at what limit, build the line management strategies that govern how those limits evolve, and partner closely with collections to manage risk once accounts are on book.

Small business cards can be underwritten on the owner, or on the business as it grows. You’ll be working with cash flow, seasonality, industry, and business bureau data, which is usually thinner and messier than consumer bureau data. We need someone who has worked across that range and can turn it into automated policy instead of file-by-file decisions.

You will collaborate cross-functionally with Engineering, Product, Data Science, Fraud, and Client Experience to translate policy into shippable adjudication and monitoring systems, and you will have significant ownership over how this portfolio’s risk appetite is defined from day one.

In this role, you will have the opportunity to:

 - Build a new lending program from the ground up with the breadth to see every part of it, from policy to funding, and the runway to grow into leading a lending line of business.

 - Design and own the adjudication policy for a new business credit card, including entity-level underwriting criteria, principal/guarantor assessment, joint-liability, initial limit-setting, and approval decisioning.

 - Own line management strategy for business credit products: credit limit increases and decreases, pricing, authorization rules, and active exposure management driven by cash-flow and balance monitoring.

 - Partner with the collections team to design risk-managed treatment strategies specific to business accounts, and to build lifecycle monitoring that catches emerging risk early.

 - Evaluate the performance of the business lending portfolio and your policies, using vintage analysis, cohort tracking, and champion/challenger testing to validate and refine underwriting decisions.

 - Propose policy enhancements that improve marginal profitability while keeping risk within appetite, informed by rigorous root-cause analysis rather than surface-level metrics.

 - Help define the data and underwriting infrastructure needed for SMB lending — including how to source, validate, and weigh business financial data alongside traditional bureau signals.

 - Influence roadmaps across partner teams (Engineering, Product, Data Science, Fraud, and Client Experience) and implement policy that drives measurable impact.

We're looking for someone who:

 - Has direct experience underwriting or setting credit policy for small and medium-sized businesses, this is a must-have for this role. Card experience isn't required; we'd love to hear from you if your background is in instalment loans or lines of credit.

 - Writes SQL hands-on to self-serve data and build monitoring and analytics.

 - Brings credit discipline to a ship-and-iterate environment, and is comfortable shaping policy while the product itself is still being defined.

 - Can turn analysis into a clear recommendation for technical and non-technical audiences, weigh incomplete or noisy information and still reach well-grounded decisions.

 - Is intellectually curious, passionate about their work, and wants ownership over their projects.

Preferred

qualifications:

- 5+ years of experience in small business lending

 - Knowledge of Canadian consumer credit bureau data (Equifax, TransUnion)

 - Working knowledge of how business credit risk differs from consumer credit risk: entity vs. personal guarantor assessment, business bureau data (e.g., business credit bureaus), cash-flow-based underwriting, industry/sector risk, and revenue seasonality.

 - Experience across the credit lifecycle: adjudication policy, line management, pricing, and collections strategy.

 - Experience with statistical/quantitative analysis: experimental design, champion/challenger (or A/B) testing, model accuracy validation, constrained optimization, decision trees, discounted cash flows, financial modeling.

 - Experience with Python, and GitHub. Airflow, AWS Redshift, and dbt are a plus.

Reporting to the Director, People Analytics, you will own that work end to end, from the question through to the thing people actually use. Success looks like recurring people decisions getting made from what you built.

About the team

People Analytics sits within People and Communications. We are growing the people domain and want to get deeper into our data, through the models, data products, and analysis that leaders across the company use to make calls about talent. We are a small team, building like a startup inside the People team. Analytics developers own the data foundation, analysts handle day-to-day reporting, and software engineers build the products that put insights in front of managers. As our first data scientist, you will help set what best in class looks like for people analytics at Wealthsimple.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the model building and the deeper analysis on people data, including attrition risk, workforce forecasting, and how talent moves and develops across the company.

 - Build people data products that leaders keep coming back to, working with our software engineers to put them in front of managers across Wealthsimple.

 - Move up and down the data stack as the question demands, from raw data through to the model and the surface it lands on.

 - Turn open questions from leaders and partners across the company into analysis they can act on, and be clear about what the data can and cannot support.

 - Bring statistical rigour to how we understand talent density and performance management, forming hypotheses and testing them so people decisions are data informed.

 - Set the analytical standard for the function and raise the level of craft around you, through how we test, document, and review our work.

SKILLS YOU BRING

 - 5+ years in data science or a related quantitative role, owning ambiguous problems end to end.

 - Advanced SQL and Python, applied to work you have taken all the way to production rather than left in a notebook.

 - Applied statistics and causal inference. You can pick a method, defend it, and explain why a correlation is not enough for the decision in front of you.

 - Experience building and evaluating predictive models on messy operational data, including the judgment to say when a model is not the right answer.

 - Experience turning analysis into recommendations that senior leaders act on, including pushing back when the question itself is wrong. You lead with the outcome, then explain how you got there.

 - Comfort working close to the data layer, with modelled datasets, point-in-time history, and a cloud data platform such as Snowflake.

NICE TO HAVE

 - HR data literacy: employee lifecycle events, job hierarchies, headcount types, and compensation structures.

 - Workforce planning or headcount forecasting.

 - Experience with survey and engagement data.

 - Experience measuring people performance, such as review ratings, calibration outcomes, or goal attainment.

People analytics experience helps, but it is not required. If you have done this kind of work in product, marketing, growth, or customer analytics and you are curious about people data, we want to hear from you.

WHO YOU ARE

 - You are energised by building, and you do not need a paved road to do good work.

 - You think about privacy the way a good engineer thinks about security, as a design constraint rather than an obstacle.

 - You would rather ship a useful answer and improve it than hold a perfect one back.

 - You are direct about uncertainty and say what you do not know before anyone asks.

 - You move between technical and non-technical conversations naturally.

 - You are pragmatic about AI tools and know where they speed you up and where they do not.

WHY YOU’LL LOVE THIS ROLE

 - Ground-floor impact: Most of this work hasn’t been done yet, so you’ll shape how it gets done.

 - Visibility: Your work goes in front of leadership and shapes real decisions about talent.

 - Builders around you: Your models ship into products managers use, not slide decks

About the Fund Operations team

Fund Operations is the team that keeps our Alternative Investment Funds products running accurately and at scale. We own the operational functions behind private credit, private equity, private markets, venture, and infrastructure fund structures, including NAV oversight, capital activity, and financial reporting. We're a small, high-ownership team that works closely with Legal, Compliance, Investment Research, and external Fund Administrators, GPs, Custodians, and Auditors to build institutional-grade processes as our alternatives platform grows.

About the role

As a Senior Specialist, Fund Operations at Wealthsimple, you'll be the primary owner of the Net Asset Value (NAV) for our private market vehicles. You won't just report on it; you'll act as the bridge between our external fund administrators and our internal product and investment teams. Our Alternative offerings, ranging from Private Credit to Private Equity funds, need to be accounted for with institutional-grade precision, and that precision starts with you. We're looking for a technical, detail-oriented self-starter who is excited about building new processes from the ground up and owning the outcomes.

What you'll do

 - Lead the month-end and year-end close process by validating the Fund Administrator's NAV, resolving breaks in valuation, fee accruals, and partner capital balances.

 - Manage the operational accounting for the full lifecycle of private investments, including capital calls, distributions, and waterfall calculations.

 - Oversee the production of audited financial statements in compliance with IFRS and ASPE, with a specific focus on Fair Value Measurement (Level 3 assets) and specialized disclosure requirements for alternatives.

 - Act as the central point of contact for a sophisticated ecosystem including external Fund Managers (GPs), Custodians, and Auditors, while providing Legal, Compliance, and Investment Research with clear, reliable financial data.

 - Lead the year-end audit process for Alternative funds, serving as the primary liaison with external auditors, supporting regulatory filings (OSC/SEC), and assisting with the preparation of T3/T5013 slips for Wealthsimple clients.

 - Identify opportunities to automate manual data feeds and improve the scalability of our operational model.

 - Handle in-kind and mutual fund transfer transactions within Fundserv, acting as a subject matter expert on Fundserv from a fund manufacturing and dealer perspective.
 
 

Skills you bring

 - 3-5 years of progressive experience in fund accounting, ideally from a top-tier fund administrator or a specialized alternatives shop

 - Deep competence in alternative fund-of-fund (FoF) and direct investment vehicles, with strong familiarity with limited partnership structures, management fee offsets, and carried interest calculations

 - Advanced Excel skills, including modeling waterfalls and reconciliation tools

 - Experience with investment accounting software (e.g., Investran, eFront, Allvue, or Geneva) is preferred

 - CPA, CFA, or an equivalent professional designation is preferred
